to.quick_def: You use to when indicating the place that someone or something visits, moves towards, or points at.

early.quick_def: Early means before the usual time that a particular event or activity happens.

man.quick_def: A man is an adult male human being.

fire.quick_def: Fire is the hot, bright flames produced by things that are burning.

was.quick_def: You use be with a present participle to form the continuous tenses of verbs.

a.quick_def: You use a or an when you are referring to someone or something for the first time or when people may not know which particular person or thing you are talking about.

divine.quick_def: You use divine to describe something that is provided by or relates to a god or goddess.

gift.quick_def: A gift is something that you give someone as a present.

randomly.quick_def: A random sample or method is one in which all the people or things involved have an equal chance of being chosen.

delivered.quick_def: If you deliver something somewhere, you take it there.

in.quick_def: Someone or something that is in something else is enclosed by it or surrounded by it. If you put something in a container, you move it so that it is enclosed by the container.

the.quick_def: You use the at the beginning of noun groups to refer to someone or something that you have already mentioned or identified.

form.quick_def: A form of something is a type or kind of it.

of.quick_def: You use of to combine two nouns when the first noun identifies the feature of the second noun that you want to talk about.

lightning.quick_def: Lightning is the very bright flashes of light in the sky that happen during thunderstorms.

forest.quick_def: A forest is a large area where trees grow close together.

or.quick_def: You use or to link two or more alternatives.

burning.quick_def: If there is a fire or a flame somewhere, you say that there is a fire or flame burning there.

lava.quick_def: Lava is the very hot liquid rock that comes out of a volcano.

unable.quick_def: If you are unable to do something, it is impossible for you to do it, for example because you do not have the necessary skill or knowledge, or because you do not have enough time or money.

make.quick_def: You can use make with a wide range of nouns to indicate that someone performs an action or says something. For example, if you make a suggestion, you suggest something.

flame.quick_def: A flame is a hot bright stream of burning gas that comes from something that is burning.

for.quick_def: If something is for someone, they are intended to have it or benefit from it.

themselves.quick_def: You use themselves to refer to people, animals, or things when the object of a verb or preposition refers to the same people or things as the subject of the verb.

earliest.quick_def: Earliest is the superlative of early.

peoples.quick_def: People are men, women, and children. People is normally used as the plural of person, instead of 'persons'.

probably.quick_def: If you say that something is probably the case, you think that it is likely to be the case, although you are not sure.  [vagueness]

stored.quick_def: A store is a building or part of a building where things are sold. In British English, store is used mainly to refer to a large shop selling a variety of goods, but in American English a store can be any size of shop.

by.quick_def: If something is done by a person or thing, that person or thing does it.

keeping.quick_def: If someone keeps or is kept in a particular state, they remain in it.

slow.quick_def: Something that is slow moves, happens, or is done without much speed.

logs.quick_def: A log is a piece of a thick branch or of the trunk of a tree that has been cut so that it can be used for fuel or for making things.

alight.quick_def: If something is alight, it is burning.

carrying.quick_def: If you carry something, you take it with you, holding it so that it does not touch the ground.

charcoal.quick_def: Charcoal is a black substance obtained by burning wood without much air. It can be burned as a fuel, and small sticks of it are used for drawing with.

pots.quick_def: A pot is a deep round container used for cooking stews, soups, and other food.

how.quick_def: You use how to ask about the way in which something happens or is done.

and.quick_def: You use and to link two or more words, groups, or clauses.

where.quick_def: You use where to ask questions about the place something or someone is in, or is coming from or going to.

learnt.quick_def: If you learn something, you obtain knowledge or a skill through studying or training.

produce.quick_def: To produce something means to cause it to happen.

at.quick_def: You use at to indicate the place or event where something happens or is situated.

will.quick_def: You use will to indicate that you hope, think, or have evidence that something is going to happen or be the case in the future.

is.quick_def: You use be with a present participle to form the continuous tenses of verbs.

unknown.quick_def: If something is unknown to you, you have no knowledge of it.

it.quick_def: You use it to refer to an object, animal, or other thing that has already been mentioned.

secondary.quick_def: If you describe something as secondary, you mean that it is less important than something else.

invention.quick_def: An invention is a machine, device, or system that has been invented by someone.

accidentally.quick_def: An accidental event happens by chance or as the result of an accident, and is not deliberately intended.

made.quick_def: Made is the past tense and past participle of make1.

during.quick_def: If something happens during a period of time or an event, it happens continuously, or happens several times between the beginning and end of that period or event.

tool-making.quick_def: Tool-making is the activity of making tools.

operations.quick_def: An operation is a highly organized activity that involves many people doing different things.

with.quick_def: If one person is with another, they are together in one place.

wood.quick_def: Wood is the material which forms the trunks and branches of trees.

stone.quick_def: Stone is a hard solid substance found in the ground and often used for building houses.

studies.quick_def: If you study, you spend time learning about a particular subject or subjects.

primitive.quick_def: Primitive means belonging to a society in which people live in a very simple way, usually without industries or a writing system.

societies.quick_def: Society is people in general, thought of as a large organized group.

suggest.quick_def: If you suggest something, you put forward a plan or idea for someone to think about.

that.quick_def: You use that to refer back to an idea or situation expressed in a previous sentence or sentences.

method.quick_def: A method is a particular way of doing something.

making.quick_def: You can use make with a wide range of nouns to indicate that someone performs an action or says something. For example, if you make a suggestion, you suggest something.

through.quick_def: To move through something such as a hole, opening, or pipe means to move directly from one side or end of it to the other.

friction.quick_def: If there is friction between people, there is disagreement and argument between them.

european.quick_def: European means belonging or relating to, or coming from Europe.

peasants.quick_def: A peasant is a poor person of low social status who works on the land; used of people who live in countries where farming is still a common way of life.

would.quick_def: You use would when you are saying what someone believed, hoped, or expected to happen or be the case.

insert.quick_def: If you insert an object into something, you put the object inside it.

wooden.quick_def: Wooden objects are made of wood.

drill.quick_def: A drill is a tool or machine that you use for making holes.

round.quick_def: To be positioned round a place or object means to surround it or be on all sides of it. To move round a place means to go along its edge, back to the point where you started.

hole.quick_def: A hole is a hollow space in something solid, with an opening on one side.

rotate.quick_def: When something rotates or when you rotate it, it turns with a circular movement.

briskly.quick_def: A brisk activity or action is done quickly and in an energetic way.

between.quick_def: If something is between two things or is in between them, it has one of the things on one side of it and the other thing on the other side.

their.quick_def: You use their to indicate that something belongs or relates to the group of people, animals, or things that you are talking about.

palms.quick_def: A palm or a palm tree is a tree that grows in hot countries. It has long leaves growing at the top, and no branches.

this.quick_def: You use this to refer back to a particular person or thing that has been mentioned or implied.

process.quick_def: A process is a series of actions which are carried out in order to achieve a particular result.

could.quick_def: You use could to indicate that someone had the ability to do something. You use could not or couldn't to say that someone was unable to do something.

be.quick_def: You use be with a present participle to form the continuous tenses of verbs.

speeded.quick_def: The speed of something is the rate at which it moves or travels.

up.quick_def: If a person or thing goes up something such as a slope, ladder, or chimney, they move away from the ground or to a higher position.

wrapping.quick_def: When you wrap something, you fold paper or cloth tightly round it to cover it completely, for example in order to protect it or so that you can give it to someone as a present.

around.quick_def: To be positioned around a place or object means to surround it or be on all sides of it. To move around a place means to go along its edge, back to your starting point.

pulling.quick_def: When you pull something, you hold it firmly and use force in order to move it towards you or away from its previous position.

on.quick_def: If someone or something is on a surface or object, the surface or object is immediately below them and is supporting their weight.

each.quick_def: If you refer to each thing or each person in a group, you are referring to every member of the group and considering them as individuals.

end.quick_def: The end of something such as a period of time, an event, a book, or a film is the last part of it or the final point in it.

ancient.quick_def: Ancient means belonging to the distant past, especially to the period in history before the end of the Roman Empire.

used.quick_def: If you use something, you do something with it in order to do a job or to achieve a particular result or effect.

lenses.quick_def: A lens is a thin curved piece of glass or plastic used in things such as cameras, telescopes, and pairs of glasses. You look through a lens in order to make things look larger, smaller, or clearer.

concave.quick_def: A surface that is concave curves inwards in the middle.

mirrors.quick_def: A mirror is a flat piece of glass which reflects light, so that when you look at it you can see yourself reflected in it.

concentrate.quick_def: If you concentrate on something, or concentrate your mind on it, you give all your attention to it.

sun.quick_def: The sun is the ball of fire in the sky that the Earth goes round, and that gives us heat and light.

s.quick_def: S is the nineteenth letter of the English alphabet.

rays.quick_def: Rays of light are narrow beams of light.

glasses.quick_def: Glass is a hard transparent substance that is used to make things such as windows and bottles.

were.quick_def: You use be with a present participle to form the continuous tenses of verbs.

also.quick_def: You can use also to give more information about a person or thing, or to add another relevant fact.

mexican.quick_def: Mexican means belonging or relating to Mexico, or to its people or culture.

aztecs.quick_def: The Aztecs were a group of people who lived in Mexico a long time ago.

chinese.quick_def: Chinese means relating to or belonging to China, or its people, languages, or culture.

percussion.quick_def: Percussion instruments are musical instruments that you hit, such as drums.

methods.quick_def: A method is a particular way of doing something.

fire-lighting.quick_def: Fire-lighting is the act of making a fire.

date.quick_def: A date is a specific time that can be named, for example a particular day or a particular year.

back.quick_def: If you move back, you move in the opposite direction to the one in which you are facing or in which you were moving before.

paleolithic.quick_def: from or connected with the early part of the Stone Age

times.quick_def: Time is what we measure in minutes, hours, days, and years.

when.quick_def: You use when to ask questions about the time at which things happen.

some.quick_def: You use some to refer to a quantity of something or to a number of people or things, when you are not stating the quantity or number precisely.

age.quick_def: Your age is the number of years that you have lived.

tool-makers.quick_def: Tool-makers are people who make tools.

discovered.quick_def: If you discover something that you did not know about before, you become aware of it or learn of it.

chipping.quick_def: Chips are long, thin pieces of potato fried in oil or fat and eaten hot, usually with a meal.  [British]

flints.quick_def: Flint is a very hard greyish-black stone that was used in former times for making tools.

produced.quick_def: To produce something means to cause it to happen.

sparks.quick_def: A spark is a tiny bright piece of burning material that flies up from something that is burning.

technique.quick_def: A technique is a particular method of doing an activity, usually a method that involves practical skills.

became.quick_def: Became is the past tense of become.

more.quick_def: You use more to indicate that there is a greater amount of something than before or than average, or than something else. You can use 'a little', 'a lot', 'a bit', ' far', and 'much' in front of more.

efficient.quick_def: If something or someone is efficient, they are able to do tasks successfully, without wasting time or energy.

after.quick_def: If something happens after a particular date or event, it happens during the period of time that follows that date or event.

discovery.quick_def: If someone makes a discovery, they become aware of something that they did not know about before.

iron.quick_def: Iron is an element which usually takes the form of a hard, dark-grey metal. It is used to make steel, and also forms part of many tools, buildings, and vehicles. Very small amounts of iron occur in your blood and in food.

about.quick_def: You use about to introduce who or what something relates to or concerns.

years.quick_def: A year is a period of twelve months or 365 or 366 days, beginning on the first of January and ending on the thirty-first of December.

ago.quick_def: You use ago when you are referring to past time. For example, if something happened one year ago, it is one year since it happened. If it happened a long time ago, it is a long time since it happened.

arctic.quick_def: The Arctic is the area of the world around the North Pole. It is extremely cold and there is very little light in winter and very little darkness in summer.

north.quick_def: The north is the direction which is on your left when you are looking towards the direction where the sun rises.

america.quick_def: one of several names for United States (of America) (1)

eskimos.quick_def: Eskimos are people who live in the Arctic regions. They have their own culture and way of life.

slow-burning.quick_def: If something is slow-burning, it burns for a long time without going out quickly.

spark.quick_def: A spark is a tiny bright piece of burning material that flies up from something that is burning.

striking.quick_def: Something that is striking is very noticeable or unusual.

quartz.quick_def: Quartz is a mineral in the form of a hard, shiny crystal. It is used in making electronic equipment and very accurate watches and clocks.

against.quick_def: If one thing is leaning or pressing against another, it is touching it.

pyrites.quick_def: a shiny yellow mineral that is made up of sulphur and a metal such as iron

compound.quick_def: A compound is an enclosed area of land that is used for a particular purpose.

contains.quick_def: If something such as a box, bag, room, or place contains things, those things are inside it.

sulphur.quick_def: Sulphur is a yellow chemical which has a strong smell.

lit.quick_def: Light is the brightness that lets you see things. Light comes from sources such as the sun, moon, lamps, and fire.

fires.quick_def: Fire is the hot, bright flames produced by things that are burning.

porcelain.quick_def: Porcelain is a hard, shiny substance made by heating clay. It is used to make delicate cups, plates, and ornaments.

bamboo.quick_def: Bamboo is a tall tropical plant with hard, hollow stems. The young shoots of the plant can be eaten and the stems are used to make furniture.

europe.quick_def: the continent next to Asia in the east, the Atlantic Ocean in the west, and the Mediterranean Sea in the south

combination.quick_def: A combination of things is a mixture of them.

steel.quick_def: Steel is a very strong metal which is made mainly from iron. Steel is used for making many things, for example bridges, buildings, vehicles, and cutlery.

flint.quick_def: Flint is a very hard greyish-black stone that was used in former times for making tools.

tinder.quick_def: Tinder consists of small pieces of something dry, especially wood or grass, that burns easily and can be used for lighting a fire.

remained.quick_def: If someone or something remains in a particular state or condition, they stay in that state or condition and do not change.

main.quick_def: The main thing is the most important one of several similar things in a particular situation.

until.quick_def: If something happens until a particular time, it happens during the period before that time and stops at that time.

mid.quick_def: in the middle of or during something, especially something that causes excitement or fear

century.quick_def: A century is a period of a hundred years that is used when stating a date. For example, the 19th century was the period from 1801 to 1900.

revolutionised.quick_def: When something revolutionizes an activity, it causes great changes in the way that it is done.

phosphorus.quick_def: Phosphorus is a poisonous yellowish-white chemical element. It glows slightly, and burns when air touches it.

isolated.quick_def: To isolate a person or organization means to cause them to lose their friends or supporters.

german.quick_def: German means belonging or relating to Germany, or to its people, language, or culture.

alchemist.quick_def: An alchemist was a scientist in the Middle Ages who tried to discover how to change ordinary metals into gold.

trying.quick_def: If you try to do something, you want to do it, and you take action which you hope will help you to do it.

transmute.quick_def: If something transmutes or is transmuted into a different form, it is changed into that form.  [formal]

silver.quick_def: Silver is a valuable pale-grey metal that is used for making jewellery and ornaments.

into.quick_def: If you put one thing into another, you put the first thing inside the second.

gold.quick_def: Gold is a valuable, yellow-coloured metal that is used for making jewellery and ornaments, and as an international currency.

impressed.quick_def: If something impresses you, you feel great admiration for it.

element.quick_def: The different elements of something are the different parts it contains.

combustibility.quick_def: Combustibility is the ability of something to catch fire and burn.

several.quick_def: Several is used to refer to an imprecise number of people or things that is not large but is greater than two.

chemists.quick_def: A chemist or a chemist's is a shop where drugs and medicines are sold or given out, and where you can buy cosmetics and some household goods.  [British]

manufacture.quick_def: To manufacture something means to make it in a factory, usually in large quantities.  [business]

devices.quick_def: A device is an object that has been invented for a particular purpose, for example for recording or measuring something.

but.quick_def: You use but to introduce something which contrasts with what you have just said, or to introduce something which adds to what you have just said.

results.quick_def: A result is something that happens or exists because of something else that has happened.

dangerously.quick_def: If something is dangerous, it is able or likely to hurt or harm you.

inflammable.quick_def: An inflammable material or chemical catches fire and burns easily.

costing.quick_def: The cost of something is the amount of money that is needed in order to buy, do, or make it.

equivalent.quick_def: If one amount or value is the equivalent of another, they are the same.

hundred.quick_def: A hundred or one hundred is the number 100.

pounds.quick_def: The pound is the unit of money which is used in the UK. It is represented by the symbol £. One UK pound is divided into a hundred pence. Some other countries, for example Egypt, also have a unit of money called a pound.

per.quick_def: You use per to express rates and ratios. For example, if something costs £50 per year, you must pay £50 each year for it. If a vehicle is travelling at 40 miles per hour, it travels 40 miles each hour.

ounce.quick_def: An ounce is a unit of weight used in Britain and the USA. There are sixteen ounces in a pound and one ounce is equal to 28.35 grams.

first.quick_def: The first thing, person, event, or period of time is the one that happens or comes before all the others of the same kind.

matches.quick_def: A match is an organized game of football, tennis, cricket, or some other sport.  [mainly British]

expensive.quick_def: If something is expensive, it costs a lot of money.

quest.quick_def: A quest is a long and difficult search for something.  [literary]

practical.quick_def: The practical aspects of something involve real situations and events, rather than just ideas and theories.

match.quick_def: A match is an organized game of football, tennis, cricket, or some other sport.  [mainly British]

really.quick_def: You can use really to emphasize a statement.  [spoken, emphasis]

began.quick_def: Began is the past tense of begin.

group.quick_def: A group of people or things is a number of people or things which are together in one place at one time.

french.quick_def: French means belonging or relating to France, or to its people, language, or culture.

came.quick_def: Came is the past tense of come.

phosphoric.quick_def: If something is phosphoric, it is related to phosphorus or contains phosphorus.

candle.quick_def: A candle is a stick of hard wax with a piece of string called a wick through the middle. You light the wick in order to give a steady flame that provides light.

ethereal.quick_def: Someone or something that is ethereal has a delicate beauty.  [formal]

sealed.quick_def: When you seal an envelope, you close it by folding part of it over and sticking it down, so that it cannot be opened without being torn.

glass.quick_def: Glass is a hard transparent substance that is used to make things such as windows and bottles.

tube.quick_def: A tube is a long hollow object that is usually round, like a pipe.

containing.quick_def: If something such as a box, bag, room, or place contains things, those things are inside it.

twist.quick_def: If you twist something, you turn it to make a spiral shape, for example by turning the two ends of it in opposite directions.

paper.quick_def: Paper is a material that you write on or wrap things with. The pages of this book are made of paper.

tipped.quick_def: The tip of something long and narrow is the end of it.

broken.quick_def: When an object breaks or when you break it, it suddenly separates into two or more pieces, often because it has been hit or dropped.

air.quick_def: Air is the mixture of gases which forms the Earth's atmosphere and which we breathe.

rushed.quick_def: If you rush somewhere, you go there quickly.

causing.quick_def: The cause of an event, usually a bad event, is the thing that makes it happen.

self-combust.quick_def: When something self-combusts, it starts to burn by itself without being lit by something else.

an.quick_def: You use a or an when you are referring to someone or something for the first time or when people may not know which particular person or thing you are talking about.

even.quick_def: You use even to suggest that what comes just after or just before it in the sentence is rather surprising.

hazardous.quick_def: Something that is hazardous is dangerous, especially to people's health or safety.

device.quick_def: A device is an object that has been invented for a particular purpose, for example for recording or measuring something.

popular.quick_def: Something that is popular is enjoyed or liked by a lot of people.

instantaneous.quick_def: Something that is instantaneous happens immediately and very quickly.

light.quick_def: Light is the brightness that lets you see things. Light comes from sources such as the sun, moon, lamps, and fire.

box.quick_def: A box is a square or rectangular container with hard or stiff sides. Boxes often have lids.

bottle.quick_def: A bottle is a glass or plastic container in which drinks and other liquids are kept. Bottles are usually round with straight sides and a narrow top.

filled.quick_def: If you fill a container or area, or if it fills, an amount of something enters it that is enough to make it full.

sulphuric.quick_def: Sulphuric is used to describe something that is related to sulphur or contains sulphur. For example, sulphuric acid is a strong acid with sulphur in it.

acid.quick_def: An acid is a chemical substance, usually a liquid, which contains hydrogen and can react with other substances to form salts. Some acids burn or dissolve other substances that they come into contact with.

which.quick_def: You use which in questions when there are two or more possible answers or alternatives.

splints.quick_def: A splint is a long piece of wood or metal that is fastened to a broken arm, leg, or back to keep it still.

treated.quick_def: If you treat someone or something in a particular way, you behave towards them or deal with them in that way.

chemicals.quick_def: Chemical means involving or resulting from a reaction between two or more substances, or relating to the substances that something consists of.

dipped.quick_def: If you dip something in a liquid, you put it into the liquid for a short time, so that only part of it is covered, and take it out again.

resembling.quick_def: If one thing or person resembles another, they are similar to each other.

those.quick_def: You use those to refer to people or things which have already been mentioned.

today.quick_def: You use today to refer to the day on which you are speaking or writing.

john.quick_def: A john is a toilet or bathroom.  [US, informal]

walker.quick_def: A walker is a person who walks, especially in the countryside for pleasure or in order to keep healthy.

english.quick_def: English means belonging or relating to England, or to its people, language, or culture. It is also often used to mean belonging or relating to Great Britain, although many people object to this.

pharmacist.quick_def: A pharmacist is a person who is qualified to prepare and sell medicines.

who.quick_def: You use who in questions when you ask about the name or identity of a person or group of people.

borrowed.quick_def: If you borrow something that belongs to someone else, you take it or use it for a period of time, usually with their permission.

formula.quick_def: A formula is a plan that is invented in order to deal with a particular problem.

from.quick_def: If something comes from a particular person or thing, or if you get something from them, they give it to you or they are the source of it.

military.quick_def: Military means relating to the armed forces of a country.

rocket-maker.quick_def: A rocket-maker is a person who makes rockets.

called.quick_def: If you call someone or something by a particular name or title, you give them that name or title.

congreve.quick_def: Congreve is a name, usually for a person.

shilling.quick_def: A shilling was a unit of money that was used in Britain until 1971 which was the equivalent of 5 p. There were twenty shillings in a pound.

congreves.quick_def: Congreves are small splints that are coated with sulphur and have a tip of potassium chlorate, often used as a kind of early match.

coated.quick_def: A coat is a piece of clothing with long sleeves which you wear over your other clothes when you go outside.

potassium.quick_def: Potassium is a soft silvery-white chemical element, which occurs mainly in compounds. These compounds are used in making such things as glass, soap, and fertilizers.

chlorate.quick_def: A chlorate is a type of chemical compound. It is often used in making things like matches.

them.quick_def: You use them to refer to a group of people, animals, or things.

user.quick_def: A user is a person or thing that uses something such as a place, facility, product, or machine.

drew.quick_def: When you draw, or when you draw something, you use a pencil or pen to produce a picture, pattern, or diagram.

quickly.quick_def: Someone or something that is quick moves or does things with great speed.

folded.quick_def: If you fold something such as a piece of paper or cloth, you bend it so that one part covers another part, often pressing the edge so that it stays in place.

never.quick_def: Never means at no time in the past or at no time in the future.

patented.quick_def: A patent is an official right to be the only person or company allowed to make or sell a new product for a certain period of time.

his.quick_def: You use his to indicate that something belongs or relates to a man, boy, or male animal.

later.quick_def: Late means near the end of a day, week, year, or other period of time.

copied.quick_def: If you make a copy of something, you produce something that looks like the original thing.

jones.quick_def: Jones is a common family name. People use it to call a person in a family.

marketed.quick_def: A market is a place where goods are bought and sold, usually outdoors.

product.quick_def: A product is something that is produced and sold in large quantities, often as a result of a manufacturing process.

as.quick_def: If something happens as something else happens, it happens at the same time.

lucifers.quick_def: Lucifers are a kind of early matches.

same.quick_def: If two or more things, actions, or qualities are the same, or if one is the same as another, they are very like each other in some way.

time.quick_def: Time is what we measure in minutes, hours, days, and years.

chemistry.quick_def: Chemistry is the scientific study of the structure of substances and of the way that they react with other substances.

student.quick_def: A student is a person who is studying at a university or college.

sauria.quick_def: Sauria is a group of reptiles. It includes lizards and some other similar animals.

strike-anywhere.quick_def: If a match is strike-anywhere, it can be lit by rubbing it on any rough surface.

substituting.quick_def: If you substitute one thing for another, or if one thing substitutes for another, it takes the place or performs the function of the other thing.

white.quick_def: Something that is white is the colour of snow or milk.

however.quick_def: You use however when you are adding a comment which is surprising or which contrasts with what has just been said.

since.quick_def: You use since when you are mentioning a time or event in the past and indicating that a situation has continued from then until now.

deadly.quick_def: If something is deadly, it is likely or able to cause someone's death, or has already caused someone's death.

poison.quick_def: Poison is a substance that harms or kills people or animals if they swallow it or absorb it.

match-makers.quick_def: Match-makers are people who make matches. A match is a small stick with a special tip that can catch fire easily, and match-makers are the ones who make these things.

exposed.quick_def: If a place is exposed, it has no natural protection against bad weather or enemies, for example because it has no trees or is on very high ground.

its.quick_def: You use its to indicate that something belongs or relates to a thing, place, or animal that has just been mentioned or whose identity is known. You can use its to indicate that something belongs or relates to a child or baby.

fumes.quick_def: Fumes are the unpleasant and often unhealthy smoke and gases that are produced by fires or by things such as chemicals, fuel, or cooking.

succumbed.quick_def: If you succumb to temptation or pressure, you do something that you want to do, or that other people want you to do, although you feel it might be wrong.  [formal]

necrosis.quick_def: Necrosis is the death of part of someone's body, for example because it is not getting enough blood.  [medicine]

disease.quick_def: A disease is an illness which affects people, animals, or plants, for example one which is caused by bacteria or infection.

eats.quick_def: When you eat something, you put it into your mouth, chew it, and swallow it.

away.quick_def: If someone or something moves or is moved away from a place, they move or are moved so that they are no longer there. If you are away from a place, you are not in the place where people expect you to be.

jaw-bones.quick_def: Jaw-bones are the bones in your face that hold your teeth and help you chew food.

t.quick_def: T is the twentieth letter of the English alphabet.

substance.quick_def: A substance is a solid, powder, liquid, or gas with particular properties.

eventually.quick_def: Eventually means in the end, especially after a lot of delays, problems, or arguments.

banned.quick_def: To ban something means to state officially that it must not be done, shown, or used.

swedish.quick_def: Swedish means belonging or relating to Sweden, or to its people, language, or culture.

chemist.quick_def: A chemist or a chemist's is a shop where drugs and medicines are sold or given out, and where you can buy cosmetics and some household goods.  [British]

pasch.quick_def: Pasch is a name of a person.

had.quick_def: Had is the past tense and past participle of have1.

non-toxic.quick_def: If something is non-toxic, it is not poisonous and will not harm you if you touch it, eat it, etc.

red.quick_def: Something that is red is the colour of blood or fire.

amorphous.quick_def: Something that is amorphous has no clear shape or structure.  [formal]

development.quick_def: Development is the gradual growth or formation of something.

exploited.quick_def: If you say that someone is exploiting you, you think that they are treating you unfairly by using your work or ideas and giving you very little in return.

commercially.quick_def: Commercial means involving or relating to the buying and selling of goods.

compatriot.quick_def: Your compatriots are people from your own country.

j.quick_def: J is the tenth letter of the English alphabet.

e.quick_def: E is the fifth letter of the English alphabet.

lundstrom.quick_def: Lundstrom is a name, usually used to call a person.

safety.quick_def: Safety is the state of being safe from harm or danger.

safe.quick_def: Something that is safe does not cause physical harm or danger.

because.quick_def: You use because when stating the reason for something.

painted.quick_def: Paint is a coloured liquid that you put onto a surface with a brush in order to protect the surface or to make it look nice, or that you use to produce a picture.

surface.quick_def: The surface of something is the flat top part of it or the outside of it.

instead.quick_def: If you do one thing  instead of another, you do the first thing and not the second thing, as the result of a choice or a change of behaviour.

tip.quick_def: The tip of something long and narrow is the end of it.

contained.quick_def: If something such as a box, bag, room, or place contains things, those things are inside it.

relatively.quick_def: Relatively means to a certain degree, especially when compared with other things of the same kind.

high.quick_def: Something that is high extends a long way from the bottom to the top when it is upright. You do not use high to describe people, animals, or plants.

ignition.quick_def: In a car engine, the ignition is the part where the fuel is ignited.

temperature.quick_def: The temperature of something is a measure of how hot or cold it is.

degrees.quick_def: You use degree to indicate the extent to which something happens or is the case, or the amount which something is felt.

centigrade.quick_def: Centigrade is a scale for measuring temperature, in which water freezes at 0 degrees and boils at 100 degrees. It is represented by the symbol °C.

lagged.quick_def: If one thing or person lags behind another thing or person, their progress is slower than that of the other.

behind.quick_def: If something is behind a thing or person, it is on the other side of them from you, or nearer their back rather than their front.

technology.quick_def: Technology refers to methods, systems, and devices which are the result of scientific knowledge being used for practical purposes.

standards.quick_def: A standard is a level of quality or achievement, especially a level that is thought to be acceptable.

diamond.quick_def: A diamond is a hard, bright, precious stone which is clear and colourless. Diamonds are used in jewellery and for cutting very hard substances.

company.quick_def: A company is a business organization that makes money by selling goods or services.

bought.quick_def: Bought is the past tense and past participle of buy.

patent.quick_def: A patent is an official right to be the only person or company allowed to make or sell a new product for a certain period of time.

did.quick_def: Did is the past tense of do1.

not.quick_def: You use not with verbs to form negative statements.

work.quick_def: People who work have a job, usually one which they are paid to do.

properly.quick_def: If something is done properly, it is done in a correct and satisfactory way.

different.quick_def: If two people or things are different, they are not like each other in one or more ways. In British English, people sometimes say that one thing is different to another. Some people consider this use to be incorrect. People sometimes say that one thing is different than another. This use is often considered incorrect in British English, but it is acceptable in American English.

climatic.quick_def: Climatic conditions, changes, and effects relate to the general weather conditions of a place.

conditions.quick_def: If you talk about the condition of a person or thing, you are talking about the state that they are in, especially how good or bad their physical state is.

prevailing.quick_def: If a proposal, principle, or opinion prevails, it gains influence or is accepted, often after a struggle or argument.

another.quick_def: Another thing or person means an additional thing or person of the same type as one that already exists.

before.quick_def: If something happens before a particular date, time, or event, it happens earlier than that date, time, or event.

scientists.quick_def: A scientist is someone who has studied science and whose job is to teach or do research in science.

finally.quick_def: You use finally to suggest that something happens after a long period of time, usually later than you wanted or expected it to happen.

adapted.quick_def: If you adapt to a new situation or adapt yourself to it, you change your ideas or behaviour in order to deal with it successfully.

us.quick_def: A speaker or writer uses us to refer both to himself or herself and to one or more other people. You can use us before a noun to make it clear which group of people you are referring to.

can.quick_def: You use can when you are mentioning a quality or fact about something which people may make use of if they want to.

claim.quick_def: If you say that someone claims that something is true, you mean they say that it is true but you are not sure whether or not they are telling the truth.

firsts.quick_def: The first thing, person, event, or period of time is the one that happens or comes before all the others of the same kind.

marketing.quick_def: A market is a place where goods are bought and sold, usually outdoors.

pioneered.quick_def: Someone who is referred to as a pioneer in a particular area of activity is one of the first people to be involved in it and develop it.

book.quick_def: A book is a number of pieces of paper, usually with words printed on them, which are fastened together and fixed inside a cover of stronger paper or cardboard. Books contain information, stories, or poetry, for example.

innovation.quick_def: An innovation is a new thing or a new method of doing something.

catch.quick_def: If you catch a person or animal, you capture them after chasing them, or by using a trap, net, or other device.

brewery.quick_def: A brewery is a place where beer is made.

novel.quick_def: A novel is a long written story about imaginary people and events.

idea.quick_def: An idea is a plan, suggestion, or possible course of action.

advertising.quick_def: If you advertise something such as a product, an event, or a job, you tell people about it online, in newspapers, on television, or on posters in order to encourage them to buy the product, go to the event, or apply for the job.

books.quick_def: A book is a number of pieces of paper, usually with words printed on them, which are fastened together and fixed inside a cover of stronger paper or cardboard. Books contain information, stories, or poetry, for example.

are.quick_def: Are is the plural and the second person singular of the present tense of the verb be1. Are is often shortened to -'re after pronouns in spoken English.

most.quick_def: You use most to refer to the majority of a group of things or people or the largest part of something.

widely.quick_def: Something that is wide measures a large distance from one side or edge to the other.

type.quick_def: A type of something is a group of those things that have particular features in common.

percent.quick_def: You use percent to talk about amounts. For example, if an amount is 10 percent (10%) of a larger amount, it is equal to 10 hundredths of the larger amount.

handed.quick_def: Your hands are the parts of your body at the end of your arms. Each hand has four fingers and a thumb.

out.quick_def: When something is in a particular place and you take it out, you remove it from that place.

free.quick_def: If something is free, you can have it or use it without paying for it.

hotels.quick_def: A hotel is a building where people stay, for example on holiday, paying for their rooms and meals.

restaurants.quick_def: A restaurant is a place where you can eat a meal and pay for it. In restaurants your food is usually served to you at your table by a waiter or waitress.

others.quick_def: You use other to refer to an additional thing or person of the same type as one that has been mentioned or is known about.

other.quick_def: You use other to refer to an additional thing or person of the same type as one that has been mentioned or is known about.

american.quick_def: American means belonging or relating to the United States of America, or to its people or culture.

innovations.quick_def: An innovation is a new thing or a new method of doing something.

include.quick_def: If one thing includes another thing, it has the other thing as one of its parts.

anti-after-glow.quick_def: Something that can stop the after-glow. After-glow means the light that stays after something stops burning. So anti-after-glow is used to prevent this light from happening.

solution.quick_def: A solution to a problem or difficult situation is a way of dealing with it so that the difficulty is removed.

prevent.quick_def: To prevent something means to ensure that it does not happen.

smouldering.quick_def: If something smoulders, it burns slowly, producing smoke but not flames.

has.quick_def: Has is the third person singular of the present tense of have.

been.quick_def: You use be with a present participle to form the continuous tenses of verbs.

blown.quick_def: When a wind or breeze blows, the air moves.

waterproof.quick_def: Something which is waterproof does not let water pass through it.

lights.quick_def: Light is the brightness that lets you see things. Light comes from sources such as the sun, moon, lamps, and fire.

hours.quick_def: An hour is a period of sixty minutes.

water.quick_def: Water is a clear thin liquid that has no colour or taste when it is pure. It falls from clouds as rain and enters rivers and seas. All animals and people need water in order to live.

london.quick_def: the capital city of England and the UK

zoo.quick_def: A zoo is a park where live animals are kept so that people can look at them.

recent.quick_def: A recent event or period of time happened only a short while ago.

advertisements.quick_def: An advertisement is an announcement online, or in a newspaper, on television, or on a poster about something such as a product, event, or job.  [written]

caused.quick_def: The cause of an event, usually a bad event, is the thing that makes it happen.

me.quick_def: A speaker or writer uses me to refer to himself or herself. Me is a first person singular pronoun. Me is used as the object of a verb or a preposition.

irritation.quick_def: Irritation is a feeling of annoyance, especially when something is happening that you cannot easily stop or control.

so.quick_def: You use so to refer back to something that has just been mentioned.

patently.quick_def: A patent is an official right to be the only person or company allowed to make or sell a new product for a certain period of time.

distort.quick_def: If you distort a statement, fact, or idea, you report or represent it in an untrue way.

reality.quick_def: You use reality to refer to real things or the real nature of things rather than imagined, invented, or theoretical ideas.

headlined.quick_def: A headline is the title of a newspaper story, printed in large letters at the top of the story, especially on the front page.

without.quick_def: You use without to indicate that someone or something does not have or use the thing mentioned.

zoos.quick_def: A zoo is a park where live animals are kept so that people can look at them.

you.quick_def: A speaker or writer uses you to refer to the person or people that they are talking or writing to. It is possible to use you before a noun to make it clear which group of people you are talking to.

might.quick_def: You use might to indicate that something will possibly happen or be true in the future, but you cannot be certain.  [vagueness]

well.quick_def: You say well to indicate that you are about to say something.

tell.quick_def: If you tell someone something, you give them information.

these.quick_def: You use these at the beginning of noun groups to refer to someone or something that you have already mentioned or identified.

animals.quick_def: An animal is a living creature such as a dog, lion, or rabbit, rather than a bird, fish, insect, or human being.

get.quick_def: You use get with adjectives to mean 'become'. For example, if someone gets cold, they become cold, and if they get angry, they become angry.

stuffed.quick_def: You can use stuff to refer to things such as a substance, a collection of things, events, or ideas, or the contents of something in a general way without mentioning the thing itself by name.  [informal]

bordered.quick_def: The border between two countries or regions is the dividing line between them. Sometimes the border also refers to the land close to this line.

illustrations.quick_def: An illustration is an example or a story which is used to make a point clear.

endangered.quick_def: To endanger something or someone means to put them in a situation where they might be harmed or destroyed completely.

species.quick_def: A species is a class of plants or animals whose members have the same main characteristics and are able to breed with each other.

went.quick_def: When you go somewhere, you move or travel there.

extol.quick_def: If you extol something or someone, you praise them enthusiastically.

myth.quick_def: A myth is a well-known story which was made up in the past to explain natural events or to justify religious beliefs or social customs.

like.quick_def: If you say that one person or thing is like another, you mean that they share some of the same qualities or features.

almost.quick_def: You use almost to indicate that something is not completely the case but is nearly the case.

certainly.quick_def: You use certainly to emphasize what you are saying when you are making a statement.  [emphasis]

disappear.quick_def: If you say that someone or something disappears, you mean that you can no longer see them, usually because you or they have changed position.

forever.quick_def: If you say that something will happen or continue forever, you mean that it will always happen or continue.

world.quick_def: The world is the planet that we live on.

rather.quick_def: You use rather when you are correcting something that you have just said, especially when you are describing a particular situation after saying what it is not.

mediocre.quick_def: If you describe something as mediocre, you mean that it is of average quality but you think it should be better.  [disapproval]

record.quick_def: If you keep a record of something, you keep a written account or photographs of it so that it can be referred to later.

conservation.quick_def: Conservation is saving and protecting the environment.

forgiven.quick_def: If you forgive someone who has done something bad or wrong, you stop being angry with them and no longer want to punish them.

being.quick_def: You use be with a present participle to form the continuous tenses of verbs.

slightly.quick_def: Something that is slight is very small in degree or quantity.

sceptical.quick_def: If you are sceptical about something, you have doubts about it.

such.quick_def: You use such to refer back to the thing or person that you have just mentioned, or a thing or person like the one that you have just mentioned. You use such as and such...as to introduce a reference to the person or thing that has just been mentioned.

advertisement.quick_def: An advertisement is an announcement online, or in a newspaper, on television, or on a poster about something such as a product, event, or job.  [written]

originally.quick_def: When you say what happened or was the case originally, you are saying what happened or was the case when something began or came into existence, often to contrast it with what happened later.

created.quick_def: To create something means to cause it to happen or exist.

places.quick_def: A place is any point, building, area, town, or country.

entertainment.quick_def: Entertainment consists of performances of plays and films, and activities such as reading and watching television, that give people pleasure.

suggested.quick_def: If you suggest something, you put forward a plan or idea for someone to think about.

involvement.quick_def: Your involvement in something is the fact that you are taking part in it.

seriously.quick_def: Serious problems or situations are very bad and cause people to be worried or afraid.

arise.quick_def: If a situation or problem arises, it begins to exist or people start to become aware of it.

zoological.quick_def: connected with the science of zoology

society.quick_def: Society is people in general, thought of as a large organized group.

held.quick_def: Held is the past tense and past participle of hold1.

formal.quick_def: Formal speech or behaviour is very correct and serious rather than relaxed and friendly, and is used especially in official situations.

international.quick_def: International means between or involving different countries.

meeting.quick_def: If you meet someone, you happen to be in the same place as them and start talking to them. You may know the other person, but be surprised to see them, or you may not know them at all.

subject.quick_def: The subject of something such as a conversation, letter, or book is the thing that is being discussed or written about.

series.quick_def: A series of things or events is a number of them that come one after the other.

conferences.quick_def: A conference is a meeting, often lasting a few days, which is organized on a particular subject or to bring together people who have a common interest.

took.quick_def: You can use take followed by a noun to talk about an action or event, when it would also be possible to use the verb that is related to that noun. For example, you can say 'she took a shower' instead of 'she showered'.

place.quick_def: A place is any point, building, area, town, or country.

entitled.quick_def: If you are entitled to something, you have the right to have it or do it.

breeding.quick_def: A breed of a pet animal or farm animal is a particular type of it. For example, terriers are a breed of dog.

point.quick_def: You use point to refer to something that someone has said or written.

onwards.quick_def: Onward means moving forward or continuing a journey.

community.quick_def: The community is all the people who live in a particular area or place.

buzzword.quick_def: A buzzword is a word or expression that has become fashionable in a particular field and is being used a lot by the media.

commitment.quick_def: Commitment is a strong belief in an idea or system.

now.quick_def: You use now to refer to the present time, often in contrast to a time in the past or the future.

clearly.quick_def: Something that is clear is easy to understand, see, or hear.

defined.quick_def: If you define something, you show, describe, or state clearly what it is and what its limits are, or what it is like.

strategy.quick_def: A strategy is a general plan or set of plans intended to achieve something, especially over a long period.

wzcs.quick_def: WZCS is an abbreviation for The World Zoo Conservation Strategy, which is a document about zoo conservation.

september.quick_def: September is the ninth month of the year in the Western calendar.

although.quick_def: You use although to introduce a subordinate clause which contains a statement which contrasts with the statement in the main clause.

important.quick_def: Something that is important is very significant, is highly valued, or is necessary.

welcome.quick_def: If you welcome someone, you greet them in a friendly way when they arrive somewhere.

document.quick_def: A document is one or more official pieces of paper with writing on them.

does.quick_def: Do is used to form the negative of main verbs, by putting 'not' after 'do' and before the main verb in its infinitive form, that is the form without 'to'.

seem.quick_def: You use seem to say that someone or something gives the impression of having a particular quality, or of happening in the way you describe.

based.quick_def: The base of something is its lowest edge or part.

unrealistic.quick_def: If you say that someone is being unrealistic, you mean that they do not recognize the truth about a situation, especially about the difficulties involved in something they want to achieve.

optimism.quick_def: Optimism is the feeling of being hopeful about the future or about the success of something in particular.

nature.quick_def: Nature is all the animals, plants, and other things in the world that are not made by people, and all the events and processes that are not caused by people.

industry.quick_def: Industry is the work and processes involved in collecting raw materials, and making them into products in factories.

estimates.quick_def: If you estimate a quantity or value, you make an approximate judgment or calculation of it.

there.quick_def: There is used as the subject of the verb 'be' to say that something exists or does not exist, or to draw attention to it.

represent.quick_def: If someone such as a lawyer or a politician represents a person or group of people, they act on behalf of that person or group.

core.quick_def: The core of a fruit is the central part of it. It contains seeds or pips.

quality.quick_def: The quality of something is how good or bad it is.

collections.quick_def: A collection of things is a group of similar things that you have deliberately acquired, usually over a period of time.

capable.quick_def: If a person or thing is capable of doing something, they have the ability to do it.

participating.quick_def: If you participate in an activity, you take part in it.

coordinated.quick_def: If you coordinate an activity, you organize the various people and things involved in it.

programmes.quick_def: A programme of actions or events is a series of actions or events that are planned to be done.

failing.quick_def: If you fail to do something that you were trying to do, you are unable to do it or do not succeed in doing it.

i.quick_def: I is the ninth letter of the English alphabet.

believe.quick_def: If you believe that something is true, you think that it is true, but you are not sure.  [formal]

serious.quick_def: Serious problems or situations are very bad and cause people to be worried or afraid.

underestimate.quick_def: If you underestimate something, you do not realize how large or great it is or will be.

total.quick_def: A total is the number that you get when you add several numbers together or when you count how many things there are in a group.

number.quick_def: A number is a word such as 'two', ' nine', or ' twelve', or a symbol such as 1, 3, or 47. You use numbers to say how many things you are referring to or where something comes in a series.

masquerading.quick_def: To masquerade as someone or something means to pretend to be that person or thing, particularly in order to deceive other people.

establishments.quick_def: The establishment of an organization or system is the act of creating it or beginning it.  [formal]

course.quick_def: Course is often used in the expression 'of course', or instead of 'of course' in informal spoken English. See of course.

difficult.quick_def: Something that is difficult is not easy to do, understand, or deal with.

accurate.quick_def: Accurate information, measurements, and statistics are correct to a very detailed level. An accurate instrument is able to give you information of this kind.

data.quick_def: You can refer to information as data, especially when it is in the form of facts or statistics that you can analyse. In American English, data is usually a plural noun. In technical or formal British English, data is sometimes a plural noun, but at other times, it is an uncount noun.

put.quick_def: When you put something in a particular place or position, you move it into that place or position.

issue.quick_def: An issue is an important subject that people are arguing about or discussing.

perspective.quick_def: A particular perspective is a particular way of thinking about something, especially one that is influenced by your beliefs or experiences.

have.quick_def: You use the forms have and has with a past participle to form the present perfect tense of verbs.

found.quick_def: If you find someone or something, you see them or learn where they are.

year.quick_def: A year is a period of twelve months or 365 or 366 days, beginning on the first of January and ending on the thirty-first of December.

working.quick_def: People who work have a job, usually one which they are paid to do.

eastern.quick_def: Eastern means in or from the east of a region, state, or country.

discover.quick_def: If you discover something that you did not know about before, you become aware of it or learn of it.

fresh.quick_def: A fresh thing or amount replaces or is added to a previous thing or amount.

weekly.quick_def: A weekly event or publication happens or appears once a week or every week.

basis.quick_def: If something is done on a particular basis, it is done according to that method, system, or principle.

second.quick_def: A second is one of the sixty parts that a minute is divided into. People often say 'a second' or 'seconds' when they simply mean a very short time.

flaw.quick_def: A flaw in something such as a theory or argument is a mistake in it, which causes it to be less effective or valid.

reasoning.quick_def: The reason for something is a fact or situation which explains why it happens or what causes it to happen.

naive.quick_def: If you describe someone as naive, you think they lack experience and so expect things to be easy or people to be honest or kind.

faith.quick_def: If you have faith in someone or something, you feel confident about their ability or goodness.

assume.quick_def: If you assume that something is true, you imagine that it is true, sometimes wrongly.

calibre.quick_def: The calibre of a person is the quality or standard of their ability or intelligence, especially when this is high.

institutions.quick_def: An institution is a large important organization such as a university, church, or bank.

carefully.quick_def: If you are careful, you give serious attention to what you are doing, in order to avoid harm, damage, or mistakes. If you are careful to do something, you make sure that you do it.

examined.quick_def: If you examine something, you look at it carefully.

appears.quick_def: If you say that something appears to be the way you describe it, you are reporting what you believe or what you have been told, though you cannot be sure it is true.  [vagueness]

criterion.quick_def: A criterion is a factor on which you judge or decide something.

inclusion.quick_def: Inclusion is the act of making a person or thing part of a group or collection.

select.quick_def: If you select something, you choose it from a number of things of the same kind.

list.quick_def: A list of things such as names or addresses is a set of them which all belong to a particular category, written down one below the other.

merely.quick_def: You use merely to emphasize that something is only what you say and not better, more important, or more exciting.  [emphasis]

member.quick_def: A member of a group is one of the people, animals, or things belonging to that group.

federation.quick_def: A federation is a federal country.

association.quick_def: An association is an official group of people who have the same job, aim, or interest.

starting.quick_def: If you start to do something, you do something that you were not doing before and you continue doing it.

premise.quick_def: The premises of a business or an institution are all the buildings and land that it occupies in one place.

members.quick_def: A member of a group is one of the people, animals, or things belonging to that group.

must.quick_def: You use must to indicate that you think it is very important or necessary for something to happen. You use must not or mustn't to indicate that you think it is very important or necessary for something not to happen.

meet.quick_def: If you meet someone, you happen to be in the same place as them and start talking to them. You may know the other person, but be surprised to see them, or you may not know them at all.

certain.quick_def: If you are certain about something, you firmly believe it is true and have no doubt about it. If you are not certain about something, you do not have definite knowledge about it.

again.quick_def: You use again to indicate that something happens a second time, or after it has already happened before.

facts.quick_def: You use the fact that after some verbs or prepositions, especially in expressions such as in view of the fact that,  apart from the fact that, and despite the fact that, to link the verb or preposition with a clause.

don.quick_def: If you don clothing, you put it on.  [written]

support.quick_def: If you support someone or their ideas or aims, you agree with them, and perhaps help them because you want them to succeed.

theory.quick_def: A theory is a formal idea or set of ideas that is intended to explain something.

greatly.quick_def: You use greatly to emphasize the degree or extent of something.  [formal, emphasis]

respected.quick_def: If you respect someone, you have a good opinion of their character or ideas.

parks.quick_def: A park is a public area of land with grass and trees, usually in a town, where people go in order to relax and enjoy themselves.

aquariums.quick_def: An aquarium is a building, often in a zoo, where fish and underwater animals are kept.

aazpa.quick_def: AAZPA is an abbreviation for the American Association of Zoological Parks and Aquariums, which is a group about zoos and aquariums in America.

extremely.quick_def: You use extremely in front of adjectives and adverbs to emphasize that the specified quality is present to a very great degree.  [emphasis]

dubious.quick_def: If you describe something as dubious, you mean that you do not consider it to be completely honest, safe, or reliable.

uk.quick_def: The UK is Great Britain and Northern Ireland. UK is an abbreviation for 'United Kingdom'.

gardens.quick_def: In British English, a garden is a piece of land next to a house, with flowers, vegetables, other plants, and often grass. In American English, the usual word is yard, and a garden refers only to land which is used for growing flowers and vegetables.

great.quick_def: You use great to describe something that is very large. Great is more formal than big.

britain.quick_def: the island containing England, Scotland and Wales

ireland.quick_def: Ireland is a country in Europe. It has its own land, people and culture.

occasionally.quick_def: Occasional means happening sometimes, but not regularly or often.

roundly.quick_def: If you are roundly condemned or criticized, you are condemned or criticized forcefully or by many people. If you are roundly defeated, you are defeated completely.

censured.quick_def: If you censure someone for something that they have done, you tell them that you strongly disapprove of it.  [formal]

national.quick_def: National means relating to the whole of a country or nation rather than to part of it or to other nations.

press.quick_def: If you press something somewhere, you push it firmly against something else.

robin.quick_def: A robin is a small brown bird found in Europe. The male has an orangey-red neck and breast.

hill.quick_def: A hill is an area of land that is higher than the land that surrounds it.

adventure.quick_def: If someone has an adventure, they become involved in an unusual, exciting, and rather dangerous journey or series of events.

park.quick_def: A park is a public area of land with grass and trees, usually in a town, where people go in order to relax and enjoy themselves.

isle.quick_def: An isle is an island; often used as part of an island's name, or in literary English.

many.quick_def: You use many to indicate that you are talking about a large number of people or things.

considered.quick_def: If you consider a person or thing to be something, you have the opinion that this is what they are.

notorious.quick_def: To be notorious means to be well-known for something bad.

collection.quick_def: A collection of things is a group of similar things that you have deliberately acquired, usually over a period of time.

country.quick_def: A country is one of the political units which the world is divided into, covering a particular area of land.

establishment.quick_def: The establishment of an organization or system is the act of creating it or beginning it.  [formal]

protected.quick_def: To protect someone or something means to prevent them from being harmed or damaged.

local.quick_def: Local means existing in or belonging to the area where you live, or to the area that you are talking about.

council.quick_def: A council is a group of people who are elected to govern a local area such as a city or, in Britain, a county.

viewed.quick_def: Your views on something are the beliefs or opinions that you have about it, for example whether you think it is good, bad, right, or wrong.

tourist.quick_def: A tourist is a person who is visiting a place for pleasure and interest, especially when they are on holiday.

amenity.quick_def: Amenities are things such as shopping centres or sports facilities that are provided for people's convenience, enjoyment, or comfort.

closed.quick_def: When you close something such as a door or lid or when it closes, it moves so that a hole, gap, or opening is covered.

down.quick_def: To go down something such as a slope or a pipe means to go towards the ground or to a lower level.

following.quick_def: If you follow someone who is going somewhere, you move along behind them because you want to go to the same place.

damning.quick_def: Damn, damn it, and dammit are used by some people to express anger or impatience.  [informal, rude, feelings]

report.quick_def: If you report something that has happened, you tell people about it.

veterinary.quick_def: Veterinary is used to describe the work of a person whose job is to treat sick or injured animals, or to describe the medical treatment of animals.

inspector.quick_def: An inspector is a person, usually employed by a government agency, whose job is to find out whether people are obeying official regulations.

appointed.quick_def: If you appoint someone to a job or official position, you formally choose them for it.

under.quick_def: If a person or thing is under something, they are at a lower level than that thing, and may be covered or hidden by it.

terms.quick_def: If you talk about something in terms of something or in particular terms, you are specifying which aspect of it you are discussing or from what point of view you are considering it.

licensing.quick_def: To license a person or activity means to give official permission for the person to do something or for the activity to take place.

act.quick_def: When you act, you do something for a particular purpose.

always.quick_def: If you always do something, you do it whenever a particular situation occurs. If you always did something, you did it whenever a particular situation occurred.

repute.quick_def: A person or thing of repute or of high repute is respected and known to be good.  [formal]

obliged.quick_def: If you are obliged to do something, a situation, rule, or law makes it necessary for you to do that thing.

reflect.quick_def: If something reflects an attitude or situation, it shows that the attitude or situation exists or it shows what it is like.

upon.quick_def: If one thing is upon another, it is on it.  [formal]

sets.quick_def: A set of things is a number of things that belong together or that are thought of as a group.

granting.quick_def: A grant is an amount of money that a government or other institution gives to an individual or to an organization for a particular purpose such as education or home improvements.

membership.quick_def: Membership of an organization is the state of being a member of it.

situation.quick_def: You use situation to refer generally to what is happening in a particular place at a particular time, or to refer to what is happening to you.

worse.quick_def: Something that is bad is unpleasant, harmful, or undesirable.

developing.quick_def: When something develops, it grows or changes over a period of time and usually becomes more advanced, complete, or severe.

countries.quick_def: A country is one of the political units which the world is divided into, covering a particular area of land.

little.quick_def: You use little to indicate that there is only a very small amount of something. You can use 'so', 'too', and 'very' in front of little.

money.quick_def: Money is the coins or bank notes that you use to buy things, or the sum that you have in a bank account.

available.quick_def: If something you want or need is available, you can find it or obtain it.

redevelopment.quick_def: When redevelopment takes place, the buildings in one area of a town are knocked down and new ones are built in their place.

hard.quick_def: Something that is hard is very firm and stiff to touch and is not easily bent, cut, or broken.

see.quick_def: When you see something, you notice it using your eyes.

way.quick_def: If you refer to a way of doing something, you are referring to how you can do it, for example the action you can take or the method you can use to achieve it.

incorporating.quick_def: If one thing incorporates another thing, it includes the other thing.  [formal]

overall.quick_def: You use overall to indicate that you are talking about a situation in general or about the whole of something.

scheme.quick_def: A scheme is a plan or arrangement involving many people which is made by a government or other organization.  [mainly British]

assuming.quick_def: If you assume that something is true, you imagine that it is true, sometimes wrongly.

all.quick_def: You use all to indicate that you are referring to the whole of a particular group or thing or to everyone or everything of a particular kind.

standard.quick_def: A standard is a level of quality or achievement, especially a level that is thought to be acceptable.

complete.quick_def: You use complete to emphasize that something is as great in extent, degree, or amount as it possibly can be.  [emphasis]

scientific.quick_def: Scientific is used to describe things that relate to science or to a particular science.

staff.quick_def: The staff of an organization are the people who work for it.

research.quick_def: Research is work that involves studying something and trying to discover facts about it.

facilities.quick_def: Facilities are buildings, pieces of equipment, or services that are provided for a particular purpose.

trained.quick_def: A train is a number of carriages, cars, or trucks which are all connected together and which are pulled by an engine along a railway. Trains carry people and goods from one place to another.

dedicated.quick_def: If you say that someone has dedicated themselves to something, you approve of the fact that they have decided to give a lot of time and effort to it because they think that it is important.  [approval]

keepers.quick_def: In football, the keeper is the same as the goalkeeper.  [British, informal]

accommodation.quick_def: Accommodation is used to refer to buildings or rooms where people live or stay.  [British]

permits.quick_def: If someone permits something, they allow it to happen. If they permit you to do something, they allow you to do it.  [formal, written]

normal.quick_def: Something that is normal is usual and ordinary, and is what people expect.

natural.quick_def: If you say that it is natural for someone to act in a particular way or for something to happen in that way, you mean that it is reasonable in the circumstances.

behaviour.quick_def: People's or animals' behaviour is the way that they behave. You can refer to a typical and repeated way of behaving as a behaviour.

policy.quick_def: A policy is a set of ideas or plans that is used as a basis for making decisions, especially in politics, economics, or business.

co-operating.quick_def: When people are co-operating, they work together to achieve a common goal.

fully.quick_def: Fully means to the greatest degree or extent possible.

what.quick_def: You use what in questions when you ask for specific information about something that you do not know.

potential.quick_def: You use potential to say that someone or something is capable of developing into the particular kind of person or thing mentioned.

tudge.quick_def: Tudge is a proper name, usually used as a person's last name.

author.quick_def: The author of a piece of writing is the person who wrote it.

last.quick_def: You use last in expressions such as last Friday, last night, and last year to refer, for example, to the most recent Friday, night, or year.

oxford.quick_def: Oxfords are low shoes with laces at the front.  [mainly US]

university.quick_def: A university is an institution where students study for degrees and where academic research is done.

argues.quick_def: If one person argues with another, they speak angrily to each other about something that they disagree about. You can also say that two people argue.

if.quick_def: You use if in conditional sentences to introduce the circumstances in which an event or situation might happen, might be happening, or might have happened.

worked.quick_def: People who work have a job, usually one which they are paid to do.

together.quick_def: If people do something together, they do it with each other.

co-operative.quick_def: If people are co-operative, they are willing to work with others and help them.

then.quick_def: Then means at a particular time in the past or in the future.

further.quick_def: Further means to a greater extent or degree.

expansion.quick_def: Expansion is the process of becoming greater in size, number, or amount.

they.quick_def: You use they to refer to a group of people, animals, or things.

save.quick_def: If you save someone or something, you help them to avoid harm or to escape from a dangerous or unpleasant situation.

land.quick_def: Land is an area of ground, especially one that is used for a particular purpose such as farming or building.

vertebrates.quick_def: A vertebrate is a creature which has a spine. Mammals, birds, reptiles, and fish are vertebrates.

seems.quick_def: You use seem to say that someone or something gives the impression of having a particular quality, or of happening in the way you describe.

optimistic.quick_def: Someone who is optimistic is hopeful about the future or the success of something in particular.

proposition.quick_def: If you describe something such as a task or an activity as, for example, a difficult proposition or an attractive proposition, you mean that it is difficult or pleasant to do.

aware.quick_def: If you are aware of something, you know about it.

failings.quick_def: The failings of someone or something are their faults or unsatisfactory features.

weaknesses.quick_def: If someone is weak, they are not healthy or do not have good muscles, so that they cannot move quickly or carry heavy things.

persuade.quick_def: If you persuade someone to do something, you cause them to do it by giving them good reasons for doing it.

devote.quick_def: If you devote yourself, your time, or your energy to something, you spend all or most of your time or energy on it.

activities.quick_def: Activity is a situation in which a lot of things are happening or being done.

moreover.quick_def: You use moreover to introduce a piece of information that adds to or supports the previous statement.  [formal]

approximately.quick_def: An approximate number, time, or position is close to the correct number, time, or position, but is not exact.

said.quick_def: Said is the past tense and past participle of say.

saved.quick_def: If you save someone or something, you help them to avoid harm or to escape from a dangerous or unpleasant situation.

captive.quick_def: A captive person or animal is being kept imprisoned or enclosed.  [literary]
