hardly.quick_def: You use hardly to modify a statement when you want to emphasize that it is only a small amount or detail which makes it true, and that therefore it is best to consider the opposite statement as being true.  [emphasis]

looked.quick_def: If you look in a particular direction, you direct your eyes in that direction, especially so that you can see what is there or see what something is like.

resounding.quick_def: When a noise resounds, it is heard very loudly and clearly.  [literary]

successes.quick_def: Success is the achievement of something that you have been trying to do.

beyond.quick_def: If something is beyond a place or barrier, it is on the other side of it.

given.quick_def: You can use give with nouns that refer to physical actions. The whole expression refers to the performing of the action. For example, She gave a smile means almost the same as 'She smiled'.

conference.quick_def: A conference is a meeting, often lasting a few days, which is organized on a particular subject or to bring together people who have a common interest.

pretty.quick_def: If you describe someone as pretty, you mean that they are attractive.

progress.quick_def: Progress is the process of gradually improving or getting nearer to achieving or completing something.

long.quick_def: Long means a great amount of time or for a great amount of time.

off.quick_def: If something is taken off something else or moves off it, it is no longer touching that thing.

target.quick_def: A target is something at which someone is aiming a weapon or other object.

architecture.quick_def: Architecture is the art of planning, designing, and constructing buildings.

art.quick_def: Art consists of paintings, sculpture, and other pictures or objects which are created for people to look at and admire or think deeply about.

science.quick_def: Science is the study of the nature and behaviour of natural things and the knowledge that we obtain about them.

designing.quick_def: When someone designs a garment, building, machine, or other object, they plan it and make a detailed drawing of it from which it can be built or made.

buildings.quick_def: A building is a structure that has a roof and walls, for example a house or a factory.

structures.quick_def: The structure of something is the way in which it is made, built, or organized.

building.quick_def: If you build something, you make it by joining things together.

reflects.quick_def: If something reflects an attitude or situation, it shows that the attitude or situation exists or it shows what it is like.

technological.quick_def: Technological means relating to or associated with technology.

achievements.quick_def: An achievement is something which someone has succeeded in doing, especially after a lot of effort.

ideas.quick_def: An idea is a plan, suggestion, or possible course of action.

aspirations.quick_def: Someone's aspirations are their desire to achieve things.

designer.quick_def: A designer is a person whose job is to design things by making drawings of them.

client.quick_def: A client of a professional person or organization is a person or company that receives a service from them in return for payment.  [business]

appearance.quick_def: When someone makes an appearance at a public event or in a broadcast, they take part in it.

individual.quick_def: Individual means relating to one person or thing, rather than to a large group.

often.quick_def: If something often happens, it happens many times or much of the time.

controversial.quick_def: If you describe something or someone as controversial, you mean that they are the subject of intense public argument, disagreement, or disapproval.

use.quick_def: If you use something, you do something with it in order to do a job or to achieve a particular result or effect.

architectural.quick_def: Architectural means relating to the design and construction of buildings.

style.quick_def: The style of something is the general way in which it is done or presented, which often shows the attitudes of the people involved.

cannot.quick_def: Cannot is the negative form of can1.

start.quick_def: If you start to do something, you do something that you were not doing before and you continue doing it.

finish.quick_def: When you finish doing or dealing with something, you do or deal with the last part of it, so that there is no more for you to do or deal with.

specific.quick_def: You use specific to refer to a particular fixed area, problem, or subject.

neither.quick_def: You use neither in front of the first of two or more words or expressions when you are linking two or more things which are not true or do not happen. The other thing is introduced by 'nor'.

possible.quick_def: If it is possible to do something, it can be done.

say.quick_def: When you say something, you speak words.

exactly.quick_def: Exact means correct in every detail. For example, an exact copy is the same in every detail as the thing it is copied from.

characterises.quick_def: If something is characterized by a particular feature or quality, that feature or quality is an obvious part of it.  [formal]

particular.quick_def: You use particular to emphasize that you are talking about one thing or one kind of thing rather than other similar ones.  [emphasis]

movement.quick_def: A movement is a group of people who share the same beliefs, ideas, or aims.

origins.quick_def: You can refer to the beginning, cause, or source of something as its origin or origins.

generally.quick_def: You use generally to give a summary of a situation, activity, or idea without referring to the particular details of it.

known.quick_def: If you know a fact, a piece of information, or an answer, you have it correctly in your mind.

modern.quick_def: Modern means relating to the present time, for example the present decade or present century.

traced.quick_def: If you trace the origin or development of something, you find out or describe how it started or developed.

social.quick_def: Social means relating to society or to the way society is organized.

changes.quick_def: If there is a change in something, it becomes different.

centuries.quick_def: A century is a period of a hundred years that is used when stating a date. For example, the 19th century was the period from 1801 to 1900.

using.quick_def: If you use something, you do something with it in order to do a job or to achieve a particular result or effect.

timber.quick_def: Timber is wood that is used for building houses and making furniture. You can also refer to trees that are grown for this purpose as timber.

traditional.quick_def: Traditional customs, beliefs, or methods are ones that have existed for a long time without changing.

techniques.quick_def: A technique is a particular method of doing an activity, usually a method that involves practical skills.

architects.quick_def: An architect is a person who designs buildings.

explore.quick_def: If you explore a place, you travel around it to find out what it is like.

ways.quick_def: If you refer to a way of doing something, you are referring to how you can do it, for example the action you can take or the method you can use to achieve it.

creating.quick_def: To create something means to cause it to happen or exist.

latest.quick_def: Late means near the end of a day, week, year, or other period of time.

materials.quick_def: A material is a solid substance.

concrete.quick_def: Concrete is a substance used for building which is made by mixing together cement, sand, small stones, and water.

strengthened.quick_def: If something strengthens a person or group or if they strengthen their position, they become more powerful and secure, or more likely to succeed.

bars.quick_def: A bar is a place where you can buy and drink alcoholic drinks.  [mainly US]

reinforced.quick_def: If something reinforces a feeling, situation, or process, it makes it stronger or more intense.

advances.quick_def: To advance means to move forward, often in order to attack someone.

helped.quick_def: If you help someone, you make it easier for them to do something, for example by doing part of the work for them or by giving them advice or money.

bring.quick_def: If you bring someone or something with you when you come to a place, they come with you or you have them with you.

decline.quick_def: If something declines, it becomes less in quantity, importance, or strength.

rural.quick_def: Rural places are far away from large towns or cities.

industries.quick_def: Industry is the work and processes involved in collecting raw materials, and making them into products in factories.

increase.quick_def: If something increases or you increase it, it becomes greater in number, level, or amount.

urban.quick_def: Urban means belonging to, or relating to, a town or city.

populations.quick_def: The population of a country or area is all the people who live in it.

people.quick_def: People are men, women, and children. People is normally used as the plural of person, instead of 'persons'.

moved.quick_def: When you move something or when it moves, its position changes and it does not remain still.

towns.quick_def: A town is a place with many streets and buildings, where people live and work. Towns are larger than villages and smaller than cities. Many places that are called towns in Britain would be called cities in the United States.

new.quick_def: Something that is new has been recently created, built, or invented or is in the process of being created, built, or invented.

factories.quick_def: A factory is a large building where machines are used to make large quantities of goods.

rapid.quick_def: A rapid change is one that happens very quickly.

uncontrolled.quick_def: If you describe someone's behaviour as uncontrolled, you mean they appear unable to stop it or to make it less extreme.

growth.quick_def: The growth of something such as an industry, organization, or idea is its development in size, wealth, or importance.

turn.quick_def: When you turn or when you turn part of your body, you move your body or part of your body so that it is facing in a different or opposite direction.

parts.quick_def: A part of something is one of the pieces, sections, or elements that it consists of.

cities.quick_def: A city is a large town.

slums.quick_def: A slum is an area of a city where living conditions are very bad and where the houses are in bad condition.

throughout.quick_def: If you say that something happens throughout a particular period of time, you mean that it happens during the whole of that period.

reacting.quick_def: When you react to something that has happened to you, you behave in a particular way because of it.

industrialisation.quick_def: Industrialisation is the process when a country or area changes from mainly farming to making a lot of goods in factories.

emerged.quick_def: To emerge means to come out from an enclosed or dark space such as a room or a vehicle, or from a position where you could not be seen.

idealistic.quick_def: If you describe someone as idealistic, you mean that they have ideals, and base their behaviour on these ideals, even though this may be impractical.

notions.quick_def: A notion is an idea or belief about something.

future.quick_def: The future is the period of time that will come after the present, or the things that will happen then.

construction.quick_def: Construction is the building of things such as houses, factories, roads, and bridges.

modernism.quick_def: Modernism was a movement in the arts in the first half of the twentieth century that rejected traditional values and techniques, and emphasized the importance of individual experience.

emerging.quick_def: To emerge means to come out from an enclosed or dark space such as a room or a vehicle, or from a position where you could not be seen.

designed.quick_def: When someone designs a garment, building, machine, or other object, they plan it and make a detailed drawing of it from which it can be built or made.

largely.quick_def: You use largely to say that a statement is not completely true but is mostly true.

characterised.quick_def: If something is characterized by a particular feature or quality, that feature or quality is an obvious part of it.  [formal]

bold.quick_def: Someone who is bold is not afraid to do things which involve risk or danger.

simple.quick_def: If you describe something as simple, you mean that it is not complicated, and is therefore easy to understand.

geometric.quick_def: Geometric or geometrical patterns or shapes consist of regular shapes or lines.

forms.quick_def: A form of something is a type or kind of it.

walls.quick_def: A wall is one of the vertical sides of a building or room.

supported.quick_def: If you support someone or their ideas or aims, you agree with them, and perhaps help them because you want them to succeed.

stilt-like.quick_def: If something is stilt-like, it looks like or is similar to stilts. Stilts are long poles that people stand on to be higher off the ground.

pillars.quick_def: A pillar is a tall solid structure, which is usually used to support part of a building.

stripped.quick_def: A strip of something such as paper, cloth, or food is a long, narrow piece of it.

unnecessary.quick_def: If you describe something as unnecessary, you mean that it is not needed or does not have to be done, and is undesirable.

decoration.quick_def: If you decorate something, you make it more attractive by adding things to it.

detract.quick_def: If one thing detracts from another, it makes it seem less good or impressive.

primary.quick_def: You use primary to describe something that is very important.  [formal]

purpose.quick_def: The purpose of something is the reason for which it is made or done.

lived.quick_def: If someone lives in a particular place or with a particular person, their home is in that place or with that person.

gropius.quick_def: Gropius is a surname. Usually, it refers to a person, like an architect.

jeanneret.quick_def: Jeanneret is a family name. It is used to call a person.

better.quick_def: Better is the comparative of good.

le.quick_def: In French, 'le' is a word used before a masculine singular noun, like 'the' in English.

corbusier.quick_def: Corbusier is a well-known architect's name. An architect is a person who designs buildings.

ludwig.quick_def: Ludwig is a common male name.

mies.quick_def: Mies is a short name or nickname for someone, usually used to refer to Ludwig Mies van der Rohe, a well-known architect.

van.quick_def: A van is a small or medium-sized road vehicle with one row of seats at the front and a space for carrying goods behind.

der.quick_def: In this context, 'der' is part of a person's name. It doesn't have a single-word meaning on its own. In some languages like German, 'der' can be a definite article, like 'the' in English.

rohe.quick_def: Rohe is a surname. It is the last name of a person, often used to refer to a specific individual.

among.quick_def: Someone or something that is situated or moving among a group of things or people is surrounded by them.

influential.quick_def: Someone or something that is influential has a lot of influence over people or events.

contributed.quick_def: If you contribute to something, you say or do things to help to make it successful.

half.quick_def: Half of an amount or object is one of two equal parts that together make up the whole number, amount, or object.

economic.quick_def: Economic means concerned with the organization of the money, industry, and trade of a country, region, or society.

depression.quick_def: Depression is a mental state in which you are sad and feel that you cannot enjoy anything, because your situation is so difficult and unpleasant.

war.quick_def: A war is a period of fighting or conflict between countries or states.

prevented.quick_def: To prevent something means to ensure that it does not happen.

realised.quick_def: If you realize that something is true, you become aware of that fact or understand it.

improved.quick_def: If something improves or if you improve it, it gets better.

war-torn.quick_def: If a place is war-torn, it has been damaged a lot because of a war.

rebuilt.quick_def: When people rebuild something such as a building or a city, they build it again after it has been damaged or destroyed.

developed.quick_def: When something develops, it grows or changes over a period of time and usually becomes more advanced, complete, or severe.

universal.quick_def: Something that is universal relates to everyone in the world or everyone in a particular group or society.

approach.quick_def: When you approach something, you get closer to it.

standardised.quick_def: To standardize things means to change them so that they all have the same features.

across.quick_def: If someone or something goes across a place or a boundary, they go from one side of it to the other.

unfortunately.quick_def: You can use unfortunately to introduce or refer to a statement when you consider that it is sad or disappointing, or when you want to express regret.  [feelings]

modernist.quick_def: Modernist means relating to the ideas and methods of modern art.

interest.quick_def: If you have an interest in something, you want to learn or hear more about it.

simplicity.quick_def: The simplicity of something is the fact that it is not complicated and can be understood or done easily.

function.quick_def: The function of something or someone is the useful thing that they do or are intended to do.

profit.quick_def: A profit is an amount of money that you gain when you are paid more for something than it cost you to make, get, or do it.

rediscovery.quick_def: The rediscovery of something good that you had forgotten or lost is the fact or process of becoming aware of it again or finding it again.

quick-and-easy-to-handle.quick_def: If something is quick-and-easy-to-handle, it can be dealt with quickly and easily.

ability.quick_def: Your ability to do something is the fact that you can do it.

prefabricate.quick_def: To prefabricate means to make parts of something, like a building, in a factory before putting them together at the final place.

sections.quick_def: A section of something is one of the parts into which it is divided or from which it is formed.

meant.quick_def: If you want to know what a word, code, signal, or gesture means, you want to know what it refers to or what its message is.

builders.quick_def: A builder is a person whose job is to build or repair houses and other buildings.

budgets.quick_def: Your budget is the amount of money that you have available to spend. The budget for something is the amount of money that a person, organization, or country has available to spend on it.

commissioning.quick_def: If you commission something or commission someone to do something, you formally arrange for someone to do a piece of work for you.

authorities.quick_def: The authorities are the people who have the power to make decisions and to make sure that laws are obeyed.

handle.quick_def: A handle is a small round object or a lever that is attached to a door and is used for opening and closing it.

renewed.quick_def: If you renew an activity, you begin it again.

demand.quick_def: If you demand something such as information or action, you ask for it in a very forceful way.

cheaply.quick_def: Goods or services that are cheap cost less money than usual or than you expected.

led.quick_def: If you lead a group of people, you walk or ride in front of them.

badly.quick_def: If something is done badly or goes badly, it is not very successful or effective.

discredited.quick_def: To discredit someone or something means to cause them to lose people's respect or trust.

original.quick_def: You use original when referring to something that existed at the beginning of a process or activity, or the characteristics that something had when it began or was made.

aims.quick_def: If you aim for something or aim to do something, you plan or hope to achieve it.

influenced.quick_def: Influence is the power to make other people agree with your opinions or do what you want.

town.quick_def: A town is a place with many streets and buildings, where people live and work. Towns are larger than villages and smaller than cities. Many places that are called towns in Britain would be called cities in the United States.

planning.quick_def: A plan is a method of achieving something that you have worked out in detail beforehand.

every.quick_def: You use every to indicate that you are referring to all the members of a group or all the parts of something and not only some of them.

large.quick_def: A large thing or person is greater in size than usual or average.

british.quick_def: British means belonging or relating to the United Kingdom, or to its people or culture.

city.quick_def: A city is a large town.

built.quick_def: If you build something, you make it by joining things together.

multi-storey.quick_def: If a building is multi-storey, it has more than one floor.

housing.quick_def: A house is a building in which people live, usually the people belonging to one family.

estates.quick_def: An estate is a large area of land in the country which is owned by a person, family, or organization.

mass-produced.quick_def: If something is mass-produced, it is made in large numbers in a factory.

low-cost.quick_def: If something is low-cost, it doesn't cost a lot of money.

high-rises.quick_def: High-rises are very tall buildings in a city.

seemed.quick_def: You use seem to say that someone or something gives the impression of having a particular quality, or of happening in the way you describe.

offer.quick_def: If you offer something to someone, you ask them if they would like to have it or use it.

problem.quick_def: A problem is a situation that is unsatisfactory and causes difficulties for people.

growing.quick_def: When people, animals, and plants grow, they increase in size and change physically over a period of time.

inner-city.quick_def: Inner-city refers to the central areas of a big city, usually with problems like poor housing and more crime.

population.quick_def: The population of a country or area is all the people who live in it.

far.quick_def: If one place, thing, or person is far away from another, there is a great distance between them.

human.quick_def: Human means relating to or concerning people.

needs.quick_def: If you need something, or need to do something, you cannot successfully achieve what you want or live properly without it.

proved.quick_def: If something proves to be true or to have a particular quality, it becomes clear after a period of time that it is true or has that quality.

windswept.quick_def: A windswept place has no shelter and is not protected against strong winds.

deserts.quick_def: A desert is a large area of land, usually in a hot region, where there is almost no water, rain, trees, or plants.

lacking.quick_def: If there is a lack of something, there is not enough of it or it does not exist at all.

essential.quick_def: Something that is essential is extremely important or absolutely necessary to a particular subject, situation, or activity.

services.quick_def: A service is something that the public needs, such as transport, communications facilities, hospitals, or energy supplies, which is provided in a planned and organized way by the government or an official body.

poorly.quick_def: Someone who is poor has very little money and few possessions.

constructed.quick_def: If you construct something such as a building, road, or machine, you build it or make it.

demolished.quick_def: To demolish something such as a building means to destroy it completely.

respect.quick_def: If you respect someone, you have a good opinion of their character or ideas.

within.quick_def: If something is within a place, area, or object, it is inside it or surrounded by it.  [formal]

existing.quick_def: If something exists, it is present in the world as a real thing.

townscape.quick_def: what you see when you look at a town, for example from a distance

arose.quick_def: If a situation or problem arises, it begins to exist or people start to become aware of it.

preserving.quick_def: If you preserve a situation or condition, you make sure that it remains as it is, and does not change or end.

historic.quick_def: Something that is historic is important in history, or likely to be considered important at some time in the future.

only.quick_def: You use only to indicate the one thing that is true, appropriate, or necessary in a particular situation, in contrast to all the other things that are not true, appropriate, or necessary.

facades.quick_def: The facade of a building, especially a large one, is its front wall or the wall that faces the street.

fronts.quick_def: The front of something is the part of it that faces you, or that faces forward, or that you normally see or use.

grew.quick_def: Grew is the past tense of grow.

common.quick_def: If something is common, it is found in large numbers or it happens often.

styles.quick_def: The style of something is the general way in which it is done or presented, which often shows the attitudes of the people involved.

area.quick_def: An area is a particular part of a town, a country, a region, or the world.

usually.quick_def: If something usually happens, it is the thing that most often happens in a particular situation.

referred.quick_def: If you refer to a particular subject or person, you talk about them or mention them.

celebrated.quick_def: If you celebrate, you do something enjoyable because of a special occasion or to mark someone's success.

engineering.quick_def: An engineer is a person who uses scientific knowledge to design, construct, and maintain engines and machines or structures such as roads, railways, and bridges.

openly.quick_def: If you do something openly, you do it without hiding any facts or hiding your feelings.

parading.quick_def: A parade is a procession of people or vehicles moving through a public place in order to celebrate an important day or event.

sophisticated.quick_def: A sophisticated machine, device, or method is more advanced or complex than others.

commonly.quick_def: If something is common, it is found in large numbers or it happens often.

metal.quick_def: Metal is a hard substance such as iron, steel, gold, or lead.

examples.quick_def: An example of something is a particular situation, object, or person which shows that what is being claimed is true.

stansted.quick_def: Stansted is the name of a place, often referring to an airport.

airport.quick_def: An airport is a place where aircraft land and take off, which has buildings and facilities for passengers.

lloyd.quick_def: Lloyd is a name for a person or can be part of a place-related name like a building's name.

disillusionment.quick_def: Disillusionment is the disappointment that you feel when you discover that something is not as good as you had expected or thought.

failure.quick_def: Failure is a lack of success in doing or achieving something, especially in relation to a particular activity.

poor.quick_def: Someone who is poor has very little money and few possessions.

imitations.quick_def: An imitation of something is a copy of it.

various.quick_def: If you say that there are various things, you mean there are several different things of the type mentioned.

past.quick_def: The past is the time before the present, and the things that have happened.

present.quick_def: You use present to describe things and people that exist now, rather than those that existed in the past or those that may exist in the future.

coexistence.quick_def: The coexistence of one thing with another is the fact that they exist together at the same time or in the same place.

post.quick_def: The post is the public service or system by which letters and packages are collected and delivered.  [mainly British]

classical.quick_def: You use classical to describe something that is traditional in form, style, or content.

tradition.quick_def: A tradition is a custom or belief that has existed for a long time.

trend.quick_def: A trend is a change or development towards something new or different.

favours.quick_def: If you regard something or someone with favour, you like or support them.

smaller.quick_def: A small person, thing, or amount of something is not large in physical size.

scale.quick_def: If you refer to the scale of something, you are referring to its size or extent, especially when it is very big.

design.quick_def: When someone designs a garment, building, machine, or other object, they plan it and make a detailed drawing of it from which it can be built or made.

public.quick_def: You can refer to people in general, or to all the people in a particular country or community, as the public.

awareness.quick_def: If you are aware of something, you know about it.

environmental.quick_def: Environmental means concerned with the protection of the natural world of land, sea, air, plants, and animals.

issues.quick_def: An issue is an important subject that people are arguing about or discussing.

energy.quick_def: Energy is the ability and strength to do active physical things and the feeling that you are full of physical power and life.

efficiency.quick_def: Efficiency is the quality of being able to do a task successfully, without wasting time or energy.

modernists.quick_def: Modernist means relating to the ideas and methods of modern art.

recognise.quick_def: If you recognize someone or something, you know who that person is or what that thing is.

environment.quick_def: Someone's environment is all the circumstances, people, things, and events around them that influence their life.

improves.quick_def: If something improves or if you improve it, it gets better.

life.quick_def: Life is the quality which people, animals, and plants have when they are not dead, and which objects and substances do not have.

necessarily.quick_def: If you say that something is not necessarily the case, you mean that it may not be the case or is not always the case.  [vagueness]

achieved.quick_def: If you achieve a particular aim or effect, you succeed in doing it or causing it to happen, usually after a lot of effort.

adopting.quick_def: If you adopt a new attitude, plan, or way of behaving, you begin to have it.

twentieth.quick_def: The twentieth item in a series is the one that you count as number twenty.

mainly.quick_def: You use mainly when mentioning the main reason or thing involved in something.

remembered.quick_def: If you remember people or events from the past, you still have an idea of them in your mind and you are able to think about them.

tall.quick_def: Someone or something that is tall has a greater height than is normal or average.

frames.quick_def: The frame of a picture or mirror is the wood, metal, or plastic that is fitted around it, especially when it is displayed or hung on a wall.

passenger.quick_def: A passenger in a vehicle such as a bus, boat, or plane is a person who is travelling in it, but who is not driving it or working on it.

lifts.quick_def: If you lift something, you move it to another position, especially upwards.

originated.quick_def: When something originates or when someone originates it, it begins to happen or exist.  [formal]

over.quick_def: If one thing is over another thing or is moving over it, the first thing is directly above the second, either resting on it, or with a space between them.

help.quick_def: If you help someone, you make it easier for them to do something, for example by doing part of the work for them or by giving them advice or money.

economical.quick_def: Something that is economical does not require a lot of money to operate. For example a car that only uses a small amount of petrol is economical.

skyscraper.quick_def: A skyscraper is a very tall building in a city.

why.quick_def: You use why in questions when you ask about the reasons for something.

do.quick_def: Do is used to form the negative of main verbs, by putting 'not' after 'do' and before the main verb in its infinitive form, that is the form without 'to'.

humans.quick_def: Human means relating to or concerning people.

virtually.quick_def: You can use virtually to indicate that something is so nearly true that for most purposes it can be regarded as true.

alone.quick_def: When you are alone, you are not with any other people.

animal.quick_def: An animal is a living creature such as a dog, lion, or rabbit, rather than a bird, fish, insect, or human being.

display.quick_def: If you display something that you want people to see, you put it in a particular place, so that people can see it easily.

distinct.quick_def: If something is distinct from something else of the same type, it is different or separate from it.

left.quick_def: If you leave a place or person, you go away from that place or person.

right-handedness.quick_def: Right-handedness is the preference for using the right hand more often than the left hand when doing things.

our.quick_def: You use our to indicate that something belongs or relates both to yourself and to one or more other people.

closest.quick_def: When you close something such as a door or lid or when it closes, it moves so that a hole, gap, or opening is covered.

relatives.quick_def: Your relatives are the members of your family.

apes.quick_def: Apes are chimpanzees, gorillas, and other animals in the same family.

possess.quick_def: If you possess something, you have it or own it.

lateral.quick_def: Lateral means relating to the sides of something, or moving in a sideways direction.

asymmetry.quick_def: Asymmetry is the appearance that something has when its two sides or halves are different in shape, size, or style.

psychologists.quick_def: A psychologist is a person who studies the human mind and tries to explain why people behave in the way that they do.

call.quick_def: If you call someone or something by a particular name or title, you give them that name or title.

yet.quick_def: You use yet in negative statements to indicate that something has not happened up to the present time, although it probably will happen. You can also use yet in questions to ask if something has happened up to the present time. In British English the simple past tense is not normally used with this meaning of 'yet'.

cent.quick_def: A cent is a small unit of money worth one-hundredth of some currencies, for example the dollar and the euro.

ever.quick_def: Ever means at any time. It is used in questions and negative statements.

right-handed.quick_def: If a person is right-handed, they use their right hand more often and more easily than their left hand.

professor.quick_def: A professor in a British university is the most senior teacher in a department.

bryan.quick_def: Bryan is a common male name.

turner.quick_def: Turner is a common surname. A surname is the family name that a person shares with other family members.

deakin.quick_def: Deakin is a proper name, often used for a person or a place like a university.

studied.quick_def: A studied action is deliberate or planned.

literature.quick_def: Novels, plays, and poetry are referred to as literature, especially when they are considered to be good or important.

left-handedness.quick_def: Left-handedness is the state of a person who prefers to use their left hand more often than the right hand when doing things.

handedness.quick_def: Handedness is the preference for using either the left or the right hand. For example, some people are more used to using their right hand to write, while others prefer their left hand.

goes.quick_def: When you go somewhere, you move or travel there.

sidedness.quick_def: Sidedness is about having a preference for one side of the body. For example, using one hand more often than the other.

right-footed.quick_def: If a person is right-footed, they use their right foot more often and more easily than their left foot.

he.quick_def: You use he to refer to a man, boy, or male animal.

noted.quick_def: A note is a short letter.

distinctive.quick_def: Something that is distinctive has a special quality or feature which makes it easily recognizable and different from other things of the same type.

itself.quick_def: Itself is used as the object of a verb or preposition when it refers to something that is the same thing as the subject of the verb.

systematic.quick_def: Something that is done in a systematic way is done according to a fixed plan, in a thorough and efficient way.

think.quick_def: If you think that something is the case, you have the opinion that it is the case.

categories.quick_def: If people or things are divided into categories, they are divided into groups in such a way that the members of each group are similar to each other in some way.

black.quick_def: Something that is black is of the darkest colour that there is, the colour of the sky at night when there is no light at all.

right.quick_def: If something is right, it is correct and agrees with the facts.

system.quick_def: A system is a way of working, organizing, or doing something which follows a fixed plan or set of rules. You can use system to refer to an organization or institution that is organized in this way.

signs.quick_def: A sign is a mark or shape that always has a particular meaning, for example in mathematics or music.

enables.quick_def: If someone or something enables you to do a particular thing, they give you the opportunity to do it.

categorise.quick_def: If you categorize people or things, you divide them into sets or you say which set they belong to.

phenomena.quick_def: Phenomena is the plural of phenomenon.

essentially.quick_def: You use essentially to emphasize a quality that someone or something has, and to say that it is their most important or basic quality.  [formal, emphasis]

ambiguous.quick_def: If you describe something as ambiguous, you mean that it is unclear or confusing because it can be understood in more than one way.

shown.quick_def: If something shows that a state of affairs exists, it gives information that proves it or makes it clear to people.

genetic.quick_def: You use genetic to describe something that is concerned with genetics or with genes.

inherited.quick_def: If you inherit money or property, you receive it from someone who has died.

while.quick_def: If something happens while something else is happening, the two things are happening at the same time.

tends.quick_def: If something tends to happen, it usually happens or it often happens.

run.quick_def: When you run, you move more quickly than when you walk, for example because you are in a hurry to get somewhere, or for exercise.

families.quick_def: A family is a group of people who are related to each other, especially parents and their children.

nor.quick_def: You use nor after 'neither' in order to introduce the second alternative or the last of a number of alternatives in a negative statement.

handers.quick_def: People who use a certain hand more often. For example, right handers use their right hands more, and left handers use their left hands more.

automatically.quick_def: An automatic machine or device is one which has controls that enable it to perform a task without needing to be constantly operated by a person. Automatic methods and processes involve the use of such machines.

offspring.quick_def: You can refer to a person's children or to an animal's young as their offspring.  [formal]

fact.quick_def: You use the fact that after some verbs or prepositions, especially in expressions such as in view of the fact that,  apart from the fact that, and despite the fact that, to link the verb or preposition with a clause.

children.quick_def: A child is a human being who is not yet an adult.

parents.quick_def: Your parents are your mother and father, or someone who looks after you as a parent would.

left-handed.quick_def: If a person is left-handed, they use their left hand more often and more skillfully than their right hand when doing things.

perhaps.quick_def: You use perhaps to express uncertainty, for example, when you do not know that something is definitely true, or when you are mentioning something that may possibly happen in the future in the way you describe.  [vagueness]

parent.quick_def: Your parents are your mother and father, or someone who looks after you as a parent would.

identical.quick_def: Things that are identical are exactly the same.

twins.quick_def: If two people are twins, they have the same mother and were born on the same day.

genes.quick_def: A gene is the part of a cell in a living thing which controls its physical characteristics, growth, and development.

pairs.quick_def: A pair of things are two things of the same size and shape that are used together or are both part of something, for example shoes, earrings, or parts of the body.

differ.quick_def: If two or more things differ, they are unlike each other in some way.

makes.quick_def: You can use make with a wide range of nouns to indicate that someone performs an action or says something. For example, if you make a suggestion, you suggest something.

simply.quick_def: If you describe something as simple, you mean that it is not complicated, and is therefore easy to understand.

factors.quick_def: A factor is one of the things that affects an event, decision, or situation.

researchers.quick_def: Research is work that involves studying something and trying to discover facts about it.

turned.quick_def: When you turn or when you turn part of your body, you move your body or part of your body so that it is facing in a different or opposite direction.

brain.quick_def: Your brain is the organ inside your head that controls your body's activities and enables you to think and to feel things such as heat and pain.

clues.quick_def: A clue to a problem or mystery is something that helps you to find the answer to it.

surgeon.quick_def: A surgeon is a doctor who is specially trained to perform surgery.

anthropologist.quick_def: a person who studies the human race, especially its origins, development, customs and beliefs

dr.quick_def: Dr is a written abbreviation for doctor.

broca.quick_def: Broca is a name, usually for a person.

remarkable.quick_def: Someone or something that is remarkable is unusual or special in a way that makes people notice them and be surprised or impressed.

finding.quick_def: If you find someone or something, you see them or learn where they are.

patients.quick_def: A patient is a person who is receiving medical treatment from a doctor or hospital. A patient is also someone who is registered with a particular doctor.

lost.quick_def: Lost is the past tense and past participle of lose.

powers.quick_def: If someone has power, they have a lot of control over people and activities.

speech.quick_def: Speech is the ability to speak or the act of speaking.

result.quick_def: A result is something that happens or exists because of something else that has happened.

stroke.quick_def: If you stroke someone or something, you move your hand slowly and gently over them.

blood.quick_def: Blood is the red liquid that flows inside your body, which you can see if you cut yourself.

clot.quick_def: A clot is a sticky lump that forms when blood dries up or becomes thick.

paralysis.quick_def: Paralysis is the loss of the ability to move and feel in all or part of your body.

body.quick_def: Your body is all your physical parts, including your head, arms, and legs.

hemisphere.quick_def: A hemisphere is one half of the earth.

controls.quick_def: Control of an organization, place, or system is the power to make all the important decisions about the way that it is run.

vice.quick_def: A vice is a habit which is regarded as a weakness in someone's character, but not usually as a serious fault.

versa.quick_def: When we say 'vice versa', it means the opposite way around. For example, if A is related to B, then vice versa means B is related to A in the same way.

damage.quick_def: To damage an object means to break it, spoil it physically, or stop it from working properly.

language.quick_def: A language is a system of communication which consists of a set of sounds and written symbols which are used by the people of a particular country or region for talking or writing.

centre.quick_def: A centre is a building where people have meetings, take part in a particular activity, or get help of some kind.

sided.quick_def: The side of something is a position to the left or right of it, rather than in front of it, behind it, or on it.

left-handers.quick_def: Left-handers are people who use their left hands more often to do things.

show.quick_def: If something shows that a state of affairs exists, it gives information that proves it or makes it clear to people.

reverse.quick_def: When someone or something reverses a decision, policy, or trend, they change it to the opposite decision, policy, or trend.

pattern.quick_def: A pattern is the repeated or regular way in which something happens or is done.

majority.quick_def: The majority of people or things in a group is more than half of them.

brinkman.quick_def: Brinkman is a surname, which is a family name used to identify a particular family.

researcher.quick_def: Research is work that involves studying something and trying to discover facts about it.

australian.quick_def: Australian means belonging or relating to Australia, or to its people or culture.

canberra.quick_def: the capital of Australia and seat of the federal government, in the Australian Capital Territory in south-eastern Australia

evolution.quick_def: Evolution is a process of gradual change that takes place over many generations, during which species of animals, plants, or insects slowly change some of their physical characteristics.

preference.quick_def: If you have a preference for something, you would like to have or do that thing rather than something else.

according.quick_def: An accord between countries or groups of people is a formal agreement, for example to end a war.

evolved.quick_def: When animals or plants evolve, they gradually change and develop into different forms.

side.quick_def: The side of something is a position to the left or right of it, rather than in front of it, behind it, or on it.

specialised.quick_def: If you specialize in a thing, you know a lot about it and concentrate a great deal of your time and energy on it, especially in your work or when you are studying or training. You also use specialize to talk about a restaurant which concentrates on a particular type of food.

fine.quick_def: You use fine to describe something that you admire and think is very good.

control.quick_def: Control of an organization, place, or system is the power to make all the important decisions about the way that it is run.

necessary.quick_def: Something that is necessary is needed in order for something else to happen.

producing.quick_def: To produce something means to cause it to happen.

along.quick_def: If you move or look along something such as a road, you move or look towards one end of it.

right-hand.quick_def: Right-hand means on the right side. It is used to describe the position that is on the right.

dominance.quick_def: The dominance of a particular person or thing is the fact that they are more powerful, successful, or important than other people or things.

capacity.quick_def: Your capacity for something is your ability to do it, or the amount of it that you are able to do.

she.quick_def: You use she to refer to a woman, girl, or female animal who has already been mentioned or whose identity is clear.

observed.quick_def: If you observe a person or thing, you watch them carefully, especially in order to learn something about them.

person.quick_def: A person is an individual human being.

brain-damaged.quick_def: If a person is brain-damaged, their brain has been hurt and doesn't work well.

recovery.quick_def: If a sick person makes a recovery, he or she becomes well again.

quite.quick_def: You use quite to indicate that something is the case to a fairly great extent. Quite is less emphatic than 'very' and ' extremely'.  [vagueness]

explained.quick_def: If you explain something, you give details about it or describe it so that it can be understood.

bilateral.quick_def: Bilateral negotiations, meetings, or agreements involve only the two groups or countries that are directly concerned.  [formal]

her.quick_def: You use her to refer to a woman, girl, or female animal.

macaque.quick_def: a type of monkey that lives in Africa and Asia

monkeys.quick_def: A monkey is an animal with a long tail which lives in hot countries and climbs trees.

noticed.quick_def: If you notice something or someone, you become aware of them.

primates.quick_def: A primate is a member of the group of mammals which includes humans, monkeys, and apes.

learn.quick_def: If you learn something, you obtain knowledge or a skill through studying or training.

hand.quick_def: Your hands are the parts of your body at the end of your arms. Each hand has four fingers and a thumb.

mother.quick_def: Your mother is the woman who gave birth to you. You can also call someone your mother if she brings you up as if she was this woman. You can call your mother 'Mother'.

specialisation.quick_def: Specialisation is when someone or something focuses on a particular area or type of work.

hemispheres.quick_def: A hemisphere is one half of the earth.

anatomical.quick_def: Anatomical means relating to the structure of the bodies of people and animals.

differences.quick_def: The difference between two things is the way in which they are unlike each other.

areas.quick_def: An area is a particular part of a town, a country, a region, or the world.

involved.quick_def: If a situation or activity involves something, that thing is a necessary part or consequence of it.

production.quick_def: Production is the process of manufacturing or growing something in large quantities.

larger.quick_def: A large thing or person is greater in size than usual or average.

than.quick_def: You use than after a comparative adjective or adverb in order to link two parts of a comparison.

acquired.quick_def: If you acquire something, you buy or obtain it for yourself, or someone gives it to you.  [formal]

expect.quick_def: If you expect something to happen, you believe that it will happen.

variation.quick_def: A variation on something is the same thing presented in a slightly different form.

claims.quick_def: If you say that someone claims that something is true, you mean they say that it is true but you are not sure whether or not they are telling the truth.

towards.quick_def: If you move, look, or point toward something or someone, you move, look, or point in their direction.

evident.quick_def: If something is evident, you notice it easily and clearly.

geschwind.quick_def: Geschwind is a proper name, usually used to call a person.

galaburda.quick_def: Galaburda is a name of a person.

brains.quick_def: Your brain is the organ inside your head that controls your body's activities and enables you to think and to feel things such as heat and pain.

embryos.quick_def: An embryo is an unborn animal or human being in the very early stages of development.

left-right.quick_def: Left-right refers to the difference or relation between the left side and the right side.

exists.quick_def: If something exists, it is present in the world as a real thing.

birth.quick_def: When a baby is born, you refer to this event as his or her birth.

develops.quick_def: When something develops, it grows or changes over a period of time and usually becomes more advanced, complete, or severe.

things.quick_def: You can use thing to refer to any object, feature, or event when you cannot, need not, or do not want to refer to it more precisely.

affect.quick_def: If something affects a person or thing, it influences them or causes them to change in some way.

initially.quick_def: Initially means soon after the beginning of a process or situation, rather than in the middle or at the end of it.

female.quick_def: Someone who is female is a woman or a girl.

organisation.quick_def: An organization is an official group of people, for example a political party, a business, a charity, or a club.

becomes.quick_def: If someone or something becomes a particular thing, they start to change and develop into that thing, or start to develop the characteristics mentioned.

male.quick_def: Someone who is male is a man or a boy.

foetus.quick_def: A foetus is an animal or human being in its later stages of development before it is born.

begins.quick_def: To begin to do something means to start doing it.

secrete.quick_def: If part of a plant, animal, or human secretes a liquid, it produces it.

hormones.quick_def: A hormone is a chemical, usually occurring naturally in your body, that makes an organ of your body do something.

knew.quick_def: Knew is the past tense of know.

mature.quick_def: When a child or young animal matures, it becomes an adult.

rates.quick_def: The rate at which something happens is the speed with which it happens.

girl.quick_def: A girl is a female child.

somewhat.quick_def: You use somewhat to indicate that something is the case to a limited extent or degree.  [formal]

faster.quick_def: Fast means happening, moving, or doing something at great speed. You also use fast in questions or statements about speed.

boy.quick_def: A boy is a child who will grow up to be a man.

something.quick_def: You use something to refer to a thing, situation, event, or idea, without saying exactly what it is.

happens.quick_def: Something that happens occurs or is done without being planned.

pregnancy.quick_def: Pregnancy is the condition of being pregnant or the period of time during which a female is pregnant.

likely.quick_def: You use likely to indicate that something is probably the case or will probably happen in a particular situation.

affected.quick_def: If something affects a person or thing, it influences them or causes them to change in some way.

may.quick_def: You use may to indicate that something will possibly happen or be true in the future, but you cannot be certain.  [vagueness]

become.quick_def: If someone or something becomes a particular thing, they start to change and develop into that thing, or start to develop the characteristics mentioned.

less.quick_def: You use less to indicate that there is a smaller amount of something than before or than average. You can use 'a little', 'a lot', 'a bit', ' far', and 'much' in front of less.

lateralised.quick_def: When something is lateralised, it is mainly controlled or used by one side of the body or brain.

superior.quick_def: If one thing or person is superior to another, the first is better than the second.

skills.quick_def: A skill is a type of work or activity which requires special training and knowledge.

logic.quick_def: Logic is a method of reasoning that involves a series of statements, each of which must be true if the statement before it is true.

rationality.quick_def: Rational decisions and thoughts are based on reason rather than on emotion.

abstraction.quick_def: An abstraction is a general idea rather than one relating to a particular object, person, or situation.  [formal]

should.quick_def: You use should when you are saying what would be the right thing to do or the right state for something to be in.

no.quick_def: You use no to give a negative response to a question.

surprise.quick_def: A surprise is an unexpected event, fact, or piece of news.

mathematicians.quick_def: A mathematician is a person who is trained in the study of numbers and calculations.

tend.quick_def: If something tends to happen, it usually happens or it often happens.

males.quick_def: Someone who is male is a man or a boy.

females.quick_def: Someone who is female is a woman or a girl.

consolation.quick_def: a thing or person that makes you feel better when you are unhappy or disappointed

suit.quick_def: A man's suit consists of a jacket, trousers, and sometimes a waistcoat, all made from the same fabric.

alarming.quick_def: Alarm is a feeling of fear or anxiety that something unpleasant or dangerous might happen.

mr.quick_def: Mr is used before a man's name when you are speaking or referring to him.

moore.quick_def: Moore is a common surname. A surname is the family name that a person shares with other family members.

writer.quick_def: A writer is a person who writes books, stories, or articles as a job.

journalist.quick_def: A journalist is a person whose job is to collect news and write about it for newspapers, magazines, television, or radio.

word.quick_def: A word is a single unit of language that can be represented in writing or speech. In English, a word has a space on either side of it when it is written.

reinforces.quick_def: If something reinforces a feeling, situation, or process, it makes it stronger or more intense.

own.quick_def: You use own to indicate that something belongs to a particular person or thing.

virtue.quick_def: Virtue is thinking and doing what is right and avoiding what is wrong.

subliminally.quick_def: Subliminal influences or messages affect your mind without you being aware of it.

says.quick_def: When you say something, you speak words.

tells.quick_def: If you tell someone something, you give them information.

anything.quick_def: You use anything in statements with negative meaning to indicate in a general way that nothing is present or that an action or event does not or cannot happen.

trusted.quick_def: If you trust someone, you believe that they are honest and sincere and will not deliberately do anything to harm you.

dangerous.quick_def: If something is dangerous, it is able or likely to hurt or harm you.

sinister.quick_def: Something that is sinister seems evil or harmful.

we.quick_def: A speaker or writer uses we to refer both to himself or herself and to one or more other people as a group. You can use we before a noun to make it clear which group of people you are referring to.

speak.quick_def: When you speak, you use your voice in order to say something.

compliments.quick_def: A compliment is a polite remark that you say to someone to show that you like their appearance, appreciate their qualities, or approve of what they have done.

coincidence.quick_def: A coincidence is when two or more similar or related events occur at the same time by chance and without any planning.

forced.quick_def: If someone forces you to do something, they make you do it even though you do not want to, for example by threatening you.

develop.quick_def: When something develops, it grows or changes over a period of time and usually becomes more advanced, complete, or severe.

stammer.quick_def: If you stammer, you speak with difficulty, hesitating and repeating words or sounds.

robbed.quick_def: If someone is robbed, they have money or property stolen from them.

freedom.quick_def: Freedom is the state of being allowed to do what you want to do. Freedoms are instances of this.

undertaken.quick_def: When you undertake a task or job, you start doing it and accept responsibility for it.

causes.quick_def: The cause of an event, usually a bad event, is the thing that makes it happen.

attitudes.quick_def: Your attitude to something is the way that you think and feel about it, especially when this shows in the way you behave.

gradually.quick_def: If something changes or is done gradually, it changes or is done in small stages over a long period of time, rather than suddenly.

changing.quick_def: If there is a change in something, it becomes different.

indeed.quick_def: You use indeed to confirm or agree with something that has just been said.  [emphasis]

champion.quick_def: A champion is someone who has won the first prize in a competition, contest, or fight.

tennis.quick_def: Tennis is a game played by two or four players on a rectangular court. The players use an oval racket with strings across it to hit a ball over a net across the middle of the court.

player.quick_def: A player in a sport or game is a person who takes part, either as a job or for fun.

lendl.quick_def: Lendl is a name, often referring to a well-known person, like a famous tennis player.

asked.quick_def: If you ask someone something, you say something to them in the form of a question because you want to know the answer.

single.quick_def: You use single to emphasize that you are referring to one thing, and no more than one thing.  [emphasis]

thing.quick_def: You can use thing to refer to any object, feature, or event when you cannot, need not, or do not want to refer to it more precisely.

choose.quick_def: If you choose someone or something from several people or things that are available, you decide which person or thing you want to have.

order.quick_def: If you do something in order to achieve a particular thing or in order that something can happen, you do it because you want to achieve that thing.

improve.quick_def: If something improves or if you improve it, it gets better.

game.quick_def: A game is an activity or sport usually involving skill, knowledge, or chance, in which you follow fixed rules and try to win against an opponent or to solve a puzzle.

left-hander.quick_def: A left-hander is a person who uses their left hand more often to do things like writing or throwing.

eke.quick_def: If you  eke a living or eke out an existence, you manage to survive with very little money.

full-time.quick_def: If a job is full-time, you work the whole working day or week, not just part of it.

living.quick_def: If someone lives in a particular place or with a particular person, their home is in that place or with that person.

honeybees.quick_def: A honeybee is a bee that makes honey.

nation.quick_def: A nation is an individual country considered together with its social and political structures.

commercial.quick_def: Commercial means involving or relating to the buying and selling of goods.

beekeepers.quick_def: A beekeeper is a person who owns and takes care of bees.

pull.quick_def: When you pull something, you hold it firmly and use force in order to move it towards you or away from its previous position.

stakes.quick_def: If something is at stake, it is being risked and might be lost or damaged if you are not successful.

spring.quick_def: Spring is the season between winter and summer when the weather becomes warmer and plants start to grow again.

migrating.quick_def: If people migrate, they move from one place to another, especially in order to find work or to live somewhere for a short time.

find.quick_def: If you find someone or something, you see them or learn where they are.

flowers.quick_def: A flower is the part of a plant which is often brightly coloured, grows at the end of a stem, and only survives for a short time.

bees.quick_def: A bee is an insect with a yellow-and-black striped body that makes a buzzing noise as it flies. Bees make honey, and can sting.

besides.quick_def: Besides something or beside something means in addition to it.

turning.quick_def: When you turn or when you turn part of your body, you move your body or part of your body so that it is facing in a different or opposite direction.

floral.quick_def: A floral fabric or design has flowers on it.

nectar.quick_def: Nectar is a sweet liquid produced by flowers, which bees and other insects collect.

honey.quick_def: Honey is a sweet, sticky, yellowish substance that is made by bees.

hardworking.quick_def: If you describe someone as hardworking, you mean that they work very hard.

insects.quick_def: An insect is a small animal that has six legs. Most insects have wings. Ants, flies, butterflies, and beetles are all insects.

pollinate.quick_def: To pollinate a plant or tree means to fertilize it with pollen. This is often done by insects.

crops.quick_def: Crops are plants such as wheat and potatoes that are grown in large quantities for food.

farmers.quick_def: A farmer is a person who owns or manages a farm.

fee.quick_def: A fee is a sum of money that you pay to be allowed to do something.

autumn.quick_def: Autumn is the season between summer and winter when the weather becomes cooler and the leaves fall off the trees.  [British]

approaches.quick_def: When you approach something, you get closer to it.

pack.quick_def: When you pack, or when you pack a bag, you put clothes and other things into it, because you are leaving a place or going on holiday.

hives.quick_def: A hive is a structure in which bees are kept, which is designed so that the beekeeper can collect the honey that they produce.

go.quick_def: When you go somewhere, you move or travel there.

south.quick_def: The south is the direction which is on your right when you are looking towards the direction where the sun rises.

scrambling.quick_def: the sport of racing motorcycles over rough ground

pollination.quick_def: To pollinate a plant or tree means to fertilize it with pollen. This is often done by insects.

contracts.quick_def: A contract is a legal agreement, usually between two companies or between an employer and employee, which involves doing work for a stated sum of money.

hot.quick_def: Something that is hot has a high temperature.

spots.quick_def: Spots are small, round, coloured areas on a surface.

california.quick_def: a US state on the Pacific Ocean, also called the Golden State. California has the largest population of all the states. Its largest city is Los Angeles and the capital is Sacramento. It is known for Hollywood, Disneyland, Silicon Valley and for its agricultural and wine products. Its history has included the Gold Rush of 1849 and the San Francisco earthquake (= a sudden, violent movement of the earth's surface) of 1906. Ronald Reagan was the governor of California from 1966 to 1974. Arnold Schwarzenegger served two terms as governor from 2003 to 2011.

fertile.quick_def: Land or soil that is fertile is able to support the growth of a large number of strong healthy plants.

central.quick_def: Something that is central is in the middle of a place or area.

valley.quick_def: A valley is a low stretch of land between hills, especially one that has a river flowing through it.

united.quick_def: If a group of people or things unite or if something unites them, they join together and act as a group.

states.quick_def: You can refer to countries as states, particularly when you are discussing politics.

migrate.quick_def: If people migrate, they move from one place to another, especially in order to find work or to live somewhere for a short time.

pays.quick_def: When you pay an amount of money to someone, you give it to them because you are buying something from them or because you owe it to them. When you pay something such as a bill or a debt, you pay the amount that you owe.

moving.quick_def: When you move something or when it moves, its position changes and it does not remain still.

summer.quick_def: Summer is the season between spring and autumn when the weather is usually warm or hot.

winter.quick_def: Winter is the season between autumn and spring when the weather is usually cold.

lets.quick_def: If you let something happen, you allow it to happen without doing anything to stop or prevent it.

longer.quick_def: Long means a great amount of time or for a great amount of time.

blooming.quick_def: A bloom is the flower on a plant.  [literary, technical]

season.quick_def: The seasons are the main periods into which a year can be divided and which each have their own typical weather conditions.

carry.quick_def: If you carry something, you take it with you, holding it so that it does not touch the ground.

need.quick_def: If you need something, or need to do something, you cannot successfully achieve what you want or live properly without it.

migratory.quick_def: A migratory bird, fish, or animal is one that migrates every year.

beekeeper.quick_def: A beekeeper is a person who owns and takes care of bees.

move.quick_def: When you move something or when it moves, its position changes and it does not remain still.

million.quick_def: A million or one million is the number 1,000,000.

flowering.quick_def: A flower is the part of a plant which is often brightly coloured, grows at the end of a stem, and only survives for a short time.

fields.quick_def: A field is an area of grass, for example in a park or on a farm. A field is also an area of land on which a crop is grown.

minnesota.quick_def: a state in the northern central US on the Canadian border. It has more than 10 000 lakes, and is also called the North Star State and the Gopher State. The largest city is Minneapolis and the capital city is St Paul. It became a state in 1858. Minnesota produces a large percentage of the country's iron ore, as well as farming products, machinery and computers. The Mayo Clinic, a famous medical centre, is in Rochester.

family.quick_def: A family is a group of people who are related to each other, especially parents and their children.

haul.quick_def: If you haul something which is heavy or difficult to move, you move it using a lot of effort.

rent.quick_def: To rend something means to tear it.  [literary]

almond.quick_def: Almonds are pale oval nuts. They are often used in cooking.

cherry.quick_def: Cherries are small, round fruit with red skins.

trees.quick_def: A tree is a tall plant that has a hard trunk, branches, and leaves.

beekeeping.quick_def: Beekeeping is the practice of owning and taking care of bees.

nothing.quick_def: Nothing means not a single thing, or not a single part of something.

egyptians.quick_def: Egyptians are people who come from Egypt.

clay.quick_def: Clay is a kind of earth that is soft when it is wet and hard when it is dry. Clay is shaped and baked to make things such as pots and bricks.

rafts.quick_def: A raft is a floating platform made from large pieces of wood or other materials tied together.

nile.quick_def: The Nile is a very long river in Africa.

follow.quick_def: If you follow someone who is going somewhere, you move along behind them because you want to go to the same place.

bloom.quick_def: A bloom is the flower on a plant.  [literary, technical]

flow.quick_def: If a liquid, gas, or electrical current flows somewhere, it moves there steadily and continuously.

toward.quick_def: If you move, look, or point toward something or someone, you move, look, or point in their direction.

cairo.quick_def: Cairo is the name of a big city which is the capital of Egypt.

experimented.quick_def: An experiment is a scientific test which is done in order to discover what happens to something in particular conditions.

barges.quick_def: A barge is a long, narrow boat with a flat bottom. Barges are used for carrying heavy loads, especially on canals.

mississippi.quick_def: a southern US state, also called the Magnolia State. Jackson is the largest city and also the capital. Mississippi became a state in 1817 and was one of the Confederate States. It has had conflicts between the races, especially in the 1960s. Its main product is cotton, but other crops include corn, soya beans, peanuts and rice. Tourists can visit the Vicksburg National Military Park and the historical buildings at Natchez.

waterways.quick_def: A waterway is a canal, river, or narrow channel of sea which ships or boats can sail along.

florida.quick_def: the most southern state in the US. It is internationally famous for its hot weather and white beaches. Florida's popular name is 'the Sunshine State'. It forms a long, flat area of land in the south-east between the Atlantic Ocean and the Gulf of Mexico. The largest city is Jacksonville and the capital city is Tallahassee. Florida was discovered in 1513 by Juan Ponce de León of Spain. Agriculture, manufacturing and tourism are all important to the state's economy. Its attractions include Disney World, Cape Canaveral, Miami Beach, the Everglades and the Florida Keys.

lighter.quick_def: Light is the brightness that lets you see things. Light comes from sources such as the sun, moon, lamps, and fire.

kept.quick_def: If someone keeps or is kept in a particular state, they remain in it.

falling.quick_def: If someone or something falls, they move quickly downwards onto or towards the ground, by accident or because of a natural force.

tried.quick_def: Tried is used in the expressions tried and tested, tried and trusted, and tried and true, which describe a product or method that has already been used and has been found to be successful.

railroad.quick_def: A railroad is a route between two places along which trains travel on steel rails.  [US]

horse-drawn.quick_def: If something is horse-drawn, it is pulled by a horse.

wagons.quick_def: A wagon is a strong vehicle with four wheels, usually pulled by horses or oxen and used for carrying heavy loads.

prove.quick_def: If something proves to be true or to have a particular quality, it becomes clear after a period of time that it is true or has that quality.

cars.quick_def: A car is a motor vehicle with room for a small number of passengers.

trucks.quick_def: A truck is a large vehicle that is used to transport goods by road.  [mainly US]

affordable.quick_def: If something is affordable, most people have enough money to buy it.

roads.quick_def: A road is a long piece of hard ground which is built between two places so that people can drive or ride easily from one place to the other.

begin.quick_def: To begin to do something means to start doing it.

californian.quick_def: A Californian is a person who comes from California.

february.quick_def: February is the second month of the year in the Western calendar.

beehives.quick_def: A beehive is a structure in which bees are kept, designed so that the beekeeper can collect the honey that they produce.

groves.quick_def: A grove is a group of trees that are close together.

acre.quick_def: An acre is an area of land measuring around 4840 square yards or 4047 square metres.

three-week.quick_def: If something lasts for a three-week period, it lasts for three weeks.

hire.quick_def: If you hire someone, you employ them or pay them to do a particular job for you.

bonanza.quick_def: You can refer to a sudden great increase in wealth, success, or luck as a bonanza.

too.quick_def: You use too after mentioning another person, thing, or aspect that a previous statement applies to or includes.

consider.quick_def: If you consider a person or thing to be something, you have the opinion that this is what they are.

bitter.quick_def: In a bitter argument or conflict, people argue very angrily or fight very fiercely.

eat.quick_def: When you eat something, you put it into your mouth, chew it, and swallow it.

keep.quick_def: If someone keeps or is kept in a particular state, they remain in it.

march.quick_def: When soldiers march somewhere, or when a commanding officer marches them somewhere, they walk there with very regular steps, as a group.

take.quick_def: You can use take followed by a noun to talk about an action or event, when it would also be possible to use the verb that is related to that noun. For example, you can say 'she took a shower' instead of 'she showered'.

nights.quick_def: The night is the part of each day when the sun has set and it is dark outside, especially the time when people are sleeping.

middle.quick_def: The middle of something is the part of it that is furthest from its edges, ends, or outside surface.

day.quick_def: A day is one of the seven twenty-four hour periods of time in a week.

homeless.quick_def: Homeless people have nowhere to live.

night.quick_def: The night is the part of each day when the sun has set and it is dark outside, especially the time when people are sleeping.

stacked.quick_def: A stack of things is a pile of them.

onto.quick_def: If something moves or is put onto an object or surface, it is then on that object or surface.

pallets.quick_def: A pallet is a narrow mattress filled with straw which is put on the floor for someone to sleep on.

back-to-back.quick_def: If things are back-to-back, they are placed with their backs touching each other.

lifted.quick_def: If you lift something, you move it to another position, especially upwards.

truck.quick_def: A truck is a large vehicle that is used to transport goods by road.  [mainly US]

wear.quick_def: When you wear something such as clothes, shoes, or jewellery, you have them on your body or on part of your body.

gloves.quick_def: Gloves are pieces of clothing which cover your hands and wrists and have individual sections for each finger. You wear gloves to keep your hands warm or dry or to protect them.

veil.quick_def: A veil is a piece of thin soft cloth that women sometimes wear over their heads and which can also cover their face.

opened.quick_def: If you open something such as a door, window, or lid, or if it opens, its position is changed so that it no longer covers a hole or gap.

remain.quick_def: If someone or something remains in a particular state or condition, they stay in that state or condition and do not change.

quiet.quick_def: Someone or something that is quiet makes only a small amount of noise.

just.quick_def: You use just to say that something happened a very short time ago, or is starting to happen at the present time. For example, if you say that someone has just arrived, you mean that they arrived a very short time ago.

case.quick_def: A particular case is a particular situation or incident, especially one that you are using as an individual example or instance of something.

still.quick_def: If a situation that used to exist still exists, it has continued and exists now.

lively.quick_def: You can describe someone as lively when they behave in an enthusiastic and cheerful way.

pacified.quick_def: If you pacify someone who is angry, upset, or not pleased, you succeed in making them calm or pleased.

few.quick_def: You use a few to indicate that you are talking about a small number of people or things. You can also say a very few.

puffs.quick_def: If someone puffs at a cigarette, cigar, or pipe, they smoke it.

smoke.quick_def: Smoke consists of gas and small bits of solid material that are sent into the air when something burns.

hive.quick_def: A hive is a structure in which bees are kept, which is designed so that the beekeeper can collect the honey that they produce.

narrow.quick_def: Something that is narrow measures a very small distance from one side to the other, especially compared to its length or height.

entrance.quick_def: The entrance to a place is the way into it, for example a door or gate.

location.quick_def: A location is the place where something happens or is situated.

pay.quick_def: When you pay an amount of money to someone, you give it to them because you are buying something from them or because you owe it to them. When you pay something such as a bill or a debt, you pay the amount that you owe.

farmer.quick_def: A farmer is a person who owns or manages a farm.

allow.quick_def: If someone is allowed to do something, it is all right for them to do it and they will not get into trouble.

feed.quick_def: If you feed a person or animal, you give them food to eat and sometimes actually put it in their mouths.

orange.quick_def: Something that is orange is of a colour between red and yellow.

here.quick_def: You use here when you are referring to the place where you are.

fragrant.quick_def: Something that is fragrant has a pleasant, sweet smell.
