sweet.quick_def: Sweet food and drink contains a lot of sugar.

sold.quick_def: If you sell something that you own, you let someone have it in return for money.

encourage.quick_def: If you encourage someone, you give them confidence, for example by letting them know that what they are doing is good and telling them that they should continue to do it.

much.quick_def: You use much to indicate the great intensity, extent, or degree of something such as an action, feeling, or change. Much is usually used with 'so', 'too', and 'very', and in negative clauses with this meaning.

period.quick_def: A period is a length of time.

open.quick_def: If you open something such as a door, window, or lid, or if it opens, its position is changed so that it no longer covers a hole or gap.

stack.quick_def: A stack of things is a pile of them.

extra.quick_def: You use extra to describe an amount, person, or thing that is added to others of the same kind, or that can be added to others of the same kind.

boxes.quick_def: A box is a square or rectangular container with hard or stiff sides. Boxes often have lids.

supers.quick_def: Supers are extra boxes that beekeepers put on top of beehives to let bees make more honey.

top.quick_def: The top of something is its highest point or part.

temporary.quick_def: Something that is temporary lasts for only a limited time.

extensions.quick_def: An extension is a new room or building which is added to an existing building or group of buildings.

contain.quick_def: If something such as a box, bag, room, or place contains things, those things are inside it.

empty.quick_def: An empty place, vehicle, or container is one that has no people or things in it.

comb.quick_def: A comb is a flat piece of plastic or metal with narrow pointed teeth along one side, which you use to tidy your hair.

fill.quick_def: If you fill a container or area, or if it fills, an amount of something enters it that is enough to make it full.

brood.quick_def: A brood is a group of baby birds that were born at the same time to the same mother.

chamber.quick_def: A chamber is a large room, especially one that is used for formal meetings.

below.quick_def: If something is below something else, it is in a lower position.

stash.quick_def: If you stash something valuable in a secret place, you store it there to keep it safe.  [informal]

queen.quick_def: A queen is a woman who rules a country as its monarch.

crawling.quick_def: When you crawl, you move forward on your hands and knees.

laying.quick_def: If you lay something somewhere, you put it there in a careful, gentle, or neat way.

eggs.quick_def: An egg is an oval object that is produced by a female bird and which contains a baby bird. Other animals such as reptiles and fish also lay eggs.

screen.quick_def: A screen is a flat vertical surface on which pictures or words are shown. Television sets and computers have screens, and films are shown on a screen in cinemas.

inserted.quick_def: If you insert an object into something, you put the object inside it.

weeks.quick_def: A week is a period of seven days. Some people consider that a week starts on Monday and ends on Sunday.

gathered.quick_def: If people gather somewhere or if someone gathers people somewhere, they come together in a group.

foul.quick_def: If you describe something as foul, you mean it is dirty and smells or tastes unpleasant.

smelling.quick_def: The smell of something is a quality it has which you become aware of when you breathe in through your nose.

irritate.quick_def: If something irritates you, it keeps annoying you.

drive.quick_def: When you drive somewhere, you operate a car or other vehicle and control its movement and direction.

bottom.quick_def: The bottom of something is the lowest or deepest part of it.

leaving.quick_def: If you leave a place or person, you go away from that place or person.

honey-filled.quick_def: If something is honey-filled, it is full of honey.

bee.quick_def: A bee is an insect with a yellow-and-black striped body that makes a buzzing noise as it flies. Bees make honey, and can sting.

pulled.quick_def: When you pull something, you hold it firmly and use force in order to move it towards you or away from its previous position.

heavy.quick_def: Something that is heavy weighs a lot.

weigh.quick_def: If someone or something weighs a particular amount, this amount is how heavy they are.

taken.quick_def: You can use take followed by a noun to talk about an action or event, when it would also be possible to use the verb that is related to that noun. For example, you can say 'she took a shower' instead of 'she showered'.

warehouse.quick_def: A warehouse is a large building where raw materials or manufactured goods are stored until they are exported to other countries or distributed to shops to be sold.

extracting.quick_def: To extract a substance means to obtain it from something else, for example by using industrial or chemical processes.

room.quick_def: A room is one of the separate sections or parts of the inside of a building. Rooms have their own walls, ceilings, floors, and doors, and are usually used for particular activities. You can refer to all the people who are in a room as the room.

lowered.quick_def: You can use lower to refer to the bottom one of a pair of things.

uncapper.quick_def: An uncapper is a thing that can take off the covers.

rotating.quick_def: When something rotates or when you rotate it, it turns with a circular movement.

blades.quick_def: The blade of a knife, axe, or saw is the flat sharp part that is used for cutting.

shave.quick_def: When you shave, you remove the hair from your face using a razor or shaver so that your face is smooth.

wax.quick_def: Wax is a solid, slightly shiny substance made of fat or oil which is used to make candles and polish. It melts when it is heated.

covers.quick_def: If you cover something, you place something else over it in order to protect it, hide it, or close it.

cell.quick_def: A cell is the smallest part of an animal or plant that is able to function independently. Every animal or plant is made up of millions of cells.

uncapped.quick_def: If something is uncapped, it doesn't have a cap on it.

carousel.quick_def: At an airport, a carousel is a moving surface from which passengers can collect their luggage.

sits.quick_def: If you are sitting somewhere, for example in a chair, your bottom is resting on the chair and the upper part of your body is upright.

stainless.quick_def: If something is stainless, it does not get stained or rusted easily.

drum.quick_def: A drum is a musical instrument consisting of a skin stretched tightly over a round frame. You play a drum by beating it with sticks or with your hands.

switch.quick_def: A switch is a small control for an electrical device which you use to turn the device on or off.

flipped.quick_def: If you flip a device on or off, or if you flip a switch, you turn it on or off by pressing the switch quickly.

whirl.quick_def: If something or someone whirls around or if you whirl them around, they move around or turn around very quickly.

revolutions.quick_def: A revolution is a successful attempt by a large group of people to change the political system of their country by force.

minute.quick_def: A minute is one of the sixty parts that an hour is divided into. People often say 'a minute' or 'minutes' when they mean a short length of time.

centrifugal.quick_def: moving or tending to move away from a centre

force.quick_def: If someone forces you to do something, they make you do it even though you do not want to, for example by threatening you.

throws.quick_def: When you throw an object that you are holding, you move your hand or arm quickly and let go of the object, so that it moves through the air.

combs.quick_def: A comb is a flat piece of plastic or metal with narrow pointed teeth along one side, which you use to tidy your hair.

poured.quick_def: If you pour a liquid or other substance, you make it flow steadily out of a container by holding the container at an angle.

barrels.quick_def: A barrel is a large, round container for liquids or food.

shipment.quick_def: A shipment is an amount of a particular kind of cargo that is sent to another country on a ship, train, aeroplane, or other vehicle.

quarter.quick_def: A quarter is one of four equal parts of something.

weakened.quick_def: If you weaken something or if it weakens, it becomes less strong or less powerful.

mites.quick_def: A mite means to a small extent or degree. It is sometimes used to make a statement less extreme.

ageing.quick_def: Your age is the number of years that you have lived.

dead.quick_def: A person, animal, or plant that is dead is no longer living.

replaced.quick_def: If one thing or person replaces another, the first is used or acts instead of the second.

create.quick_def: To create something means to cause it to happen or exist.

colonies.quick_def: A colony is a country which is controlled by a more powerful country.

healthy.quick_def: Someone who is healthy is well and is not suffering from any illness.

double.quick_def: You use double to indicate that something includes or is made of two things of the same kind.

teeming.quick_def: If you say that a place is teeming with people or animals, you mean that it is crowded and the people and animals are moving around a lot.

separated.quick_def: If one thing is separate from another, there is a barrier, space, or division between them, so that they are clearly two things.

hold.quick_def: When you hold something, you carry or support it, using your hands or your arms.

young.quick_def: A young person, animal, or plant has not lived or existed for very long and is not yet mature.

already.quick_def: You use already to show that something has happened, or that something had happened before the moment you are referring to. Speakers of British English use already with a verb in a perfect tense, putting it after 'have', 'has', or 'had', or at the end of a clause. Some speakers of American English use already with the simple past tense of the verb instead of a perfect tense.

mated.quick_def: You can refer to someone's friends as their mates.  [British, informal]

queens.quick_def: A queen is a woman who rules a country as its monarch.

filling.quick_def: If you fill a container or area, or if it fills, an amount of something enters it that is enough to make it full.

worker.quick_def: A particular kind of worker does the kind of work mentioned.

tourism.quick_def: Tourism is the business of providing services for people on holiday, for example hotels, restaurants, and trips.

holidaymaking.quick_def: Holidaymaking is the activity of taking a holiday. It means going to a place to relax and have fun during a vacation.

travel.quick_def: If you travel, you go from one place to another, often to a place that is far away.

days.quick_def: A day is one of the seven twenty-four hour periods of time in a week.

significant.quick_def: A significant amount or effect is large enough to be important or affect a situation to a noticeable degree.

commentators.quick_def: A commentator is a broadcaster who gives a radio or television commentary on an event.

face.quick_def: Your face is the front part of your head from your chin to the top of your forehead, where your mouth, eyes, nose, and other features are.

trivial.quick_def: If you describe something as trivial, you think that it is unimportant and not serious.

considerable.quick_def: Considerable means great in amount or degree.  [formal]

explaining.quick_def: If you explain something, you give details about it or describe it so that it can be understood.

weightier.quick_def: If you describe something such as an issue or a decision as weighty, you mean that it is serious or important.  [formal]

topics.quick_def: A topic is a particular subject that you discuss or write about.

politics.quick_def: Politics are the actions or activities concerned with achieving and using power in a country or society. The verb that follows politics may be either singular or plural.

thought.quick_def: If you think that something is the case, you have the opinion that it is the case.

accounting.quick_def: If you have an account with a bank or a similar organization, you have an arrangement to leave your money there and take some out when you need it.

interesting.quick_def: If you have an interest in something, you want to learn or hear more about it.

parallels.quick_def: If something has a parallel, it is similar to something else, but exists or happens in a different place or at a different time. If it has no parallel or is without parallel, it is not similar to anything else.

study.quick_def: If you study, you spend time learning about a particular subject or subjects.

deviance.quick_def: a difference from what most people consider to be normal or acceptable

involves.quick_def: If a situation or activity involves something, that thing is a necessary part or consequence of it.

investigation.quick_def: If someone, especially an official, investigates an event, situation, or claim, they try to find out what happened or what is the truth.

bizarre.quick_def: Something that is bizarre is very odd and strange.

idiosyncratic.quick_def: If you describe someone's actions or characteristics as idiosyncratic, you mean that they are rather unusual.

practices.quick_def: You can refer to something that people do regularly as a practice.

happen.quick_def: Something that happens occurs or is done without being planned.

deviant.quick_def: Deviant behaviour or thinking is different from what people normally consider to be acceptable.

assumption.quick_def: If you make an assumption that something is true or will happen, you accept that it is true or will happen, often without any real proof.

reveal.quick_def: To reveal something means to make people aware of it.

aspects.quick_def: An aspect of something is one of the parts of its character or nature.

similar.quick_def: If one thing is similar to another, or if two things are similar, they have features that are the same.

analysis.quick_def: Analysis is the process of considering something carefully or using statistical methods in order to understand it or explain it.

applied.quick_def: An applied subject of study has a practical use, rather than being concerned only with theory.

leisure.quick_def: Leisure is the time when you are not working and you can relax and do things that you enjoy.

activity.quick_def: Activity is a situation in which a lot of things are happening or being done.

presupposes.quick_def: If one thing presupposes another, the first thing cannot be true or exist unless the second thing is true or exists.

opposite.quick_def: If one thing is opposite another, it is on the other side of a space from it.

namely.quick_def: You use namely to introduce detailed information about the subject you are discussing, or a particular aspect of it.

regulated.quick_def: To regulate an activity or process means to control it, especially by means of rules.

organised.quick_def: If you organize an event or activity, you make sure that the necessary arrangements are made.

manifestation.quick_def: A manifestation of something is one of the different ways in which it can appear.  [formal]

separate.quick_def: If one thing is separate from another, there is a barrier, space, or division between them, so that they are clearly two things.

spheres.quick_def: A sphere is an object that is completely round in shape like a ball.

practice.quick_def: You can refer to something that people do regularly as a practice.

acting.quick_def: When you act, you do something for a particular purpose.

defining.quick_def: If you define something, you show, describe, or state clearly what it is and what its limits are, or what it is like.

characteristics.quick_def: The characteristics of a person or thing are the qualities or features that belong to them and make them recognizable.

concept.quick_def: A concept is an idea or abstract principle.

regularised.quick_def: If someone regularizes a situation or system, they make it officially acceptable or put it under a system of rules.  [formal]

periods.quick_def: A period is a length of time.

relationships.quick_def: The relationship between two people or groups is the way in which they feel and behave towards each other.

stay.quick_def: If you stay where you are, you continue to be there and do not leave.

destinations.quick_def: The destination of someone or something is the place to which they are going or being sent.

journey.quick_def: When you make a journey, you travel from one place to another.

definition.quick_def: A definition is a statement giving the meaning of a word or expression, especially in a dictionary.

outside.quick_def: The outside of something is the part which surrounds or encloses the rest of it.

residence.quick_def: A residence is a house where people live.  [formal]

short.quick_def: If something is short or lasts for a short time, it does not last very long.

term.quick_def: If you talk about something in terms of something or in particular terms, you are specifying which aspect of it you are discussing or from what point of view you are considering it.

clear.quick_def: Something that is clear is easy to understand, see, or hear.

intention.quick_def: An intention is an idea or plan of what you are going to do.

return.quick_def: When you return to a place, you go back there after you have been away.

home.quick_def: Someone's home is the house or flat where they live.

substantial.quick_def: Substantial means large in amount or degree.  [formal]

proportion.quick_def: A proportion of a group or an amount is a part of it.  [formal]

engages.quick_def: If you engage in an activity, you do it or are actively involved with it.  [formal]

socialised.quick_def: If you socialize, you meet other people socially, for example at parties.

provision.quick_def: The provision of something is the act of giving it or making it available to people who need or want it.

cope.quick_def: If you cope with a problem or task, you deal with it successfully.

mass.quick_def: A mass of things is a large number of them grouped together.

character.quick_def: The character of a person or place consists of all the qualities they have that make them distinct from other people or places.

gazes.quick_def: If you gaze at someone or something, you look steadily at them for a long time, for example because you find them attractive or interesting, or because you are thinking about something else.

tourists.quick_def: A tourist is a person who is visiting a place for pleasure and interest, especially when they are on holiday.

opposed.quick_def: If you oppose someone or oppose their plans or ideas, you disagree with what they want to do and try to prevent them from doing it.

chosen.quick_def: If you choose someone or something from several people or things that are available, you decide which person or thing you want to have.

visited.quick_def: If you visit someone, you go to see them and spend time with them.

gazed.quick_def: If you gaze at someone or something, you look steadily at them for a long time, for example because you find them attractive or interesting, or because you are thinking about something else.

anticipation.quick_def: Anticipation is a feeling of excitement about something pleasant or exciting that you know is going to happen.

especially.quick_def: You use especially to emphasize that what you are saying applies more to one person, thing, or area than to any others.  [emphasis]

daydreaming.quick_def: If you daydream, you think about pleasant things for a period of time, usually about things that you would like to happen.

fantasy.quick_def: A fantasy is a pleasant situation or event that you think about and that you want to happen, especially one that is unlikely to happen.

intense.quick_def: Intense is used to describe something that is very great or extreme in strength or degree.

pleasures.quick_def: If something gives you pleasure, you get a feeling of happiness, satisfaction, or enjoyment from it.

either.quick_def: You use either in front of the first of two or more alternatives, when you are stating the only possibilities or choices that there are. The last of the other alternatives is introduced by 'or'.

involving.quick_def: If a situation or activity involves something, that thing is a necessary part or consequence of it.

senses.quick_def: Your senses are the physical abilities of sight, smell, hearing, touch, and taste.

customarily.quick_def: according to what is usual in a particular place or situation

encountered.quick_def: If you encounter problems or difficulties, you experience them.

sustained.quick_def: If you sustain something, you continue it or maintain it for a period of time.

variety.quick_def: If something has variety, it consists of things which are different from each other.

non-tourist.quick_def: A non-tourist is a person who is not traveling for pleasure or visiting a place as a tourist.

films.quick_def: A film consists of moving pictures that have been recorded so that they can be shown at the cinema or on television. A film tells a story, or shows a real situation.  [mainly British]

tv.quick_def: TV means the same as television.

magazines.quick_def: A magazine is a publication with a paper cover which is issued regularly, usually every week or every month, and which contains articles, stories, photographs, and advertisements.

records.quick_def: If you keep a record of something, you keep a written account or photographs of it so that it can be referred to later.

videos.quick_def: A video is a film or television programme recorded digitally (or in the past on tape) for people to watch on a television set.

construct.quick_def: If you construct something such as a building, road, or machine, you build it or make it.

reinforce.quick_def: If something reinforces a feeling, situation, or process, it makes it stronger or more intense.

visit.quick_def: If you visit someone, you go to see them and spend time with them.

features.quick_def: A feature of something is an interesting or important part or characteristic of it.

landscape.quick_def: The landscape is everything you can see when you look across an area of land, including hills, rivers, buildings, trees, and plants.

everyday.quick_def: You use everyday to describe something which happens or is used every day, or forms a regular and basic part of your life, so it is not especially interesting or unusual.

experience.quick_def: Experience is knowledge or skill in a particular job or activity, which you have gained because you have done that job or activity for a long time.

sense.quick_def: Your senses are the physical abilities of sight, smell, hearing, touch, and taste.

ordinary.quick_def: Ordinary people or things are normal and not special or different in any way.

viewing.quick_def: Your views on something are the beliefs or opinions that you have about it, for example whether you think it is good, bad, right, or wrong.

sights.quick_def: Someone's sight is their ability to see.

patterning.quick_def: Patterning is the forming of fixed ways of behaving or of doing things by constantly repeating something or copying other people.  [formal]

greater.quick_def: You use great to describe something that is very large. Great is more formal than big.

sensitivity.quick_def: If you are sensitive to other people's needs, problems, or feelings, you show understanding and awareness of them.  [approval]

visual.quick_def: Visual means relating to sight, or to things that you can see.

elements.quick_def: The different elements of something are the different parts it contains.

normally.quick_def: If you say that something normally happens or that you normally do a particular thing, you mean that it is what usually happens or what you usually do.

linger.quick_def: When something such as an idea, feeling, or illness lingers, it continues to exist for a long time, often much longer than expected.

vision.quick_def: Your vision of a future situation or society is what you imagine or hope it would be like, if things were very different from the way they are now.

objectified.quick_def: When someone is objectified, they are treated as an object, not as a person with feelings and thoughts.

captured.quick_def: If you capture someone or something, you catch them, especially in a war.

photographs.quick_def: A photograph is a picture made using a camera.

postcards.quick_def: A postcard is a piece of thin card, often with a picture on one side, which you can write on and send to people without using an envelope.

enable.quick_def: If someone or something enables you to do a particular thing, they give you the opportunity to do it.

memory.quick_def: Your memory is your ability to remember things.

endlessly.quick_def: If you say that something is endless, you mean that it is very large or lasts for a very long time, and it seems as if it will never stop.

reproduced.quick_def: If you try to reproduce something, you try to copy it.

recaptured.quick_def: When soldiers recapture an area of land or a place, they gain control of it again from an opposing army who had taken it from them.

dissertations.quick_def: A dissertation is a long formal piece of writing on a particular subject, especially for a university degree.

boorstins.quick_def: Boorstins is a name. A name is what we call a person.

pseudo.quick_def: If something is pseudo, it is false or not real, but it seems to be real.

event.quick_def: An event is something that happens, especially when it is unusual or important. You can use events to describe all the things that are happening in a particular situation.

contemporary.quick_def: Contemporary things are modern and relate to the present time.

directly.quick_def: Direct means moving towards a place or object, without changing direction and without stopping, for example in a journey.

thrive.quick_def: If someone or something thrives, they do well and are successful, healthy, or strong.

events.quick_def: An event is something that happens, especially when it is unusual or important. You can use events to describe all the things that are happening in a particular situation.

host.quick_def: The host at a party is the person who has invited the guests and provides the food, drink, or entertainment.

travels.quick_def: If you travel, you go from one place to another, often to a place that is far away.

guided.quick_def: A guide is a book that gives you information or instructions to help you do or understand something.

groups.quick_def: A group of people or things is a number of people or things which are together in one place at one time.

finds.quick_def: If you find someone or something, you see them or learn where they are.

pleasure.quick_def: If something gives you pleasure, you get a feeling of happiness, satisfaction, or enjoyment from it.

inauthentic.quick_def: Something that is inauthentic is false or copied, often in a way that does not follow tradition.

contrived.quick_def: If you contrive an event or situation, you succeed in making it happen, often by tricking someone.  [formal]

attractions.quick_def: Attraction is a feeling of liking someone, and often of being sexually interested in them.

gullibly.quick_def: If you do something gullibly, you do it easily believing what others say without thinking carefully.

enjoying.quick_def: If you enjoy something, you find pleasure and satisfaction in doing it or experiencing it.

disregarding.quick_def: If you disregard something, you ignore it or do not take account of it.

real.quick_def: Something that is real actually exists and is not imagined, invented, or theoretical.

images.quick_def: If you have an image of something or someone, you have a picture or idea of them in your mind.

generated.quick_def: To generate something means to cause it to begin and develop.

come.quick_def: When a person or thing comes to a particular place, especially to a place where you are, they move there.

constitute.quick_def: If something constitutes a particular thing, it can be regarded as being that thing.

self-perpetuating.quick_def: If something is self-perpetuating, it can keep going or existing by itself without needing much outside help.

illusions.quick_def: An illusion is a false idea or belief.

provide.quick_def: If you provide something that someone needs or wants, or if you provide them with it, you give it to them or make it available to them.

selecting.quick_def: If you select something, you choose it from a number of things of the same kind.

evaluating.quick_def: If you evaluate something or someone, you consider them in order to make a judgment about them, for example about how good or bad they are.

visits.quick_def: If you visit someone, you go to see them and spend time with them.

boorstin.quick_def: Boorstin is a name of a person.

bubble.quick_def: Bubbles are small balls of air or gas in a liquid.

familiar.quick_def: If someone or something is familiar to you, you recognize them or know them well.

hotel.quick_def: A hotel is a building where people stay, for example on holiday, paying for their rooms and meals.

insulates.quick_def: If a person or group is insulated from the rest of society or from outside influences, they are protected from them.

strangeness.quick_def: Something that is strange is unusual or unexpected, and makes you feel slightly nervous or afraid.

service.quick_def: A service is something that the public needs, such as transport, communications facilities, hospitals, or energy supplies, which is provided in a planned and organized way by the government or an official body.

burgeoning.quick_def: If something burgeons, it grows or develops rapidly.  [literary]

array.quick_def: An array of different things or people is a large number or wide range of them.

professionals.quick_def: Professional means relating to a person's work, especially work that requires special training.

attempt.quick_def: If you attempt to do something, especially something difficult, you try to do it.

reproduce.quick_def: If you try to reproduce something, you try to copy it.

ever-new.quick_def: If something is ever-new, it always seems new and fresh.

objects.quick_def: An object is anything that has a fixed shape or form, that you can touch or see, and that is not alive.

look.quick_def: If you look in a particular direction, you direct your eyes in that direction, especially so that you can see what is there or see what something is like.

located.quick_def: If you locate something or someone, you find out where they are.  [formal]

complex.quick_def: Something that is complex has many different parts, and is therefore often difficult to understand.

hierarchy.quick_def: A hierarchy is a system of organizing people into different ranks or levels of importance, for example in society or in a company.

depends.quick_def: If you say that one thing depends on another, you mean that the first thing will be affected or determined by the second.

interplay.quick_def: The interplay between two or more things or people is the way that they have an effect on each other or react to each other.

competition.quick_def: Competition is a situation in which two or more people or groups are trying to get something which not everyone can have.

interests.quick_def: If you have an interest in something, you want to learn or hear more about it.

class.quick_def: A class is a group of pupils or students who are taught together.

gender.quick_def: Gender is the state of being male or female in relation to the social and cultural roles that are considered appropriate for men and women.

generational.quick_def: Generational means relating to a particular generation, or to the relationship between particular generations.

distinctions.quick_def: A distinction between similar things is a difference.

taste.quick_def: Taste is one of the five senses that people have. When you have food or drink in your mouth, your sense of taste makes it possible for you to recognize what it is.

visitors.quick_def: A visitor is someone who is visiting a person or place.

possessing.quick_def: If you possess something, you have it or own it.

car.quick_def: A car is a motor vehicle with room for a small number of passengers.

nice.quick_def: If you say that something is nice, you mean that you find it attractive, pleasant, or enjoyable.

house.quick_def: A house is a building in which people live, usually the people belonging to one family.

marker.quick_def: A marker is an object which is used to show the position of something, or is used to help someone remember something.

status.quick_def: Your status is your social or professional position.

health.quick_def: A person's health is the condition of their body and the extent to which it is free from illness or is able to resist illness.

role.quick_def: If you have a role in a situation or in society, you have a particular position and function in it.

professional.quick_def: Professional means relating to a person's work, especially work that requires special training.

therefore.quick_def: You use therefore to introduce a logical result or conclusion.

cater.quick_def: In British English, to cater for a group of people means to provide all the things that they need or want. In American English, you say you cater to a person or group of people.

tastes.quick_def: Taste is one of the five senses that people have. When you have food or drink in your mouth, your sense of taste makes it possible for you to recognize what it is.

accordance.quick_def: If something is done in accordance with a particular rule or system, it is done in the way that the rule or system says that it should be done.

expectations.quick_def: Your expectations are your strong hopes or beliefs that something will happen or that you will get something that you want.

compiling.quick_def: When you compile something such as a report, book, or programme, you produce it by collecting and putting together many pieces of information.

dictionaries.quick_def: A dictionary is a book in which the words and phrases of a language are listed alphabetically, together with their meanings or their translations in another language.

historically.quick_def: Historical people, situations, or things existed in the past and are considered to be a part of history.

provenance.quick_def: The provenance of something is the place that it comes from or that it originally came from.  [formal]

studious.quick_def: Someone who is studious spends a lot of time reading and studying books.

professorial.quick_def: If you describe someone as professorial, you mean that they look or behave like a professor.

types.quick_def: A type of something is a group of those things that have particular features in common.

bespectacled.quick_def: Someone who is bespectacled is wearing glasses.  [written]

love.quick_def: If you love someone, you feel romantically or sexually attracted to them, and they are very important to you.

pore.quick_def: Your pores are the tiny holes in your skin.

weighty.quick_def: If you describe something such as an issue or a decision as weighty, you mean that it is serious or important.  [formal]

tomes.quick_def: A tome is a very large, heavy book.  [formal]

pronouncements.quick_def: Pronouncements are public or official statements on an important subject.

finer.quick_def: You use fine to describe something that you admire and think is very good.

nuances.quick_def: A nuance is a small difference in sound, feeling, appearance, or meaning.

meaning.quick_def: If you want to know what a word, code, signal, or gesture means, you want to know what it refers to or what its message is.

crosswords.quick_def: A crossword or crossword puzzle is a word game in which you work out the answers and write them in the white squares of a pattern of small black and white squares.

definitely.quick_def: You use definitely to emphasize that something is the case, or to emphasize the strength of your intention or opinion.  [emphasis]

lot.quick_def: A lot of something or lots of it is a large amount of it. A lot of people or things, or lots of them, is a large number of them.

words.quick_def: A word is a single unit of language that can be represented in writing or speech. In English, a word has a space on either side of it when it is written.

image.quick_def: If you have an image of something or someone, you have a picture or idea of them in your mind.

dry.quick_def: If something is dry, there is no water or moisture on it or in it.

dusty.quick_def: If places, roads, or other things outside are dusty, they are covered with tiny bits of earth or sand, usually because it has not rained for a long time.

revolutionising.quick_def: When something is revolutionising a thing, it is making big and important changes to the way it is done.

content.quick_def: The contents of a container such as a bottle, box, or room are the things that are inside it.

dictionary.quick_def: A dictionary is a book in which the words and phrases of a language are listed alphabetically, together with their meanings or their translations in another language.

publishers.quick_def: A publisher is a person or a company that publishes books, newspapers, or magazines.

spoken.quick_def: When you speak, you use your voice in order to say something.

gives.quick_def: You can use give with nouns that refer to physical actions. The whole expression refers to the performing of the action. For example, She gave a smile means almost the same as 'She smiled'.

lexicographers.quick_def: Lexicography is the activity or profession of writing dictionaries.

write.quick_def: When you write something on a surface, you use something such as a pen or pencil to produce words, letters, or numbers on the surface.

access.quick_def: If you have access to a building or other place, you are able or allowed to go into it.

vibrant.quick_def: Someone or something that is vibrant is full of life, energy, and enthusiasm.

up-to-date.quick_def: If something is up-to-date, it has the latest information or is the newest version.

vernacular.quick_def: The vernacular is the language or dialect that is most widely spoken by ordinary people in a region or country.

project.quick_def: A project is a task that requires a lot of time and effort.

volunteers.quick_def: A volunteer is someone who does work without being paid for it, because they want to do it.

agreed.quick_def: If people agree with each other about something, they have the same opinion about it or say that they have the same opinion.

discreetly.quick_def: If you are discreet, you are polite and careful in what you do or say, because you want to avoid embarrassing or offending someone.

tie.quick_def: If you tie two things together or tie them, you fasten them together with a knot.

walkman.quick_def: A Walkman is a small cassette player with light headphones which people carry around so that they can listen to music, for example while they are travelling.  [trademark]

recorder.quick_def: A recorder is a wooden or plastic musical instrument in the shape of a pipe. You play the recorder by blowing into the top of it and covering and uncovering the holes with your fingers.

waist.quick_def: Your waist is the middle part of your body where it narrows slightly above your hips.

leave.quick_def: If you leave a place or person, you go away from that place or person.

running.quick_def: When you run, you move more quickly than when you walk, for example because you are in a hurry to get somewhere, or for exercise.

conversation.quick_def: If you have a conversation with someone, you talk with them, usually in an informal situation.

recorded.quick_def: If you keep a record of something, you keep a written account or photographs of it so that it can be referred to later.

collected.quick_def: If you collect a number of things, you bring them together from several places or from several people.

length.quick_def: The length of something is the amount that it measures from one end to the other along the longest side.

tapes.quick_def: Tape is a narrow plastic strip covered with a magnetic substance. It is used to record sounds, pictures, and computer information.

depth.quick_def: The depth of something such as a river or hole is the distance downwards from its top surface, or between its upper and lower surfaces.

atlantic.quick_def: The Atlantic is an ocean between America and Europe and Africa.

teams.quick_def: A team is a group of people who play a particular sport or game together against other similar groups of people.

audio.quick_def: Audio equipment is used for recording and reproducing sound.

typists.quick_def: A typist is someone who works in an office typing letters and other documents.

transcribed.quick_def: If you transcribe a speech or text, you write it out in a different form from the one in which it exists, for example by writing it out in full from notes or from a tape recording.

computerised.quick_def: To computerize a system, process, or type of work means to arrange for a lot of the work to be done by computer.

database.quick_def: A database is a collection of data that is stored in a computer and that can easily be used and added to.

written.quick_def: When you write something on a surface, you use something such as a pen or pencil to produce words, letters, or numbers on the surface.

corpus.quick_def: A corpus is a large collection of written or spoken texts that is used for language research.  [technical]

activator.quick_def: An activator is something that makes a process or activity start or work faster.

described.quick_def: If you describe a person, object, event, or situation, you say what they are like or what happened.

lexicographer.quick_def: a person who writes and edits dictionaries

quirk.quick_def: A quirk is something unusual or interesting that happens by chance.

waiting.quick_def: When you wait for something or someone, you spend some time doing very little, because you cannot act until that thing happens or that person arrives.

shows.quick_def: If something shows that a state of affairs exists, it gives information that proves it or makes it clear to people.

advanced.quick_def: To advance means to move forward, often in order to attack someone.

foreign.quick_def: Something or someone that is foreign comes from or relates to a country that is not your own.

learners.quick_def: A learner is someone who is learning about a particular subject or how to do something.

key.quick_def: A key is a specially shaped piece of metal that you place in a lock and turn in order to open or lock a door, or to start or stop the engine of a vehicle.

followed.quick_def: If you follow someone who is going somewhere, you move along behind them because you want to go to the same place.

related.quick_def: If something relates to a particular subject, it concerns that subject.

phrases.quick_def: A phrase is a short group of words that people often use as a way of saying something. The meaning of a phrase is often not obvious from the meaning of the individual words in it.

wolf.quick_def: A wolf is a wild animal that looks like a large dog.

picky.quick_def: Someone who is picky is difficult to please and only likes a small range of things.  [informal, disapproval]

eater.quick_def: You use eater to refer to someone who eats in a particular way or who eats particular kinds of food.

allowing.quick_def: If someone is allowed to do something, it is all right for them to do it and they will not get into trouble.

appropriate.quick_def: Something that is appropriate is suitable or acceptable for a particular situation.

phrase.quick_def: A phrase is a short group of words that people often use as a way of saying something. The meaning of a phrase is often not obvious from the meaning of the individual words in it.

kind.quick_def: If you talk about a particular kind of thing, you are talking about one of the types or sorts of that thing.

impossible.quick_def: Something that is impossible cannot be done or cannot happen.

computers.quick_def: A computer is an electronic machine that can store and deal with large amounts of information.

summers.quick_def: Summer is the season between spring and autumn when the weather is usually warm or hot.

director.quick_def: The director of a play, film, or television programme is the person who decides how it will appear on stage or screen, and who tells the actors and technical staff what to do.

transformed.quick_def: To transform something into something else means to change or convert it into that thing.

intuitively.quick_def: If you have an intuitive idea or feeling about something, you feel that it is true although you have no evidence or proof of it.

frequent.quick_def: If something is frequent, it happens often.

verb.quick_def: A verb is a word such as ' sing', ' feel', or ' die' which is used with a subject to say what someone or something does or what happens to them, or to give information about them.

swimming.quick_def: When you swim, you move through water by making movements with your arms and legs.

preposition.quick_def: A preposition is a word such as 'by', 'for', 'into', or 'with' which usually has a noun group as its object.

walked.quick_def: When you walk, you move forward by putting one foot in front of the other in a regular way.

duck.quick_def: A duck is a very common water bird with short legs, a short neck, and a large flat beak.

mean.quick_def: If you want to know what a word, code, signal, or gesture means, you want to know what it refers to or what its message is.

ends.quick_def: The end of something such as a period of time, an event, a book, or a film is the last part of it or the final point in it.

sifting.quick_def: If you sift a powder such as flour or sand, you put it through a sieve in order to remove large pieces or lumps.

vital.quick_def: If you say that something is vital, you mean that it is necessary or very important.

search.quick_def: If you search for something or someone, you look carefully for them.

frequently.quick_def: If something is frequent, it happens often.

guessed.quick_def: If you guess something, you give an answer or provide an opinion which may not be true because you do not have definite knowledge about the matter concerned.

works.quick_def: People who work have a job, usually one which they are paid to do.

very.quick_def: Very is used to give emphasis to an adjective or adverb.  [emphasis]

literally.quick_def: You can use literally to emphasize a statement. Some careful speakers of English think that this use is incorrect.  [emphasis]

means.quick_def: If you want to know what a word, code, signal, or gesture means, you want to know what it refers to or what its message is.

feel.quick_def: If you feel a particular emotion or physical sensation, you experience it.

want.quick_def: If you want something, you feel a desire or a need for it.

evidence.quick_def: Evidence is anything that you see, experience, read, or are told that causes you to believe that something is true or has really happened.

someone.quick_def: You use someone or somebody to refer to a person without saying exactly who you mean.

voicing.quick_def: When someone speaks or sings, you hear their voice.

disagreement.quick_def: Disagreement means objecting to something such as a proposal.

question.quick_def: A question is something that you say or write in order to ask a person about something.

enquiry.quick_def: an official process to find out the cause of something or to find out information about something

learner.quick_def: A learner is someone who is learning about a particular subject or how to do something.

computer.quick_def: A computer is an electronic machine that can store and deal with large amounts of information.

inventive.quick_def: An inventive person is good at inventing things or has clever and original ideas.

humorous.quick_def: If someone or something is humorous, they are amusing, especially in a clever or witty way.

twisting.quick_def: If you twist something, you turn it to make a spiral shape, for example by turning the two ends of it in opposite directions.

effect.quick_def: The effect of one thing on another is the change that the first thing causes in the second thing.

reveals.quick_def: To reveal something means to make people aware of it.

power.quick_def: If someone has power, they have a lot of control over people and activities.

pauses.quick_def: If you pause while you are doing something, you stop for a short period and then continue.

noises.quick_def: Noise is a loud or unpleasant sound.

play.quick_def: When children, animals, or perhaps adults play, they spend time doing enjoyable things, such as using toys and taking part in games.

convey.quick_def: To convey information or feelings means to cause them to be known or understood by someone.

emotion.quick_def: An emotion is a feeling such as happiness, love, fear, anger, or hatred, which can be caused by the situation that you are in or the people you are with.

doubt.quick_def: If you have doubt or doubts about something, you feel uncertain about it and do not know whether it is true or possible. If you say you have no doubt about it, you mean that you are certain it is true.

irony.quick_def: Irony is a subtle form of humour which involves saying things that you do not mean.

moment.quick_def: You can refer to a very short period of time, for example a few seconds, as a moment or moments.

benefiting.quick_def: The benefit of something is the help that you get from it or the advantage that results from it.

leech.quick_def: A leech is a small animal which looks like a worm and lives in water. Leeches feed by attaching themselves to other animals and sucking their blood.

lancaster.quick_def: a city in Lancashire, England, on the River Lune. John of Gaunt became Duke of Lancaster in 1362, and since 1399 the Duchy of Lancaster has been a possession of the British Crown. The Lancastrians in the Wars of the Roses were supporters of the royal house descended from John of Gaunt.

give.quick_def: You can use give with nouns that refer to physical actions. The whole expression refers to the performing of the action. For example, She gave a smile means almost the same as 'She smiled'.

part.quick_def: A part of something is one of the pieces, sections, or elements that it consists of.

initiative.quick_def: An initiative is an important act or statement that is intended to solve a problem.

carried.quick_def: If you carry something, you take it with you, holding it so that it does not touch the ground.

learning.quick_def: If you learn something, you obtain knowledge or a skill through studying or training.

universities.quick_def: A university is an institution where students study for degrees and where academic research is done.

library.quick_def: A public library is a building where things such as books, newspapers, videos, and music are kept for people to read, use, or borrow.

anybody.quick_def: Anybody means the same as anyone.

dutchman.quick_def: A Dutchman is a man who is a native of the Netherlands.

frank.quick_def: If someone is frank, they state or express things in an open and honest way.

siegmund.quick_def: Siegmund is a name for a person.

workmen.quick_def: A workman is a man who works with his hands, for example building or repairing houses or roads.

tramping.quick_def: A tramp is a person who has no home or job, and very little money. Tramps go from place to place, and get food or money by asking people or by doing casual work.

field.quick_def: A field is an area of grass, for example in a park or on a farm. A field is also an area of land on which a crop is grown.

chimney.quick_def: A chimney is a pipe through which smoke goes up into the air, usually through the roof of a building.

protruding.quick_def: If something protrudes from somewhere, it sticks out.  [formal]

grass.quick_def: Grass is a very common plant consisting of large numbers of thin, spiky, green leaves that cover the surface of the ground.

closer.quick_def: When you close something such as a door or lid or when it closes, it moves so that a hole, gap, or opening is covered.

inspection.quick_def: If you inspect something, you look at every part of it carefully in order to find out about it or check that it is all right.

revealed.quick_def: To reveal something means to make people aware of it.

chink.quick_def: A chink in a surface is a very narrow crack or opening in it.

sky-light.quick_def: A sky-light is a window in the roof that lets light from the sky come into a building.

window.quick_def: A window is a space in the wall of a building or in the side of a vehicle, which has glass in it so that light can come in and you can see out.

thistles.quick_def: A thistle is a wild plant which has leaves with sharp points and purple flowers.

amazed.quick_def: If something amazes you, it surprises you very much.

investigators.quick_def: An investigator is someone who carries out investigations, especially as part of their job.

pine.quick_def: A pine tree or a pine is a tall tree which has very thin, sharp leaves and a fresh smell. Pine trees have leaves all year round.

door.quick_def: A door is a piece of wood, glass, or metal, which is moved to open and close the entrance to a building, room, cupboard, or vehicle.

leaded.quick_def: Leaded petrol has had lead added to it.

brass.quick_def: Brass is a yellow-coloured metal made from copper and zinc. It is used especially for making ornaments and musical instruments.

knocker.quick_def: A knocker is a piece of metal on the front door of a building, which you use to hit the door in order to attract the attention of the people inside.

set.quick_def: A set of things is a number of things that belong together or that are thought of as a group.

underground.quick_def: Something that is underground is below the surface of the ground.

siegmunds.quick_def: Siegmunds is a family name. It refers to a family with this name.

managed.quick_def: If you manage an organization, business, or system, or the people who work in it, you are responsible for controlling them.

live.quick_def: If someone lives in a particular place or with a particular person, their home is in that place or with that person.

undetected.quick_def: If you are undetected or if you do something undetected, people do not find out where you are or what you are doing.

border.quick_def: The border between two countries or regions is the dividing line between them. Sometimes the border also refers to the land close to this line.

breda.quick_def: Breda is the name of a town in Holland.

holland.quick_def: Holland is a region in the Netherlands. It is a well-known place in Europe.

clutch.quick_def: If you clutch at something or clutch something, you hold it tightly, usually because you are afraid or anxious.

individualistic.quick_def: If you say that someone is individualistic, you mean that they like to think and do things in their own way, rather than imitating other people. You can also say that a society is individualistic if it encourages people to behave in this way.

homemakers.quick_def: A homemaker is someone who spends a lot of time looking after their home and family. You usually use homemaker to refer to someone who does not have a job outside the home.

burrowed.quick_def: A burrow is a tunnel or hole in the ground that is dug by an animal such as a rabbit.

tranquillity.quick_def: Something that is tranquil is calm and peaceful.

strict.quick_def: A strict rule or order is very clear and precise or severe and must always be obeyed completely.

regulations.quick_def: Regulations are rules made by a government or other authority in order to control the way something is done or the way people behave.

dismantle.quick_def: If you dismantle a machine or structure, you carefully separate it into its different parts.

homes.quick_def: Someone's home is the house or flat where they live.

conventional.quick_def: Someone who is conventional has behaviour or opinions that are ordinary and normal.

lifestyles.quick_def: The lifestyle of a particular person or group of people is the living conditions, behaviour, and habits that are typical of them or are chosen by them.

subterranean.quick_def: A subterranean river or tunnel is under the ground.  [formal]

suburbia.quick_def: Journalists often use suburbia to refer to the suburbs of cities and large towns considered as a whole.

dutch-style.quick_def: If something is Dutch-style, it is made or done in the way that the Dutch people do.

respectable.quick_def: Someone or something that is respectable is approved of by society and considered to be morally correct.

chic.quick_def: Something or someone that is chic is fashionable and sophisticated.

luxury.quick_def: Luxury is very great comfort, especially among beautiful and expensive surroundings.

cosseted.quick_def: If someone is cosseted, everything possible is done for them and they are protected from anything unpleasant.

inside.quick_def: Something or someone that is inside a place, container, or object is in it or is surrounded by it.

earth-covered.quick_def: If something is earth-covered, it has a layer of earth on it.

noise.quick_def: Noise is a loud or unpleasant sound.

embankment.quick_def: An embankment is a thick wall of earth that is built to carry a road or railway over an area of low ground, or to prevent water from a river or the sea from flooding the area.

next.quick_def: The next period of time, event, person, or thing is the one that comes immediately after the present one or after the previous one.

tilburg.quick_def: Tilburg is the name of a city. It's a place where people live, work and do many things.

road.quick_def: A road is a long piece of hard ground which is built between two places so that people can drive or ride easily from one place to the other.

recently.quick_def: If you have done something recently or if something happened recently, it happened only a short time ago.

market.quick_def: A market is a place where goods are bought and sold, usually outdoors.

foundations.quick_def: The foundation of something such as a belief or way of life is the things on which it is based.

dug.quick_def: If people or animals dig, they make a hole in the ground or in a pile of earth, stones, or rubbish.

customers.quick_def: A customer is someone who buys goods or services, especially from a shop.

queued.quick_def: A queue is a line of people or vehicles that are waiting for something.  [mainly British]

buy.quick_def: If you buy something, you obtain it by paying money for it.

unusual.quick_def: If something is unusual, it does not happen very often or you do not see it or hear it very often.

part-submerged.quick_def: If something is part-submerged, it is partly under water.

houses.quick_def: A house is a building in which people live, usually the people belonging to one family.

whose.quick_def: You use whose at the beginning of a relative clause where you mention something that belongs to or is associated with the person or thing mentioned in the previous clause.

wall.quick_def: A wall is one of the vertical sides of a building or room.

consists.quick_def: Something that consists of particular things or people is formed from them.

grassy.quick_def: A grassy area of land is covered in grass.

mound.quick_def: A mound of something is a large rounded pile of it.

front.quick_def: The front of something is the part of it that faces you, or that faces forward, or that you normally see or use.

gallery.quick_def: A gallery is a place that has permanent exhibitions of works of art in it.

dutch.quick_def: Dutch means relating to or belonging to the Netherlands, or to its people, language, or culture.

would-be.quick_def: A would-be person is someone who wants to be a certain kind of person but has not yet become one.

moles.quick_def: A mole is a natural dark spot or small dark lump on someone's skin.

numbers.quick_def: A number is a word such as 'two', ' nine', or ' twelve', or a symbol such as 1, 3, or 47. You use numbers to say how many things you are referring to or where something comes in a series.

burrowing.quick_def: A burrow is a tunnel or hole in the ground that is dug by an animal such as a rabbit.

ground.quick_def: If you grind a substance such as corn, you crush it between two hard surfaces or with a machine until it becomes a fine powder.

offices.quick_def: An office is a room or a part of a building where people work sitting at desks.

discos.quick_def: A disco is a place or event at which people dance to pop music.

shopping.quick_def: A shop is a building or part of a building where things are sold.  [mainly British]

malls.quick_def: A mall is a very large enclosed shopping area.

proving.quick_def: If something proves to be true or to have a particular quality, it becomes clear after a period of time that it is true or has that quality.

extreme.quick_def: Extreme means very great in degree or intensity.

climates.quick_def: The climate of a place is the general weather conditions that are typical of it.

months.quick_def: A month is one of the twelve periods of time that a year is divided into, for example January or February.

montreal.quick_def: the largest city in the Canadian province of Quebec, on the St Lawrence River. Montreal was under French rule until 1763 and over two-thirds of its population are French-speaking.

canada.quick_def: a large country in the northern half of North America. The parts of the country away from the coasts have very cold winters, and much of the land is covered with forests and lakes. Canada used to be owned by Britain and France, and is now an independent member of the Commonwealth. Its capital city is Ottawa, and its official languages are English and French. Today there are still some tensions between English and French speakers, especially in Quebec, where many French speakers wish to form a separate country.

instance.quick_def: You use for instance to introduce a particular event, situation, or person that is an example of what you are talking about.

citizens.quick_def: Someone who is a citizen of a particular country is legally accepted as belonging to that country.

escape.quick_def: If you escape from a place, you succeed in getting away from it.

cold.quick_def: Something that is cold has a very low temperature or a lower temperature than is normal or acceptable.

shops.quick_def: A shop is a building or part of a building where things are sold.  [mainly British]

clinics.quick_def: A clinic is a building where people go to receive medical advice or treatment.

tokyo.quick_def: Tokyo is the capital city of Japan, where many people live and there are lots of buildings and activities.

massive.quick_def: Something that is massive is very large in size, quantity, or extent.  [emphasis]

begun.quick_def: To begin to do something means to start doing it.

decade.quick_def: A decade is a period of ten years, especially one that begins with a year ending in 0, for example 1980 to 1989.

japan.quick_def: a country consisting of a group of islands in eastern Asia

squeezed.quick_def: If you squeeze something, you press it firmly, usually with your hands.

landspace.quick_def: Landspace means the area of land. It refers to how much land there is in a place.

big.quick_def: A big person or thing is large in physical size.

avoid.quick_def: If you avoid something unpleasant that might happen, you take action in order to prevent it from happening.

disfiguring.quick_def: If someone is disfigured, their appearance is spoiled.

threatening.quick_def: If a person threatens to do something unpleasant to you, or if they threaten you, they say or imply that they will do something unpleasant to you, especially if you do not do what they want.

beautiful.quick_def: A beautiful person is very attractive to look at.

environmentally.quick_def: Environmental means concerned with the protection of the natural world of land, sea, air, plants, and animals.

sensitive.quick_def: If you are sensitive to other people's needs, problems, or feelings, you show understanding and awareness of them.  [approval]

consume.quick_def: If you consume something, you eat or drink it.  [formal]

cinemas.quick_def: A cinema is a place where people go to watch films for entertainment.  [mainly British]

supermarkets.quick_def: A supermarket is a large shop which sells all kinds of food and some household goods.

theatres.quick_def: A theatre is a building with a stage in it, on which plays, shows, and other performances take place.

warehouses.quick_def: A warehouse is a large building where raw materials or manufactured goods are stored until they are exported to other countries or distributed to shops to be sold.

libraries.quick_def: A public library is a building where things such as books, newspapers, videos, and music are kept for people to read, use, or borrow.

windows.quick_def: A window is a space in the wall of a building or in the side of a vehicle, which has glass in it so that light can come in and you can see out.

advantages.quick_def: An advantage is something that puts you in a better position than other people.

comes.quick_def: When a person or thing comes to a particular place, especially to a place where you are, they move there.

private.quick_def: Private industries and services are owned or controlled by an individual person or a commercial company, rather than by the state or an official organization.  [business]

hectares.quick_def: A hectare is a measurement of an area of land which is equal to 10,000 square metres, or 2.471 acres.

above.quick_def: If one thing is above another one, it is directly over it or higher than it.

occupy.quick_def: The people who occupy a building or a place are the people who live or work there.

halved.quick_def: When you halve something or when it halves, it is reduced to half its previous size or amount.

metres.quick_def: A metre is a metric unit of length equal to 100 centimetres.

earth.quick_def: Earth or the Earth is the planet on which we live. People usually say Earth when they are referring to the planet as part of the universe, and the Earth when they are talking about the planet as the place where we live.

minimal.quick_def: Something that is minimal is very small in quantity, value, or degree.

insulation.quick_def: If a person or group is insulated from the rest of society or from outside influences, they are protected from them.

excellent.quick_def: Something that is excellent is very good indeed.

enquiries.quick_def: an official process to find out the cause of something or to find out information about something

week.quick_def: A week is a period of seven days. Some people consider that a week starts on Monday and ends on Sunday.

peter.quick_def: If something  peters out, it gradually comes to an end.

carpenter.quick_def: A carpenter is a person whose job is making and repairing wooden things.

secretary.quick_def: A secretary is a person who is employed to do office work, such as typing letters, answering phone calls, and arranging meetings.

sheltering.quick_def: A shelter is a small building or covered place which is made to protect people from bad weather or danger.

builds.quick_def: If you build something, you make it by joining things together.

dweller.quick_def: A city dweller or slum dweller, for example, is a person who lives in the kind of place or house indicated.

himself.quick_def: You use himself to refer to a man, boy, or male animal.

paid.quick_def: Paid is the past tense and past participle of pay.

heating.quick_def: When you heat something, you raise its temperature, for example by using a flame or a special piece of equipment.

bill.quick_def: A bill is a written statement of money that you owe for goods or services.

thanks.quick_def: You use thank you or, in more informal English, thanks to express your gratitude when someone does something for you or gives you what you want.  [formulae]

solar.quick_def: Solar is used to describe things relating to the sun.

panels.quick_def: A panel is a small group of people who are chosen to do something, for example to discuss something in public or to make a decision.

obstacle.quick_def: An obstacle is an object that makes it difficult for you to go where you want to go, because it is in your way.

conservative.quick_def: A Conservative politician or voter is a member of or votes for the Conservative Party in Britain.

developers.quick_def: A developer is a person or a company that buys land and builds houses, offices, shops, or factories on it, or buys existing buildings and makes them more modern.  [business]

prefer.quick_def: If you prefer someone or something, you like that person or thing better than another, and so you are more likely to choose them if there is a choice.

ensure.quick_def: To ensure something, or to ensure that something happens, means to make certain that it happens.  [formal]

quick.quick_def: Someone or something that is quick moves or does things with great speed.

sales.quick_def: The sale of goods is the act of selling them for money.

greeted.quick_def: When you greet someone, you say 'Hello' or shake hands with them.

undisguised.quick_def: If you describe someone's feelings as undisguised, you mean that they show them openly and do not make any attempt to hide them.

relief.quick_def: If you feel a sense of relief, you feel happy because something unpleasant has not happened or is no longer happening.

limburg.quick_def: Limburg is the name of a region. It can refer to areas in the Netherlands, Belgium and Germany.

planners.quick_def: Planners are people whose job is to make decisions about what is going to be done in the future. For example, town planners decide how land should be used and what new buildings should be built.

chronic.quick_def: A chronic illness or disability lasts for a very long time. Compare acute.

shortage.quick_def: If there is a shortage of something, there is not enough of it.

architect.quick_def: An architect is a person who designs buildings.

jo.quick_def: a first name for girls, short for Joanna, Joanne, Jodie or Josephine

hurkmans.quick_def: Hurkmans is a family name. People with this name are part of the Hurkmans family.

hit.quick_def: If you hit someone or something, you deliberately touch them with a lot of force, with your hand or an object held in your hand.

embankments.quick_def: An embankment is a thick wall of earth that is built to carry a road or railway over an area of low ground, or to prevent water from a river or the sea from flooding the area.

two-floored.quick_def: If a building is two-floored, it has two floors.

four-bedroomed.quick_def: If a house is four-bedroomed, it has four bedrooms.

two-bathroomed.quick_def: If a place is two-bathroomed, it has two bathrooms.

detached.quick_def: If you detach one thing from another that it is fixed to, you remove it. If one thing detaches from another, it becomes separated from it.  [formal]

taking.quick_def: You can use take followed by a noun to talk about an action or event, when it would also be possible to use the verb that is related to that noun. For example, you can say 'she took a shower' instead of 'she showered'.

shape.quick_def: The shape of an object, a person, or an area is the appearance of their outside edges or surfaces, for example whether they are round, square, curved, or fat.

runs.quick_def: When you run, you move more quickly than when you walk, for example because you are in a hurry to get somewhere, or for exercise.

floor.quick_def: The floor of a room is the part of it that you walk on.

ceiling.quick_def: A ceiling is the horizontal surface that forms the top part or roof inside a room.

lighting.quick_def: Light is the brightness that lets you see things. Light comes from sources such as the sun, moon, lamps, and fire.

nobody.quick_def: Nobody means not a single person, or not a single member of a particular group or set.

notices.quick_def: If you notice something or someone, you become aware of them.

dark.quick_def: When it is dark, there is not enough light to see properly, for example because it is night.

energy-efficient.quick_def: If something is energy-efficient, it uses less energy to do the same job.

oil.quick_def: Oil is a smooth, thick liquid that is used as a fuel and for making the parts of machines move smoothly. Oil is found underground.

crisis.quick_def: A crisis is a situation in which something or someone is affected by one or more very serious problems.

terrace.quick_def: A terrace is a row of similar houses joined together by their side walls.  [British]

nottinghamshire.quick_def: a county in the Midlands of England, famous (especially in the past) as a centre of the coal-mining industry. Its administrative centre is Nottingham.

outstanding.quick_def: If you describe someone or something as outstanding, you think that they are very remarkable and impressive.

example.quick_def: An example of something is a particular situation, object, or person which shows that what is being claimed is true.

olivetti.quick_def: Olivetti is the name of a well-known company or brand. It is often related to products like typewriters, computers, etc.

residential.quick_def: A residential area contains houses rather than offices or factories.

ivrea.quick_def: Ivrea is the name of a place, a town in Italy.

commissioned.quick_def: If you commission something or commission someone to do something, you formally arrange for someone to do a piece of work for you.

roberto.quick_def: Roberto is a name for a man.

comprises.quick_def: If you say that something comprises or is comprised of a number of things or people, you mean it has them as its parts or members.  [formal]

one-bedroomed.quick_def: If a place is one-bedroomed, it has only one bedroom.

apartments.quick_def: An apartment is a set of rooms for living in, usually on one floor of a large building.  [mainly US]

maisonettes.quick_def: A maisonette is a flat that usually has a separate door to the outside from other flats in the same building. Many maisonettes are on two floors.  [British]

employees.quick_def: An employee is a person who is paid to work for an organization or for another person.

seen.quick_def: When you see something, you notice it using your eyes.

except.quick_def: You use except to introduce the only thing or person that a statement does not apply to, or a fact that prevents a statement from being completely true.

facade.quick_def: The facade of a building, especially a large one, is its front wall or the wall that faces the street.

patnzia.quick_def: Patnzia is a name of a person.

vallecchi.quick_def: Vallecchi is a family name. A family name is what a family members share.

resident.quick_def: The residents of a house or area are the people who live there.

apartment.quick_def: An apartment is a set of rooms for living in, usually on one floor of a large building.  [mainly US]

everyone.quick_def: You use everyone or everybody to refer to all the people in a particular group.

adapts.quick_def: If you adapt to a new situation or adapt yourself to it, you change your ideas or behaviour in order to deal with it successfully.

shimizu.quick_def: Shimizu is a proper name, often used as the name of a company, place or person.

corporation.quick_def: A corporation is a large business or company.  [business]

space.quick_def: You use space to refer to an area that is empty or available. The area can be any size. For example, you can refer to a large area outside as a large open space or to a small area between two objects as a small space.

creation.quick_def: To create something means to cause it to happen or exist.

systems.quick_def: A system is a way of working, organizing, or doing something which follows a fixed plan or set of rules. You can use system to refer to an organization or institution that is organized in this way.

mix.quick_def: If two substances mix or if you mix one substance with another, you stir or shake them together, or combine them in some other way, so that they become a single substance.

sounds.quick_def: A sound is something that you hear.

breezes.quick_def: A breeze is a gentle wind.

scents.quick_def: The scent of something is the pleasant smell that it has.

stimulate.quick_def: To stimulate something means to encourage it to begin or develop further.

spend.quick_def: When you spend money, you pay money for things that you want.

equipped.quick_def: If you equip a person or thing with something, you give them the tools or equipment that are needed.

virtual.quick_def: You can use virtual to indicate that something is so nearly true that for most purposes it can be regarded as true.

departments.quick_def: A department is one of the sections in an organization such as a government, business, or university. A department is also one of the sections in a large shop.

periscopes.quick_def: A periscope is a vertical tube which people inside submarines can look through to see above the surface of the water.

views.quick_def: Your views on something are the beliefs or opinions that you have about it, for example whether you think it is good, bad, right, or wrong.

hobbit.quick_def: A hobbit is a small person with hairy feet who lives in a hole in the ground.

lifestyle.quick_def: The lifestyle of a particular person or group of people is the living conditions, behaviour, and habits that are typical of them or are chosen by them.

cool.quick_def: Something that is cool has a temperature which is low but not very low.

bakery.quick_def: A bakery is a building where bread, pastries, and cakes are baked, or the shop where they are sold.

business.quick_def: Business is work relating to the production, buying, and selling of goods or services.

heatwave.quick_def: A heatwave is a period of time during which the weather is much hotter than usual.

sleeping.quick_def: Sleep is the natural state of rest in which your eyes are closed, your body is inactive, and your mind does not think.

felt.quick_def: If you feel a particular emotion or physical sensation, you experience it.

peace.quick_def: If countries or groups involved in a war or violent conflict are discussing peace, they are talking to each other in order to try to end the conflict.

close.quick_def: When you close something such as a door or lid or when it closes, it moves so that a hole, gap, or opening is covered.

adding.quick_def: If you add one thing to another, you put it in or on the other thing, to increase, complete, or improve it.

rooms.quick_def: A room is one of the separate sections or parts of the inside of a building. Rooms have their own walls, ceilings, floors, and doors, and are usually used for particular activities. You can refer to all the people who are in a room as the room.

strange.quick_def: Something that is strange is unusual or unexpected, and makes you feel slightly nervous or afraid.

draw.quick_def: When you draw, or when you draw something, you use a pencil or pen to produce a picture, pattern, or diagram.

strength.quick_def: Your strength is the physical energy that you have, which gives you the ability to perform various actions, such as lifting or moving things.

vibrations.quick_def: If something vibrates or if you vibrate it, it shakes with repeated small, quick movements.

child.quick_def: A child is a human being who is not yet an adult.
