confirmed.quick_def: You use confirmed to describe someone who has a particular habit or belief that they are very unlikely to change.

annual.quick_def: Annual events happen once every year.

boards.quick_def: A board is a flat, thin, rectangular piece of wood or plastic which is used for a particular purpose.

directors.quick_def: The director of a play, film, or television programme is the person who decides how it will appear on stage or screen, and who tells the actors and technical staff what to do.

korn.quick_def: Korn is the name of a company. A company is a business organization that makes or sells things.

ferry.quick_def: A ferry is a boat that transports passengers and sometimes also vehicles, usually across rivers or short stretches of sea.

carre.quick_def: Carre is a name, often used as part of a company's name.

orban.quick_def: Orban is a name, usually used for a person.

doubling.quick_def: You use double to indicate that something includes or is made of two things of the same kind.

non-executive.quick_def: A non-executive person is someone who doesn't have the main responsibility for running a company's daily operations.

previous.quick_def: A previous event or thing is one that happened or existed before the one that you are talking about.

remains.quick_def: If someone or something remains in a particular state or condition, they stay in that state or condition and do not change.

painfully.quick_def: If a part of your body is painful, it hurts because it is injured or because there is something wrong with it.

posts.quick_def: The post is the public service or system by which letters and packages are collected and delivered.  [mainly British]

surveyed.quick_def: If you carry out a survey, you try to find out detailed information about a lot of different people or things, usually by asking people a series of questions.

hilary.quick_def: a first name for boys or girls

sears.quick_def: To sear something means to burn its surface with a sudden intense heat.

partner.quick_def: Your partner is the person you are married to or are having a romantic or sexual relationship with.

raised.quick_def: If you raise something, you move it so that it is in a higher position.

level.quick_def: A level is a point on a scale, for example a scale of amount, quality, or difficulty.

grades.quick_def: If something is graded, its quality is judged, and it is often given a number or a name that indicates how good or bad it is.

employed.quick_def: If a person or company employs you, they pay you to work for them.

barriers.quick_def: A barrier is something such as a rule, law, or policy that makes it difficult or impossible for something to happen or be achieved.

feature.quick_def: A feature of something is an interesting or important part or characteristic of it.

recession.quick_def: A recession is a period when the economy of a country is doing badly, for example because industry is producing less and more people are becoming unemployed.

delayering.quick_def: Delayering is the process of simplifying the administrative structure of a large organization in order to make it more efficient.  [business]

halted.quick_def: When a person or a vehicle halts or when something halts them, they stop moving in the direction they were going and stand still.

layers.quick_def: A layer of a material or substance is a quantity or piece of it that covers a surface or that is between two other things.

aspire.quick_def: If you aspire to something such as an important job, you have a strong desire to achieve it.

started.quick_def: If you start to do something, you do something that you were not doing before and you continue doing it.

whole.quick_def: If you refer to the whole of something, you mean all of it.

prospect.quick_def: If there is some prospect of something happening, there is a possibility that it will happen.

equality.quick_def: Equality is the same status, rights, and responsibilities for all the members of a society, group, or family.

workforce.quick_def: The workforce is the total number of people in a country or region who are physically able to do a job and are available for work.

demographic.quick_def: Demographic means relating to or concerning demography.

trends.quick_def: A trend is a change or development towards something new or different.

steadily.quick_def: gradually and in an even and regular way

increasing.quick_def: If something increases or you increase it, it becomes greater in number, level, or amount.

addition.quick_def: You use in addition when you want to mention another item connected with the subject you are discussing.

passing.quick_def: To pass someone or something means to go past them without stopping.

education.quick_def: Education involves teaching people various subjects, usually at a school or college, or being taught.

organisations.quick_def: Organisations are groups of people who work together for a certain purpose.

network.quick_def: A network of lines, roads, veins, or other long thin things is a large number of them which cross each other or meet at many points.

opportunities.quick_def: An opportunity is a situation in which it is possible for you to do something that you want to do.

enhance.quick_def: To enhance something means to improve its value, quality, or attractiveness.

contacts.quick_def: Contact involves meeting or communicating with someone, especially regularly.

pan-european.quick_def: If something is pan-European, it involves or relates to the whole of Europe.

workshops.quick_def: A workshop is a period of discussion or practical work on a particular subject in which a group of people share their knowledge or experience.

ariane.quick_def: Ariane is a name for a person, usually a female name.

berthoin.quick_def: Berthoin is a surname, which is a family name used to identify a particular family.

antal.quick_def: Antal is a proper name, usually used for a person.

organisational.quick_def: Organizational abilities and methods relate to the way that work, activities, or events are planned and arranged.

archamps.quick_def: Archamps is the name of a place, like a town or a location.

anecdotal.quick_def: Anecdotal evidence is based on individual accounts, rather than on reliable research or statistics, and so may not be valid.

patterns.quick_def: A pattern is the repeated or regular way in which something happens or is done.

hurdles.quick_def: A hurdle is a problem, difficulty, or part of a process that may prevent you from achieving something.

belief.quick_def: Belief is a feeling of certainty that something exists, is true, or is good.

value.quick_def: The value of something such as a quality, attitude, or method is its importance or usefulness. If you place a particular value on something, that is the importance or usefulness you think it has.

difference.quick_def: The difference between two things is the way in which they are unlike each other.

political.quick_def: Political means relating to the way power is achieved and used in a country or society.

decisions.quick_def: When you make a decision, you choose what should be done or which is the best of various possible actions.

extent.quick_def: If you are talking about how great, important, or serious a difficulty or situation is, you can refer to the extent of it.

forestry.quick_def: Forestry is the science or skill of growing and taking care of trees in forests, especially in order to obtain wood.

region.quick_def: A region is a large area of land that is different from other areas of land, for example because it is one of the different parts of a country with its own customs and characteristics, or because it has a particular geographical feature.

understand.quick_def: If you understand someone or understand what they are saying, you know what they mean.

consequences.quick_def: The consequences of something are the results or effects of it.

tool.quick_def: A tool is any instrument or simple piece of equipment that you hold in your hands and use to do a particular kind of work. For example, spades, hammers, and knives are all tools.

assessing.quick_def: When you assess a person, thing, or situation, you consider them in order to make a judgment about them.

impact.quick_def: The impact that something has on a situation, process, or person is a sudden and powerful effect that it has on them.

ecosystem.quick_def: An ecosystem is all the plants and animals that live in a particular area together with the complex relationship that exists between them and their environment.  [technical]

viability.quick_def: the fact that something can be done and can be successful

pva.quick_def: PVA is short for population viability analysis, which is a tool to assess the impact of something (like forestry) on the ecosystem.

predicting.quick_def: If you predict an event, you say that it will happen.

probability.quick_def: The probability of something happening is how likely it is to happen, sometimes expressed as a fraction or a percentage.

extinct.quick_def: A species of animal or plant that is extinct no longer has any living members, either in the world or in a particular place.

input.quick_def: Input consists of information or resources that a group or project receives.

resource.quick_def: The resources of an organization or person are the materials, money, and other things that they have and can use in order to function properly.

exploitation.quick_def: If you say that someone is exploiting you, you think that they are treating you unfairly by using your work or ideas and giving you very little in return.

assist.quick_def: If you assist someone, you help them to do a job or task by doing part of the work for them.

wildlife.quick_def: You can use wildlife to refer to the animals and other living things that live in the wild.

enormous.quick_def: Something that is enormous is extremely large in size or amount.

australia.quick_def: a large island country and continent in the south-west Pacific Ocean. Its capital city is Canberra and its official language is English. The first people to live in Australia were the Aborigines, who now form less than 3% of the population. In 1770 the country was visited by Captain Cook, and in the 18th and 19th centuries it was used by the British as a place to send criminals. Many of the people living in Australia today are descended from British people. It is now independent from Britain, although it remains a member of the Commonwealth. Most of the population live on or near the coast in the east and south of the country, and there are large areas in the west, north and centre of the country where very few people live. The climate is generally warm. Australian culture is popular in Britain. A number of Australian programmes, including soap operas such as Neighbours, appear regularly on British television. A popular informal name for Australia is Down Under.

forests.quick_def: A forest is a large area where trees grow close together.

dies.quick_def: When people, animals, and plants die, they stop living.

observation.quick_def: Observation is the action or process of carefully watching someone or something.

useful.quick_def: If something is useful, you can use it to do something or to help you in some way.

discussion.quick_def: If there is discussion about something, people talk about it, often in order to reach a decision.

extinction.quick_def: The extinction of a species of animal or plant is the death of all its remaining living members.

highlights.quick_def: If someone or something highlights a point or problem, they emphasize it or make you think about it.

luck.quick_def: Luck or good luck is success or good things that happen to you, that do not come from your own abilities or efforts.

chance.quick_def: If there is a chance of something happening, it is possible that it will happen.

prediction.quick_def: If you make a prediction about something, you say what you think will happen.

processes.quick_def: A process is a series of actions which are carried out in order to achieve a particular result.

contribute.quick_def: If you contribute to something, you say or do things to help to make it successful.

fall.quick_def: If someone or something falls, they move quickly downwards onto or towards the ground, by accident or because of a natural force.

broad.quick_def: Something that is broad is wide.

discussed.quick_def: If people discuss something, they talk about it, often in order to reach a decision.

attempts.quick_def: If you attempt to do something, especially something difficult, you try to do it.

predict.quick_def: If you predict an event, you say that it will happen.

uncertainty.quick_def: Uncertainty is a state of doubt about the future or about what is the right thing to do.

survives.quick_def: If a person or living thing survives in a dangerous situation such as an accident or an illness, they do not die.

matter.quick_def: A matter is a task, situation, or event which you have to deal with or think about, especially one that involves problems.

none.quick_def: None of something means not even a small amount of it. None of a group of people or things means not even one of them.

fluctuate.quick_def: If something fluctuates, it changes a lot in an irregular way.

enormously.quick_def: Something that is enormous is extremely large in size or amount.

death.quick_def: Death is the permanent end of the life of a person or animal.

fluctuations.quick_def: If something fluctuates, it changes a lot in an irregular way.

cause.quick_def: The cause of an event, usually a bad event, is the thing that makes it happen.

extinctions.quick_def: Extinctions are the situations when a kind of animal or plant completely dies out and no longer exists.

size.quick_def: The size of something is how big or small it is. Something's size is determined by comparing it to other things, counting it, or measuring it.

account.quick_def: If you have an account with a bank or a similar organization, you have an arrangement to leave your money there and take some out when you need it.

unlikely.quick_def: If you say that something is unlikely to happen or unlikely to be true, you believe that it will not happen or that it is not true, although you are not completely sure.

individuals.quick_def: Individual means relating to one person or thing, rather than to a large group.

inbreeding.quick_def: Inbreeding is the repeated breeding of closely related animals or people.

particularly.quick_def: You use particularly to indicate that what you are saying applies especially to one thing or situation.

sex.quick_def: The two sexes are the two groups, male and female, into which people and animals are divided according to the function they have in producing young.

descended.quick_def: If you descend or if you descend a staircase, you move downwards from a higher to a lower level.  [formal]

survive.quick_def: If a person or living thing survives in a dangerous situation such as an accident or an illness, they do not die.

increases.quick_def: If something increases or you increase it, it becomes greater in number, level, or amount.

acts.quick_def: When you act, you do something for a particular purpose.

variability.quick_def: the fact of something being likely to vary

lacks.quick_def: If there is a lack of something, there is not enough of it or it does not exist at all.

evolve.quick_def: When animals or plants evolve, they gradually change and develop into different forms.

adapt.quick_def: If you adapt to a new situation or adapt yourself to it, you change your ideas or behaviour in order to deal with it successfully.

predators.quick_def: A predator is an animal that kills and eats other animals.

diseases.quick_def: A disease is an illness which affects people, animals, or plants, for example one which is caused by bacteria or infection.

loss.quick_def: Loss is the fact of no longer having something or having less of it than before.

diversity.quick_def: The diversity of something is the fact that it contains many very different elements.

associated.quick_def: If you associate someone or something with another thing, the two are connected in your mind.

reductions.quick_def: When there is a reduction in something, it is made smaller.

likelihood.quick_def: The likelihood of something happening is how likely it is to happen.

fluctuates.quick_def: If something fluctuates, it changes a lot in an irregular way.

add.quick_def: If you add one thing to another, you put it in or on the other thing, to increase, complete, or improve it.

degree.quick_def: You use degree to indicate the extent to which something happens or is the case, or the amount which something is felt.

survival.quick_def: If you refer to the survival of something or someone, you mean that they manage to continue or exist in spite of difficult circumstances.

catastrophes.quick_def: A catastrophe is an unexpected event that causes great suffering or damage.

flood.quick_def: If there is a flood, a large amount of water covers an area which is usually dry, for example when a river flows over its banks or a pipe bursts.

drought.quick_def: A drought is a long period of time during which no rain falls.

epidemic.quick_def: If there is an epidemic of a particular disease somewhere, it affects a very large number of people there and spreads quickly to other areas.

reduce.quick_def: If you reduce something, you make it smaller in size or amount, or less in degree.

sizes.quick_def: The size of something is how big or small it is. Something's size is determined by comparing it to other things, counting it, or measuring it.

fraction.quick_def: A fraction of something is a tiny amount or proportion of it.

allowance.quick_def: An allowance is money that is given to someone, usually on a regular basis, in order to help them pay for the things that they need.

additional.quick_def: Additional things are extra things apart from the ones already present.

confident.quick_def: If you are confident about something, you are certain that it will happen in the way you want it to.

persistence.quick_def: If you have persistence, you continue to do something even though it is difficult or other people are against it.

thousand.quick_def: A thousand or one thousand is the number 1,000.

bear.quick_def: If you bear something somewhere, you carry it there or take it there.  [literary]

mind.quick_def: You refer to someone's mind when talking about their thoughts. For example, if you say that something is in your mind, you mean that you are thinking about it, and if you say that something is at the back of your mind, you mean that you are aware of it, although you are not thinking about it very much.

distribution.quick_def: The distribution of things involves giving or delivering them to a number of people or places.

locality.quick_def: A locality is a small area of a country or city.  [formal]

logging.quick_def: A log is a piece of a thick branch or of the trunk of a tree that has been cut so that it can be used for fuel or for making things.

cutting.quick_def: If you cut something, you use a knife or a similar tool to divide it into pieces, or to mark it or damage it. If you cut a shape or a hole in something, you make the shape or hole by using a knife or similar tool.

forest-dependent.quick_def: If a creature or thing is forest-dependent, it needs the forest to live or exist.

creatures.quick_def: You can refer to any living thing that is not a plant as a creature, especially when it is of an unknown or unfamiliar kind. People also refer to imaginary animals and beings as creatures.

ground-dwelling.quick_def: If an animal is ground-dwelling, it lives on the ground.

herbivores.quick_def: A herbivore is an animal that only eats plants.

marsupials.quick_def: A marsupial is an animal such as a kangaroo or an opossum. Female marsupials carry their babies in a pouch on their stomach.

recover.quick_def: When you recover from an illness or an injury, you become well again.

pre-logging.quick_def: Pre-logging means the time or situation before logging (cutting down trees) happens.

densities.quick_def: Density is the extent to which something is filled or covered with people or things.

logged.quick_def: A log is a piece of a thick branch or of the trunk of a tree that has been cut so that it can be used for fuel or for making things.

regardless.quick_def: If something happens  regardless of something else, it is not affected or influenced at all by that other thing.

model.quick_def: A model of an object is a physical representation that shows what it looks like or how it works. The model is often smaller than the object it represents.

reduction.quick_def: When there is a reduction in something, it is made smaller.

listed.quick_def: A list of things such as names or addresses is a set of them which all belong to a particular category, written down one below the other.

loaded.quick_def: If you load a vehicle or a container, you put a large quantity of things into it.

sixth.quick_def: The sixth item in a series is the one that you count as number six.

seventh.quick_def: The seventh item in a series is the one that you count as number seven.

inhabitants.quick_def: The inhabitants of a place are the people who live there.

modern-day.quick_def: Modern-day means belonging to or happening in the present time.

gujarat.quick_def: Gujarat is a state in north-western India.

rajasthan.quick_def: Rajasthan is a state in north-western India.

north-western.quick_def: North-western means in or from the north-west part of a place.

india.quick_def: a country in southern Asia which used to be part of the British Empire. It became independent and a member of the Commonwealth in 1947.

gaining.quick_def: If a person or place gains something such as an ability or quality, they gradually get more of it.

clean.quick_def: Something that is clean is free from dirt or unwanted marks.

groundwater.quick_def: Groundwater is water that is found under the ground. Groundwater has usually passed down through the soil and become trapped by rocks.

drinking.quick_def: When you drink a liquid, you take it into your mouth and swallow it.

bathing.quick_def: A bath is a container, usually a long rectangular one, which you fill with water and sit in while you wash your body.  [British]

watering.quick_def: Water is a clear thin liquid that has no colour or taste when it is pure. It falls from clouds as rain and enters rivers and seas. All animals and people need water in order to live.

irrigation.quick_def: To irrigate land means to supply it with water in order to help crops grow.

significance.quick_def: The significance of something is the importance that it has, usually because it will have an effect on a situation or shows something about a situation.

stepwell.quick_def: A stepwell is a well with steps leading down to the water. People can use these steps to get to the water easily.

utilitarian.quick_def: Utilitarian means based on the idea that the morally correct course of action is the one that produces benefit for the greatest number of people.  [technical]

application.quick_def: An application for something such as a job or membership of an organization is a formal written request for it.

unique.quick_def: Something that is unique is the only one of its kind.

stepwells.quick_def: Stepwells are wells with steps leading down to the water. People can use these steps to go down and get water.

architecturally.quick_def: Architectural means relating to the design and construction of buildings.

vary.quick_def: If things vary, they are different from each other in size, amount, or degree.

heyday.quick_def: Someone's heyday is the time when they are most powerful, successful, or popular.

gathering.quick_def: If people gather somewhere or if someone gathers people somewhere, they come together in a group.

relaxation.quick_def: Relaxation is a way of spending time in which you rest and feel comfortable.

worship.quick_def: If you worship a god, you show your respect to the god, for example by saying prayers.

villagers.quick_def: You refer to the people who live in a village, especially the people who have lived there for most or all of their lives, as the villagers.

lowest.quick_def: Something that is low measures only a short distance from the bottom to the top, or from the ground to the top.

classes.quick_def: A class is a group of pupils or students who are taught together.

dotted.quick_def: A dot is a very small round mark, for example one that is used as the top part of the letter 'i', as a full stop, or as a decimal point.

desert.quick_def: A desert is a large area of land, usually in a hot region, where there is almost no water, rain, trees, or plants.

vav.quick_def: A vav is a kind of step-well in the desert areas of Gujarat.

baori.quick_def: A baori is a kind of step-well in Rajasthan.

delhi.quick_def: Delhi is the name of a big city and a union territory in India. It is an important place with many people living there and lots of buildings.

near.quick_def: If something is near a place, thing, or person, it is a short distance from them.

villages.quick_def: A village consists of a group of houses, together with other buildings such as a church and a school, in a country area.

spaces.quick_def: You use space to refer to an area that is empty or available. The area can be any size. For example, you can refer to a large area outside as a large open space or to a small area between two objects as a small space.

positioned.quick_def: The position of someone or something is the place where they are in relation to other things.

beside.quick_def: Something that is beside something else is at the side of it or next to it.

resting.quick_def: The rest is used to refer to all the parts of something or all the things in a group that remain or that you have not already mentioned.

travellers.quick_def: A traveller is a person who is making a journey or a person who travels a lot.

name.quick_def: The name of a person, place, or thing is the word or group of words that is used to identify them.

suggests.quick_def: If you suggest something, you put forward a plan or idea for someone to think about.

comprise.quick_def: If you say that something comprises or is comprised of a number of things or people, you mean it has them as its parts or members.  [formal]

steps.quick_def: If you take a step, you lift your foot and put it down in a different place, for example when you are walking.

descending.quick_def: If you descend or if you descend a staircase, you move downwards from a higher to a lower level.  [formal]

source.quick_def: The source of something is the person, place, or thing which you get it from.

aquifer.quick_def: In geology, an aquifer is an area of rock underneath the surface of the earth which absorbs and holds water.  [technical]

recedes.quick_def: If something recedes from you, it moves away.

rains.quick_def: Rain is water that falls from the clouds in small drops.

needed.quick_def: If you need something, or need to do something, you cannot successfully achieve what you want or live properly without it.

descend.quick_def: If you descend or if you descend a staircase, you move downwards from a higher to a lower level.  [formal]

reach.quick_def: When someone or something reaches a place, they arrive there.

low.quick_def: Something that is low measures only a short distance from the bottom to the top, or from the ground to the top.

levels.quick_def: A level is a point on a scale, for example a scale of amount, quality, or difficulty.

negotiated.quick_def: If people negotiate with each other or negotiate an agreement, they talk about a problem or a situation such as a business arrangement in order to solve the problem or complete the arrangement.

wells.quick_def: You say well to indicate that you are about to say something.

vast.quick_def: Something that is vast is extremely large.

craters.quick_def: A crater is a very large hole in the ground, which has been caused by something hitting it or by an explosion.

paving.quick_def: If a road or an area of ground has been paved, it has been covered with flat blocks of stone or concrete, so that it is suitable for walking or driving on.

sloping.quick_def: A slope is the side of a mountain, hill, or valley.

tiers.quick_def: A tier is a row or layer of something that has other layers above or below it.

elaborate.quick_def: You use elaborate to describe something that is very complex because it has a lot of different parts.

stepped.quick_def: If you take a step, you lift your foot and put it down in a different place, for example when you are walking.

passages.quick_def: A passage is a long narrow space with walls or fences on both sides, which connects one place or room with another.

leading.quick_def: If you lead a group of people, you walk or ride in front of them.

via.quick_def: If you go somewhere via a particular place, you go through that place on the way to your destination.

storeys.quick_def: A storey of a building is one of its different levels, which is situated above or below other levels.

included.quick_def: If one thing includes another thing, it has the other thing as one of its parts.

pavilions.quick_def: A pavilion is a building on the edge of a sports field where players can change their clothes and wash.  [British]

sheltered.quick_def: A shelter is a small building or covered place which is made to protect people from bad weather or danger.

relentless.quick_def: Something bad that is relentless never stops or never becomes less intense.

heat.quick_def: When you heat something, you raise its temperature, for example by using a flame or a special piece of equipment.

impressive.quick_def: Something that is impressive impresses you, for example because it is great in size or degree, or is done with a great deal of skill.

intricate.quick_def: You use intricate to describe something that has many small parts or details.

decorative.quick_def: Something that is decorative is intended to look pretty or attractive.

sculptures.quick_def: A sculpture is a work of art that is produced by carving or shaping stone, wood, clay, or other materials.

embellish.quick_def: If something is embellished with decorative features or patterns, it has those features or patterns on it and they make it look more attractive.

showing.quick_def: If something shows that a state of affairs exists, it gives information that proves it or makes it clear to people.

fighting.quick_def: If you fight something unpleasant, you try in a determined way to prevent it or stop it happening.

dancing.quick_def: When you dance, you move your body and feet in a way which follows a rhythm, usually in time to music.

combing.quick_def: A comb is a flat piece of plastic or metal with narrow pointed teeth along one side, which you use to tidy your hair.

hair.quick_def: Your hair is the fine threads that grow in a mass on your head.

churning.quick_def: A churn is a container which is used for making butter.

butter.quick_def: Butter is a soft yellow substance made from cream. You spread it on bread or use it in cooking.

thousands.quick_def: A thousand or one thousand is the number 1,000.

fallen.quick_def: If someone or something falls, they move quickly downwards onto or towards the ground, by accident or because of a natural force.

disuse.quick_def: If something falls into disuse, people stop using it. If something becomes worse as a result of disuse, it becomes worse because no one uses it.

derelict.quick_def: A place or building that is derelict is empty and in a bad state of repair because it has not been used or lived in for a long time.

diverted.quick_def: To divert vehicles or travellers means to make them follow a different route or go to a different destination than they originally intended. You can also say that someone or something diverts from a particular route or to a particular place.  [British]

table.quick_def: A table is a piece of furniture with a flat top that you put things on or sit at.

condition.quick_def: If you talk about the condition of a person or thing, you are talking about the state that they are in, especially how good or bad their physical state is.

spells.quick_def: When you spell a word, you write or speak each letter in the word in the correct order.

southern.quick_def: Southern means in or from the south of a region, state, or country.

suffered.quick_def: If you suffer pain, you feel it in your body or in your mind.

eight-year.quick_def: Eight-year means lasting for eight years.

sites.quick_def: A site is a piece of ground that is used for a particular purpose or where a particular thing happens.

undergone.quick_def: If you undergo something necessary or unpleasant, it happens to you.

major.quick_def: You use major when you want to describe something that is more important, serious, or significant than other things in a group or situation.

restoration.quick_def: The Restoration was the event in 1660 when Charles the Second became King of England, Scotland, and Ireland after a period when there had been no King or Queen.

state.quick_def: You can refer to countries as states, particularly when you are discussing politics.

government.quick_def: The government of a country is the group of people who are responsible for governing it.

announced.quick_def: If you announce something, you tell people about it publicly or officially.

june.quick_def: June is the sixth month of the year in the Western calendar.

plans.quick_def: A plan is a method of achieving something that you have worked out in detail beforehand.

restore.quick_def: To restore a situation or practice means to cause it to exist again.

patan.quick_def: Patan is the name of a place, like a city or a town.

capital.quick_def: Capital is a large sum of money which you use to start a business, or which you invest in order to make more money.  [business]

rani.quick_def: an Indian queen; the wife of a raja

ki.quick_def: Ki is a word from some languages, often used in names. It doesn't have a simple general meaning like common English words.

finest.quick_def: You use fine to describe something that you admire and think is very good.

udayamati.quick_def: Udayamati is a name, usually for a person, like a queen or someone else.

late.quick_def: Late means near the end of a day, week, year, or other period of time.

silted.quick_def: Silt is fine sand, soil, or mud which is carried along by a river.

archaeological.quick_def: connected with the study of cultures of the past and of periods of history by examining the parts of buildings and objects found in the ground

restoring.quick_def: To restore a situation or practice means to cause it to exist again.

pristine.quick_def: Pristine things are extremely clean or new.  [formal]

wide.quick_def: Something that is wide measures a large distance from one side or edge to the other.

deep.quick_def: If something is deep, it extends a long way down from the ground or from the top surface of something.

carved.quick_def: If you carve an object, you make it by cutting it out of a substance such as wood or stone. If you carve something such as wood or stone into an object, you make the object by cutting it out.

niches.quick_def: A niche in the market is a specific area of marketing which has its own particular requirements, customers, and products.  [business]

monument.quick_def: A monument is a large structure, usually made of stone, which is built to remind people of an event in history or of a famous person.

incredibly.quick_def: If you describe something or someone as incredible, you like them very much or are impressed by them, because they are extremely or unusually good.  [approval]

january.quick_def: January is the first month of the year in the Western calendar.

survived.quick_def: If a person or living thing survives in a dangerous situation such as an accident or an illness, they do not die.

earthquake.quick_def: An earthquake is a shaking of the ground caused by movement of the Earth's crust.

measured.quick_def: If you measure the quality, value, or effect of something, you discover or judge how great it is.

richter.quick_def: Richter is used in the name of a scale that measures the strength of an earthquake.

surya.quick_def: Surya is the name of the sun god in Hinduism.

kund.quick_def: a tank or small natural or artificial lake where water that has fallen as rain is collected for drinking

modhera.quick_def: Modhera is a place name, which is a specific location.

northern.quick_def: Northern means in or from the north of a region, state, or country.

temple.quick_def: A temple is a building used for the worship of a god or gods, especially in the Buddhist and Hindu religions, and in ancient Greek and Roman times.

king.quick_def: A king is a man who is the most important member of the royal family of his country, and who is considered to be the Head of State of that country.

bhima.quick_def: Bhima is a name, usually for a person.

honour.quick_def: Honour means doing what you believe to be right and being confident that you have done what is right.

god.quick_def: The name God is given to the spirit or being who is worshipped as the creator and ruler of the world, especially by Jews, Christians, and Muslims.

actually.quick_def: You use actually to indicate that a situation exists or happened, or to emphasize that it is true.  [emphasis]

resembles.quick_def: If one thing or person resembles another, they are similar to each other.

tank.quick_def: A tank is a large container for holding liquid or gas.

reservoir.quick_def: A reservoir is a lake that is used for storing water before it is supplied to people.

pond.quick_def: A pond is a small area of water that is smaller than a lake. Ponds are often made artificially.

hallmarks.quick_def: The hallmark of something or someone is their most typical quality or feature.

including.quick_def: If one thing includes another thing, it has the other thing as one of its parts.

sides.quick_def: The side of something is a position to the left or right of it, rather than in front of it, behind it, or on it.

stunning.quick_def: If you are stunned by something, you are extremely shocked or surprised by it and are therefore unable to speak or do anything.

geometrical.quick_def: If something is geometrical, it has shapes like squares, circles, triangles, etc. that follow geometric rules.

formation.quick_def: The formation of something is the starting or creation of it.

terraces.quick_def: A terrace is a row of similar houses joined together by their side walls.  [British]

intricately.quick_def: You use intricate to describe something that has many small parts or details.

shrines.quick_def: A shrine is a place of worship which is associated with a particular holy person or object.

wealth.quick_def: Wealth is the possession of a large amount of money, property, or other valuable things. You can also refer to a particular person's money or property as their wealth.

bundi.quick_def: Bundi is the name of an ancient city.

kilometres.quick_def: A kilometre is a metric unit of distance or length. One kilometre is a thousand metres and is equal to around 0.62 miles.

jaipur.quick_def: Jaipur is the name of a city in India.

renowned.quick_def: A person or place that is renowned for something, usually something good, is well known because of it.

raniji.quick_def: Raniji is a title for a queen or a noble woman in some Indian cultures.

nathavatji.quick_def: Nathavatji is a name of a person.

baoris.quick_def: A baoris is a kind of monument that is often intricately carved.

old.quick_def: Someone who is old has lived for many years and is no longer young.

ruined.quick_def: To ruin something means to severely harm, damage, or spoil it.

abhaneri.quick_def: Abhaneri is the name of an old ruined town.

east.quick_def: The east is the direction which you look towards in the morning in order to see the sun rise.

chand.quick_def: Chand is a proper name, often used for names of places, people or things in some cultures.

oldest.quick_def: Someone who is old has lived for many years and is no longer young.

deepest.quick_def: If something is deep, it extends a long way down from the ground or from the top surface of something.

aesthetically.quick_def: Aesthetic is used to talk about beauty or art, and people's appreciation of beautiful things.

harshat.quick_def: Harshat is a name, often used for a person or a place.

mata.quick_def: a title that is used before the name of a female Hindu spiritual leader or the mother or wife of a Sikh spiritual leader

zigzagging.quick_def: A zigzag is a line which has a series of angles in it like a continuous series of 'W's.

steeply.quick_def: A steep slope rises at a very sharp angle and is difficult to go up.

afar.quick_def: Afar means a long way away.  [literary]

fourth.quick_def: The fourth item in a series is the one that you count as number four.

verandas.quick_def: A veranda is a roofed platform along the outside of a house.

ornate.quick_def: An ornate building, piece of furniture, or object is decorated with complicated patterns or shapes.

overlook.quick_def: If a building or window overlooks a place, you can see the place clearly from the building or window.

neemrana.quick_def: Neemrana is the name of a place.

jaipur-delhi.quick_def: It refers to something related to both Jaipur and Delhi, like a route or connection between these two places.

highway.quick_def: A highway is a main road, especially one that connects towns or cities.  [mainly US]

underwater.quick_def: Something that exists or happens underwater exists or happens below the surface of the sea, a river, or a lake.

colonnaded.quick_def: A colonnaded building has evenly-spaced columns.

openings.quick_def: If you open something such as a door, window, or lid, or if it opens, its position is changed so that it no longer covers a hole or gap.

visitor.quick_def: A visitor is someone who is visiting a person or place.

descends.quick_def: If you descend or if you descend a staircase, you move downwards from a higher to a lower level.  [formal]

neglect.quick_def: If you neglect someone or something, you fail to look after them properly.

monuments.quick_def: A monument is a large structure, usually made of stone, which is built to remind people of an event in history or of a famous person.

medieval.quick_def: Something that is medieval relates to or was made in the period of European history between the end of the Roman Empire in 476 AD and about 1500 AD.

recognised.quick_def: If you recognize someone or something, you know who that person is or what that thing is.

importance.quick_def: The importance of something is its quality of being significant, valued, or necessary in a particular situation.

rich.quick_def: A rich person has a lot of money or valuable possessions.

history.quick_def: You can refer to the events of the past as history. You can also refer to the past events which concern a particular topic or place as its history.

flock.quick_def: A flock of birds, sheep, or goats is a group of them.

far-flung.quick_def: If something is far-flung, it is spread over a large area and far away from each other.

corners.quick_def: A corner is a point or an area where two or more edges, sides, or surfaces of something join.

gaze.quick_def: If you gaze at someone or something, you look steadily at them for a long time, for example because you find them attractive or interesting, or because you are thinking about something else.

marvels.quick_def: If you marvel at something, you express your great surprise, wonder, or admiration.

serve.quick_def: If you serve your country, an organization, or a person, you do useful work for them.

reminder.quick_def: Something that serves as a reminder of another thing makes you think about the other thing.  [written]

ingenuity.quick_def: Ingenuity is skill at working out how to achieve things or skill at inventing new things.

artistry.quick_def: Artistry is the creative skill of an artist, writer, actor, or musician.

civilisations.quick_def: Civilisations are advanced human societies with their own ways of life, cultures, and systems.

existence.quick_def: The existence of something is the fact that it is present in the world as a real thing.

conceive.quick_def: If you cannot conceive of something, you cannot imagine it or believe it.

vigorous.quick_def: Vigorous physical activities involve using a lot of energy, usually to do short and repeated actions.

transport.quick_def: Transport refers to any vehicle that you can travel in or carry goods in.  [mainly British]

physical.quick_def: Physical qualities, actions, or things are connected with a person's body, rather than with their mind.

facilitating.quick_def: To facilitate an action or process, especially one that you would like to happen, means to make it easier or more likely to happen.

teleworking.quick_def: Teleworking is working from home using equipment such as telephones, the internet, and email to contact people.  [business]

teleservices.quick_def: Teleservices are services that are provided through telecommunications, like using the phone or the Internet.

requirement.quick_def: A requirement is a quality or qualification that you must have in order to be allowed to do something or to be suitable for something.

continues.quick_def: If someone or something continues to do something, they keep doing it and do not stop.

determining.quick_def: If a particular factor determines the nature of a thing or event, it causes it to be of a particular kind.  [formal]

factor.quick_def: A factor is one of the things that affects an event, decision, or situation.

spectacular.quick_def: Something that is spectacular is very impressive or dramatic.

union.quick_def: A union is a workers' organization which represents its members and which aims to improve things such as their working conditions and pay.

eu.quick_def: The EU is an organization of European countries which have joint policies on matters such as trade, agriculture, and finance. EU is an abbreviation for 'European Union'.

saw.quick_def: Saw is the past tense of see.

fleet.quick_def: A fleet is a group of ships organized to do something together, for example to fight battles or to catch fish.

concerned.quick_def: Concern is worry about a situation.

due.quick_def: If an event is due to something, it happens or exists as a direct result of that thing.

economy.quick_def: An economy is the system according to which the money, industry, and trade of a country or region are organized.

internal.quick_def: Internal is used to describe things that exist or happen inside a country or organization.

frontiers.quick_def: A frontier is a border between two countries.  [British]

abolished.quick_def: If someone in authority abolishes a system or practice, they formally put an end to it.

stock.quick_def: Stocks are shares in the ownership of a company, or investments on which a fixed amount of interest will be paid.  [business]

phenomenon.quick_def: A phenomenon is something that is observed to happen or exist.  [formal]

emphasised.quick_def: To emphasize something means to indicate that it is particularly important or true, or to draw special attention to it.

relocation.quick_def: If people or businesses relocate or if someone relocates them, they move to a different place.

intensive.quick_def: Intensive activity involves concentrating a lot of effort or people on one particular task in order to try to achieve a great deal in a short time.

costs.quick_def: The cost of something is the amount of money that is needed in order to buy, do, or make it.

though.quick_def: You use though to introduce a statement in a subordinate clause which contrasts with the statement in the main clause. You often use though to introduce a fact which you regard as less important than the fact in the main clause.

site.quick_def: A site is a piece of ground that is used for a particular purpose or where a particular thing happens.

final.quick_def: In a series of events, things, or people, the final one is the last one.

assembly.quick_def: An assembly is a large group of people who meet regularly to make decisions or laws for a particular region or country.

plant.quick_def: A plant is a living thing that grows in the earth and has a stem, leaves, and roots.

users.quick_def: A user is a person or thing that uses something such as a place, facility, product, or machine.

strong.quick_def: Someone who is strong is healthy with good muscles and can move or carry heavy things, or do hard physical work.

expected.quick_def: If you expect something to happen, you believe that it will happen.

candidates.quick_def: A candidate is someone who is being considered for a position, for example someone who is running in an election or applying for a job.

entry.quick_def: If you gain entry to a particular place, you are able to go in.

flows.quick_def: If a liquid, gas, or electrical current flows somewhere, it moves there steadily and continuously.

haulage.quick_def: Haulage is the business of transporting goods by road.  [mainly British]

traffic.quick_def: Traffic refers to all the vehicles that are moving along the roads in a particular area.

exported.quick_def: To export products or raw materials means to sell them to another country.

twice.quick_def: If something happens twice, there are two actions or events of the same kind.

volumes.quick_def: The volume of something is the amount of it that there is.

imported.quick_def: To import products or raw materials means to buy them from another country for use in your own country.

encourages.quick_def: If you encourage someone, you give them confidence, for example by letting them know that what they are doing is good and telling them that they should continue to do it.

rail.quick_def: A rail is a horizontal bar attached to posts or fixed round the edge of something as a fence or support.

modes.quick_def: A mode of life or behaviour is a particular way of living or behaving.  [formal]

sharply.quick_def: A sharp point or edge is very thin and can cut through things very easily. A sharp knife, tool, or other object has a point or edge of this kind.

favour.quick_def: If you regard something or someone with favour, you like or support them.

decreased.quick_def: When something decreases or when you decrease it, it becomes less in quantity, size, or intensity.

benefit.quick_def: The benefit of something is the help that you get from it or the advantage that results from it.

enlarged.quick_def: When you enlarge something or when it enlarges, it becomes bigger.

imperative.quick_def: If it is imperative that something is done, that thing is extremely important and must be done.  [formal]

sustainable.quick_def: You use sustainable to describe the use of natural resources when this use is kept at a steady level that is not likely to damage the environment.

offers.quick_def: If you offer something to someone, you ask them if they would like to have it or use it.

opportunity.quick_def: An opportunity is a situation in which it is possible for you to do something that you want to do.

adapting.quick_def: If you adapt to a new situation or adapt yourself to it, you change your ideas or behaviour in order to deal with it successfully.

objective.quick_def: Your objective is what you are trying to achieve.

gothenburg.quick_def: Gothenburg is a city in Sweden.

integrating.quick_def: If someone integrates into a social group, or is integrated into it, they behave in such a way that they become part of the group or are accepted into it.

considerations.quick_def: Consideration is careful thought about something.

policies.quick_def: A policy is a set of ideas or plans that is used as a basis for making decisions, especially in politics, economics, or business.

shifting.quick_def: If you shift something or if it shifts, it moves slightly.

balance.quick_def: If you balance something somewhere, or if it balances there, it remains steady and does not fall.

heart.quick_def: Your heart is the organ in your chest that pumps the blood around your body. People also use heart to refer to the area of their chest that is closest to their heart.

ambitious.quick_def: Someone who is ambitious has a strong desire to be successful, rich, or powerful.

proposed.quick_def: If you propose something such as a plan or an idea, you suggest it for people to think about and decide upon.

measures.quick_def: If you measure the quality, value, or effect of something, you discover or judge how great it is.

nonetheless.quick_def: Nonetheless means the same as nevertheless.  [formal]

step.quick_def: If you take a step, you lift your foot and put it down in a different place, for example when you are walking.

ideally.quick_def: If you say that ideally a particular thing should happen or be done, you mean that this is what you would like to happen or be done, but you know that this may not be possible or practical.

consumption.quick_def: The consumption of fuel or natural resources is the amount of them that is used or the act of using them.

sector.quick_def: A particular sector of a country's economy is the part connected with that specified type of industry.

blame.quick_def: If you blame a person or thing for something bad, you believe or say that they are responsible for it or that they caused it.

emissions.quick_def: An emission of something such as gas or radiation is the release of it into the atmosphere.  [formal]

greenhouse.quick_def: A greenhouse is a glass building in which you grow plants that need to be protected from bad weather.

gas.quick_def: Gas is a substance like air that is neither liquid nor solid and burns easily. It is used as a fuel for cooking and heating.

done.quick_def: Do is used to form the negative of main verbs, by putting 'not' after 'do' and before the main verb in its infinitive form, that is the form without 'to'.

tonnes.quick_def: A tonne is a metric unit of weight that is equal to 1000 kilograms.

culprit.quick_def: When you are talking about a crime or something wrong that has been done, you can refer to the person who did it as the culprit.

accounts.quick_def: If you have an account with a bank or a similar organization, you have an arrangement to leave your money there and take some out when you need it.

attributable.quick_def: If something is attributable to an event, situation, or person, it is likely that it was caused by that event, situation or person.

alternative.quick_def: If one thing is an alternative to another, the first can be found, used, or done instead of the second.

fuels.quick_def: Fuel is a substance such as coal, oil, or petrol that is burned to provide heat or power.

improving.quick_def: If something improves or if you improve it, it gets better.

ecological.quick_def: Ecological means involved with or concerning ecology.

necessity.quick_def: The necessity of something is the fact that it must happen or exist.

challenge.quick_def: A challenge is something new and difficult which requires great effort and determination.

efforts.quick_def: If you make an effort to do something, you try very hard to do it.

achieve.quick_def: If you achieve a particular aim or effect, you succeed in doing it or causing it to happen, usually after a lot of effort.

modal.quick_def: In grammar, a modal or a modal auxiliary is a word such as 'can' or 'would' which is used with a main verb to express ideas such as possibility, intention, or necessity.  [technical]

shift.quick_def: If you shift something or if it shifts, it moves slightly.

overnight.quick_def: If something happens overnight, it happens throughout the night or at some point during the night.

constant.quick_def: You use constant to describe something that happens all the time or is always there.

deterioration.quick_def: If something deteriorates, it becomes worse in some way.

reached.quick_def: When someone or something reaches a place, they arrive there.

pitch.quick_def: A pitch is an area of ground that is marked out and used for playing a game such as football, cricket, or hockey.  [mainly British]

freight.quick_def: Freight is the movement of goods by lorries, trains, ships, or aeroplanes.

facing.quick_def: Your face is the front part of your head from your chin to the top of your forehead, where your mouth, eyes, nose, and other features are.

marginalisation.quick_def: Marginalisation is the process of making someone or something less important or pushed to the edge of a group or society.

share.quick_def: A company's shares are the many equal parts into which its ownership is divided. Shares can be bought by people as an investment.  [business]

trains.quick_def: A train is a number of carriages, cars, or trucks which are all connected together and which are pulled by an engine along a railway. Trains carry people and goods from one place to another.

struggling.quick_def: If you struggle to do something, you try hard to do it, even though other people or things may be making it difficult for you to succeed.

speed.quick_def: The speed of something is the rate at which it moves or travels.

h.quick_def: H is the eighth letter of the English alphabet.

options.quick_def: An option is something that you can choose to do in preference to one or more alternatives.

consist.quick_def: Something that consists of particular things or people is formed from them.

focusing.quick_def: If you focus on a particular topic or if your attention is focused on it, you concentrate on it and think about it, discuss it, or deal with it, rather than dealing with other topics.

solely.quick_def: If something involves solely one thing or one person, it involves only this thing or this one person and no others.

pricing.quick_def: The price of something is the amount of money that you have to pay in order to buy it.

option.quick_def: An option is something that you can choose to do in preference to one or more alternatives.

accompanied.quick_def: If you accompany someone, you go somewhere with them.  [formal]

complementary.quick_def: Complementary things are different from each other but make a good combination.  [formal]

curb.quick_def: If you curb something, you control it and keep it within limits.

loading.quick_def: If you load a vehicle or a container, you put a large quantity of things into it.

ratio.quick_def: A ratio is a relationship between two things when it is expressed in numbers or amounts. For example, if there are ten boys and thirty girls in a room, the ratio of boys to girls is 1:3, or one to three.

vehicles.quick_def: A vehicle is a machine such as a car, bus, or truck which has an engine and is used to carry people from place to place.

occupancy.quick_def: Occupancy is the act of using a room, building, or area of land, usually for a fixed period of time.  [formal]

lack.quick_def: If there is a lack of something, there is not enough of it or it does not exist at all.

revitalise.quick_def: To revitalize something that has lost its activity or its health means to make it active or healthy again.

baton.quick_def: A baton is a short heavy stick which is sometimes used as a weapon by the police.  [British]

concentrates.quick_def: If you concentrate on something, or concentrate your mind on it, you give all your attention to it.

logistics.quick_def: If you refer to the logistics of doing something complicated that involves a lot of people or equipment, you are referring to the skilful organization of it so that it can be done successfully and efficiently.

investment.quick_def: Investment is the activity of investing money.

infrastructure.quick_def: The infrastructure of a country, society, or organization consists of the basic facilities such as transport, communications, power supplies, and buildings, which enable it to function.

guarantee.quick_def: If one thing guarantees another, the first is certain to cause the second thing to happen.

regional.quick_def: Regional is used to describe things which relate to a particular area of a country or of the world.

cohesion.quick_def: If there is cohesion within a society, organization, or group, the different members fit together well and form a united whole.

uncoupling.quick_def: If two vehicles or pieces of equipment are uncoupled, they have been unfastened and are no longer joined together.

lion.quick_def: A lion is a large wild member of the cat family that is found in Africa. Lions have yellowish fur, and male lions have long hair on their head and neck.

saturated.quick_def: If people or things saturate a place or object, they fill it completely so that no more can be added.

arteries.quick_def: Arteries are the tubes in your body that carry blood from your heart to the rest of your body. Compare vein.

despite.quick_def: You use despite to introduce a fact which makes the other part of the sentence surprising.

polluting.quick_def: To pollute water, air, or land means to make it dirty and dangerous to live in or to use, especially with poisonous chemicals or sewage.

enough.quick_def: Enough means as much as you need or as much as is necessary.

third.quick_def: The third item in a series is the one that you count as number three.

ranging.quick_def: A range of things is a number of different things of the same general kind.

revitalising.quick_def: When you are revitalising something, you are making it become active, healthy and full of energy again.

targeting.quick_def: A target is something at which someone is aiming a weapon or other object.

trans-european.quick_def: If something is trans-European, it involves or covers the whole of Europe from one side to the other.

integrated.quick_def: If someone integrates into a social group, or is integrated into it, they behave in such a way that they become part of the group or are accepted into it.

shares.quick_def: A company's shares are the many equal parts into which its ownership is divided. Shares can be bought by people as an investment.  [business]

looks.quick_def: If you look in a particular direction, you direct your eyes in that direction, especially so that you can see what is there or see what something is like.

bearing.quick_def: If you bear something somewhere, you carry it there or take it there.  [literary]

historical.quick_def: Historical people, situations, or things existed in the past and are considered to be a part of history.

imbalance.quick_def: If there is an imbalance in a situation, the things involved are not the same size, or are not the right size in proportion to each other.

marked.quick_def: A mark is a small area of something such as dirt that has accidentally got onto a surface or piece of clothing.

break.quick_def: When an object breaks or when you break it, it suddenly separates into two or more pieces, often because it has been hit or dropped.

link.quick_def: If there is a link between two things or situations, there is a relationship between them, for example because one thing causes or affects the other.

placing.quick_def: A place is any point, building, area, town, or country.

restrictions.quick_def: A restriction is an official rule that limits what you can do or that limits the amount or size of something.

mobility.quick_def: You use mobile to describe something large that can be moved easily from place to place.

resources.quick_def: The resources of an organization or person are the materials, money, and other things that they have and can use in order to function properly.

inspiring.quick_def: If someone or something inspires you to do something new or unusual, they make you want to do it.

nevertheless.quick_def: You use nevertheless when saying something that contrasts with what has just been said.  [formal]

luxurious.quick_def: If you describe something as luxurious, you mean that it is very comfortable and expensive.

state-of-the-art.quick_def: If something is state-of-the-art, it is the most modern and advanced of its kind.

centres.quick_def: A centre is a building where people have meetings, take part in a particular activity, or get help of some kind.

creative.quick_def: A creative person has the ability to invent and develop original ideas, especially in the arts.

budget.quick_def: Your budget is the amount of money that you have available to spend. The budget for something is the amount of money that a person, organization, or country has available to spend on it.

innovate.quick_def: To innovate means to introduce changes and new ideas in the way something is done or made.

cambridge.quick_def: the main city and administrative centre of Cambridgeshire, England, on the River Cam. It is famous for its university, the second oldest in Britain, and is visited by many tourists.Culture OxbridgeOxbridgeOxbridge is a word made from the names Oxford and Cambridge and is used to refer to the universities of Oxford and Cambridge together.Oxford and Cambridge are the oldest universities in Britain. They are generally also thought to be the best universities to study at. An Oxbridge degree makes a good impression with many employers, and graduates of these universities may have an advantage when applying for jobs. Although efforts are made to attract more students from state schools, many of the undergraduates at each university have been educated at independent schools. The upper class have traditionally sent their children to Oxbridge, and many prime ministers and politicians studied there. To many people, Oxford and Cambridge seem very remote places where only the very privileged can study.Students at Oxford and Cambridge must be accepted at one of around 30 partly independent colleges. Students are chosen after an interview in the college they want to go to. The teachers are called dons. Each college has its own teaching and research staff, who are fellows of the college, and its own buildings, including hall (= where members of the college eat), a library, a chapel, and rooms for students to live in during the term. The buildings are often arranged round a quad (= square). Until the 1970s colleges were single-sex, but now all Oxford colleges and almost all Cambridge colleges are mixed. The universities provide other facilities for all students to use, including laboratories, lecture rooms and libraries.The teaching system is different from that at most other universities. Students have tutorials, called supervisions at Cambridge, at which they read their essays to their tutor, a fellow who is a specialist in what they are studying. There are usually no more than one or two students at a tutorial and tutorials are arranged by the college. Students also go to lectures that are arranged by the university and open to all students. Terms are short, and students are expected to prepare for them in the vacations. Final examinations at Oxford are called schools, and at Cambridge the tripos. Undergraduates at Oxford and Cambridge study for a BA degree, but after a period of time graduates can convert their BA to an MA (Oxon) or an MA (Cantab) without doing any further study. Oxon is short for Oxoniensis, and Cantab for Cantabrigiensis, Latin for 'of Oxford' and 'of Cambridge'.At Oxford students sometimes have to wear gowns (= black robes), at dinner in hall or when they go to see the college principal (= head). When they sit examinations or go to a degree ceremony they have to wear academic dress. This is known as subfusc, and consists of black trousers or skirt, black shoes and socks or tights, a white shirt and a black or white tie. They also wear their gown and a mortar board (= a black hat with a flat, square top) and, when they graduate, a hood that shows their status. At Cambridge students only have to wear gowns when they matriculate (= become members of the university) and at graduation.The two universities are academic rivals, and also compete in debating and sport. The Boat Race, held each year around Easter, attracts national attention. Rugby and cricket teams play against each other in varsity matches, as well as against professional teams.
