santa.quick_def: Santa is a kind-old man in red clothes. People believe he brings gifts to children on Christmas Eve.

ana.quick_def: Ana is a name for a girl.

experts.quick_def: An expert is a person who is very skilled at doing something or who knows a lot about a particular subject.

hotter.quick_def: Something that is hot has a high temperature.

erratically.quick_def: Something that is erratic does not follow a regular pattern, but happens at unexpected times or moves along in an irregular way.

megafires.quick_def: Megafires are very large and serious fires that burn a huge area.

siege.quick_def: A siege is a military or police operation in which soldiers or police surround a place in order to force the people there to come out or give up control of the place.

increasingly.quick_def: You can use increasingly to indicate that a situation or quality is becoming greater in intensity or more common.

burn.quick_def: If there is a fire or a flame somewhere, you say that there is a fire or flame burning there.

acres.quick_def: An acre is an area of land measuring around 4840 square yards or 4047 square metres.

biggest.quick_def: A big person or thing is large in physical size.

acreage.quick_def: Acreage is a large area of farm land.  [formal]

burned.quick_def: If there is a fire or a flame somewhere, you say that there is a fire or flame burning there.

figures.quick_def: A figure is a particular amount expressed as a number, especially a statistic.

news.quick_def: News is information about a recently changed situation or a recent event.

superhot.quick_def: If something is superhot, it is extremely hot.

precipitation.quick_def: Precipitation is rain, snow, or hail.  [technical]

century-long.quick_def: If something is century-long, it lasts for a whole century (100 years).

stop.quick_def: If you have been doing something and then you stop doing it, you no longer do it.

unintentional.quick_def: Something that is unintentional is not done deliberately, but happens by accident.

consequence.quick_def: The consequences of something are the results or effects of it.

halt.quick_def: When a person or a vehicle halts or when something halts them, they stop moving in the direction they were going and stand still.

eradication.quick_def: To eradicate something means to get rid of it completely.  [formal]

underbrush.quick_def: Underbrush consists of bushes and plants growing close together under trees in a forest.  [US]

fuel.quick_def: Fuel is a substance such as coal, oil, or petrol that is burned to provide heat or power.

fahrenheit.quick_def: Fahrenheit is a scale for measuring temperature, in which water freezes at 32 degrees and boils at 212 degrees. It is represented by the symbol ° F.

yearly.quick_def: A yearly event happens once a year or every year.

seasons.quick_def: The seasons are the main periods into which a year can be divided and which each have their own typical weather conditions.

wooded.quick_def: A wooded area is covered in trees.

fire-prone.quick_def: If a place is fire-prone, it is easy for fires to happen there.

ecosystems.quick_def: An ecosystem is all the plants and animals that live in a particular area together with the complex relationship that exists between them and their environment.  [technical]

dominik.quick_def: Dominik is a name for a person.

kulakowski.quick_def: Kulakowski is a surname, which is a family name used to identify a particular family.

adjunct.quick_def: Something that is an adjunct to something larger or more important is connected with it or helps to perform the same task.

biology.quick_def: Biology is the science which is concerned with the study of living things.

graduate.quick_def: In Britain, a graduate is a person who has successfully completed a degree at a university or college and has received a certificate that shows this.

worcester.quick_def: a city in west central England, on the River Severn. It is the administrative centre of the county of Worcestershire. It was an Anglo-Saxon town and has a famous cathedral, which was mostly built in the 14th century. The city is known as the place where Royal Worcester porcelain is produced and it is also one of the cities where the Three Choirs Festival is held.

volcano.quick_def: A volcano is a mountain from which hot melted rock, gas, steam, and ash from inside the Earth sometimes burst.

averaged.quick_def: An average is the result that you get when you add two or more numbers together and divide the total by the number of numbers you added together.

providing.quick_def: If you provide something that someone needs or wants, or if you provide them with it, you give it to them or make it available to them.

terry.quick_def: Terry or terry cloth is a type of fabric which has a lot of very small loops covering both sides. It is used especially for making things like towels and babies' nappies.

mchale.quick_def: McHale is a surname, which is a family name used to identify a particular family.

department.quick_def: A department is one of the sections in an organization such as a government, business, or university. A department is also one of the sections in a large shop.

firefighters.quick_def: Firefighters are people whose job is to put out fires.

dryness.quick_def: If something is dry, there is no water or moisture on it or in it.

fight.quick_def: If you fight something unpleasant, you try in a determined way to prevent it or stop it happening.

incredible.quick_def: If you describe something or someone as incredible, you like them very much or are impressed by them, because they are extremely or unusually good.  [approval]

scorched.quick_def: To scorch something means to burn it slightly.

killed.quick_def: If a person, animal, or other living thing is killed, something or someone causes them to die.

stung.quick_def: If a plant, animal, or insect stings you, a sharp part of it, usually covered with poison, is pushed into your skin so that you feel a sharp pain.

bungling.quick_def: If you bungle something, you fail to do it properly, because you make mistakes or are clumsy.

peculiar.quick_def: If you describe someone or something as peculiar, you think that they are strange or unusual, sometimes in an unpleasant way.

challenges.quick_def: A challenge is something new and difficult which requires great effort and determination.

canyon-hopping.quick_def: Canyon-hopping means moving quickly from one canyon to another.

previously.quick_def: Previously means at some time before the period that you are talking about.

observers.quick_def: You can refer to someone who sees or notices something as an observer.

promises.quick_def: If you promise that you will do something, you say to someone that you will definitely do it.

engines.quick_def: The engine of a car or other vehicle is the part that produces the power which makes the vehicle move.

planes.quick_def: A plane is a vehicle with wings and one or more engines, which can fly through the air.

helicopters.quick_def: A helicopter is an aircraft with long blades on top that go round very fast. It is able to stay still in the air and to move straight upwards or downwards.

fulfilled.quick_def: If you fulfil something such as a promise, dream, or hope, you do what you said or hoped you would do.

unions.quick_def: A union is a workers' organization which represents its members and which aims to improve things such as their working conditions and pay.

complained.quick_def: If you complain about a situation, you say that you are not satisfied with it.

dilapidated.quick_def: A building that is dilapidated is old and in a generally bad condition.

equipment.quick_def: Equipment consists of the things which are used for a particular purpose, for example a hobby or job.

insufficient.quick_def: Something that is insufficient is not large enough in amount or degree for a particular purpose.  [formal]

blueprints.quick_def: A blueprint for something is a plan or set of proposals that shows how it is expected to work.

praising.quick_def: If you praise someone or something, you express approval for their achievements or qualities.

noting.quick_def: A note is a short letter.

funding.quick_def: Funds are amounts of money that are available to be spent, especially money that is given to an organization or person for a particular purpose.

firefighting.quick_def: Firefighting is the work of putting out fires.

cuts.quick_def: If you cut something, you use a knife or a similar tool to divide it into pieces, or to mark it or damage it. If you cut a shape or a hole in something, you make the shape or hole by using a knife or similar tool.

pleased.quick_def: You say please when you are politely asking or inviting someone to do something.  [politeness]

administration.quick_def: Administration is the range of activities connected with organizing and supervising the way that an organization or institution functions.

proactive.quick_def: Proactive actions are intended to cause changes, rather than just reacting to change.

budgetary.quick_def: A budgetary matter or policy is concerned with the amount of money that is available to a country or organization, and how it is to be spent.  [formal]

upgrade.quick_def: If equipment or services are upgraded, they are improved or made more efficient.

traverse.quick_def: If someone or something traverses an area of land or water, they go across it.  [literary]

mammoth.quick_def: You can use mammoth to emphasize that a task or change is very large and needs a lot of effort to achieve.  [emphasis]

serpentine.quick_def: Something that is serpentine is curving and winding in shape, like a snake when it moves.  [literary]

canyon.quick_def: A canyon is a long, narrow valley with very steep sides.

invested.quick_def: If you invest in something, or if you invest a sum of money, you use your money in a way that you hope will increase its value, for example by paying it into a bank, or buying shares or property.

command-and-control.quick_def: Command-and-control refers to a way of managing or leading where someone gives orders and controls what others do.

sieges.quick_def: A siege is a military or police operation in which soldiers or police surround a place in order to force the people there to come out or give up control of the place.

jurisdictions.quick_def: Jurisdiction is the power that a court of law or an official has to carry out legal judgments or to enforce laws.  [formal]

mutual-aid.quick_def: Mutual-aid means people or groups help each other.

communicate.quick_def: If you communicate with someone, you share or exchange information with them, for example by speaking, writing, or using equipment. You can also say that two people communicate.

adequately.quick_def: in a way that is enough in quantity, or good enough in quality, for a particular purpose or need

kim.quick_def: a first name now usually for girls, short for Kimberly or Kimberley

zagaris.quick_def: Zagaris is a surname, which is a family name used to identify a person's family.

chief.quick_def: The chief of an organization is the person who is in charge of it.

emergency.quick_def: An emergency is an unexpected and difficult or dangerous situation, especially an accident, which happens suddenly and which requires quick action to deal with it.

rescue.quick_def: If you rescue someone, you get them out of a dangerous or unpleasant situation.

branch.quick_def: The branches of a tree are the parts that grow out from its trunk and have leaves, flowers, or fruit growing on them.

revamped.quick_def: If someone revamps something, they make changes to it in order to try and improve it.

communications.quick_def: Communications are the systems and processes that are used to communicate or broadcast information, especially by means of electricity or radio waves.

procedures.quick_def: A procedure is a way of doing something, especially the usual or correct way.

statewide.quick_def: Statewide means across or throughout the whole of one of the states of the United States.

response.quick_def: Your response to an event or to something that is said is your reply or reaction to it.

responsive.quick_def: A responsive person is quick to react to people or events and to show emotions such as pleasure and affection.

dedication.quick_def: If you say that someone has dedicated themselves to something, you approve of the fact that they have decided to give a lot of time and effort to it because they think that it is important.  [approval]

coordination.quick_def: Coordination means organizing the activities of two or more groups so that they work together efficiently and know what the others are doing.

codes.quick_def: A code is a set of rules about how people should behave or about how something must be done.

evacuation.quick_def: To evacuate someone means to send them to a place of safety, away from a dangerous building, town, or area.

procurement.quick_def: Procurement is the act of obtaining something such as supplies for an army or other organization.  [formal]

am.quick_def: Am is the first person singular of the present tense of be1. Am is often shortened to 'm in spoken English. The negative forms are 'I am not' and 'I'm not'. In questions and tags in spoken English, these are usually changed to 'aren't I'.

extraordinarily.quick_def: in a way that is unexpected, surprising or strange

witnessed.quick_def: A witness to an event such as an accident or crime is a person who saw it.

randy.quick_def: Someone who is randy is sexually excited and eager to have sex.  [British, informal]

jacobs.quick_def: Jacobs is a common family name. People with this name are called Jacobs.

california-based.quick_def: If a person or an organization is California-based, it means they are located or have their main place in California.

lawyer.quick_def: A lawyer is a person who is qualified to advise people about the law and represent them in court.

evacuate.quick_def: To evacuate someone means to send them to a place of safety, away from a dangerous building, town, or area.

notwithstanding.quick_def: If something is true notwithstanding something else, it is true in spite of that other thing.  [formal]

suffer.quick_def: If you suffer pain, you feel it in your body or in your mind.

endured.quick_def: If you endure a painful or difficult situation, you experience it and do not avoid it or give up, usually because you cannot.

prevention.quick_def: To prevent something means to ensure that it does not happen.

undergo.quick_def: If you undergo something necessary or unpleasant, it happens to you.

transformation.quick_def: To transform something into something else means to change or convert it into that thing.

meaningful.quick_def: If you describe something as meaningful, you mean that it is serious, important, or useful in some way.

traits.quick_def: A trait is a particular characteristic, quality, or tendency that someone or something has.

personality.quick_def: Your personality is your whole character and nature.

looking.quick_def: If you look in a particular direction, you direct your eyes in that direction, especially so that you can see what is there or see what something is like.

identified.quick_def: If you can identify someone or something, you are able to recognize them or distinguish them from others.

qualities.quick_def: The quality of something is how good or bad it is.

admire.quick_def: If you admire someone or something, you like and respect them very much.

loyalty.quick_def: Loyalty is the quality of staying firm in your friendship or support for someone or something.

kindness.quick_def: Kindness is the quality of being gentle, caring, and helpful.

studying.quick_def: If you study, you spend time learning about a particular subject or subjects.

naturally.quick_def: If you say that it is natural for someone to act in a particular way or for something to happen in that way, you mean that it is reasonable in the circumstances.

habitual.quick_def: A habitual action, state, or way of behaving is one that someone usually does or has, especially one that is considered to be typical or characteristic of them.

determines.quick_def: If a particular factor determines the nature of a thing or event, it causes it to be of a particular kind.  [formal]

respond.quick_def: When you respond to something that is done or said, you react to it by doing or saying something yourself.

requires.quick_def: If you require something or if something is required, you need it or it is necessary.  [formal]

mastering.quick_def: A servant's master is the man that he or she works for.

surprising.quick_def: A surprise is an unexpected event, fact, or piece of news.

joy.quick_def: Joy is a feeling of great happiness.

passion.quick_def: Passion is strong sexual feelings towards someone.

experiencing.quick_def: Experience is knowledge or skill in a particular job or activity, which you have gained because you have done that job or activity for a long time.

cultivating.quick_def: If you cultivate land or crops, you prepare land and grow crops on it.

realise.quick_def: If you realize that something is true, you become aware of that fact or understand it.

altered.quick_def: If something alters or if you alter it, it changes.

peterson.quick_def: Peterson is a common family name. People with this name can be anyone in the world.

michigan.quick_def: a northern US state, also called the Wolverine State and the Great Lakes State, because it is divided into two parts by Lake Michigan and Lake Huron, and also has borders with Lake Superior and Lake Erie. The largest city is Detroit, and the capital city is Lansing. Michigan became a state in 1837. Its products include iron and other minerals, cars and cereals (= grains processed as food). Tourists visit the Henry Ford Museum in Dearborn, and Mackinac Island. People who live in the state are called Michiganders.

inherently.quick_def: The inherent qualities of something are the necessary and natural parts of it.

introverted.quick_def: Introverted people enjoy solitary activities and calm environments, and prefer to interact with individuals or in small groups.

reticence.quick_def: a dislike of telling people about things

disastrous.quick_def: A disastrous event has extremely bad consequences and effects.

lecture.quick_def: A lecture is a talk someone gives in order to teach people about a particular subject, usually at a university or college.

hall.quick_def: The hall in a house or flat is the area just inside the front door, into which some of the other rooms open.  [British]

outgoing.quick_def: You use outgoing to describe a person in charge of something who is soon going to leave that position.

entertain.quick_def: If a performer, performance, or activity entertains you, it amuses you, interests you, or gives you pleasure.

my.quick_def: A speaker or writer uses my to indicate that something belongs or relates to himself or herself.

extroverted.quick_def: Someone who is extroverted enjoys interacting with other people.  [mainly US]

fajgenbaum.quick_def: Fajgenbaum is a family name. People use it to tell one family from another.

transition.quick_def: Transition is the process in which something changes from one state to another.

accident.quick_def: An accident happens when a vehicle hits a person, an object, or another vehicle, causing injury or damage.

sports.quick_def: Sports are games such as football and basketball and other competitive leisure activities which need physical effort and skill.

campus.quick_def: A campus is an area of land that contains the main buildings of a university or college.

students.quick_def: A student is a person who is studying at a university or college.

undergoing.quick_def: If you undergo something necessary or unpleasant, it happens to you.

rehabilitation.quick_def: To rehabilitate someone who has been ill or in prison means to help them to live a normal life again. To rehabilitate someone who has a drug or alcohol problem means to help them stop using drugs or alcohol.

suffering.quick_def: If you suffer pain, you feel it in your body or in your mind.

launched.quick_def: To launch a rocket, missile, or satellite means to send it into the air or into space.

action.quick_def: Action is doing something for a particular purpose.

pain.quick_def: Pain is the feeling of great discomfort you have, for example when you have been hurt or when you are ill.

typical.quick_def: You use typical to describe someone or something that shows the most usual characteristics of a particular type of person or thing, and is therefore a good example of that type.

optimist.quick_def: An optimist is someone who is hopeful about the future.

segerstrom.quick_def: Segerstrom is a surname, which is a family name used to identify a particular family.

kentucky.quick_def: a south-eastern US state, also known as the Bluegrass State. The capital city is Frankfort, and the largest city is Louisville. It became a state in 1792. It produces agricultural products, coal and whiskey and is well known for breeding horses for racing. Its tourist attractions include the place where Abraham Lincoln was born (near the village of Hodgenville) and Mammoth Cave National Park, a World Heritage Site since 1981.

recommends.quick_def: If someone recommends a person or thing to you, they suggest that you would find that person or thing good or useful.

train.quick_def: A train is a number of carriages, cars, or trucks which are all connected together and which are pulled by an engine along a railway. Trains carry people and goods from one place to another.

yourself.quick_def: A speaker or writer uses yourself to refer to the person that they are talking or writing to. Yourself is used when the object of a verb or preposition refers to the same person as the subject of the verb.

fortune.quick_def: You can refer to a large sum of money as a fortune or a small fortune to emphasize how large it is.  [emphasis]

outcomes.quick_def: The outcome of an activity, process, or situation is the situation that exists at the end of it.

passionate.quick_def: A passionate person has very strong feelings about something or a strong belief in something.

pursuit.quick_def: Your pursuit of something is your attempts at achieving it. If you do something in pursuit of a particular result, you do it in order to achieve that result.

strongly.quick_def: Someone who is strong is healthy with good muscles and can move or carry heavy things, or do hard physical work.

tanya.quick_def: Tanya is a name for a person, usually a girl or a woman.

streeter.quick_def: A person with the last name Streeter.

freediving.quick_def: Freediving is a sport where people swim deep in the water without using tanks or other breathing equipment.

plunging.quick_def: If something or someone plunges in a particular direction, especially into water, they fall, rush, or throw themselves in that direction.

tanks.quick_def: A tank is a large container for holding liquid or gas.

breathing.quick_def: When people or animals breathe, they take air into their lungs and let it out again. When they breathe smoke or a particular kind of air, they take it into their lungs and let it out again as they breathe.

breath.quick_def: Your breath is the air that you let out through your mouth when you breathe. If someone has  bad breath, their breath smells unpleasant.

minutes.quick_def: A minute is one of the sixty parts that an hour is divided into. People often say 'a minute' or 'minutes' when they mean a short length of time.

stamina.quick_def: Stamina is the physical or mental energy needed to do a tiring activity for a long time.

overwhelming.quick_def: If you are overwhelmed by a feeling or event, it affects you very strongly, and you do not know how to deal with it.

untangle.quick_def: If you untangle something that is knotted or has become twisted around something, you undo the knots in it or free it.

fears.quick_def: Fear is the unpleasant feeling you have when you think that you are in danger.

judgment.quick_def: A judgment is an opinion that you have or express after thinking carefully about something.

competitive.quick_def: Competitive is used to describe situations or activities in which people or firms compete with each other.

freediver.quick_def: A freediver is a person who dives underwater without using breathing equipment.

anywhere.quick_def: You use anywhere in statements with negative meaning to indicate that a place does not exist.

excites.quick_def: If something excites you, it makes you feel very happy, eager, or enthusiastic.

anyone.quick_def: You use anyone or anybody in statements with negative meaning to indicate in a general way that nobody is present or involved in an action.

consuming.quick_def: If you consume something, you eat or drink it.  [formal]

passions.quick_def: Passion is strong sexual feelings towards someone.

psychologist.quick_def: A psychologist is a person who studies the human mind and tries to explain why people behave in the way that they do.

silvia.quick_def: Silvia is a common female name.

carolina.quick_def: Carolina is a place name. There are North Carolina and South Carolina in the United States.

require.quick_def: If you require something or if something is required, you need it or it is necessary.  [formal]

discipline.quick_def: Discipline is the practice of making people obey rules or standards of behaviour, and punishing them when they do not.

rewarding.quick_def: A reward is something that you are given, for example because you have behaved well, worked hard, or provided a service to the community.

todd.quick_def: Todd is a common male first-name.

kashdan.quick_def: Kashdan is a surname. It is the family name of a person.

newcomer.quick_def: A newcomer is a person who has recently arrived in a place, joined an organization, or started a new activity.

tolerate.quick_def: If you tolerate a situation or person, you accept them although you do not particularly like them.

laugh.quick_def: When you laugh, you make a sound with your throat while smiling and show that you are happy or amused. People also sometimes laugh when they feel nervous or are being unfriendly.

ignorance.quick_def: Ignorance of something is lack of knowledge about it.

physician-scientist.quick_def: A physician-scientist is a person who is both a doctor (physician) and a scientist. They can treat patients and do scientific research.

mauro.quick_def: Mauro is a name for a person.

zappaterra.quick_def: Zappaterra is a family name. People use it to identify a particular person or a family.

phd.quick_def: A PhD is a degree awarded to people who have done advanced research into a particular subject. PhD is an abbreviation for 'Doctor of Philosophy'.

miserable.quick_def: If you are miserable, you are very unhappy.

compatible.quick_def: If things, for example systems, ideas, and beliefs, are compatible, they work well together or can exist together successfully.

healing.quick_def: When a broken bone or other injury heals or when something heals it, it becomes healthy and normal again.

taught.quick_def: Taught is the past tense and past participle of teach.

switched.quick_def: A switch is a small control for an electrical device which you use to turn the device on or off.

labs.quick_def: A lab is the same as a laboratory.

cerebrospinal.quick_def: Cerebrospinal means related to the brain and the spinal cord.

nourishes.quick_def: To nourish a person, animal, or plant means to provide them with the food that is necessary for life, growth, and good health.

nervous.quick_def: If someone is nervous, they are frightened or worried about something that is happening or might happen, and show this in their behaviour.

vowed.quick_def: If you vow to do something, you make a serious promise or decision that you will do it.

concentration.quick_def: Concentration on something involves giving all your attention to it.

avoiding.quick_def: If you avoid something unpleasant that might happen, you take action in order to prevent it from happening.

forward.quick_def: If you move or look forward, you move or look in a direction that is in front of you. In British English, you can also move or look forwards.

goals.quick_def: In games such as football, netball, or hockey, the goal is the space into which the players try to get the ball in order to score a point for their team.

hoping.quick_def: If you hope that something is true, or if you hope for something, you want it to be true or to happen, and you usually believe that it is possible or likely.

lunch.quick_def: Lunch is the meal that you have in the middle of the day.

embarrassing.quick_def: If something or someone embarrasses you, they make you feel shy or ashamed.

fascinating.quick_def: If something fascinates you, it interests and delights you so much that your thoughts tend to concentrate on it.

else.quick_def: You use else after words such as ' anywhere', 'someone', and 'what', to refer in a vague way to another person, place, or thing.

pedeleose.quick_def: Pedeleose is a proper name, usually used to call a person.

speaking.quick_def: When you speak, you use your voice in order to say something.

ethically.quick_def: Ethical means relating to beliefs about right and wrong.

intimidating.quick_def: If you describe someone or something as intimidating, you mean that they are frightening and make people lose confidence.

bullying.quick_def: A bully is someone who often hurts or frightens other people.

knowing.quick_def: A knowing gesture or remark is one that shows that you understand something, for example the way that someone is feeling or what they really mean, even though it has not been mentioned directly.

pury.quick_def: Pury is a surname, which is a family name used to identify a person's family.

clemson.quick_def: Clemson is the name of a place, often related to a well-known university.

proves.quick_def: If something proves to be true or to have a particular quality, it becomes clear after a period of time that it is true or has that quality.

motivated.quick_def: If you are motivated by something, especially an emotion, it causes you to behave in a particular way.

fearlessness.quick_def: the quality of not being afraid, in a way that people admire

moral.quick_def: Morals are principles and beliefs concerning right and wrong behaviour.

obligation.quick_def: If you have an obligation to do something, it is your duty to do that thing.

acquire.quick_def: If you acquire something, you buy or obtain it for yourself, or someone gives it to you.  [formal]

faced.quick_def: Your face is the front part of your head from your chin to the top of your forehead, where your mouth, eyes, nose, and other features are.

calm.quick_def: A calm person does not show or feel any worry, anger, or excitement.

mitigate.quick_def: To mitigate something means to make it less unpleasant, serious, or painful.  [formal]

danger.quick_def: Danger is the possibility that someone may be harmed or killed.

documenting.quick_def: A document is one or more official pieces of paper with writing on them.

allegations.quick_def: An allegation is a statement saying that someone has done something wrong.

picking.quick_def: If you pick a particular person or thing, you choose that one.

trait.quick_def: A trait is a particular characteristic, quality, or tendency that someone or something has.

surprisingly.quick_def: Something that is surprising is unexpected or unusual and makes you feel surprised.

description.quick_def: A description of someone or something is an account which explains what they are or what they look like.

evolutionary.quick_def: Evolutionary means relating to a process of gradual change and development.

throwback.quick_def: If you say that something is a throwback to a former time, you mean that it is like something that existed a long time ago.

biologists.quick_def: Biology is the science which is concerned with the study of living things.

reluctant.quick_def: If you are reluctant to do something, you are unwilling to do it and hesitate before doing it, or do it slowly and without enthusiasm.

mindful.quick_def: If you are mindful of something, you think about it and consider it when taking action.  [formal]

backwards.quick_def: If you move or look backwards, you move or look in the direction that your back is facing.

genetics.quick_def: Genetics is the study of heredity and how qualities and characteristics are passed on from one generation to another by means of genes.

enters.quick_def: When you enter a place such as a room or building, you go into it or come into it.  [formal]

scene.quick_def: A scene in a play, film, or book is part of it in which a series of events happen in the same place.

rewritten.quick_def: If someone rewrites a piece of writing such as a book, an article, or a law, they write it in a different way in order to improve it.

throwbacks.quick_def: If you say that something is a throwback to a former time, you mean that it is like something that existed a long time ago.

technical.quick_def: Technical means involving the sorts of machines, processes, and materials that are used in industry, transport, and communications.

atavism.quick_def: An atavism is when a characteristic that an ancestor had comes back in a later generation.

latin.quick_def: Latin is the language which the ancient Romans used to speak.

atavus.quick_def: An atavus is an ancestor in the past.

forefather.quick_def: Your forefathers are your ancestors, especially your male ancestors.  [literary]

ugly.quick_def: If you say that someone or something is ugly, you mean that they are very unattractive and unpleasant to look at.

connotations.quick_def: The connotations of a particular word or name are the ideas or qualities which it makes you think of.

cesare.quick_def: Cesare is a name for a person.

lombroso.quick_def: Lombroso is a person's name. Usually, it refers to Cesare Lombroso, an Italian doctor who had ideas about criminals being born with certain physical features.

italian.quick_def: Italian means belonging or relating to Italy, or to its people, language, or culture.

medic.quick_def: A medic is a doctor or medical student.  [informal]

criminals.quick_def: A criminal is a person who regularly commits crimes.

born.quick_def: When a baby is born, it comes out of its mother's body at the beginning of its life. In formal English, if you say that someone is born of someone or to someone, you mean that person is their parent.

sub-human.quick_def: If someone or something is sub-human, it means they are considered less than human, not as good as normal humans.

measuring.quick_def: If you measure the quality, value, or effect of something, you discover or judge how great it is.

belgian.quick_def: Belgian means belonging or relating to Belgium or to its people.

dollo.quick_def: Dollo is a name, usually used to call a person.

fossil.quick_def: A fossil is the hard remains of a prehistoric animal or plant that are found inside a rock.

coming.quick_def: When a person or thing comes to a particular place, especially to a place where you are, they move there.

irreversible.quick_def: If a change is irreversible, things cannot be changed back to the way they were before.

organism.quick_def: An organism is an animal or plant, especially one that is so small that you cannot see it without using a microscope.

partially.quick_def: If something happens or exists partially, it happens or exists to some extent, but not completely.

stage.quick_def: A stage of an activity, process, or period is one part of it.

stating.quick_def: You can refer to countries as states, particularly when you are discussing politics.

irreversibility.quick_def: Irreversibility means the state that something cannot be changed back to its previous state.

stuck.quick_def: A stick is a thin branch which has fallen off a tree.

law.quick_def: The law is a system of rules that a society or government develops in order to deal with crime, business agreements, and social relationships. You can also use the law to refer to the people who work in this system.

atavisms.quick_def: Atavisms are traits or features that appear again in an organism after not being present for many generations.

root.quick_def: The roots of a plant are the parts of it that grow under the ground.

exceptions.quick_def: An exception is a particular thing, person, or situation that is not included in a general statement, judgment, or rule.

cropping.quick_def: Crops are plants such as wheat and potatoes that are grown in large quantities for food.

humpback.quick_def: A humpback or a humpback whale is a large whale with a curved back.

whale.quick_def: Whales are very large mammals that live in the sea.

pair.quick_def: A pair of things are two things of the same size and shape that are used together or are both part of something, for example shoes, earrings, or parts of the body.

leg-like.quick_def: If something is leg-like, it looks or is similar to a leg.

appendages.quick_def: An appendage is something that is joined to or connected with something larger or more important.  [formal]

metre.quick_def: A metre is a metric unit of length equal to 100 centimetres.

limb.quick_def: Your limbs are your arms and legs.

bones.quick_def: Your bones are the hard parts inside your body which together form your skeleton.

caught.quick_def: If you catch a person or animal, you capture them after chasing them, or by using a trap, net, or other device.

vancouver.quick_def: a city and port in the Canadian province of British Columbia, located on the mainland opposite Vancouver Island. It is the largest city in western Canada and its chief Pacific port.

explorer.quick_def: An explorer is someone who travels to places about which very little is known, in order to discover what is there.

chapman.quick_def: Chapman is a common surname. A surname is a family name passed down from parents to children.

andrews.quick_def: Andrews is a surname. A surname is the family name that people in a family share.

land-living.quick_def: If an animal is land-living, it lives on the land instead of in the water or the air.

ancestor.quick_def: Your ancestors are the people from whom you are descended.

poses.quick_def: If something poses a problem or a danger, it is the cause of that problem or danger.

disappeared.quick_def: If you say that someone or something disappears, you mean that you can no longer see them, usually because you or they have changed position.

millions.quick_def: A million or one million is the number 1,000,000.

reappear.quick_def: When people or things reappear, they return again after they have been away or out of sight for some time.

rudolf.quick_def: Rudolf is a name for a person.

raff.quick_def: Raff is a name, usually used to call a person.

colleagues.quick_def: Your colleagues are the people you work with, especially in a professional job.

indiana.quick_def: a US state in the Middle West which is both agricultural and industrial. It became a state in 1816. Its popular name is the Hoosier State, but nobody knows why. People from Indiana are called Hoosiers, and Americans sometimes joke that they are innocent, old-fashioned farmers. Indianapolis is the capital city and the largest in the state.

usa.quick_def: The USA is an abbreviation for the United States of America.

reasoned.quick_def: The reason for something is a fact or situation which explains why it happens or what causes it to happen.

silent.quick_def: Someone who is silent is not speaking.

somehow.quick_def: You use somehow to say that you do not know or cannot say how something was done or will be done.

long-lost.quick_def: If something or someone is long-lost, they have been gone or not seen for a very long time.

calculate.quick_def: If you calculate a number or amount, you discover it from information that you already have, by using arithmetic, mathematics, or a special machine.

happening.quick_def: Something that happens occurs or is done without being planned.

accumulate.quick_def: When you accumulate things or when they accumulate, they collect or are gathered over a period of time.

mutations.quick_def: If an animal or plant mutates, or something mutates it, it develops different characteristics as the result of a change in its genes.

rendering.quick_def: You can use render with an adjective that describes a particular state to say that someone or something is changed into that state. For example, if someone or something makes a thing harmless, you can say that they render it harmless.

useless.quick_def: If something is useless, you cannot use it.

gene.quick_def: A gene is the part of a cell in a living thing which controls its physical characteristics, growth, and development.

calculated.quick_def: If you calculate a number or amount, you discover it from information that you already have, by using arithmetic, mathematics, or a special machine.

pointed.quick_def: You use point to refer to something that someone has said or written.

mole.quick_def: A mole is a natural dark spot or small dark lump on someone's skin.

salamanders.quick_def: A salamander is an animal that looks rather like a lizard, and that can live both on land and in water.

mexico.quick_def: a country in southern North America

amphibians.quick_def: Amphibians are animals such as frogs and toads that can live both on land and in water.

juvenile.quick_def: A juvenile is a child or young person who is not yet old enough to be regarded as an adult.  [formal]

tadpole.quick_def: Tadpoles are small water creatures which grow into frogs or toads.

metamorphose.quick_def: To metamorphose or be metamorphosed means to develop and change into something completely different.  [formal]

adult.quick_def: An adult is a mature, fully developed person. An adult has reached the age when they are legally responsible for their actions.

axolotl.quick_def: An axolotl is a kind of amphibian that can stay in its juvenile form all its life.

famously.quick_def: You use famously to refer to a fact that is well known, usually because it is remarkable or extreme.

entire.quick_def: You use entire when you want to emphasize that you are referring to the whole of something, for example, the whole of a place, time, or population.  [emphasis]

simplest.quick_def: If you describe something as simple, you mean that it is not complicated, and is therefore easy to understand.

lineage.quick_def: Someone's lineage is the series of families from which they are directly descended.  [formal]

retained.quick_def: To retain something means to continue to have that thing.  [formal]

lineages.quick_def: Someone's lineage is the series of families from which they are directly descended.  [formal]

metamorphosis.quick_def: When a metamorphosis occurs, a person or thing develops and changes into something completely different.  [formal]

salamander.quick_def: A salamander is an animal that looks rather like a lizard, and that can live both on land and in water.

fits.quick_def: If something fits, it is the right size and shape to go onto a person's body or onto a particular object.

frame.quick_def: The frame of a picture or mirror is the wood, metal, or plastic that is fitted around it, especially when it is displayed or hung on a wall.

suggesting.quick_def: If you suggest something, you put forward a plan or idea for someone to think about.

gunter.quick_def: Gunter is a name for a person.

wagner.quick_def: Wagner is a common surname. It can be used to call a person with this family name.

yale.quick_def: Yale is a very famous and old university in the United States.

lizards.quick_def: A lizard is a reptile with short legs and a long tail.

bachia.quick_def: Bachia is a kind of South American lizard.

minuscule.quick_def: If you describe something as minuscule, you mean that it is very small.

limbs.quick_def: Your limbs are your arms and legs.

snakes.quick_def: A snake is a long, thin reptile without legs.

completely.quick_def: You use complete to emphasize that something is as great in extent, degree, or amount as it possibly can be.  [emphasis]

toes.quick_def: Your toes are the five movable parts at the end of each foot.

hind.quick_def: An animal's hind legs are at the back of its body.

legs.quick_def: A person or animal's legs are the long parts of their body that they use to stand on.

toed.quick_def: Your toes are the five movable parts at the end of each foot.

begs.quick_def: If you beg someone to do something, you ask them very anxiously or eagerly to do it.

re-evolved.quick_def: When something re-evolved, it changed and developed again to a new state after it had changed before.

toeless.quick_def: If something is toeless, it doesn't have toes.

digit.quick_def: A digit is a written symbol for any of the ten numbers from 0 to 9.

occasion.quick_def: An occasion is a time when something happens, or a case of it happening.

possibility.quick_def: If you say there is a possibility that something is the case or that something will happen, you mean that it might be the case or it might happen.

independently.quick_def: If one thing or person is independent of another, they are separate and not connected, so the first one is not affected or influenced by the second.

unrelated.quick_def: If one thing is unrelated to another, there is no connection between them. You can also say that two things are unrelated.

dorsal.quick_def: Dorsal means relating to the back of a fish or animal.  [technical]

fins.quick_def: A fish's fins are the flat objects which stick out of its body and help it to swim and keep its balance.

sharks.quick_def: A shark is a very large fish. Some sharks have very sharp teeth and may attack people.

killer.quick_def: A killer is a person who has killed someone, or who intends to kill someone.

whales.quick_def: Whales are very large mammals that live in the sea.

intriguing.quick_def: Intrigue is the making of secret plans to harm or deceive people.

reactivated.quick_def: If people reactivate a system or organization, they make it work again after a period in which it has not been working.

atavistic.quick_def: Atavistic feelings or behaviour seem to be very primitive, like the feelings or behaviour of our earliest ancestors.  [formal]

advantage.quick_def: An advantage is something that puts you in a better position than other people.

degrade.quick_def: Something that degrades someone causes people to have less respect for them.

timescales.quick_def: The timescale of an event is the length of time during which it happens or develops.

lie.quick_def: If you are lying somewhere, you are in a horizontal position and are not standing or sitting.

womb.quick_def: A woman's womb is the part inside her body where a baby grows before it is born.

ancestral.quick_def: You use ancestral to refer to a person's family in former times, especially when the family is important and has property or land which they have had for a long time.

snake.quick_def: A snake is a long, thin reptile without legs.

sprout.quick_def: When plants, vegetables, or seeds sprout, they produce new shoots or leaves.

buds.quick_def: A bud is a small pointed lump that appears on a tree or plant and develops into a leaf or flower.

developmental.quick_def: Developmental means relating to the development of someone or something.

leg.quick_def: A person or animal's legs are the long parts of their body that they use to stand on.

farming.quick_def: Farming is the activity of growing crops or keeping animals on a farm.

practised.quick_def: If you practise something, you keep doing it regularly in order to be able to do it better.

suitable.quick_def: Someone or something that is suitable for a particular purpose or occasion is right or acceptable for it.

raising.quick_def: If you raise something, you move it so that it is in a higher position.

laid.quick_def: Laid is the past tense and past participle of lay1.

indoor.quick_def: Indoor activities or things are ones that happen or are used inside a building and not outside.

hothouse.quick_def: A hothouse is a heated building, usually made of glass, in which plants and flowers can be grown.

tomatoes.quick_def: Tomatoes are small, soft, red fruit that you can eat raw in salads or cooked as a vegetable.

vogue.quick_def: If there is a vogue for something, it is very popular and fashionable.

urgent.quick_def: If something is urgent, it needs to be dealt with as soon as possible.

accommodate.quick_def: If a building or space can accommodate someone or something, it has enough room for them.

cutting-edge.quick_def: Cutting-edge means the most advanced and modern. It describes something that is at the forefront of new development.

proposal.quick_def: A proposal is a plan or an idea, often a formal or written one, which is suggested for people to think about and decide upon.

vertical.quick_def: Something that is vertical stands or points straight up.

farm.quick_def: A farm is an area of land, together with the buildings on it, that is used for growing crops or raising animals, usually in order to sell them.

controlled.quick_def: done or arranged in a very careful way

situated.quick_def: If you situate something such as an idea or fact in a particular context, you relate it to that context, especially in order to understand it better.  [formal]

drastically.quick_def: If you have to take drastic action in order to solve a problem, you have to do something extreme and basic to solve it.

consumers.quick_def: A consumer is a person who buys things or uses services.

farms.quick_def: A farm is an area of land, together with the buildings on it, that is used for growing crops or raising animals, usually in order to sell them.

operate.quick_def: If you operate a business or organization, you work to keep it running properly. If a business or organization operates, it carries out its work.

implemented.quick_def: If you implement something such as a plan, you ensure that what has been planned is done.

proponents.quick_def: If you are a proponent of a particular idea or course of action, you actively support it.  [formal]

promise.quick_def: If you promise that you will do something, you say to someone that you will definitely do it.

renewal.quick_def: If there is a renewal of an activity or a situation, it starts again.

varied.quick_def: Something that is varied consists of things of different types, sizes, or qualities.

year-round.quick_def: If something happens year-round, it happens all through the year without stopping.

eventual.quick_def: You use eventual to indicate that something happens or is the case at the end of a process or period of time.

repair.quick_def: If you repair something that has been damaged or is not working properly, you mend it.

sacrificed.quick_def: If you sacrifice something that is valuable or important, you give it up, usually to obtain something else for yourself or for other people.

horizontal.quick_def: Something that is horizontal is flat and level with the ground, rather than at an angle to it.

granted.quick_def: A grant is an amount of money that a government or other institution gives to an individual or to an organization for a particular purpose such as education or home improvements.

despoiled.quick_def: To despoil a place means to make it less attractive, valuable, or important by taking things away from it or by destroying it.  [formal]

verdant.quick_def: If you describe a place as verdant, you mean that it is covered with green grass, trees, and plants.  [literary]

ecozones.quick_def: Ecozones are areas where the environment and living things are similar.

semi-arid.quick_def: If an area is semi-arid, it is quite dry but not completely dry like a desert.

shelter.quick_def: A shelter is a small building or covered place which is made to protect people from bad weather or danger.

rigours.quick_def: If you refer to the rigours of an activity or job, you mean the difficult, demanding, or unpleasant things that are associated with it.

outdoors.quick_def: If something happens outdoors, it happens outside in the fresh air rather than in a building.

hope.quick_def: If you hope that something is true, or if you hope for something, you want it to be true or to happen, and you usually believe that it is possible or likely.

weather.quick_def: The weather is the condition of the atmosphere in one area at a particular time, for example if it is raining, hot, or windy.

rapidly.quick_def: A rapid change is one that happens very quickly.

floods.quick_def: If there is a flood, a large amount of water covers an area which is usually dry, for example when a river flows over its banks or a pipe bursts.

droughts.quick_def: A drought is a long period of time during which no rain falls.

hurricanes.quick_def: A hurricane is an extremely violent wind or storm.

monsoons.quick_def: The monsoon is the season in Southern Asia when there is a lot of very heavy rain.

toll.quick_def: When a bell tolls or when someone tolls it, it rings slowly and repeatedly, often as a sign that someone has died.

destroying.quick_def: To destroy something means to cause so much damage to it that it is completely ruined or does not exist any more.

tons.quick_def: A ton is a unit of weight that is equal to 2240 pounds in Britain and to 2000 pounds in the United States.

supporters.quick_def: Supporters are people who support someone or something, for example a political leader or a sports team.

artificially.quick_def: Artificial objects, materials, or processes do not occur naturally and are created by human beings, for example using science or technology.

optimum.quick_def: The optimum or optimal level or state of something is the best level or state that it could achieve.  [formal]

weather-related.quick_def: If something is weather-related, it has a connection with the weather.

crop.quick_def: Crops are plants such as wheat and potatoes that are grown in large quantities for food.

failures.quick_def: Failure is a lack of success in doing or achieving something, especially in relation to a particular activity.

pests.quick_def: Pests are insects or small animals which damage crops or food supplies.

organically.quick_def: Organic methods of farming and gardening use only natural animal and plant products to help the plants or animals grow and be healthy, rather than using chemicals.

eliminating.quick_def: To eliminate something, especially something you do not want or need, means to remove it completely.  [formal]

herbicides.quick_def: A herbicide is a chemical that is used to destroy plants, especially weeds.

pesticides.quick_def: Pesticides are chemicals which farmers put on their crops to kill harmful insects.

fertilisers.quick_def: Fertilizer is a substance such as solid animal waste or a chemical mixture that you spread on the ground in order to make plants grow more successfully.

infectious.quick_def: A disease that is infectious can be caught by being near a person who has it. Compare contagious.

interface.quick_def: The interface between two subjects or systems is the area in which they affect each other or have links with each other.

grid.quick_def: A grid is something which is in a pattern of straight lines that cross over each other, forming squares. On maps the grid is used to help you find a particular thing or place.

methane.quick_def: Methane is a colourless gas that has no smell. Natural gas consists mostly of methane.

composting.quick_def: Compost is a mixture of decayed plants and vegetable waste which is added to the soil to help plants grow.

non-edible.quick_def: If something is non-edible, it cannot be eaten safely.

tractors.quick_def: A tractor is a farm vehicle that is used to pull farm machinery and to provide the energy needed for the machinery to work.

ploughs.quick_def: A plough is a large farming tool with sharp blades which is pulled across the soil to turn it over, usually before seeds are planted.

shipping.quick_def: A ship is a large boat which carries passengers or cargo.

drawback.quick_def: A drawback is an aspect of something or someone that makes them less acceptable than they would otherwise be.

artificial.quick_def: Artificial objects, materials, or processes do not occur naturally and are created by human beings, for example using science or technology.

nearest.quick_def: If something is near a place, thing, or person, it is a short distance from them.

reducing.quick_def: If you reduce something, you make it smaller in size or amount, or less in degree.

single-storey.quick_def: A single-storey building has only one floor.

greenhouses.quick_def: A greenhouse is a glass building in which you grow plants that need to be protected from bad weather.

overhead.quick_def: You use overhead to indicate that something is above you or above the place that you are talking about.

facility.quick_def: Facilities are buildings, pieces of equipment, or services that are provided for a particular purpose.

generating.quick_def: To generate something means to cause it to begin and develop.

prohibitively.quick_def: If the cost of something is prohibitive, it is so high that many people cannot afford it.  [formal]

unless.quick_def: You use unless to introduce the only circumstances in which an event you are mentioning will not take place or in which a statement you are making is not true.

renewable.quick_def: Renewable resources are natural ones such as wind, water, and sunlight which are always available.

aspiration.quick_def: Someone's aspirations are their desire to achieve things.

trays.quick_def: A tray is a flat piece of wood, plastic, or metal, which usually has raised edges and which is used for carrying things, especially food and drinks.

rails.quick_def: A rail is a horizontal bar attached to posts or fixed round the edge of something as a fence or support.

operation.quick_def: If you operate a business or organization, you work to keep it running properly. If a business or organization operates, it carries out its work.

address.quick_def: Your address is the number of the house, flat, or apartment and the name of the street and the town where you live or work.

undoubted.quick_def: You can use undoubted to emphasize that something exists or is true.  [emphasis]

detrimental.quick_def: Something that is detrimental to something else has a harmful or damaging effect on it.

regards.quick_def: If you regard someone or something as being a particular thing or as having a particular quality, you believe that they are that thing or have that quality.

skyscrapers.quick_def: A skyscraper is a very tall building in a city.

currently.quick_def: A current is a steady and continuous flowing movement of some of the water in a river, lake, or sea.

rooftops.quick_def: A rooftop is the outside part of the roof of a building.

falkirk.quick_def: Falkirk is the name of a place, like a town or a city.

scotland.quick_def: a country forming the northernmost part of Great Britain and of the United Kingdom

boat.quick_def: A boat is something in which people can travel across water.

lift.quick_def: If you lift something, you move it to another position, especially upwards.

millennium.quick_def: A millennium is a period of one thousand years, especially one which begins and ends with a year ending in '000', for example the period from the year 1000 to the year 2000.  [formal]

navigability.quick_def: the degree to which a river, lake, etc. is wide enough for ships and boats to sail on

reconnecting.quick_def: If a company reconnects your electricity, water, gas, or phone after it has been stopped, they provide you with it once again.

forth.quick_def: When someone goes forth from a place, they leave it.  [literary]

clyde.quick_def: Clyde is a proper name, often used for a person, a place or a thing.

canals.quick_def: A canal is a long, narrow stretch of water that has been made for boats to travel along or to bring water to a particular area.

canal.quick_def: A canal is a long, narrow stretch of water that has been made for boats to travel along or to bring water to a particular area.

joined.quick_def: If one person or vehicle joins another, they move or go to the same place, for example so that both of them can do something together.

locks.quick_def: When you lock something such as a door, drawer, or case, you fasten it, usually with a key, so that other people cannot open it.

enclosed.quick_def: If a place or object is enclosed by something, the place or object is inside that thing or completely surrounded by it.

km.quick_def: km is a written abbreviation for kilometre.

dismantled.quick_def: If you dismantle a machine or structure, you carefully separate it into its different parts.

thereby.quick_def: You use thereby to introduce an important result or consequence of the event or action you have just mentioned.  [formal]

keen.quick_def: If you are keen on doing something, you very much want to do it. If you are keen that something should happen, you very much want it to happen.  [mainly British]

twenty-first-century.quick_def: It refers to the time period from the year 2001 to 2100. It describes things that belong to or are related to this time.

landmark.quick_def: A landmark is a building or feature which is easily noticed and can be used to judge your position or the position of other buildings or features.

fitting.quick_def: If something fits, it is the right size and shape to go onto a person's body or onto a particular object.

commemoration.quick_def: To commemorate an important event or person means to remember them by means of a special action, ceremony, or specially-created object.

lasting.quick_def: You use last in expressions such as last Friday, last night, and last year to refer, for example, to the most recent Friday, night, or year.

symbol.quick_def: Something that is a symbol of a society or an aspect of life seems to represent it because it is very typical of it.

regeneration.quick_def: To regenerate something means to develop and improve it to make it more active, successful, or important, especially after a period when it has been getting worse.

submitted.quick_def: If you submit to something, you unwillingly allow something to be done to you, or you do what someone wants, for example because you are not powerful enough to resist.

tilting.quick_def: If you tilt an object or if it tilts, it moves into a sloping position with one end or side higher than the other.

giant.quick_def: Something that is described as giant is much larger or more important than most others of its kind.

see-saws.quick_def: See-saws are long boards that are balanced in the middle. Two people can sit on each end and go up and down.

monorails.quick_def: A monorail is a system of transport in which small trains travel along a single rail which is usually high above the ground.

winner.quick_def: The winner of a prize, race, or competition is the person, animal, or thing that wins it.

plan.quick_def: A plan is a method of achieving something that you have worked out in detail beforehand.

claimed.quick_def: If you say that someone claims that something is true, you mean they say that it is true but you are not sure whether or not they are telling the truth.

sources.quick_def: The source of something is the person, place, or thing which you get it from.

manmade.quick_def: If something is manmade, it is made by people, not by nature.

notably.quick_def: You use notably to specify an important or typical example of something that you are talking about.

celtic.quick_def: If you describe something as Celtic, you mean that it is connected with the people and the culture of Scotland, Wales, Ireland, and some other areas such as Brittany.

double-headed.quick_def: If something is double-headed, it has two heads.

axe.quick_def: An axe is a tool used for cutting wood. It consists of a heavy metal blade which is sharp at one edge and attached by its other edge to the end of a long handle.

propeller.quick_def: A propeller is a device with blades which is attached to a boat or aircraft. The engine makes the propeller spin round and causes the boat or aircraft to move.

bows.quick_def: When you bow to someone, you briefly bend your body towards them as a formal way of greeting them or showing respect.

pump.quick_def: A pump is a machine or device that is used to force a liquid or gas to flow in a particular direction.

faded.quick_def: When a coloured object fades or when the light fades it, it gradually becomes paler.

obscurity.quick_def: Obscurity is the state of being known by only a few people.

amateur.quick_def: An amateur is someone who does something as a hobby and not as a job.

mckee.quick_def: McKee is a surname, which is a family name used to identify a person's family.

conjunction.quick_def: A conjunction of two or more things is the occurrence of them at the same time or place.  [formal]

sub-aqua.quick_def: Sub-Aqua is related to activities under the water, like diving.

club.quick_def: A club is an organization of people interested in a particular activity or subject who usually meet on a regular basis.

initiated.quick_def: If you initiate something, you start it or cause it to happen.

examine.quick_def: If you examine something, you look at it carefully.

wrecks.quick_def: To wreck something means to completely destroy or ruin it.

hoped.quick_def: If you hope that something is true, or if you hope for something, you want it to be true or to happen, and you usually believe that it is possible or likely.

unsatisfactory.quick_def: If you describe something as unsatisfactory, you mean that it is not as good as it should be, and cannot be considered acceptable.

collaboration.quick_def: Collaboration is the act of working together to produce a piece of work, especially a book or some research.

edgerton.quick_def: Edgerton is a name of a person.

electrical.quick_def: Electrical goods, equipment, or appliances work by means of electricity.

side-scan.quick_def: Side-scan is a way to look at things from the side. It helps to find and see things on the sides.

sonar.quick_def: Sonar is equipment on a ship which can calculate the depth of the sea or the position of an underwater object using sound waves.

shaped.quick_def: The shape of an object, a person, or an area is the appearance of their outside edges or surfaces, for example whether they are round, square, curved, or fat.

excavations.quick_def: When archaeologists or other people excavate a piece of land, they remove earth carefully from it and look for things such as pots, bones, or buildings which are buried there, in order to discover information about the past.

stray.quick_def: If someone strays somewhere, they wander away from where they are supposed to be.

climax.quick_def: The climax of something is the most exciting or important moment in it, usually near the end.

wreck.quick_def: To wreck something means to completely destroy or ruin it.

unaware.quick_def: If you are unaware of something, you do not know about it.

trove.quick_def: A trove is a collection of valuable things.

beautifully.quick_def: A beautiful person is very attractive to look at.

preserved.quick_def: If you preserve a situation or condition, you make sure that it remains as it is, and does not change or end.

artefacts.quick_def: An artefact is an ornament, tool, or other object that is made by a human being, especially one that is historically or culturally interesting.

trust.quick_def: If you trust someone, you believe that they are honest and sincere and will not deliberately do anything to harm you.

formed.quick_def: A form of something is a type or kind of it.

prince.quick_def: A prince is a male member of a royal family, especially the son of the king or queen of a country.

president.quick_def: The president of a country that has no king or queen is the person who is the head of state of that country.

excavation.quick_def: When archaeologists or other people excavate a piece of land, they remove earth carefully from it and look for things such as pots, bones, or buildings which are buried there, in order to discover information about the past.

raise.quick_def: If you raise something, you move it so that it is in a higher position.

aim.quick_def: If you aim for something or aim to do something, you plan or hope to achieve it.

feasible.quick_def: If something is feasible, it can be done, made, or achieved.

go-ahead.quick_def: The go-ahead is the permission or approval to start doing something.

shell.quick_def: The shell of a nut or egg is the hard covering which surrounds it.

lifting.quick_def: If you lift something, you move it to another position, especially upwards.

stages.quick_def: A stage of an activity, process, or period is one part of it.

wires.quick_def: A wire is a long thin piece of metal that is used to fasten things or to carry electric current.

sucked.quick_def: If you suck something, you hold it in your mouth and pull at it with the muscles in your cheeks and tongue, for example in order to get liquid out of it.

downwards.quick_def: If you move or look downwards, you move or look towards the ground or a lower level.

overcome.quick_def: If you overcome a problem or a feeling, you successfully deal with it and control it.

jacks.quick_def: A jack is a device for lifting a heavy object off the ground, for example a car.

centimetres.quick_def: A centimetre is a unit of length in the metric system equal to ten millimetres or one-hundredth of a metre.

slowly.quick_def: Something that is slow moves, happens, or is done without much speed.

hanging.quick_def: If something hangs in a high place or position, or if you hang it there, it is attached there so it does not touch the ground.

freely.quick_def: If something is free, you can have it or use it without paying for it.

suction.quick_def: Suction is the process by which liquids, gases, or other substances are drawn out of somewhere.

surrounding.quick_def: If a person or thing is surrounded by something, that thing is situated all around them.

progressed.quick_def: Progress is the process of gradually improving or getting nearer to achieving or completing something.

hook.quick_def: A hook is a bent piece of metal or plastic that is used for catching or holding things, or for hanging things up.

transferred.quick_def: If you transfer something or someone from one place to another, or they transfer from one place to another, they go from the first place to the second.

undewater.quick_def: If something is underwater, it is below the surface of water.

cradle.quick_def: A cradle is a baby's bed with high sides. Cradles often have curved bases so that they rock from side to side.

positioning.quick_def: The position of someone or something is the place where they are in relation to other things.

locate.quick_def: If you locate something or someone, you find out where they are.  [formal]

stabbing.quick_def: If someone stabs you, they push a knife or sharp object into your body.

guides.quick_def: A guide is a book that gives you information or instructions to help you do or understand something.

bags.quick_def: A bag is a container made of thin paper or plastic, for example one that is used in shops to put things in that a customer has bought.

cushioning.quick_def: A cushion is a fabric case filled with soft material, which you put on a seat to make it more comfortable.

framework.quick_def: A framework is a particular set of rules, ideas, or beliefs which you use in order to deal with problems or to decide what to do.

october.quick_def: October is the tenth month of the year in the Western calendar.

skeleton.quick_def: Your skeleton is the framework of bones in your body.

ready.quick_def: If someone is ready, they are properly prepared for something. If something is ready, it has been properly prepared and is now able to be used.

returned.quick_def: When you return to a place, you go back there after you have been away.

easter.quick_def: Easter is a Christian festival when Jesus Christ's return to life is celebrated. It is celebrated on a Sunday in March or April.

rapu.quick_def: Rapu is part of the name of a place. Rapu Nui is another name for Easter Island.

nui.quick_def: Nui is a proper name, often used for a place. It can refer to a specific island or area.

locally.quick_def: Local means existing in or belonging to the area where you live, or to the area that you are talking about.

statues.quick_def: A statue is a large sculpture of a person or an animal, made of stone or metal.

moai.quick_def: Moai are ancient human-shaped statues. They are very old and look like people.

remote.quick_def: Remote areas are far away from cities and places where most people live, and are therefore difficult to get to.

settled.quick_def: If people settle an argument or problem, or if something settles it, they solve it, for example by making a decision about who is right or about what to do.

kilos.quick_def: A kilo is the same as a kilogram.

landed.quick_def: Land is an area of ground, especially one that is used for a particular purpose such as farming or building.

wheels.quick_def: The wheels of a vehicle are the circular objects which are fixed underneath it and which enable it to move along the ground.

platforms.quick_def: A platform is a flat, raised structure, usually made of wood, which people stand on when they make speeches or give a performance.

identity.quick_def: Your identity is who you are.

thor.quick_def: Thor is a god in Norse mythology. He is very strong and is often shown as a hero who can fight against bad guys with his hammer.

heyerdahl.quick_def: Heyerdahl is a surname. It is the family name of a person.

norwegian.quick_def: Norwegian means belonging or relating to Norway, or to its people, language, or culture.

ethnographer.quick_def: a person who studies different peoples and cultures, with their customs, habits and differences

adventurer.quick_def: An adventurer is a person who enjoys going to new, unusual, and exciting places.

pre-inca.quick_def: Pre-Inca means before the Inca period. It refers to things that happened or existed before the time of the Inca civilization.

bestselling.quick_def: bought by large numbers of people

swiss.quick_def: Swiss means belonging or relating to Switzerland, or to its people or culture.

erich.quick_def: Erich is a name for a person.

von.quick_def: Von is a part of some people's names, often used in German-speaking areas to show a family's noble or important background.

daniken.quick_def: Daniken is a surname. It is the family name of a person.

stranded.quick_def: A strand of something such as hair, wire, or thread is a single thin piece of it.

extraterrestrials.quick_def: Extraterrestrial means happening, existing, or coming from somewhere beyond the planet Earth.  [formal]

linguistic.quick_def: Linguistic abilities or ideas relate to language or linguistics.

definitively.quick_def: Something that is definitive provides a firm conclusion that cannot be questioned.

folklore.quick_def: Folklore is the traditional stories, customs, and habits of a particular community or nation.

tended.quick_def: If something tends to happen, it usually happens or it often happens.

dragged.quick_def: If you drag something, you pull it along the ground, often with difficulty.

arrived.quick_def: When a person or vehicle arrives at a place, they come to it at the end of a journey.

rapa.quick_def: Rapa is a name, often used for a place. It can refer to a specific island or area.

grassland.quick_def: Grassland is land covered with wild grass.

scrawny.quick_def: If you describe a person or animal as scrawny, you mean that they look unattractive because they are so thin.  [disapproval]

pollen.quick_def: Pollen is a fine powder produced by flowers. It fertilizes other flowers of the same species so that they produce seeds.

lake.quick_def: A lake is a large area of fresh water, surrounded by land.

sediments.quick_def: Sediment is solid material that settles at the bottom of a liquid, especially earth and pieces of rock that have been carried along and then left somewhere by water, ice, or wind.

lush.quick_def: Lush fields or gardens have a lot of very healthy grass or plants.

palm.quick_def: A palm or a palm tree is a tree that grows in hot countries. It has long leaves growing at the top, and no branches.

jared.quick_def: Jared is a common male first name.

rapanui.quick_def: Rapanui refers to the people or things related to Easter Island. They are descendants of Polynesian settlers.

polynesian.quick_def: Polynesian refers to the people, languages, or things related to Polynesia, a group of islands in the Pacific Ocean.

settlers.quick_def: Settlers are people who go to live in a new country.

wrecked.quick_def: To wreck something means to completely destroy or ruin it.

fragile.quick_def: If you describe a situation as fragile, you mean that it is weak or uncertain, and unlikely to be able to resist strong pressure or attack.  [journalism]

fertilised.quick_def: When an egg from the ovary of a woman or female animal is fertilized, a sperm from the male joins with the egg, causing a baby or young animal to begin forming. A female plant is fertilized when its reproductive parts come into contact with pollen from the male plant.

windblown.quick_def: You can use windblown to indicate that something has been blown from one place to another by the wind.

ash.quick_def: Ash is the grey or black powdery substance that is left after something is burnt. You can also refer to this substance as ashes.

cleared.quick_def: Something that is clear is easy to understand, see, or hear.

firewood.quick_def: Firewood is wood that has been cut into pieces so that it can be burned on a fire.

scarce.quick_def: If something is scarce, there is not enough of it.

fishing.quick_def: A fish is a creature that lives in water and has a tail and fins. There are many different kinds of fish.

ate.quick_def: Ate is the past tense of eat.

soil.quick_def: Soil is the substance on the surface of the earth in which plants grow.

yields.quick_def: If you yield to someone or something, you stop resisting them.  [formal]

civil.quick_def: You use civil to describe events that happen within a country and that involve the different groups of people in it.

cannibalism.quick_def: If a group of people practise cannibalism, they eat the flesh of other human beings.

collapse.quick_def: If a building or other structure collapses, it falls down very suddenly.

civilisation.quick_def: A civilisation is a developed society with its own culture, laws, and ways of life.

writes.quick_def: When you write something on a surface, you use something such as a pen or pencil to produce words, letters, or numbers on the surface.

worst-case.quick_def: Worst-case means the most bad or difficult situation that could possibly happen.

accelerated.quick_def: If the process or rate of something accelerates or if something accelerates it, it gets faster and faster.

self-destruction.quick_def: Self-destruction is when someone or something destroys themselves.

interprets.quick_def: If you interpret something in a particular way, you decide that this is its meaning or significance.

chieftains.quick_def: A chieftain is the leader of a tribe.

trapped.quick_def: A trap is a device which is placed somewhere or a hole which is dug somewhere in order to catch animals or birds.

lacked.quick_def: If there is a lack of something, there is not enough of it or it does not exist at all.

asserting.quick_def: If someone asserts a fact or belief, they state it firmly.  [formal]
