henderson.quick_def: Henderson is a surname. A surname is the family name that people in a family share.

son.quick_def: Someone's son is their male child.

grandfather.quick_def: Your grandfather is the father of your father or mother. You can call your grandfather 'Grandfather'.

founded.quick_def: Found is the past tense and past participle of find.

chairman.quick_def: The chairman of a committee, organization, or company is the head of it.

landholdings.quick_def: Landholdings are the pieces of land that a person or a group owns.

edinburgh.quick_def: the capital city of Scotland and a popular tourist centre. It has a famous castle, the Scottish Parliament, a zoo (= a place where wild animals are kept for the public to see them), two universities and many museums and art galleries. Other famous features of the city include the Royal Mile and Princes Street. In the 18th century Edinburgh was known as 'the Athens of the north'. The name Edinburgh means 'Edwin's fort'. The city was made a World Heritage Site in 1995. Since 1996 it has been governed as a unitary authority (officially called City of Edinburgh).

farmland.quick_def: Farmland is land which is farmed, or which is suitable for farming.

stayed.quick_def: If you stay where you are, you continue to be there and do not leave.

castle.quick_def: A castle is a large building with thick, high walls. Castles were built by important people, such as kings, in former times, especially for protection during wars and battles.

mansion.quick_def: A mansion is a very large house.

beach.quick_def: A beach is an area of sand or stones beside the sea.

eyemouth.quick_def: Eyemouth is the name of a place, like a town or a village.

murcheston.quick_def: Murcheston is the name of a place.

outskirts.quick_def: The outskirts of a city or town are the parts of it that are farthest away from its centre.

weekends.quick_def: A weekend is Saturday and Sunday.

three-year.quick_def: If something is three-year, it lasts for three years.

apprenticeship.quick_def: Someone who has an apprenticeship works for a fixed period of time for a person who has a particular skill in order to learn the skill. Apprenticeship is the system of learning a skill like this.

accountant.quick_def: An accountant is a person whose job is to keep financial accounts.

emigrated.quick_def: If you emigrate, you leave your own country to live in another country.

agnes.quick_def: Agnes is a female name. People use it to call a girl or a woman.

elder.quick_def: The elder of two people is the one who was born first.

robertson.quick_def: Robertson is a common family name. People with this name can be part of a family or a group in society.

photography.quick_def: Photography is the skill, job, or process of producing photographs.

friend.quick_def: A friend is someone who you know well and like, but who is not related to you.

scottish-canadian.quick_def: A Scottish-Canadian is a person who has both Scottish and Canadian backgrounds or is related to both Scotland and Canada.

photographer.quick_def: A photographer is someone who takes photographs as a job or hobby.

notman.quick_def: Notman is a name of a person.

photographic.quick_def: Photographic means connected with photographs or photography.

excursion.quick_def: You can refer to a short journey as an excursion, especially if it is made for pleasure or enjoyment.

niagara.quick_def: Niagara is the name of a place, which is well-known for its big and beautiful waterfalls.

falls.quick_def: If someone or something falls, they move quickly downwards onto or towards the ground, by accident or because of a natural force.

cooperated.quick_def: If you cooperate with someone, you work with them or help them for a particular purpose. You can also say that two people cooperate.

magnesium.quick_def: Magnesium is a light silvery-white metal which burns with a bright white flame.

flares.quick_def: A flare is a small device that produces a bright flame. Flares are used as signals, for example on ships.

belonged.quick_def: If something belongs to you, you own it.

founding.quick_def: Found is the past tense and past participle of find.

studio.quick_def: A studio is a room where a painter, photographer, or designer works.

spite.quick_def: You use in spite of to introduce a fact which makes the rest of the statement you are making seem surprising.

romantic.quick_def: Someone who is romantic or does romantic things says and does things that make their wife, husband, girlfriend, or boyfriend feel special and loved.

publication.quick_def: The publication of a book or magazine is the act of printing it and sending it to shops to be sold.

circulation.quick_def: If a piece of writing circulates or is circulated, copies of it are passed round among a group of people.

copies.quick_def: If you make a copy of something, you produce something that looks like the original thing.

canadian.quick_def: Canadian means belonging or relating to Canada, or to its people or culture.

portraiture.quick_def: Portraiture is the art of painting or drawing portraits.  [formal]

specialize.quick_def: If you specialize in a thing, you know a lot about it and concentrate a great deal of your time and energy on it, especially in your work or when you are studying or training. You also use specialize to talk about a restaurant which concentrates on a particular type of food.

street.quick_def: A street is a road in a city, town, or village, usually with houses along it.

alive.quick_def: If people or animals are alive, they are not dead.

pursuits.quick_def: Your pursuit of something is your attempts at achieving it. If you do something in pursuit of a particular result, you do it in order to achieve that result.

woodland.quick_def: Woodland is land with a lot of trees.

stream.quick_def: A stream is a small narrow river.

lumber.quick_def: Lumber consists of trees and large pieces of wood that have been roughly cut up.  [mainly US]

steamboats.quick_def: A steamboat is a boat or ship that has an engine powered by steam.

time-consuming.quick_def: If something is time-consuming, it takes a lot of time to do.

souvenirs.quick_def: A souvenir is something which you buy or keep to remind you of a holiday, place, or event.

catering.quick_def: In British English, to cater for a group of people means to provide all the things that they need or want. In American English, you say you cater to a person or group of people.

dublin.quick_def: the capital city of the Republic of Ireland, located on its east coast on the River Liffey. Dublin was the scene of the 1916 Easter Rising against the British, who ruled Ireland from Dublin's 13th-century castle until the south of Ireland became an independent state in 1922. Many great writers and poets have come from Dublin, including Jonathan Swift, Oscar Wilde, George Bernard Shaw, W B Yeats and James Joyce.

philadelphia.quick_def: the fifth largest city in the US and the largest in Pennsylvania. It is a major port on the Delaware River and was established by William Penn. Philadelphia is one of America's most historic cities. It is the place where the Declaration of Independence was signed and the American Constitution was written. Independence Hall and the Liberty Bell are also there.

prizes.quick_def: A prize is money or something valuable that is given to someone who has the best results in a competition or game, or as a reward for doing good work.

lambertype.quick_def: Lambertype is a kind of process used for making pictures, like in photography.

ontario.quick_def: a province of eastern Canada, between Hudson Bay and the Great Lakes. The capital is Toronto.

provinces.quick_def: A province is a large section of a country which has its own administration.

fond.quick_def: If you are fond of someone, you feel affection for them.

wilderness.quick_def: A wilderness is a desert or other area of natural land which is not used by people.

blanche.quick_def: Blanche is a proper name, often used for a person or a place.

lievre.quick_def: Lievre is a French word which means 'hare' in English. A hare is a small animal like a rabbit but with longer ears and legs.

lawrence.quick_def: Lawrence is a name for a person.

principal.quick_def: Principal means first in order of importance.

almost-completed.quick_def: If something is almost-completed, it is nearly finished but not fully done yet.

connecting.quick_def: If something or someone connects one thing to another, or if one thing connects to another, the two things are joined together.

commissions.quick_def: If you commission something or commission someone to do something, you formally arrange for someone to do a piece of work for you.

rogers.quick_def: Rogers is a common family name. People with this name can be men or women.

columbia.quick_def: the first US space shuttle (= spacecraft that can be used again). Its first flight was in 1981 with two astronauts, John Young and Robert Crippen. By 1996 Columbia had made 20 flights and that year made the longest one (more than 405 hours). In 2003 all seven of its crew members died when the space shuttle exploded as it was returning to earth.

administer.quick_def: If someone administers something such as a country, the law, or a test, they take responsibility for organizing and supervising it.

duties.quick_def: Duty is work that you have to do for your job.

photographing.quick_def: A photograph is a picture made using a camera.

victoria.quick_def: a state in south-eastern Australia. The capital is Melbourne.

basement.quick_def: The basement of a building is a floor built partly or completely below ground level.

archives.quick_def: The archive or archives are a collection of documents and records that contain historical information. You can also use archives to refer to the place where archives are stored.

mccord.quick_def: McCord is a proper name, often used for a person or a place.

culmination.quick_def: Something, especially something important, that is the culmination of an activity, process, or series of events happens at the end of it.

award-winning.quick_def: If something is award-winning, it has won an award.

maths.quick_def: Maths is the same as mathematics.  [British]

gadgets.quick_def: A gadget is a small machine or device which does something useful. You sometimes refer to something as a gadget when you are suggesting that it is complicated and unnecessary.

squander.quick_def: If you squander money, resources, or opportunities, you waste them.

mechanically.quick_def: A mechanical device has parts that move when it is working, often using power from an engine or from electricity.

sweeping.quick_def: If you sweep an area of floor or ground, you push dirt or rubbish off it using a brush with a long handle.

reinvention.quick_def: Reinvention is the act of changing something completely to make it new again.

reliance.quick_def: A person's or thing's reliance on something is the fact that they need it and often cannot live or work without it.

exist.quick_def: If something exists, it is present in the world as a real thing.

conditioning.quick_def: If you talk about the condition of a person or thing, you are talking about the state that they are in, especially how good or bad their physical state is.

units.quick_def: If you consider something as a unit, you consider it as a single, complete thing.

ventilation.quick_def: If you ventilate a room or building, you allow fresh air to get into it.

aggressively.quick_def: An aggressive person or animal has a quality of anger and determination that makes them ready to attack other people.

inventors.quick_def: An inventor is a person who has invented something, or whose job is to invent things.

habitable.quick_def: If a place is habitable, it is good enough for people to live in.

usage.quick_def: Usage is the way in which words are actually used in particular contexts, especially with regard to their meanings.

catching.quick_def: If you catch a person or animal, you capture them after chasing them, or by using a trap, net, or other device.

air-conditioned.quick_def: If a place is air-conditioned, it has a system that keeps the air cool and comfortable.

ventilating.quick_def: If you ventilate a room or building, you allow fresh air to get into it.

ingeniously.quick_def: Something that is ingenious is very clever and involves new ideas, methods, or equipment.

hospitals.quick_def: A hospital is a place where people who are ill are looked after by nurses and doctors.

designs.quick_def: When someone designs a garment, building, machine, or other object, they plan it and make a detailed drawing of it from which it can be built or made.

shaw.quick_def: Shaw is a common surname. A surname is the family name that a person shares with other family members.

billings.quick_def: the largest city in the US state of Montana

johns.quick_def: A john is a toilet or bathroom.  [US, informal]

hopkins.quick_def: Hopkins is a common surname. A surname is the family name people share in a family.

digitally.quick_def: Digital systems record or transmit information in the form of thousands of very small signals.

modelling.quick_def: A model of an object is a physical representation that shows what it looks like or how it works. The model is often smaller than the object it represents.

airstreams.quick_def: Airstreams are moving streams of air.

wards.quick_def: A ward is a room in a hospital which has beds for many people, often people who need similar treatment.

theatre.quick_def: A theater is a building with a stage in it, on which plays, shows, and other performances take place.

communal.quick_def: Communal means relating to particular groups in a country or society.

dementia.quick_def: Dementia is a serious illness of the mind.  [medicine]

skill-sets.quick_def: Skill-sets are a group of different skills that a person has.

lamenting.quick_def: If you lament something, you express your sadness, regret, or disappointment about it.  [mainly formal, or written]

disappearance.quick_def: If you refer to someone's disappearance, you are referring to the fact that nobody knows where they have gone.

expertly.quick_def: An expert is a person who is very skilled at doing something or who knows a lot about a particular subject.

panicked.quick_def: Panic is a very strong feeling of anxiety or fear, which makes you act without thinking carefully.

clamouring.quick_def: If people are clamouring for something, they are demanding it in a noisy or angry way.  [journalism]

continuum.quick_def: A continuum is a set of things on a scale, which have a particular characteristic to different degrees.  [formal]

dispositional.quick_def: If something is dispositional, it is related to a person's natural qualities or tendencies.

intrinsically.quick_def: If something has intrinsic value or intrinsic interest, it is valuable or interesting because of its basic nature or character, and not because of its connection with other things.  [formal]

extrinsically.quick_def: If something is done extrinsically, it is because of outside reasons, not from inside yourself.

oriented.quick_def: When you orient yourself to a new situation or course of action, you learn about it and prepare to deal with it.  [formal]

voluntary.quick_def: Voluntary actions or activities are done because someone chooses to do them and not because they have been forced to do them.

pressured.quick_def: Pressure is force that you produce when you press hard on something.

physically.quick_def: Physical qualities, actions, or things are connected with a person's body, rather than with their mind.

non-literal.quick_def: If something is non-literal, it doesn't mean exactly what the words say. It uses words in a different way to show a deeper or different meaning.

make-believe.quick_def: Make-believe is when you pretend something is real, like kids pretending to be pirates.

dimension.quick_def: A particular dimension of something is a particular aspect of it.

playfulness.quick_def: A playful gesture or person is friendly or humorous.

orientation.quick_def: If you talk about the orientation of an organization or country, you are talking about the kinds of aims and interests it has.

pellegrini.quick_def: Pellegrini is a name, usually used to call a person.

blend.quick_def: If you blend substances together or if they blend, you mix them together so that they become one substance.

motives.quick_def: Your motive for doing something is your reason for doing it.

enjoyable.quick_def: Something that is enjoyable gives you pleasure.

joan.quick_def: Joan is a common female name.

goodman.quick_def: Goodman is a common surname. A surname is the family name passed down from parents to children.

detriment.quick_def: If something happens to the detriment of something or to a person's detriment, it causes harm or damage to them.  [formal]

optimal.quick_def: the best possible; producing the best possible results

contexts.quick_def: The context of an idea or event is the general situation that relates to it, and which helps it to be understood.

goal-directed.quick_def: If an activity is goal-directed, it is done with a clear goal in mind and all actions are aimed at achieving that goal.

mid-point.quick_def: A mid-point is the middle place or time between two other places or times.

critically.quick_def: A critical time, factor, or situation is extremely important.

fisher.quick_def: a fisherman (= a person who catches fish, either as a job or as a sport)

hirsch-pasek.quick_def: Hirsch-Pasek is a person's name. People use names to call and identify different individuals.

curriculum.quick_def: A curriculum is all the different courses of study that are taught in a school, college, or university.

co-player.quick_def: A co-player is a person who plays with others in a game or an activity.

commenting.quick_def: If you comment on something, you give your opinion about it or you give an explanation for it.

child-centered.quick_def: If something is child-centered, it focuses on children and their needs, interests, and development.

nicolopolou.quick_def: Nicolopolou is a name of a person.

avenue.quick_def: Avenue is sometimes used in the names of streets. The written abbreviation Ave. is also used.

predominantly.quick_def: You use predominantly to indicate which feature or quality is most noticeable in a situation.

child-directed.quick_def: If something is child-directed, it is led or controlled by a child.

pheidole.quick_def: Pheidole is a kind of ant.

dentata.quick_def: Dentata is a scientific name part. It's often used in the names of animals or plants to describe something with teeth-like parts.

ant.quick_def: Ants are small crawling insects that live in large groups.

south-eastern.quick_def: South-eastern means in or from the direction between south and east.

immortal.quick_def: Someone or something that is immortal is famous and likely to be remembered for a long time.

ysabel.quick_def: Ysabel is a name used for a person, like a girl's name.

giraldo.quick_def: Giraldo is a name used to call a person.

doctoral.quick_def: A doctoral thesis or piece of research is written or done in order to obtain a doctor's degree.

thesis.quick_def: A thesis is an idea or theory that is expressed as a statement and is discussed in a logical way.

age-defying.quick_def: If something is age-defying, it makes you look or seem younger than your real age.

feats.quick_def: If you refer to an action, or the result of an action, as a feat, you admire it because it is an impressive and difficult achievement.  [approval]

naked.quick_def: Someone who is naked is not wearing any clothes.

deteriorate.quick_def: If something deteriorates, it becomes worse in some way.

complexity.quick_def: Complexity is the state of having many different parts connected or related to each other in a complicated way.

mice.quick_def: Mice is the plural of mouse.

worms.quick_def: A worm is a small animal with a long thin body, no bones and no legs.

pupae.quick_def: A pupa is an insect that is in the stage of development between a larva and a fully grown adult. It has a protective covering and does not move.  [technical]

colony.quick_def: A colony is a country which is controlled by a more powerful country.

telltale.quick_def: Something that is described as telltale gives away information, often about something bad that would otherwise not be noticed.

trail.quick_def: A trail is a rough path across open country or through forests.

counting.quick_def: When you count, you say all the numbers one after another up to a particular number.

dish.quick_def: A dish is a shallow container with a wide uncovered top. You eat and serve food from dishes and cook food in them.

tethered.quick_def: If you say that you are at the end of your tether, you mean that you are so worried, tired, and unhappy because of your problems that you feel you cannot cope.

elderly.quick_def: You use elderly as a polite way of saying that someone is old.

caretakers.quick_def: A caretaker is a person whose job it is to look after a large building such as a school or a block of flats or apartments, and deal with small repairs to it.  [British]

trail-followers.quick_def: Trail-followers are people or animals that follow a path or a trail.

attacked.quick_def: To attack a person or place means to try to hurt or damage them using physical violence.

flaring.quick_def: A flare is a small device that produces a bright flame. Flares are used as signals, for example on ships.

mandibles.quick_def: A mandible is the bone in the lower jaw of a person or animal.  [technical]

dying.quick_def: When people, animals, and plants die, they stop living.

mushroom.quick_def: Mushrooms are fungi that you can eat.

density.quick_def: Density is the extent to which something is filled or covered with people or things.

synaptic.quick_def: relating to synapses (= connections between nerve cells)

complexes.quick_def: Something that is complex has many different parts, and is therefore often difficult to understand.

serotonin.quick_def: Serotonin is a chemical produced naturally in your brain that affects the way you feel, for example making you feel happier, calmer, or less hungry.

coincides.quick_def: If one event coincides with another, they happen at the same time.

royal.quick_def: Royal is used to indicate that something is connected with a king, queen, or emperor, or their family. A royal person is a king, queen, or emperor, or a member of their family.

age-related.quick_def: If something is age-related, it has a connection with a person's age and usually happens as people get older.

senescence.quick_def: the process of becoming old and showing the effects of being old

raises.quick_def: If you raise something, you move it so that it is in a higher position.

stays.quick_def: If you stay where you are, you continue to be there and do not leave.

harsher.quick_def: Harsh climates or conditions are very difficult for people, animals, and plants to live in.

comforts.quick_def: If you are doing something in comfort, you are physically relaxed and contented, and are not feeling any pain or other unpleasant sensations.

steep.quick_def: A steep slope rises at a very sharp angle and is difficult to go up.

robinson.quick_def: Robinson is a common surname. A surname is the family name that a person shares with other family members.

urbana-champaign.quick_def: Urbana-Champaign is the name of a place where the University of Illinois is located. It's a combination of two cities' names.

broader.quick_def: Something that is broad is wide.

supplements.quick_def: If you supplement something, you add something to it in order to improve it.

spared.quick_def: You use spare to describe something that is the same as things that you are already using, but that you do not need yet and are keeping ready in case another one is needed.

ostracism.quick_def: Ostracism is the state of being ostracized or the act of ostracizing someone.  [formal]

injuries.quick_def: An injury is damage done to a person's or an animal's body.

counterpart.quick_def: Someone's or something's counterpart is another person or thing that has a similar function or position in a different place.

starvation.quick_def: Starvation is extreme suffering or death, caused by lack of food.

jaws.quick_def: Your jaw is the lower part of your face below your mouth. The movement of your jaw is sometimes considered to express a particular emotion. For example, if your jaw drops, you are very surprised.

nasty.quick_def: Something that is nasty is very unpleasant to see, experience, or feel.

error.quick_def: An error is something you have done which is considered to be incorrect or wrong, or which should not have been done.

colossal.quick_def: If you describe something as colossal, you are emphasizing that it is very large.  [emphasis]

collapses.quick_def: If a building or other structure collapses, it falls down very suddenly.

bred.quick_def: Bred is the past tense and past participle of breed.

fox.quick_def: A fox is a wild animal which looks like a dog and has reddish-brown fur, a pointed face and ears, and a thick tail. Foxes eat smaller animals.

pigeon.quick_def: A pigeon is a bird, usually grey in colour, which has a fat body. Pigeons often live in towns.

documentaries.quick_def: A documentary is a television or radio programme, or a film, which shows real events or provides information about a particular subject.

specimens.quick_def: A specimen is a single plant or animal which is an example of a particular species or type and is examined by scientists.

talks.quick_def: When you talk, you use spoken language to express your thoughts, ideas, or feelings.

presentations.quick_def: You use present to describe things and people that exist now, rather than those that existed in the past or those that may exist in the future.

communication.quick_def: If you communicate with someone, you share or exchange information with them, for example by speaking, writing, or using equipment. You can also say that two people communicate.

outreach.quick_def: Outreach programmes and schemes try to find people who need help or advice rather than waiting for those people to come and ask for help.

educate.quick_def: When someone, especially a child, is educated, he or she is taught at a school or college.

reintroductions.quick_def: Reintroductions are actions of bringing something or someone back to a place where they were before.

variables.quick_def: Something that is variable changes quite often, and there usually seems to be no fixed pattern to these changes.

effected.quick_def: The effect of one thing on another is the change that the first thing causes in the second thing.

oestrus.quick_def: a period of time in which a female animal is fertile and ready to have sex

at-risk.quick_def: If someone or something is at-risk, they are in a situation where they might be harmed or in danger.

bolstered.quick_def: If you bolster something such as someone's confidence or courage, you increase it.

anaesthetics.quick_def: Anaesthetic is a substance that doctors use to stop you feeling pain during an operation, either in the whole of your body when you are unconscious, or in a part of your body when you are awake.

handling.quick_def: A handle is a small round object or a lever that is attached to a door and is used for opening and closing it.

human-animal.quick_def: Human-animal refers to things related to both humans and animals.

conflicts.quick_def: Conflict is serious disagreement and argument about something important. If two people or groups are in conflict, they have had a serious disagreement or argument and have not yet reached agreement.

ongoing.quick_def: An ongoing situation has been happening for quite a long time and seems likely to continue for some time in the future.

educating.quick_def: When someone, especially a child, is educated, he or she is taught at a school or college.

informing.quick_def: If you inform someone of something, you tell them about it.

chelsea.quick_def: a district of London, on the north bank of the Thames west of Westminster. In the 19th and early 20th centuries many artists lived there and it had a reputation as an artistic area. Now it is one of the most fashionable and expensive parts of London to live in.

rochman.quick_def: Rochman is a family name. People with this name can be someone you know or meet.

ecologist.quick_def: An ecologist is a person who studies ecology.

davis.quick_def: Davis is a common surname. A surname is the family name that a person shares with other family members.

dismal.quick_def: Something that is dismal is bad in a sad or depressing way.

terrible.quick_def: A terrible experience or situation is very serious or very unpleasant.

synthesis.quick_def: A synthesis of different ideas or styles is a mixture or combination of these ideas or styles.  [formal]

marine-debris.quick_def: Marine-debris means trash that is in the ocean.

debris.quick_def: Debris is pieces from something that has been destroyed or pieces of rubbish or unwanted material that are spread around.

trash.quick_def: Trash consists of unwanted things or waste material such as used paper, empty containers and bottles, and waste food.  [US]

sounded.quick_def: A sound is something that you hear.

bells.quick_def: A bell is a device that makes a ringing sound and is used to give a signal or to attract people's attention.

warn.quick_def: If you warn someone about something such as a possible danger or problem, you tell them about it so that they are aware of it.

validity.quick_def: A valid argument, comment, or idea is based on sensible reasoning.

conclusions.quick_def: When you come to a conclusion, you decide that something is true after you have thought about it carefully and have considered all the relevant facts.

faulty.quick_def: A faulty piece of equipment has something wrong with it and is not working properly.

strikingly.quick_def: Something that is striking is very noticeable or unusual.

well-designed.quick_def: If something is well-designed, it is made in a good way, with careful planning and good ideas.

mussels.quick_def: Mussels are a kind of shellfish that you can eat from their shells.

ingesting.quick_def: When animals or plants ingest a substance, they take it into themselves, for example by eating or absorbing it.  [technical]

microscopic.quick_def: Microscopic objects are extremely small, and usually can be seen only through a microscope.

bits.quick_def: A bit of something is a small amount of it.

stomachs.quick_def: Your stomach is the organ inside your body where food is digested before it moves into the intestines.

bloodstreams.quick_def: Your bloodstream is the blood that flows around your body.

shellfish.quick_def: Shellfish are small creatures that live in the sea and have a shell.

eating.quick_def: When you eat something, you put it into your mouth, chew it, and swallow it.

bothersome.quick_def: Someone or something that is bothersome is annoying or irritating.  [old-fashioned]

entangled.quick_def: If one thing entangles itself with another, the two things become caught together very tightly.

injuring.quick_def: If you injure a person or animal, you damage some part of their body.

microplastic.quick_def: extremely small pieces of plastic in the environment that come from consumer products and industrial waste

millimeters.quick_def: A millimeter is a metric unit of length that is equal to a tenth of a centimeter or a thousandth of a meter.

toiletries.quick_def: Toiletries are things that you use when washing or taking care of your body, for example soap and toothpaste.

fibers.quick_def: A fiber is a thin thread of a natural or artificial substance, especially one that is used to make cloth or rope.

wash.quick_def: If you wash something, you clean it using water and usually a substance such as soap or detergent.

remnants.quick_def: The remnants of something are small parts of it that are left over when the main part has disappeared or been destroyed.

cutoff.quick_def: A cutoff or a cutoff point is the level or limit at which you decide that something should stop happening.

sea-creature.quick_def: A sea-creature is an animal that lives in the sea.

tissues.quick_def: In animals and plants, tissue consists of cells that are similar to each other in appearance and that have the same function.

turtles.quick_def: A turtle is a large reptile which has a thick shell covering its body and which lives in the sea most of the time.  [British]

ecologically.quick_def: Ecological means involved with or concerning ecology.

disasters.quick_def: A disaster is a very bad accident such as an earthquake or a plane crash, especially one in which a lot of people are killed.

tanker.quick_def: A tanker is a very large ship used for transporting large quantities of gas or liquid, especially oil.

spilling.quick_def: If a liquid spills or if you spill it, it accidentally flows over the edge of a container.

ecologists.quick_def: An ecologist is a person who studies ecology.

slow-moving.quick_def: If something is slow-moving, it moves at a low speed.

garbage.quick_def: Garbage is rubbish, especially waste from a kitchen.  [mainly US]

patch.quick_def: A patch on a surface is a part of it which is different in appearance from the area around it.

conjure.quick_def: If you conjure something out of nothing, you make it appear as if by magic.

cleanup.quick_def: A cleanup is the removing of dirt, pollution, crime, or corruption from somewhere.

suck.quick_def: If you suck something, you hold it in your mouth and pull at it with the muscles in your cheeks and tongue, for example in order to get liquid out of it.

simulations.quick_def: Simulation is the process of simulating something or the result of simulating it.

strategically.quick_def: in a way that is meant to achieve a particular purpose or to gain an advantage

clearing.quick_def: Something that is clear is easy to understand, see, or hear.

misperceptions.quick_def: A misperception is an idea or impression that is not correct.  [US]

strandings.quick_def: Strandings are situations where whales, dolphins or other sea animals are left on the beach and can't get back into the water.

entanglement.quick_def: An entanglement is a complicated or difficult relationship or situation.

killing.quick_def: If a person, animal, or other living thing is killed, something or someone causes them to die.

interrogating.quick_def: If someone, especially a police officer, interrogates someone, they question them thoroughly for a long time in order to get some information from them.

absorbing.quick_def: If something absorbs a liquid, gas, or other substance, it soaks it up or takes it in.

ignoring.quick_def: If you ignore someone or something, you pay no attention to them.

nutmeg.quick_def: Nutmeg is a spice made from the seed of a tree that grows in hot countries. Nutmeg is usually used to flavour sweet food.

myristica.quick_def: Myristica is the name of a kind of plant, like a type of tree.

fragrans.quick_def: If a plant is called fragrans, it has a nice smell.

banda.quick_def: Banda is the name of a place, like an area or a group of islands.

moluccas.quick_def: The Moluccas are a group of islands in northeastern Indonesia.

northeastern.quick_def: Northeastern means in or from the northeast of a region or country.

indonesia.quick_def: a country consisting of a group of islands in South East Asia

thickly.quick_def: Something that is thick has a large distance between its two opposite sides.

branched.quick_def: The branches of a tree are the parts that grow out from its trunk and have leaves, flowers, or fruit growing on them.

dense.quick_def: Something that is dense contains a lot of things or people in a small area.

foliage.quick_def: The leaves of a plant are referred to as its foliage.

oval.quick_def: Oval things have a shape that is like a circle but is wider in one direction than the other.

bell-shaped.quick_def: If something is bell-shaped, it has the same shape as a bell.

pear-shaped.quick_def: If something is pear-shaped, it has a shape like a pear, wider at the bottom and narrower at the top.

encased.quick_def: If a person or an object is encased in something, they are completely covered or surrounded by it.

fleshy.quick_def: If you describe someone as fleshy, you mean that they are slightly too fat.

ripe.quick_def: Ripe fruit or grain is fully grown and ready to eat.

halves.quick_def: Half of an amount or object is one of two equal parts that together make up the whole number, amount, or object.

ridge.quick_def: A ridge is a long, narrow piece of raised land.

purple-brown.quick_def: Purple-brown is a color that is a mix of purple and brown.

shiny.quick_def: Shiny things are bright and reflect light.

surrounded.quick_def: If a person or thing is surrounded by something, that thing is situated all around them.

lacy.quick_def: Lacy things are made from lace or have pieces of lace attached to them.

crimson.quick_def: Something that is crimson is deep red in colour.

aril.quick_def: An aril is a thin covering that grows around a seed.

mace.quick_def: A mace is an ornamental stick carried by an official or placed somewhere as a symbol of authority.

costly.quick_def: If you say that something is costly, you mean that it costs a lot of money, often more than you would want to pay.

cuisine.quick_def: The cuisine of a country or district is the style of cooking that is characteristic of that place.

flavouring.quick_def: The flavour of a food or drink is its taste.

medicinal.quick_def: Medicinal substances or substances with medicinal effects can be used to treat and cure illnesses.

preservative.quick_def: A preservative is a chemical that prevents things from decaying. Some preservatives are added to food, and others are used to treat wood or metal.

importers.quick_def: An importer is a country, firm, or person that buys goods from another country for use in their own country.

arab-venetian.quick_def: Arab-Venetian refers to something related to both Arabs and Venetians.

neighbouring.quick_def: Neighbouring places or things are near other things of the same kind.

subcontracting.quick_def: If one firm subcontracts part of its work to another firm, it pays the other firm to do part of the work that it has been employed to do.  [business]

swiftly.quick_def: A swift event or process happens very quickly or without delay.

quietly.quick_def: Someone or something that is quiet makes only a small amount of noise.

pepper.quick_def: Pepper is a hot-tasting spice which is used to flavour food.

soared.quick_def: If the amount, value, level, or volume of something soars, it quickly increases by a great deal.  [journalism]

voc.quick_def: VOC is a short name for a big trading company called the Dutch East India Company.

richest.quick_def: A rich person has a lot of money or valuable possessions.

army.quick_def: An army is a large organized group of people who are armed and trained to fight on land in a war. Most armies are organized and controlled by governments.

plague.quick_def: A plague is a very infectious disease that spreads quickly and kills large numbers of people.

contagious.quick_def: A disease that is contagious can be caught by touching people or things that are infected with it. Compare infectious.

doctors.quick_def: A doctor is someone who is qualified in medicine and treats people who are ill.

spare.quick_def: You use spare to describe something that is the same as things that you are already using, but that you do not need yet and are keeping ready in case another one is needed.

pennies.quick_def: Pennies is the plural of penny. Pennies is mainly used to refer only to coins, rather than to amounts.

sultans.quick_def: A sultan is a ruler in some Muslim countries.

insisted.quick_def: If you insist that something should be done, you say so very firmly and refuse to give in about it. If you insist on something, you say firmly that it must be done or provided.

neutral.quick_def: If a person or country adopts a neutral position or remains neutral, they do not support anyone in a disagreement, war, or contest.

troops.quick_def: Troops are soldiers, especially when they are in a large organized group doing a particular task.

unprotected.quick_def: An unprotected person or place is not looked after or defended, and so they may be harmed or attacked.

securely.quick_def: If you secure something that you want or need, you obtain it, often after a lot of effort.  [formal]

bandas.quick_def: Bandas are some specific places or areas.

uprooting.quick_def: If you uproot yourself or if you are uprooted, you leave, or are made to leave, a place where you have lived for a long time.

proper.quick_def: You use proper to describe things that you consider to be real and satisfactory rather than inadequate in some way.

punished.quick_def: To punish someone means to make them suffer in some way because they have done something wrong.

lime.quick_def: A lime is a green fruit that tastes like a lemon. Limes grow on trees in tropical countries.

domination.quick_def: To dominate a situation means to be the most powerful or important person or thing in it.

sliver.quick_def: A sliver of something is a small thin piece or amount of it.

compromise.quick_def: A compromise is a situation in which people accept something slightly different from what they really want, because of circumstances or because they are considering the wishes of other people.

treaty.quick_def: A treaty is a written agreement between countries in which they agree to do a particular thing or to help each other.

nutmeg-producing.quick_def: If a place is nutmeg-producing, it can make or grow nutmeg.

manhattan.quick_def: an alcoholic drink made by mixing whisky with vermouth

frenchman.quick_def: A Frenchman is a man who comes from France.

pierre.quick_def: Pierre is a name for a man.

poivre.quick_def: Poivre is a family name. A family name is what a family members share.

mauritius.quick_def: an island in the Indian Ocean which is a member of the Commonwealth. Before it became independent in 1968, it was at various times a colony of the Netherlands, France, and finally Britain. Its main industries are sugar and tourism.

thrived.quick_def: If someone or something thrives, they do well and are successful, healthy, or strong.

grenada.quick_def: a country consisting of the island of Grenada and a group of smaller islands in the Caribbean. It has been an independent state and a member of the Commonwealth since 1974. In 1983, after the Prime Minister had been killed, Grenada was attacked and taken over by US armed forces, who set up a new government. Many people around the world protested against the US action.

tsunami.quick_def: A tsunami is a very large wave, often caused by an earthquake, that flows onto the land and destroys things.

transplanting.quick_def: A transplant is a medical operation in which a part of a person's body is replaced because it is diseased.

malaysia.quick_def: a country in south-east Asia. It consists of the area to the south of Thailand known in the past as Malaya, and the states of Sarawak and Sabah in the north-west of the island of Borneo. Its capital city is Kuala Lumpur and its official language is Malay. It was formed in 1963 from former British colonies in the area and is now a part of the Commonwealth. Its main exports are oil, gas, electronic equipment and chemicals. Singapore was a part of Malaysia until 1965.

sri.quick_def: a title used before the names of gods or holy books, showing respect

lanka.quick_def: Lanka is another name for Sri Lanka, which is an island country in South Asia.

automotive.quick_def: Automotive is used to refer to things relating to cars.

automation.quick_def: To automate a factory, office, or process means to put in machines which can do the work instead of people.

implementation.quick_def: If you implement something such as a plan, you ensure that what has been planned is done.

robotic.quick_def: Robotic equipment can perform certain tasks automatically.

savings.quick_def: A saving is a reduction in the amount of time or money that is used or needed.

reliability.quick_def: the quality of being able to be trusted to do what somebody wants or needs

flexibility.quick_def: the ability to change to suit new conditions or situations

vehicle.quick_def: A vehicle is a machine such as a car, bus, or truck which has an engine and is used to carry people from place to place.

self-driving.quick_def: If a vehicle is self-driving, it can move by itself without a person driving it.

assistance.quick_def: If you give someone assistance, you help them do a job or task by doing part of the work for them.

trialling.quick_def: When you are trialling something, you are testing it to see if it works well or is suitable.

pace.quick_def: The pace of something is the speed at which it happens or is done.

advancing.quick_def: To advance means to move forward, often in order to attack someone.

fast.quick_def: Fast means happening, moving, or doing something at great speed. You also use fast in questions or statements about speed.

collisions.quick_def: A collision occurs when a moving object crashes into something.

contributory.quick_def: A contributory factor of a problem or accident is one of the things which caused it to exist or happen.  [formal]

socialise.quick_def: If you socialize, you meet other people socially, for example at parties.

relax.quick_def: If you relax or if something relaxes you, you feel more calm and less worried or tense.

disabled.quick_def: If an injury or illness disables someone, it affects them so badly that it restricts the way that they can live their life.

parked.quick_def: A park is a public area of land with grass and trees, usually in a town, where people go in order to relax and enjoy themselves.

car-sharing.quick_def: Car-sharing is a way where people share a car instead of each person having their own car. They can use the car when they need it and share the cost.

sharing.quick_def: A company's shares are the many equal parts into which its ownership is divided. Shares can be bought by people as an investment.  [business]

partly.quick_def: You use partly to indicate that something happens or exists to some extent, but not completely.

consecutive.quick_def: Consecutive periods of time or events happen one after the other without interruption.

quit.quick_def: If you quit your job, you choose to leave it.  [informal]

replicated.quick_def: If you replicate someone's experiment, work, or research, you do it yourself in exactly the same way.  [formal]

multiplication.quick_def: Multiplication is the process of calculating the total of one number multiplied by another.

relieve.quick_def: If something relieves an unpleasant feeling or situation, it makes it less unpleasant or causes it to disappear completely.

distract.quick_def: If something distracts you or your attention from something, it takes your attention away from it.

conclude.quick_def: If you conclude that something is true, you decide that it is true using the facts you know as a basis.

energising.quick_def: If something is energising, it makes you feel full of energy.

leeds.quick_def: a city in West Yorkshire, England. In the 16th century it began to be an important centre for the production of woollen cloth, and later became a centre of the Industrial Revolution. The Leeds and Liverpool Canal was opened in 1816. It remains an important industrial city. Its famous buildings include the Town Hall (1853-8), the City Art Gallery (1888) and Armley Mills, a museum of local industrial history. The Royal Armouries Museum opened there in 1996 and Thackray's Medical Museum in 1997. There are two universities in the city. The Leeds International Pianoforte Competition, open to professional piano players under 30, was started in 1963 and held in the city every three years.

grammar.quick_def: Grammar is the ways that words can be put together in order to make sentences.

gostick.quick_def: Gostick is a name, usually for a person.

sculptor.quick_def: A sculptor is someone who creates sculptures.

complied.quick_def: If someone or something complies with an order or set of rules, they are in accordance with what is required or expected.

father.quick_def: Your father is your male parent. You can also call someone your father if he brings you up as if he was this man. You can call your father 'Father'.

schoolteacher.quick_def: A schoolteacher is a teacher in a school.

enrolled.quick_def: If you enrol or are enrolled at an institution or on a course, you officially join it and pay a fee for it.

scholarship.quick_def: If you get a scholarship to a school or university, your studies are paid for by the school or university or by some other organization.

wide-ranging.quick_def: If something is wide-ranging, it covers a lot of different things or areas.

egyptian.quick_def: Egyptian means belonging or relating to Egypt or to its people, language, or culture.

african.quick_def: African means belonging or relating to the continent of Africa, or to its countries or people.

graduating.quick_def: In Britain, a graduate is a person who has successfully completed a degree at a university or college and has received a certificate that shows this.

trocadero.quick_def: Trocadero is a place name, usually referring to a specific location in Paris.

mayan.quick_def: Mayan refers to the people, language, or things related to the ancient Mayan civilization.

spirit.quick_def: Your spirit is the part of you that is not physical and that consists of your character and feelings.

reclining.quick_def: If you recline on something, you sit or lie on it with the upper part of your body supported at an angle.

knees.quick_def: Your knee is the place where your leg bends.

drawn.quick_def: When you draw, or when you draw something, you use a pencil or pen to produce a picture, pattern, or diagram.

originality.quick_def: You use original when referring to something that existed at the beginning of a process or activity, or the characteristics that something had when it began or was made.

possessed.quick_def: If you possess something, you have it or own it.

mother-and-child.quick_def: It refers to a combination of a mother and her child.

masks.quick_def: A mask is a piece of cloth or other material, which you wear over your face so that people cannot see who you are, or so that you look like someone or something else.

merits.quick_def: If something has merit, it has good or worthwhile qualities.

enthusiastically.quick_def: If you are enthusiastic about something, you show how much you like or enjoy it by the way that you behave and talk.

welcomed.quick_def: If you welcome someone, you greet them in a friendly way when they arrive somewhere.

fellow.quick_def: You use fellow to describe people who are in the same situation as you, or people you feel you have something in common with.

sculptors.quick_def: A sculptor is someone who creates sculptures.

reviews.quick_def: A review of a situation or system is its formal examination by people in authority. This is usually done in order to see whether it can be improved or corrected.

resignation.quick_def: Your resignation is a formal statement of your intention to leave a job or position.

expired.quick_def: When something such as a contract, deadline, or visa expires, it comes to an end or is no longer valid.

pablo.quick_def: Pablo is a common male name. It is used to call a man.

picasso.quick_def: Picasso is a very famous Spanish artist. Many people know and like his paintings.

sketchbooks.quick_def: A sketchbook is a book of plain paper for drawing on.

resemblance.quick_def: If there is a resemblance between two people or things, they are similar to each other.

farmhouse.quick_def: A farmhouse is the main house on a farm, usually where the farmer lives.

sketches.quick_def: A sketch is a drawing that is done quickly without a lot of details. Artists often use sketches as a preparation for a more detailed painting or drawing.

miners.quick_def: A miner is a person who works underground in mines in order to obtain minerals such as coal, diamonds, or gold.

harlow.quick_def: Harlow is the name of a town. A town is a place where many people live and there are shops, houses, etc.

signifies.quick_def: If an event, a sign, or a symbol signifies something, it is a sign of that thing or represents that thing.

experimentation.quick_def: An experiment is a scientific test which is done in order to discover what happens to something in particular conditions.

humanistic.quick_def: A humanistic idea, condition, or practice relates to humanism.

issued.quick_def: An issue is an important subject that people are arguing about or discussing.

editions.quick_def: An edition is a particular version of a book, magazine, or newspaper that is printed at one time.

demanded.quick_def: If you demand something such as information or action, you ask for it in a very forceful way.

critics.quick_def: A critic is a person who writes about and expresses opinions about things such as books, films, music, or art.

angular.quick_def: Angular things have shapes that seem to contain a lot of straight lines and sharp points.

pierced.quick_def: If a sharp object pierces something, or if you pierce something with a sharp object, the object goes into it and makes a hole in it.

impression.quick_def: Your impression of a person or thing is what you think they are like, usually after having seen or heard them. Your impression of a situation is what you think is going on.

warrior.quick_def: A warrior is a fighter or soldier, especially one in former times who was very brave and experienced in fighting.

shield.quick_def: Something or someone which is a shield against a particular danger or risk provides protection from it.

owe.quick_def: If you owe money to someone, they have lent it to you and you have not yet paid it back. You can also say that the money is owing.

acclaim.quick_def: If someone or something is acclaimed, they are praised enthusiastically.  [formal]

thailand.quick_def: a country in South East Asia

janssen.quick_def: Janssen is a common surname. A surname is the family name that a person shares with other family members.

rooftop.quick_def: A rooftop is the outside part of the roof of a building.

portable.quick_def: A portable machine or device is designed to be easily carried or moved.

purify.quick_def: If you purify a substance, you make it pure by removing any harmful, dirty, or inferior substances from it.

desolenator.quick_def: A Desolenator is a machine that can turn dirty water like sea-water into clean water for people to drink.

desalination.quick_def: Desalination is the process of removing salt from sea water so that it can be used for drinking, or for watering crops.

boreholes.quick_def: A borehole is a deep round hole made by a special tool or machine, especially one that is made in the ground when searching for oil or water.

polluted.quick_def: To pollute water, air, or land means to make it dirty and dangerous to live in or to use, especially with poisonous chemicals or sewage.

seawater.quick_def: water from the sea, which contains salt

emirates.quick_def: An emirate is a country that is ruled by an emir.

confronted.quick_def: If you are confronted with a problem, task, or difficulty, you have to deal with it.

footprint.quick_def: A footprint is a mark in the shape of a foot that a person or animal makes in or on a surface.

gulf.quick_def: A gulf is an important or significant difference between two people, things, or groups.

sustain.quick_def: If you sustain something, you continue it or maintain it for a period of time.

pipe.quick_def: A pipe is a long, round, hollow object, usually made of metal or plastic, through which a liquid or gas can flow.

thin.quick_def: Something that is thin is much narrower than it is long.

sheet.quick_def: A sheet is a large rectangular piece of cotton or other cloth that you sleep on or cover yourself with in a bed.

glazing.quick_def: A glaze is a thin layer of liquid which is put on a piece of pottery and becomes hard and shiny when the pottery is heated in a very hot oven.

panel.quick_def: A panel is a small group of people who are chosen to do something, for example to discuss something in public or to make a decision.

heated.quick_def: When you heat something, you raise its temperature, for example by using a flame or a special piece of equipment.

boiler.quick_def: A boiler is a device which burns gas, oil, electricity, or coal in order to provide hot water, especially for the central heating in a building.

solar-powered.quick_def: If something is solar-powered, it gets its power from the sun.

battery.quick_def: Batteries are small devices that provide the power for electrical items such as torches and children's toys.

converted.quick_def: If one thing is converted or converts into another, it is changed into a different form.

filter.quick_def: To filter a substance means to pass it through a device which is designed to remove certain particles contained in it.

shaken.quick_def: If you shake something, you hold it and move it quickly backwards and forwards or up and down. You can also shake a person, for example, because you are angry with them or because you want them to wake up.

fluoride.quick_def: Fluoride is a mixture of chemicals that is sometimes added to drinking water and toothpaste because it is considered to be good for people's teeth.

transmitted.quick_def: When radio and television programmes, computer data, or other electronic messages are transmitted, they are sent from one place to another, using wires, radio waves, or satellites.

servicing.quick_def: A service is something that the public needs, such as transport, communications facilities, hospitals, or energy supplies, which is provided in a planned and organized way by the government or an official body.

two-thirds.quick_def: Two-thirds means two parts out of three equal parts. For example, if you divide a pizza into three equal slices and take two of them, you take two-thirds of the pizza.

scarcity.quick_def: If there is a scarcity of something, there is not enough of it for the people who need it or want it.  [formal]

maintenance.quick_def: The maintenance of a building, vehicle, road, or machine is the process of keeping it in good condition by regularly checking it and repairing it when necessary.

diesel.quick_def: Diesel or diesel oil is the heavy oil used in a diesel engine.

homeowners.quick_def: A homeowner is a person who owns the house or apartment that they live in.

self-sufficient.quick_def: If a person or a place is self-sufficient, they can provide everything they need by themselves without help from others.

outright.quick_def: You use outright to describe behaviour and actions that are open and direct, rather than indirect.

microfinance.quick_def: Microfinance is the same as microcredit.  [business]

middle-income.quick_def: If you are middle-income, you earn an amount of money that is in the middle level compared to others. It's not very high and not very low.

lease.quick_def: A lease is a legal agreement by which the owner of a building, a piece of land, or something such as a car allows someone else to use it for a period of time in return for money.

fridge.quick_def: A fridge is a large metal container which is kept cool, usually by electricity, so that food that is put in it stays fresh.  [mainly British]

roof.quick_def: The roof of a building is the covering on top of it that protects the people and things inside from the weather.

municipal.quick_def: Municipal means associated with or belonging to a city or town that has its own local government.

unavailable.quick_def: When things or people are unavailable, you cannot obtain them, meet them, or talk to them.

envisioned.quick_def: If you envision something, you envisage it.  [US, also British, literary]

humanitarian.quick_def: If a person or society has humanitarian ideas or behaviour, they try to avoid making people suffer or they help people who are suffering.

proceed.quick_def: If you proceed to do something, you do it, often after doing something else first.

uae.quick_def: UAE is a short name for the United Arab Emirates, which is a country in the Middle East.

chile.quick_def: a country in western South America

texas.quick_def: a large south-western US state, also called the Lone Star State because it was once an independent republic. It has the second largest population of all US states. Its biggest cities are Houston, San Antonio and Dallas, and the capital city is Austin. Texas became independent of Mexico in 1836 and a US state in 1845. It was also one of the Confederate States. It has been well known for its cowboys and now produces a lot of oil and gas as well as beef and many agricultural products. Tourists visit the Alamo, Big Bend National Park and the Lyndon B Johnson Space Center.

fairy.quick_def: A fairy is an imaginary creature with magical powers. Fairies are often represented as small people with wings.

tales.quick_def: A tale is a story, often involving magic or exciting events.

hood.quick_def: A hood is a part of a coat which you can pull up to cover your head. It is in the shape of a triangular bag attached to the neck of the coat at the back.

grandmother.quick_def: Your grandmother is the mother of your father or mother. You can call your grandmother 'Grandmother'.

disposes.quick_def: If you  dispose of something that you no longer want or need, you throw it away.

dressed.quick_def: A dress is a piece of clothing for a woman or girl that covers the body and part or all of the legs.

version.quick_def: A version of something is a particular form of it in which some details are different from earlier or later forms.

swallows.quick_def: If you swallow something, you cause it to go from your mouth down into your stomach.

woodcutter.quick_def: A woodcutter is someone who cuts down trees or who chops wood as their job.  [old-fashioned]

cries.quick_def: When you cry, tears come from your eyes, usually because you are unhappy or hurt.

appeal.quick_def: If you appeal to someone to do something, you make a serious and urgent request to them.

attributed.quick_def: If you attribute something to an event or situation, you think that it was caused by that event or situation.

cautionary.quick_def: A cautionary story or a cautionary note to a story is one that is intended to give a warning to people.

messages.quick_def: A message is a piece of information or a request that you send to someone or leave for them when you cannot speak to them directly.

survival-relevant.quick_def: If something is survival-relevant, it is related to the ability to stay alive.

jamie.quick_def: a first name for boys, short for James, or for girls

tehrani.quick_def: A Tehrani is a person from Tehran, the capital city of Iran.

durham.quick_def: a county in north-east England that used to be a major centre of coal mining, shipbuilding and steel -making

storytelling.quick_def: Storytelling is the activity of telling or writing stories.

folklorists.quick_def: Folklorists are people who study folklore, which includes traditional stories, customs, and beliefs of a group of people.

devising.quick_def: If you devise a plan, system, or machine, you have the idea for it and design it.

borrowing.quick_def: If you borrow something that belongs to someone else, you take it or use it for a period of time, usually with their permission.

phylogenetic.quick_def: If something is phylogenetic, it is related to the evolutionary development and relationships of organisms.

longest.quick_def: Long means a great amount of time or for a great amount of time.

tale.quick_def: A tale is a story, often involving magic or exciting events.

checking.quick_def: If you check something such as a piece of information or a document, you make sure that it is correct or satisfactory.

variants.quick_def: A variant of a particular thing is something that has a different form to that thing, although it is related to it.

evolves.quick_def: When animals or plants evolve, they gradually change and develop into different forms.

scary.quick_def: Something that is scary is rather frightening.  [informal]

disguise.quick_def: If you are in disguise, you are not wearing your usual clothes or you have altered your appearance in other ways, so that people will not recognize you.

siblings.quick_def: Your siblings are your brothers and sisters.  [formal]

incidents.quick_def: An incident is something that happens, often something that is unpleasant.  [formal]

episodes.quick_def: You can refer to an event or a short period of time as an episode if you want to suggest that it is important or unusual, or has some particular quality.

lots.quick_def: A lot of something or lots of it is a large amount of it. A lot of people or things, or lots of them, is a large number of them.

conserved.quick_def: If you conserve a supply of something, you use it carefully so that it lasts for a long time.

hunter-gatherer.quick_def: A hunter-gatherer is a person who lives by hunting animals and gathering wild plants for food.

folk.quick_def: You can refer to people as folk or folks.

narratives.quick_def: A narrative is a story or an account of a series of events.

stuff.quick_def: You can use stuff to refer to things such as a substance, a collection of things, events, or ideas, or the contents of something in a general way without mentioning the thing itself by name.  [informal]

blood-thirsty.quick_def: If someone is blood-thirsty, they like to see or cause violence and killing.

gruesome.quick_def: Something that is gruesome is extremely unpleasant and shocking.

storytellers.quick_def: A storyteller is someone who tells or writes stories.

teller.quick_def: A teller is someone who works in a bank and who customers pay money to or get money from.  [mainly US, or Scottish]

storyteller.quick_def: A storyteller is someone who tells or writes stories.

swallowed.quick_def: If you swallow something, you cause it to go from your mouth down into your stomach.

stomach.quick_def: Your stomach is the organ inside your body where food is digested before it moves into the intestines.

gripping.quick_def: If you grip something, you take hold of it with your hand and continue to hold it firmly.

jack.quick_def: A jack is a device for lifting a heavy object off the ground, for example a car.

zipes.quick_def: Zipes is a surname, which is a family name used to identify a particular family.

minneapolis.quick_def: the largest city in the US state of Minnesota. It is an industrial port near the northern end of the Mississippi River. The river separates it from St Paul, Minnesota, and they are together called the 'twin cities'. Minneapolis was settled in 1847 and became a town in 1867. It is an agricultural centre for the northern Middle West. Other companies there make computers and provide health services.

unconvinced.quick_def: If you are unconvinced that something is true or right, you are not at all certain that it is true or right.

perennial.quick_def: You use perennial to describe situations or states that keep occurring or which seem to exist all the time; used especially to describe problems or difficulties.

villain.quick_def: A villain is someone who deliberately harms other people or breaks the law in order to get what he or she wants.

nigeria.quick_def: a large country on the west coast of Africa. It was a British colony from 1914 and has been a member of the Commonwealth since becoming independent in 1960, although between 1995 and 1999 its membership was stopped after an argument over the execution of nine men. The capital city of Nigeria is Abuja, in the middle of the country, although its biggest city is Lagos, on the coast. The official language is English.

mathias.quick_def: Mathias is a name for a person.

clasen.quick_def: Clasen is a surname, which is a family name used to identify a particular family.

aarhus.quick_def: Aarhus is a city in Denmark.

morals.quick_def: Morals are principles and beliefs concerning right and wrong behaviour.

scare.quick_def: If something scares you, it frightens or worries you.

strip.quick_def: A strip of something such as paper, cloth, or food is a long, narrow piece of it.

huarango.quick_def: A huarango is a kind of tree.

sucking.quick_def: If you suck something, you hold it in your mouth and pull at it with the muscles in your cheeks and tongue, for example in order to get liquid out of it.

subsoil.quick_def: The subsoil is a layer of earth that is just below the surface soil but above hard rock.

beresford-jones.quick_def: Beresford-Jones is a family name. People with this name can be someone you know or meet.

archaeobotanist.quick_def: An archaeobotanist is a person who studies ancient plants.

lea.quick_def: an open area of land covered in grass

huarangos.quick_def: Huarangos are a kind of trees.

pods.quick_def: A pod is a seed container that grows on plants such as peas or beans.

herbal.quick_def: Herbal means made from or using herbs.

remedies.quick_def: A remedy is a successful way of dealing with a problem.

disappearing.quick_def: If you say that someone or something disappears, you mean that you can no longer see them, usually because you or they have changed position.

smallholdings.quick_def: A smallholding is a piece of land that is used for farming and is smaller than a normal farm.  [British]

botanist.quick_def: A botanist is a scientist who studies plants.

whaley.quick_def: Whaley is a name, usually used for a person.

kew.quick_def: Kew is a place in London. It's well-known for Kew Gardens.

ethnobotanist.quick_def: An ethnobotanist is a person who studies how different groups of people use plants.

milliken.quick_def: Milliken is a name, usually used for a person.

overcoming.quick_def: If you overcome a problem or a feeling, you successfully deal with it and control it.

prejudices.quick_def: Prejudice is an unreasonable dislike of a particular group of people or things, or a preference for one group of people or things over another.

aspirational.quick_def: If you describe someone as aspirational, you mean that they have strong hopes of moving to a higher social status.  [journalism]

locals.quick_def: Local means existing in or belonging to the area where you live, or to the area that you are talking about.

resuscitation.quick_def: If you resuscitate someone who has stopped breathing, you cause them to start breathing again.

festival.quick_def: A festival is an organized series of events such as musical concerts or drama productions.

reinstate.quick_def: If you reinstate someone, you give them back a job or position which had been taken away from them.

eco-heritage.quick_def: Eco-heritage refers to the natural and ecological things passed down from the past, like special plants, animals, or natural places.

schoolchildren.quick_def: Schoolchildren are children who go to school.

boil.quick_def: When a hot liquid boils or when you boil it, bubbles appear in it and it starts to change into steam or vapour.

beans.quick_def: Beans such as green beans, French beans, or broad beans are the seeds of a climbing plant or the long thin cases which contain those seeds.

syrup.quick_def: Syrup is a sweet liquid made by cooking sugar with water, and sometimes with fruit juice as well.

molasses.quick_def: Molasses is a thick, dark brown syrup which is produced when sugar is processed. It is used in cooking.

soups.quick_def: Soup is liquid food made by boiling meat, fish, or vegetables in water.

stews.quick_def: A stew is a meal which you make by cooking meat and vegetables in liquid at a low temperature.

flour.quick_def: Flour is a white or brown powder that is made by grinding grain. It is used to make bread, cakes, and pastry.

cakes.quick_def: A cake is a sweet food made by baking a mixture of flour, eggs, sugar, and fat in an oven. Cakes may be large and cut into slices or small and intended for one person only.

roasted.quick_def: When you roast meat or other food, you cook it by dry heat in an oven or over a fire.

chocolatey.quick_def: having the flavour or colour of chocolate

packed.quick_def: When you pack, or when you pack a bag, you put clothes and other things into it, because you are leaving a place or going on holiday.

vitamins.quick_def: Vitamins are substances that you need in order to remain healthy, which are found in food or can be eaten in the form of pills.

alberto.quick_def: Alberto is a name for a person.

benevides.quick_def: Benevides is a name of a person. People use it to call someone.

certified.quick_def: If someone in an official position certifies something, they officially state that it is true.

sells.quick_def: If you sell something that you own, you let someone have it in return for money.

lima.quick_def: Lima is the name of the capital city of Peru.

hopes.quick_def: If you hope that something is true, or if you hope for something, you want it to be true or to happen, and you usually believe that it is possible or likely.

investing.quick_def: If you invest in something, or if you invest a sum of money, you use your money in a way that you hope will increase its value, for example by paying it into a bank, or buying shares or property.

corridors.quick_def: A corridor is a long passage in a building, with doors and rooms on one or both sides.

counteracting.quick_def: To counteract something means to reduce its effect by doing something that produces an opposite effect.

persuading.quick_def: If you persuade someone to do something, you cause them to do it by giving them good reasons for doing it.

refuge.quick_def: If you take refuge somewhere, you try to protect yourself from physical harm by going there.

bio-control.quick_def: Bio-control is a way to control pests or diseases by using living things like other animals or plants instead of chemicals.

rainforest.quick_def: A rainforest is a thick forest of tall trees which is found in tropical areas where there is a lot of rain.

expanse.quick_def: An expanse of something, usually sea, sky, or land, is a very large amount of it.

arrives.quick_def: When a person or vehicle arrives at a place, they come to it at the end of a journey.

rolled.quick_def: When something rolls or when you roll it, it moves along a surface, turning over many times.

arid.quick_def: Arid land is so dry that very few plants can grow on it.

la.quick_def: the 6th note of a major scale

gomera.quick_def: Gomera is the name of an island. Islands are pieces of land surrounded by water.

canary.quick_def: Canaries are small yellow birds which sing beautifully and are often kept as pets.

rocky.quick_def: A rocky place is covered with rocks or consists of large areas of rock and has nothing growing on it.

slopes.quick_def: A slope is the side of a mountain, hill, or valley.

ravines.quick_def: A ravine is a very deep narrow valley with steep sides.

whistle.quick_def: When you whistle or when you whistle a tune, you make a series of musical notes by forcing your breath out between your lips, or your teeth.

transmitting.quick_def: When radio and television programmes, computer data, or other electronic messages are transmitted, they are sent from one place to another, using wires, radio waves, or satellites.

silbo.quick_def: Silbo is a kind of 'language' that uses whistles to communicate.

gomero.quick_def: Gomero refers to something or someone related to La Gomera, an island in the Canary Islands.

shedding.quick_def: A shed is a small building that is used for storing things such as garden tools.

language-processing.quick_def: Language-processing is the act of dealing with and understanding language. It's like when you listen to someone speak and figure out what they mean.

corina.quick_def: Corina is a name for a person, usually a girl or a woman.

seattle.quick_def: the largest city in the north-western US, also known as the 'Emerald City'. It is in the state of Washington and is a Pacific port on Elliott Bay. It was settled in 1852 and named after a Native American leader. It is the home of the Boeing aircraft company and other industries, but tourists are attracted by its clean air and beautiful scenery.

recoded.quick_def: When something is recoded, it is changed and written down in a new form.

whistles.quick_def: When you whistle or when you whistle a tune, you make a series of musical notes by forcing your breath out between your lips, or your teeth.

low-frequency.quick_def: If something is low-frequency, it has a low number of times it happens or changes in a certain period.

tones.quick_def: The tone of a sound is its particular quality.

whistler.quick_def: A whistler is a person who makes a whistling sound with their mouth.

silbador.quick_def: A silbador is a person who can make a loud and clear sound by blowing air through the lips or using fingers in the mouth.

puts.quick_def: When you put something in a particular place or position, you move it into that place or position.

finger.quick_def: Your fingers are the four long thin parts at the end of each hand.

cupped.quick_def: A cup is a small round container that you drink from. Cups usually have handles and are made from china or plastic.

ambiguity.quick_def: If you say that there is ambiguity in something, you mean that it is unclear or confusing, or it can be understood in more than one way.

whistled.quick_def: When you whistle or when you whistle a tune, you make a series of musical notes by forcing your breath out between your lips, or your teeth.

manuel.quick_def: Manuel is a common male name.

carreiras.quick_def: Carreiras is a surname. A surname is the family name that a person shares with other family members.

laguna.quick_def: Laguna is a proper name, often used for a place like a university, a town or an area.

tenerife.quick_def: Tenerife is an island. It is a place where people can go to travel and have fun.
