geoglyphs.quick_def: Geoglyphs are large designs or figures made on the ground, usually by moving earth or stones.

hillsides.quick_def: A hillside is the sloping side of a hill.

scattered.quick_def: If you scatter things over an area, you throw or drop them so that they spread all over the area.

chalk.quick_def: Chalk is a type of soft white rock. You can use small pieces of it for writing or drawing with.

downlands.quick_def: Downlands are large areas of open, gently rolling hills, usually covered with grass.

counties.quick_def: A county is a region of Britain, Ireland, or the USA which has its own local government.

giants.quick_def: Something that is described as giant is much larger or more important than most others of its kind.

horses.quick_def: A horse is a large animal which people can ride. Some horses are used for pulling ploughs and carts.

crosses.quick_def: If you cross something such as a room, a road, or an area of land or water, you move or travel to the other side of it. If you cross to a place, you move or travel over a room, road, or area of land or water in order to reach that place.

regimental.quick_def: Regimental means belonging to a particular regiment.

badges.quick_def: A badge is a piece of metal or cloth which you wear to show that you belong to an organization or support a cause. American English usually uses button to refer to a small round metal badge.

uffington.quick_def: Uffington is the name of a place. It can be a town, village or an area.

horse.quick_def: A horse is a large animal which people can ride. Some horses are used for pulling ploughs and carts.

oxfordshire.quick_def: a county in central southern England. It contains the city of Oxford and some attractive countryside, and the Thames runs through it. Its administrative centre is Oxford.

re-dated.quick_def: When something is re-dated, its date is changed to a new one.

pre-roman.quick_def: Pre-Roman means before the time when the Romans came or when the Roman influence started.

enigmatic.quick_def: Someone or something that is enigmatic is mysterious and difficult to understand.

wilmington.quick_def: a city in the US state of Delaware

sussex.quick_def: a former county on the coast of south-east England. In 1974 it was divided into the smaller administrative counties of East Sussex and West Sussex, but many people still refer to the whole area as Sussex.

monk.quick_def: A monk is a member of a male religious community that is usually separated from the outside world.

priory.quick_def: A priory is a place where a small group of monks live and work together.

overlying.quick_def: If something is overlying another thing, it is on top of that thing.

gleaming.quick_def: If an object or a surface gleams, it reflects light because it is shiny and clean.

geoglyph.quick_def: A geoglyph is a large design or pattern made on the ground, usually by moving rocks or earth.

cleaned.quick_def: Something that is clean is free from dirt or unwanted marks.

scoured.quick_def: If you scour something such as a place or a book, you make a thorough search of it to try to find what you are looking for.

fairly.quick_def: Something or someone that is fair is reasonable, right, and just.

expose.quick_def: to show something that is usually hidden

outlines.quick_def: If you outline an idea or a plan, you explain it in a general way.

testament.quick_def: If one thing is a testament to another, it shows that the other thing exists or is true.  [formal]

continuity.quick_def: Continuity is the fact that something continues to happen or exist, with no great changes or interruptions.

customs.quick_def: A custom is an activity, a way of behaving, or an event which is usual or traditional in a particular society or in particular circumstances.

stylised.quick_def: Something that is stylized is shown or done in a way that is not natural in order to create an artistic effect.

consisting.quick_def: Something that consists of particular things or people is formed from them.

disjointed.quick_def: Disjointed words, thoughts, or ideas are not presented in a smooth or logical way and are therefore difficult to understand.

streaming.quick_def: A stream is a small narrow river.

bird-like.quick_def: If something is bird-like, it has features or looks similar to a bird.

beaked.quick_def: having a beak, or the type of beak mentioned

elegant.quick_def: If you describe a person or thing as elegant, you mean that they are pleasing and graceful in appearance or style.

melts.quick_def: When a solid substance melts or when you melt it, it changes to a liquid, usually because it has been heated.

slope.quick_def: A slope is the side of a mountain, hill, or valley.

bce.quick_def: Many people now use BCE in dates to indicate a number of years or centuries before AD 1 or before the year in which Jesus is believed to have been born. Compare CE.

hillfort.quick_def: A hillfort is a place on a hill that was built long ago for protection. People lived there and could defend themselves from enemies.

ridgeway.quick_def: A Ridgeway is a long-distance old track on a ridge or high ground.

long-distance.quick_def: If something is long-distance, it covers a great distance.

neolithic.quick_def: Neolithic is used to describe things relating to the period when people had started farming but still used stone for making weapons and tools.

mounds.quick_def: A mound of something is a large rounded pile of it.

lambourn.quick_def: Lambourn is the name of a place, like a town or a village.

barrows.quick_def: A barrow is the same as a wheelbarrow.

well-preserved.quick_def: If something is well-preserved, it is kept in a good condition over a long time.

appreciated.quick_def: If you appreciate something, for example a piece of music or good food, you like it because you recognize its good qualities.

ce.quick_def: Many people now use CE in dates to indicate a number of years or centuries after AD 1 or after the year in which Jesus is believed to have been born. Compare BCE.

documents.quick_def: A document is one or more official pieces of paper with writing on them.

abingdon.quick_def: Abingdon is the name of a place, like a town or a village.

reference.quick_def: Reference to someone or something is the act of talking about them or mentioning them. A reference is a particular example of this.

similarity.quick_def: If there is a similarity between two or more things, they are similar to each other.

coins.quick_def: A coin is a small piece of metal which is used as money.

optically.quick_def: in a way that is connected with the sense of sight or the relationship between light and sight

luminescence.quick_def: Luminescence is a soft, glowing light.  [literary]

osl.quick_def: OSL is a short way to say Optically Stimulated Luminescence, which is a method used to test things like soil.

emblem.quick_def: An emblem is a design representing a country or organization.

marking.quick_def: A mark is a small area of something such as dirt that has accidentally got onto a surface or piece of clothing.

goddess.quick_def: In many religions, a goddess is a female spirit or being that is believed to have power over a particular part of the world or nature.

epona.quick_def: Epona is a Celtic goddess who is regarded as the protector of horses and is related to fertility.

worshipped.quick_def: If you worship a god, you show your respect to the god, for example by saying prayers.

protector.quick_def: If you refer to someone as your protector, you mean that they protect you from being harmed.

fertility.quick_def: Land or soil that is fertile is able to support the growth of a large number of strong healthy plants.

gaul.quick_def: Gaul is an old name for an area in Western Europe that is now mainly France.

attested.quick_def: To attest something or attest to something means to say, show, or prove that it is true.  [formal]

jewellery.quick_def: Jewellery is ornaments that people wear, for example rings, bracelets, and necklaces. It is often made of a valuable metal such as gold, and sometimes decorated with precious stones.

mythology.quick_def: Mythology is a group of myths, especially all the myths from a particular country, religion, or culture.

rhiannon.quick_def: Rhiannon is a name, often for a woman, especially in Welsh-related stories.

welsh.quick_def: If someone welches on a deal or an agreement, they do not do the things they promised to do as part of that deal or agreement.  [informal]

rituals.quick_def: A ritual is a religious service or other ceremony which involves a series of actions performed in a fixed order.

lessen.quick_def: If something lessens or you lessen it, it becomes smaller in size, amount, degree, or importance.

carvings.quick_def: A carving is an object or a design that has been cut out of a material such as stone or wood.

creators.quick_def: The creator of something is the person who made it or invented it.

outlive.quick_def: If one person outlives another, they are still alive after the second person has died. If one thing outlives another thing, the first thing continues to exist after the second has disappeared or been replaced.

inhabit.quick_def: If a place or region is inhabited by a group of people or a species of animal, those people or animals live there.

seaweed.quick_def: Seaweed is a plant that grows in the sea. There are many kinds of seaweed.

yong.quick_def: Yong is a name, which is used to call a person.

utterly.quick_def: You use utterly to emphasize that something is very great in extent, degree, or amount.  [emphasis]

mess.quick_def: If you say that something is a mess or in a mess, you think that it is in an untidy state.

microbiome.quick_def: A microbiome is all the microscopic organisms that live in a particular environment, for example the human gut.  [biology]

microbial.quick_def: Microbial means relating to or caused by microbes.

informs.quick_def: If you inform someone of something, you tell them about it.

holobiont.quick_def: A holobiont is a single unit made up of a species and its microbes.

armpit.quick_def: Your armpits are the areas of your body under your arms where your arms join your shoulders.

peacefully.quick_def: Peaceful activities and situations do not involve war.

contentedly.quick_def: If you are contented, you are satisfied with your life or the situation you are in.

gut.quick_def: A person's or animal's guts are all the organs inside them.

stars.quick_def: A star is a large ball of burning gas in space. Stars appear to us as small points of light in the sky on clear nights.

galaxy.quick_def: A galaxy is an extremely large group of stars and planets that extends over many billions of light years.

bloodstream.quick_def: Your bloodstream is the blood that flows around your body.

swallow.quick_def: If you swallow something, you cause it to go from your mouth down into your stomach.

swapping.quick_def: If you swap something with someone, you give it to them and receive a different thing in exchange.

pets.quick_def: A pet is an animal that you keep in your home to give you company and pleasure.

lightness.quick_def: Light is the brightness that lets you see things. Light comes from sources such as the sun, moon, lamps, and fire.

panache.quick_def: If you do something with panache, you do it in a confident, stylish, and elegant way.

knack.quick_def: A knack is a particularly clever or skilful way of doing something successfully, especially something which most people find difficult.

enthralling.quick_def: If you are enthralled by something, you enjoy it and give it your complete attention and interest.

gently.quick_def: Someone who is gentle is kind, mild, and calm.

bid.quick_def: A bid for something or a bid to do something is an attempt to obtain it or do it.  [journalism]

lens-maker.quick_def: A lens-maker is a person who makes lenses.

antony.quick_def: Antony is a name for a man.

leeuwenhoek.quick_def: Leeuwenhoek is a name of a person.

magnify.quick_def: To magnify an object means to make it appear larger than it really is, by means of a special lens or mirror.

animalcules.quick_def: Animalcules are very tiny living things that you can't see with your eyes, only with a microscope.

pasteur.quick_def: Pasteur is a well-known last name. Usually, it refers to Louis Pasteur, a very famous scientist.

indicated.quick_def: If one thing indicates another, the first thing shows that the second is true or exists.

germ.quick_def: A germ is a very small organism that causes disease.

endures.quick_def: If you endure a painful or difficult situation, you experience it and do not avoid it or give up, usually because you cannot.

plea.quick_def: A plea is an appeal or request for something, made in an intense or emotional way.  [journalism]

acknowledges.quick_def: If you acknowledge a fact or a situation, you accept or admit that it is true or that it exists.  [formal]

yoghurts.quick_def: Yoghurts are thick, creamy foods made from milk that has been fermented. They often have a sour taste and can come in different flavors.

supposedly.quick_def: If you say that something is supposed to happen, you mean that it is planned or expected. Sometimes this use suggests that the thing does not really happen in this way.

friendly.quick_def: If someone is friendly, they behave in a pleasant, kind way, and like to be with other people.

villains.quick_def: A villain is someone who deliberately harms other people or breaks the law in order to get what he or she wants.

symbiotic.quick_def: A symbiotic relationship is one in which organisms, people, or things exist together in a way that benefits them all.

digestion.quick_def: Digestion is the process of digesting food.

immune.quick_def: If you are immune to a particular disease, you cannot be affected by it.

eliminate.quick_def: To eliminate something, especially something you do not want or need, means to remove it completely.  [formal]

toxins.quick_def: A toxin is any poisonous substance produced by bacteria, animals, or plants.

hygiene.quick_def: Hygiene is the practice of keeping yourself and your surroundings clean, especially in order to prevent illness or the spread of diseases.

low-fibre.quick_def: If food is low-fibre, it has only a small amount of fibre in it.

diets.quick_def: Your diet is the type and range of food that you regularly eat.

disrupting.quick_def: If someone or something disrupts an event, system, or process, they cause difficulties that prevent it from continuing or operating in a normal way.

soaring.quick_def: If the amount, value, level, or volume of something soars, it quickly increases by a great deal.  [journalism]

allergies.quick_def: If you have a particular allergy, you become ill or get a rash when you eat, smell, or touch something that does not normally make people ill.

inflammatory.quick_def: If you accuse someone of saying or doing inflammatory things, you mean that what they say or do is likely to make people react very angrily.  [disapproval]

bowel.quick_def: Your bowels are the tubes in your body through which digested food passes from your stomach to your anus.

ibd.quick_def: IBD is a kind of disease that makes the bowel become inflamed.

norms.quick_def: Norms are ways of behaving that are considered normal in a particular society.

upside.quick_def: the more positive aspect of a situation that is generally bad

excessive.quick_def: If you describe the amount or level of something as excessive, you disapprove of it because it is more or higher than is necessary or reasonable.  [disapproval]

detergents.quick_def: Detergent is a chemical substance, usually in the form of a powder or liquid, which is used for washing things such as clothes or dishes.

destroys.quick_def: To destroy something means to cause so much damage to it that it is completely ruined or does not exist any more.

bay.quick_def: A bay is a part of a coast where the land curves inwards.

fungus.quick_def: A fungus is a plant that has no flowers, leaves, or green colouring, such as a mushroom or a toadstool. Other types of fungus such as mould are extremely small and look like a fine powder.

wiping.quick_def: If you wipe something, you rub its surface to remove dirt or liquid from it.

frogs.quick_def: A frog is a small creature with smooth skin, big eyes, and long back legs which it uses for jumping. Frogs usually live near water.

bacterium.quick_def: Bacterium is the singular of bacteria.

squid.quick_def: A squid is a sea creature with a long soft body and many soft arms called tentacles.

distaste.quick_def: If you feel distaste for someone or something, you dislike them and consider them to be unpleasant, disgusting, or immoral.

dengue.quick_def: a disease caused by a virus carried by mosquitoes that is found in tropical areas and causes a high temperature and severe pain in the joints

infects.quick_def: To infect people, animals, or plants means to cause them to have a disease or illness.

block.quick_def: A block of flats or offices is a large building containing them.

neonatal.quick_def: Neonatal means relating to the first few days of life of a new born baby.

ward.quick_def: A ward is a room in a hospital which has beds for many people, often people who need similar treatment.

specially.quick_def: If something has been done specially for a particular person or purpose, it has been done only for that person or purpose.

wise.quick_def: A wise person is able to use their experience and knowledge in order to make sensible decisions and judgments.

empirical.quick_def: Empirical evidence or study relies on practical experience rather than theories.

handful.quick_def: A handful of people or things is a small number of them.

bearded.quick_def: A bearded man has a beard.

experiential.quick_def: Experiential means relating to or resulting from experience.  [formal]

situational.quick_def: connected with or changing according to the particular situation that exists

shaping.quick_def: The shape of an object, a person, or an area is the appearance of their outside edges or surfaces, for example whether they are round, square, curved, or fat.

igor.quick_def: Igor is a name for a person.

grossmann.quick_def: Grossmann is a surname, which is a family name used to identify a particular family.

cumulatively.quick_def: If a series of events have a cumulative effect, each event makes the effect greater.

wisely.quick_def: A wise person is able to use their experience and knowledge in order to make sensible decisions and judgments.

contextual.quick_def: A contextual issue or account relates to the context of something.  [formal]

characterize.quick_def: If something is characterized by a particular feature or quality, that feature or quality is an obvious part of it.  [formal]

unfolds.quick_def: If a situation unfolds, it develops and becomes known or understood.

humility.quick_def: Someone who has humility is not proud and does not believe they are better than other people.

limits.quick_def: A limit is the greatest amount, extent, or degree of something that is possible.

perspectives.quick_def: A particular perspective is a particular way of thinking about something, especially one that is influenced by your beliefs or experiences.

integration.quick_def: If someone integrates into a social group, or is integrated into it, they behave in such a way that they become part of the group or are accepted into it.

third-party.quick_def: A third-party is a person or group that is not directly involved in an activity or situation, but may be related to it in some way.

first-person.quick_def: First-person means using 'I' or 'we' to tell a story or talk about oneself. It's like when you say things from your own point of view.

viewpoint.quick_def: Someone's viewpoint is the way that they think about things in general, or the way they think about a particular thing.

focal.quick_def: Focal is used to describe something that relates to the point where a number of rays or lines meet.

third-person.quick_def: The third-person is when you talk about someone or something, not yourself or the person you're speaking to.

observer.quick_def: You can refer to someone who sees or notices something as an observer.

interpersonal.quick_def: Interpersonal means relating to relationships between people.

ideals.quick_def: An ideal is a principle, idea, or standard that seems very good and worth trying to achieve.

impartiality.quick_def: Someone who is impartial is not directly involved in a particular situation, and is therefore able to give a fair opinion or decision about it.

expansive.quick_def: If something is expansive, it covers or includes a large area or many things.  [formal]

spouse.quick_def: Someone's spouse is the person they are married to.

negotiating.quick_def: If people negotiate with each other or negotiate an agreement, they talk about a problem or a situation such as a business arrangement in order to solve the problem or complete the arrangement.

stake.quick_def: If something is at stake, it is being risked and might be lost or damaged if you are not successful.

seniors.quick_def: The senior people in an organization or profession have the highest and most important jobs.

instructed.quick_def: If you instruct someone to do something, you formally tell them to do it.  [formal]

displayed.quick_def: If you display something that you want people to see, you put it in a particular place, so that people can see it easily.

wisdom-related.quick_def: If something is wisdom-related, it has a connection with wisdom.

couples.quick_def: If you refer to a couple of people or things, you mean two or approximately two of them, although the exact number is not important or you are not sure of it.

visualize.quick_def: If you visualize something, you imagine what it is like by forming a mental picture of it.

incident.quick_def: An incident is something that happens, often something that is unpleasant.  [formal]

thoughts.quick_def: Thought is the past tense and past participle of think.

reasoning-recognizing.quick_def: Reasoning-recognizing means being able to understand and identify the way of thinking and reasons.

compromise-compared.quick_def: When we say 'compromise-compared', it means making a compromise and then comparing it with something else. A compromise is when two or more people give up some of what they want to reach an agreement.

egocentric.quick_def: Someone who is egocentric thinks only of themselves and their own wants, and does not consider other people.  [disapproval]

ego-decentering.quick_def: Ego-decentering means moving your focus away from yourself and starting to pay more attention to others.

promotes.quick_def: If people promote something, they help or encourage it to happen, increase, or spread.

conceptual.quick_def: Conceptual means related to ideas and concepts formed in the mind.

affording.quick_def: If you cannot afford something, you do not have enough money to pay for it.

crystallized.quick_def: If you crystallize an opinion or idea, or if it crystallizes, it becomes fixed and definite in someone's mind.

openness.quick_def: If you open something such as a door, window, or lid, or if it opens, its position is changed so that it no longer covers a hole or gap.

agreeableness.quick_def: Agreeableness is a quality of being friendly, kind and easy to get along with.

generalized.quick_def: If you generalize, you say something that seems to be true in most situations or for most people, but that may not be completely true in all cases.

behaves.quick_def: The way that you behave is the way that you do and say things, and the things that you do and say.

informative.quick_def: Something that is informative gives you useful information.

forgive.quick_def: If you forgive someone who has done something bad or wrong, you stop being angry with them and no longer want to punish them.

retaliate.quick_def: If you retaliate when someone harms or annoys you, you do something which harms or annoys them in return.

relying.quick_def: If you rely on someone or something, you need them and depend on them in order to live or work properly.

estimation.quick_def: Your estimation of a person or situation is the opinion or impression that you have formed about them.  [formal]

land-based.quick_def: If something is land-based, it exists or operates on the land, not in the sea or air.

sails.quick_def: Sails are large pieces of material attached to the mast of a ship. The wind blows against the sails and pushes the ship along.

shipbuilders.quick_def: A shipbuilder is a company or a person that builds ships.

proceeded.quick_def: If you proceed to do something, you do it, often after doing something else first.

planks.quick_def: A plank is a long, flat, rectangular piece of wood.

sewn.quick_def: When you sew something such as clothes, you make them or repair them by joining pieces of cloth together by passing thread through them with a needle.

mortise.quick_def: a hole cut in a piece of wood, etc. to receive the end of another piece of wood, so that the two are held together

tenon.quick_def: an end of a piece of wood that has been cut to fit into a mortise so that the two are held together

plank.quick_def: A plank is a long, flat, rectangular piece of wood.

stitching.quick_def: If you stitch cloth, you use a needle and thread to join two pieces together or to make a decoration.

shifted.quick_def: If you shift something or if it shifts, it moves slightly.

proceeding.quick_def: If you proceed to do something, you do it, often after doing something else first.

shortened.quick_def: If you shorten an event or the length of time that something lasts, or if it shortens, it does not last as long as it would otherwise do or as it used to do.

warships.quick_def: A warship is a ship with guns that is used for fighting in wars.

unequalled.quick_def: If you describe something as unequalled, you mean that it is greater, better, or more extreme than anything else of the same kind.

lightweight.quick_def: Something that is lightweight weighs less than most other things of the same type.

speedy.quick_def: A speedy process, event, or action happens or is done very quickly.

ballast.quick_def: Ballast is any substance that is used in ships or hot-air balloons to make them heavier and more stable. Ballast usually consists of water, sand, or iron.

load.quick_def: If you load a vehicle or a container, you put a large quantity of things into it.

sink.quick_def: A sink is a large fixed container in a kitchen, with taps to supply water. It is mainly used for washing dishes.

crippled.quick_def: A person with a physical disability or a serious permanent injury is sometimes referred to as a cripple.  [offensive]

naval.quick_def: Naval means belonging to, relating to, or involving a country's navy.

battering.quick_def: If someone is battered, they are regularly hit and badly hurt by a member of their family or by their partner.

ram.quick_def: If a vehicle rams something such as another vehicle, it crashes into it with a lot of force, usually deliberately.

hulls.quick_def: The hull of a boat or tank is the main body of it.

oars.quick_def: Oars are long poles with a wide, flat blade at one end which are used for rowing a boat.

enemy.quick_def: If someone is your enemy, they hate you or want to harm you.

oarsmen.quick_def: a man who rows a boat, especially as a member of a crew (= team)

navy.quick_def: A country's navy consists of the people it employs to fight at sea, and the ships they use.

mare.quick_def: A mare is an adult female horse.

nostrum.quick_def: You can refer to ideas or theories about how something should be done as nostrums, especially when you think they are old-fashioned or wrong in some way.  [formal]

trireme.quick_def: a long flat ship with three rows of oars on each side, used in war by the ancient Greeks and Romans

rowers.quick_def: A rower is a person who rows a boat, especially as a sport.

uncomfortable.quick_def: If you are uncomfortable, you are slightly worried or embarrassed, and not relaxed and confident.

entering.quick_def: When you enter a place such as a room or building, you go into it or come into it.  [formal]

oar-holes.quick_def: Oar-holes are holes in a boat through which oars can be put.

contrary.quick_def: Ideas, attitudes, or reactions that are contrary to each other are completely different from each other.

slaves.quick_def: A slave is someone who is the property of another person and has to work for that person.

planking.quick_def: Planking is wood that has been cut into long flat pieces. It is used especially to make floors.

stability.quick_def: the quality or state of being steady and not changing or being upset in any way (= the quality of being stable)

v-shaped.quick_def: If something is V-shaped, it has the shape like the letter V.

rudders.quick_def: A rudder is a device for steering a boat. It consists of a vertical piece of wood or metal at the back of the boat.

stern.quick_def: Stern words or actions are very severe.

tiller.quick_def: The tiller of a boat is a handle that is fixed to the rudder. It is used to turn the rudder, which then steers the boat.

bar.quick_def: A bar is a place where you can buy and drink alcoholic drinks.  [mainly US]

masts.quick_def: The masts of a boat are the tall upright poles that support its sails.

square.quick_def: A square is a shape with four sides that are all the same length and four corners that are all right angles.

triangular.quick_def: Something that is triangular is in the shape of a triangle.

bow.quick_def: When you bow to someone, you briefly bend your body towards them as a formal way of greeting them or showing respect.

coordinating.quick_def: If you coordinate an activity, you organize the various people and things involved in it.

granite.quick_def: Granite is a very hard rock used in building.

pozzuoli.quick_def: Pozzuoli is the name of a place, a city or a port.

naples.quick_def: Naples is a well-known city in Italy.

gigantic.quick_def: If you describe something as gigantic, you are emphasizing that it is extremely large in size, amount, or degree.  [emphasis]

ostia.quick_def: Ostia is the name of a place, a port city in Italy.

tiber.quick_def: The Tiber is the name of a river in Italy.

intercepted.quick_def: If you intercept someone or something that is travelling from one place to another, you stop them before they get to their destination.

towboats.quick_def: Towboats are small boats that can pull or drag bigger boats or ships to move them.

drag.quick_def: If you drag something, you pull it along the ground, often with difficulty.

quay.quick_def: A quay is a long platform beside the sea or a river where boats can be tied up and loaded or unloaded.

navigation.quick_def: When someone navigates a ship or an aircraft somewhere, they decide which course to follow and steer it there. You can also say that a ship or an aircraft navigates somewhere.

compasses.quick_def: A compass is an instrument that you use for finding directions. It has a dial and a magnetic needle that always points to the north.

visibility.quick_def: Visibility means how far or how clearly you can see in particular weather conditions.

seamen.quick_def: A seaman is a sailor, especially one who is not an officer.

succession.quick_def: A succession of things of the same kind is a number of them that exist or happen one after the other.

showcase.quick_def: A showcase is a glass container with valuable objects inside it, for example at an exhibition or in a museum.

flourishing.quick_def: If something flourishes, it is successful, active, or common, and developing quickly and strongly.

agripolis.quick_def: Agripolis is the name of a consultancy that works on urban agriculture, helping to design, build and equip inner-city farms.

fielding.quick_def: A field is an area of grass, for example in a park or on a farm. A field is also an area of land on which a crop is grown.

equip.quick_def: If you equip a person or thing with something, you give them the tools or equipment that are needed.

generators.quick_def: A generator is a machine which produces electricity.

gases.quick_def: Gas is a substance like air that is neither liquid nor solid and burns easily. It is used as a fuel for cooking and heating.

refrigerated.quick_def: If you refrigerate food, you make it cold, for example by putting it in a fridge, usually in order to preserve it.

wholesalers.quick_def: A wholesaler is a person whose business is buying large quantities of goods and selling them in smaller amounts, for example to shops.  [business]

enriched.quick_def: To enrich something means to improve its quality, usually by adding something to it.

pipes.quick_def: A pipe is a long, round, hollow object, usually made of metal or plastic, through which a liquid or gas can flow.

showers.quick_def: A shower is a device for washing yourself. It consists of a pipe which ends in a flat cover with a lot of holes in it so that water comes out in a spray.

shanghai.quick_def: to trick or force somebody into doing something that they do not really want to do

detroit.quick_def: the largest city in the US state of Michigan. It began in 1701 as a French trading post. It is on the Detroit River and connected by a bridge to Windsor, Canada. Detroit is the centre of the US car industry and often has many unemployed workers because of the increase in imports of foreign cars. It also has a music industry and produces salt from local mines, steel and chemicals.

bangkok.quick_def: Bangkok is the capital city of Thailand.

disused.quick_def: A disused place or building is empty and is no longer used.

mushrooms.quick_def: Mushrooms are fungi that you can eat.

carparks.quick_def: Carparks are places where people can park their cars.

virtuous.quick_def: A virtuous person behaves in a moral and correct way.

soil-based.quick_def: If something is soil-based, it depends on or is related to soil.

radishes.quick_def: Radishes are small red or white vegetables that are the roots of a plant. They are eaten raw in salads.

carrots.quick_def: Carrots are long, thin, orange-coloured vegetables. They grow under the ground, and have green shoots above the ground.

potatoes.quick_def: Potatoes are quite round vegetables with brown or red skins and white insides. They grow under the ground.

fast-changing.quick_def: If something is fast-changing, it changes very quickly.

accessibility.quick_def: how easy something is to reach, enter, use, see, etc.

landowner.quick_def: A landowner is a person who owns land, especially a large amount of land.

likewise.quick_def: You use likewise when you are comparing two methods, states, or situations and saying that they are similar.

suffers.quick_def: If you suffer pain, you feel it in your body or in your mind.

knot.quick_def: If you tie a knot in a piece of string, rope, cloth, or other material, you pass one end or part of it through a loop and pull it tight.

woodworker.quick_def: A woodworker is a person who makes things from wood.

pennsylvania.quick_def: a state in the north-eastern US, also called the Keystone State for its central position among the 13 original states. The largest city is Philadelphia, and the capital city is Harrisburg. The area was established for Quakers in 1681 by William Penn, who named it Pennsylvania ('Penn's small forest') for his father. The Battle of Gettysburg was fought there during the American Civil War. The state produces chemicals, medicines, electronic equipment and farm products. Tourist attractions include Valley Forge and the Pennsylvania Dutch region.

high-grading.quick_def: High-grading is a practice of only taking the best or most valuable things and leaving the rest.

low-use.quick_def: If something is low-use, it is not used very often.

junk.quick_def: Junk is old and used goods that have little value and that you do not want any more.

higher-value.quick_def: If something is higher-value, it has more value than other similar things.

combustion.quick_def: Combustion is the act of burning something or the process of burning.  [technical]

gasified.quick_def: If something is gasified, it is changed into a gas.

ethanol.quick_def: Ethanol is another name for alcohol.  [technical]

gasoline.quick_def: Gasoline is the same as petrol.  [US]

plant-cutting.quick_def: Plant-cutting is the act of cutting plants. It can be done for different reasons, like managing a forest or getting parts of plants for other uses.

tsi.quick_def: TSI is an abbreviation. It stands for Timber Stand Improvement, which is a way to make a forest better.

poor-quality.quick_def: If something is poor-quality, it is not good and has many problems.

highest-valued.quick_def: If something is highest-valued, it has the greatest value among a group of things.

removing.quick_def: If you remove something from a place, you take it away.  [written]

invasive.quick_def: You use invasive to describe something undesirable which spreads very quickly and which is very difficult to stop from spreading.

tops.quick_def: The top of something is its highest point or part.

coverage.quick_def: The coverage of something in the news is the reporting of it.

tailored.quick_def: A tailor is a person whose job is to make men's clothes.

wooly.quick_def: If something is wooly, it is like wool, soft and fuzzy.

adelgid.quick_def: An adelgid is a small insect that can harm trees.

longhorned.quick_def: If an animal is longhorned, it has long horns.

beetle.quick_def: A beetle is an insect with a hard covering to its body.

emerald.quick_def: An emerald is a precious stone which is clear and bright green.

gypsy.quick_def: A Gypsy is a member of a race of people who travel from place to place, usually in caravans, rather than living in one place. Some Gypsies object to this name, and prefer to be called Romany.

moth.quick_def: A moth is an insect like a butterfly which usually flies about at night.

outbreak.quick_def: If there is an outbreak of something unpleasant, such as violence or a disease, it suddenly starts to happen.

shelterwood.quick_def: A shelterwood is a group of trees left in a forest to protect young trees growing under them.

thinned.quick_def: Something that is thin is much narrower than it is long.

forester.quick_def: A forester is a person whose job is to look after the trees in a forest and to plant new ones.

regenerated.quick_def: To regenerate something means to develop and improve it to make it more active, successful, or important, especially after a period when it has been getting worse.

two-tier.quick_def: If something is two-tier, it has two levels or parts.

thinnings.quick_def: Thinnings are the parts of trees or plants that are removed to make the rest grow better.

removal.quick_def: The removal of something is the act of removing it.

classify.quick_def: To classify things means to divide them into groups or types so that things with similar characteristics are in the same group.

cavities.quick_def: A cavity is a space or hole in something such as a solid object or a person's body.  [formal]

woodpeckers.quick_def: A woodpecker is a type of bird with a long sharp beak. Woodpeckers use their beaks to make holes in tree trunks.

resilience.quick_def: the ability of people or things to recover quickly after something unpleasant, such as shock, injury, etc.

hawthorn.quick_def: A hawthorn is a small tree which has sharp thorns and produces white or pink flowers.

amateurs.quick_def: An amateur is someone who does something as a hobby and not as a job.

satellites.quick_def: A satellite is an object which has been sent into space in order to collect information or to be part of a communications system. Satellites move continually round the Earth or around another planet.

deploy.quick_def: To deploy troops, weapons, or resources means to make them ready to be used.

constellations.quick_def: A constellation is a group of stars which form a pattern and have a name.

iridium.quick_def: a chemical element. Iridium is a very hard yellow-white metal, used especially in making alloys.

smashed.quick_def: If you smash something or if it smashes, it breaks into many pieces, for example when it is hit or dropped.

shrapnel.quick_def: Shrapnel consists of small pieces of metal which are scattered from exploding bombs and shells.

threaten.quick_def: If a person threatens to do something unpleasant to you, or if they threaten you, they say or imply that they will do something unpleasant to you, especially if you do not do what they want.

stretching.quick_def: Something that stretches over an area or distance covers or exists in the whole of that area or distance.

altitude.quick_def: If something is at a particular altitude, it is at that height above sea level.

human-made.quick_def: If something is human-made, it is made by people, not by nature.

rocket.quick_def: A rocket is a space vehicle that is shaped like a long tube.

consumes.quick_def: If you consume something, you eat or drink it.  [formal]

attacking.quick_def: To attack a person or place means to try to hurt or damage them using physical violence.

ever-more-crowded.quick_def: If a place is ever-more-crowded, it becomes more and more full of people or things over time.

compile.quick_def: When you compile something such as a report, book, or programme, you produce it by collecting and putting together many pieces of information.

taxonomies.quick_def: Taxonomy is the process of naming and classifying things such as animals and plants into groups within a larger system, according to their similarities and differences.  [technical]

unthinkable.quick_def: If you say that something is unthinkable, you are emphasizing that it cannot possibly be accepted or imagined as a possibility.  [emphasis]

crashes.quick_def: A crash is an accident in which a moving vehicle hits something and is damaged or destroyed.

runaway.quick_def: You use runaway to describe a situation in which something increases or develops very quickly and cannot be controlled.

cascade.quick_def: If you refer to a cascade of something, you mean that there is a large amount of it.  [literary]

near-earth.quick_def: Near-Earth means close to the Earth.

unusable.quick_def: Something that is unusable is not in a good enough state or condition to be used.

carolin.quick_def: Carolin is a name for a person, usually a girl.

frueh.quick_def: Frueh is a surname, which is a family name passed down from one's family.

astrodynamical.quick_def: Astrodynamical means related to the study of the movement of objects in space, like planets and satellites.

purdue.quick_def: Purdue is the name of a well-known university in the United States.

lafayette.quick_def: Lafayette is a name, often used for places or people.

monitor.quick_def: If you monitor something, you regularly check its development or progress, and sometimes comment on it.

collaborating.quick_def: When one person or group collaborates with another, they work together, especially on a book or on some research.

inter-agency.quick_def: Inter-Agency means between different agencies. It is used when different agencies work together or have something to do with each other.

inactivating.quick_def: When you are inactivating something, you are making it stop working or being active.

venting.quick_def: A vent is a hole in something through which air can come in and smoke, gas, or smells can go out.

pressurised.quick_def: If you are pressurized into doing something, you are forcefully persuaded to do it.

leftover.quick_def: You can refer to food that has not been eaten after a meal as leftovers.

intergovernmental.quick_def: involving the governments of two or more countries

advise.quick_def: If you advise someone to do something, you tell them what you think they should do.

disintegrate.quick_def: If something disintegrates, it becomes seriously weakened, and is divided or destroyed.

missions.quick_def: A mission is an important task that people are given to do, especially one that involves travelling to another country.

abided.quick_def: If you can't abide someone or something, you dislike them very much.

holger.quick_def: Holger is a name for a person.

krag.quick_def: Krag is a name, usually for a person.

agency.quick_def: An agency is a business which provides a service on behalf of other businesses.  [business]

space-debris.quick_def: Space-debris means the waste or junk left in space, like old satellites or parts of rockets.

darmstadt.quick_def: Darmstadt is a city in Germany.

worries.quick_def: If you worry, you keep thinking about problems that you have or about unpleasant things that might happen.

intentions.quick_def: An intention is an idea or plan of what you are going to do.

bankrupt.quick_def: People or organizations that go bankrupt do not have enough money to pay their debts.  [business]

vastness.quick_def: Something that is vast is extremely large.

nearing.quick_def: If something is near a place, thing, or person, it is a short distance from them.

precision.quick_def: If you do something with precision, you do it exactly as it should be done.

manoeuvres.quick_def: If you manoeuvre something into or out of an awkward position, you skilfully move it there.

marlon.quick_def: Marlon is a name for a person.

sorge.quick_def: Sorge is a surname, which is a family name used to identify a person's family.

aerospace.quick_def: Aerospace companies are involved in developing and making aircraft, rockets, missiles, space vehicles, and related equipment.

segundo.quick_def: Segundo is a Spanish word that means 'second'. It can be used to talk about the second position or the second unit of time.

moriba.quick_def: Moriba is a name used to call a person.

jah.quick_def: Jah is a name for God in the Rastafari religion.

astrodynamicist.quick_def: An astrodynamicist is a person who studies how objects move in space, like satellites and spaceships.

austin.quick_def: the capital city of the US state of Texas, on the Colorado river

choreographed.quick_def: When someone choreographs a ballet or other dance, they invent the steps and movements and tell the dancers how to perform them.

air-traffic.quick_def: Air-traffic refers to the movement of airplanes in the air. It includes all the planes flying in a certain area.

consistently.quick_def: Someone who is consistent always behaves in the same way, has the same attitudes towards people or things, or achieves the same level of success in something.

authoritative.quick_def: Someone or something that is authoritative gives an impression of power and importance and is likely to be obeyed.

catalogue.quick_def: A catalog is a list of things such as the goods you can buy from a particular company, the objects in a museum, or the books in a library.

accurately.quick_def: Accurate information, measurements, and statistics are correct to a very detailed level. An accurate instrument is able to give you information of this kind.

orbits.quick_def: An orbit is the curved path in space that is followed by an object going round and round a planet, moon, or star.

web-based.quick_def: If something is web-based, it works or exists on the internet.

catalogues.quick_def: A catalogue is a list of things such as the goods you can buy from a particular company, the objects in a museum, or the books in a library.

maintained.quick_def: If you maintain something, you continue to have it, and do not let it stop or grow weaker.

visualise.quick_def: If you visualize something, you imagine what it is like by forming a mental picture of it.

identifier.quick_def: a series of characters used to refer to a program or set of data within a program

designate.quick_def: When you designate someone or something as a particular thing, you formally give them that description or name.

designated.quick_def: When you designate someone or something as a particular thing, you formally give them that description or name.

cross-correlate.quick_def: When you cross-correlate things, you compare them to find relationships between them.

devolving.quick_def: If you devolve power, authority, or responsibility to a less powerful person or group, or if it devolves upon them, it is transferred to them.

tragedy.quick_def: A tragedy is an extremely sad event or situation.

spaceflight.quick_def: Spaceflight is the act of traveling in space using a spacecraft.

mysteries.quick_def: A mystery is something that is not understood or known about.

stonehenge.quick_def: Britain's most famous prehistoric monument, on Salisbury Plain in southern England. It consists of two circles of large standing stones, one inside the other. The inner circle consisted of arches made by laying one stone across the tops of two others. Some of these have fallen, but some are still in position. Stonehenge was built between 3000 and 1500 BC. Nobody knows why it was built, but many people think it was to study the stars and planets or to worship the sun, because a line through its centre would point directly to the position of the rising sun at the summer solstice or of the setting sun at the winter solstice. Many people go to Stonehenge for midsummer celebrations, and it is now one of the only times of year when the public are allowed near the stones. Stonehenge was made a World Heritage Site in 1986.

erect.quick_def: If people erect something such as a building, bridge, or barrier, they build it or create it.  [formal]

salisbury.quick_def: a town in Wiltshire, southern England, on the River Avon. It is famous for its cathedral, which has the highest spire (= pointed tower) in Britain, and for the ancient remains at Old Sarum, the original place where the town was built, to the north of the present town. Salisbury and its cathedral appear in many of the paintings of John Constable.

plain.quick_def: A plain object, surface, or fabric is entirely in one colour and has no pattern, design, or writing on it.

comprised.quick_def: If you say that something comprises or is comprised of a number of things or people, you mean it has them as its parts or members.  [formal]

layout.quick_def: The layout of a garden, building, or piece of writing is the way in which the parts of it are arranged.

iconic.quick_def: An iconic image or thing is important or impressive because it seems to be a symbol of something.  [formal]

ruin.quick_def: To ruin something means to severely harm, damage, or spoil it.

ditch.quick_def: A ditch is a long narrow channel cut into the ground at the side of a road or field.

henge.quick_def: a circle of large standing wooden or stone objects built in prehistoric times

pits.quick_def: A pit is a coal mine.

hoisted.quick_def: If you hoist something heavy somewhere, you lift it or pull it up there.

bluestones.quick_def: Bluestones are stones that are blue in color.

horseshoe.quick_def: A horseshoe is a piece of metal shaped like a U, which is fixed with nails to the bottom of a horse's foot in order to protect it.

preseli.quick_def: Preseli is the name of a place, like a hill area.

long-standing.quick_def: If something is long-standing, it has existed for a very long time.

rollers.quick_def: A roller is a cylinder that turns round in a machine or device.

trunks.quick_def: The trunk of a tree is the large main stem from which the branches grow.

lug.quick_def: If you lug a heavy or awkward object somewhere, you carry it there with difficulty.  [informal]

floated.quick_def: If something or someone is floating in a liquid, they are in the liquid, on or just below the surface, and are being supported by it. You can also float something on a liquid.

avon.quick_def: any of three rivers with the same name in south-west England. The longest of these flows through Warwick and Stratford-upon-Avon. Shakespeare, who was born at Stratford, is sometimes called the Bard of Avon.

towed.quick_def: If one vehicle tows another, it pulls it along behind it.

supersized.quick_def: If something is supersized, it is much bigger than the normal size.

wicker.quick_def: Wicker is long thin sticks, stems, or reeds that have been woven together to make things such as baskets and furniture.

baskets.quick_def: A basket is a stiff container that is used for carrying or storing objects. Baskets are made from thin strips of materials such as straw, plastic, or wire woven together.

ball.quick_def: A ball is a round object that is used in games such as tennis, baseball, football, basketball, and cricket.

bearings.quick_def: If something has a bearing on a situation or event, it is relevant to it.

grooved.quick_def: Something that is grooved has grooves on its surface.

oxen.quick_def: An ox is a bull that has been castrated. Oxen are used in some countries for pulling vehicles or carrying things.

geologists.quick_def: Geology is the study of the Earth's structure, surface, and origins.

voices.quick_def: When someone speaks or sings, you hear their voice.

industrious.quick_def: If you describe someone as industrious, you mean they work very hard.

pushing.quick_def: When you push something, you use force to make it move away from you or away from its previous position.

carting.quick_def: A cart is an old-fashioned wooden vehicle that is used for transporting goods or people. Some carts are pulled by animals.

hauling.quick_def: If you haul something which is heavy or difficult to move, you move it using a lot of effort.

faraway.quick_def: A faraway place is a long distance from you or from a particular place.

sandstone.quick_def: Sandstone is a type of rock which contains a lot of sand. It is often used for building houses and walls.

crescent.quick_def: A crescent is a curved shape that is wider in the middle than at its ends, like the shape of the moon during its first and last quarters. It is the most important symbol of the Islamic faith.

three-pieced.quick_def: If something is three-pieced, it is made up of three parts.

trilithons.quick_def: Trilithons are structures made up of three pieces. Usually, two pieces stand upright and one lies across them on top.

radiocarbon.quick_def: Radiocarbon is a type of carbon which is radioactive, and which therefore breaks up slowly at a regular rate. Its presence in an object can be measured in order to find out how old the object is.

repositioned.quick_def: To reposition an object means to move it to another place or to change its position.

aubrey.quick_def: Aubrey is a name for a person.

druids.quick_def: Druids are people who had important religious, judicial and political roles in Celtic society.

judicial.quick_def: Judicial means relating to the legal system and to judgments made in a court of law.

popularized.quick_def: To popularize something means to make a lot of people interested in it and able to enjoy it.

antiquarian.quick_def: Antiquarian means concerned with old and rare objects.

stukeley.quick_def: Stukeley is a name, usually used for a person.

graves.quick_def: A grave is a place where a dead person is buried.

gather.quick_def: If people gather somewhere or if someone gathers people somewhere, they come together in a group.

solstice.quick_def: The summer solstice is the day of the year with the most hours of daylight, and the winter solstice is the day of the year with the fewest hours of daylight.

celts.quick_def: The Celts are a group of people who lived in ancient times in some parts of Europe.

agrarians.quick_def: Agrarians are people who work in farming and live by agriculture.

isles.quick_def: An isle is an island; often used as part of an island's name, or in literary English.

immigrants.quick_def: An immigrant is a person who has come to live in a country from some other country. Compare emigrant.

continent.quick_def: A continent is a very large area of land, such as Africa or Asia, that consists of several countries.

shadowy.quick_def: A shadowy place is dark or full of shadows.

megalithic.quick_def: connected with megaliths (= very large stones that were put in a place that was used for ceremonies in ancient times)

operated.quick_def: If you operate a business or organization, you work to keep it running properly. If a business or organization operates, it carries out its work.

solstices.quick_def: The summer solstice is the day of the year with the most hours of daylight, and the winter solstice is the day of the year with the fewest hours of daylight.

equinoxes.quick_def: An equinox is one of the two days in the year when day and night are of equal length.

eclipses.quick_def: An eclipse of the sun is an occasion when the moon is between the Earth and the sun, so that for a short time you cannot see part or all of the sun. An eclipse of the moon is an occasion when the Earth is between the sun and the moon, so that for a short time you cannot see part or all of the moon.

speculate.quick_def: If you speculate about something, you make guesses about its nature or identity, or about what might happen.

curative.quick_def: Something that has curative properties can cure people's illnesses.  [formal]

chessplaying.quick_def: Chessplaying means the activity of playing chess.

human-programmed.quick_def: If something is human-programmed, it is made to work in a certain way by humans.

yesterday.quick_def: You use yesterday to refer to the day before today.

prodigious.quick_def: Something that is prodigious is very large or impressive.  [literary]

restriction.quick_def: If you restrict something, you put a limit on it in order to reduce it or prevent it becoming too great.

mid-century.quick_def: Mid-century means the middle part of a century.

agi.quick_def: AGI means artificial general intelligence. It refers to machines that can do tasks as well as humans.

human-level.quick_def: If something is human-level, it has the same ability or performance as a human being.

biochemical.quick_def: Biochemical changes, reactions, and mechanisms relate to the chemical processes that happen in living things.

speeds.quick_def: The speed of something is the rate at which it moves or travels.

handicaps.quick_def: A handicap is a physical or mental disability.

webb.quick_def: the name of a married couple who were important figures in socialist politics in Britain during the late 19th and early 20th century. Sidney Webb (1859-1947) and his wife Beatrice Webb (1858-1943) wrote several books together which had a great influence on political thought at the time. These included The History of Trade Unionism (1894) and Industrial Democracy (1897). Together they helped to establish the London School of Economics and the New Statesman magazine. Sidney was made a baron in 1929.

smarter.quick_def: Smart people and things are pleasantly neat and clean in appearance.  [mainly British]

specify.quick_def: If you specify something, you give information about what is required or should happen in a certain situation.

midas.quick_def: Midas is a king in folklore. He has the power that everything he touches turns into gold.

touched.quick_def: If you touch something, you put your hand onto it in order to feel it or to make contact with it.

intend.quick_def: If you intend to do something, you have decided or planned to do it.

human-friendly.quick_def: If something is human-friendly, it is easy and safe for people to use or interact with.

superintelligent.quick_def: If someone or something is superintelligent, it means they are extremely smart and have much higher intelligence than normal.

amplifying.quick_def: If you amplify a sound, you make it louder, usually by using electronic equipment.

fallible.quick_def: If you say that someone or something is fallible, you mean that they are not perfect and are likely to make mistakes or to fail in what they are doing.  [formal]

natures.quick_def: Nature is all the animals, plants, and other things in the world that are not made by people, and all the events and processes that are not caused by people.

cognitively.quick_def: Cognitively means in a way that relates to thinking and understanding.

troughs.quick_def: A trough is a long narrow container from which farm animals drink or eat.

luckily.quick_def: You add luckily to a statement to indicate that it is good that a particular thing happened or is the case because otherwise the situation would have been difficult or unpleasant.

steering.quick_def: When you steer a car, boat, or plane, you control it so that it goes in the direction that you want.

utopian.quick_def: If you describe a plan or idea as utopian, you are criticizing it because it is unrealistic and shows a belief that things can be improved much more than is possible.  [disapproval]

clarity.quick_def: The clarity of something such as a book or argument is its quality of being well explained and easy to understand.

conflicted.quick_def: Conflict is serious disagreement and argument about something important. If two people or groups are in conflict, they have had a serious disagreement or argument and have not yet reached agreement.

indirectly.quick_def: An indirect result or effect is not caused immediately and obviously by a thing or person, but happens because of something else that they have done.

hands.quick_def: Your hands are the parts of your body at the end of your arms. Each hand has four fingers and a thumb.

gatekeepers.quick_def: A gatekeeper is a person who is in charge of a gate and who allows people through it.

sacrificing.quick_def: If you sacrifice something that is valuable or important, you give it up, usually to obtain something else for yourself or for other people.

sticking.quick_def: A stick is a thin branch which has fallen off a tree.

lapses.quick_def: A lapse is a moment or instance of bad behaviour by someone who usually behaves well.

presently.quick_def: If you say that something is presently happening, you mean that it is happening now.

discriminate.quick_def: If you can discriminate between two things, you can recognize that they are different.

denying.quick_def: When you deny something, you state that it is not true.

silicon.quick_def: Silicon is an element that is found in sand and in minerals such as quartz and granite. Silicon is used to make parts of computers and other electronic equipment.

far-fetched.quick_def: If an idea or story is far-fetched, it is very unlikely to be true or to happen.

nhs.quick_def: NHS is an abbreviation for National Health Service.

taxpayers.quick_def: Taxpayers are people who pay a percentage of their income to the government as tax.

depriving.quick_def: If you deprive someone of something that they want or need, you take it away from them, or you prevent them from having it.

specified.quick_def: If you specify something, you give information about what is required or should happen in a certain situation.

willingness.quick_def: If someone is willing to do something, they are fairly happy about doing it and will do it if they are asked or required to do it.

self-interest.quick_def: Self-interest means caring about your own benefits and advantages more than others.

package.quick_def: A package is a small parcel.

humanist.quick_def: Humanism is the belief that people can achieve happiness and live well without religion.

iron-making.quick_def: Iron-making is the process of making iron from raw materials.

inventor.quick_def: An inventor is a person who has invented something, or whose job is to invent things.

newcomen.quick_def: Newcomen is a name, usually for a person. It can refer to someone who is an inventor or has made some contributions.

watt.quick_def: A watt is a unit of measurement of electrical power.

boulton.quick_def: Boulton is a name, usually a person's last name.

backward.quick_def: A backward movement or look is in the direction that your back is facing. Some people use backwards for this meaning.

strokes.quick_def: If you stroke someone or something, you move your hand slowly and gently over them.

piston.quick_def: A piston is a cylinder or metal disc that is part of an engine. Pistons slide up and down inside tubes and cause various parts of the engine to move.

rotary.quick_def: Rotary means turning or able to turn round a fixed point.

trevithick.quick_def: Trevithick is a name, usually for a person.

manchester.quick_def: a large city in north-west England, in the county of Greater Manchester. It first became important as an industrial city during the 18th century, producing wool and cotton goods for sale in Britain and abroad. It was also a cultural and intellectual centre with a tradition of left-wing politics. Its famous buildings include Manchester Town Hall (built 1868-77) and the Bridgewater Hall (where concerts are held, opened in 1996).

linen.quick_def: Linen is a kind of cloth that is made from a plant called flax. It is used for making clothes and things such as tablecloths and sheets.

cotton.quick_def: Cotton is a type of cloth made from soft fibres from a particular plant.

textile.quick_def: Textiles are types of cloth or fabric, especially ones that have been woven.

cottage.quick_def: A cottage is a small house, usually in the country.

spinners.quick_def: A spinner is a cricketer who makes the ball spin when he or she bowls it so that it changes direction when it hits the ground or the bat.

dyers.quick_def: Dyers are people whose job is to dye things, like cloth or hair, to change their color.

spinning.quick_def: If something spins or if you spin it, it turns quickly around a central point.

loom.quick_def: If something looms over you, it appears as a large or unclear shape, often in a frightening way.

mechanised.quick_def: If someone mechanizes a process, they cause it to be done by a machine or machines, when it was previously done by people.

coke.quick_def: Coke is a solid black substance that is produced from coal and is burned as a fuel.

metals.quick_def: Metal is a hard substance such as iron, steel, gold, or lead.

napoleonic.quick_def: Napoleonic means related to Napoleon or the time when Napoleon was powerful. Napoleon was a very famous French leader.

cooke.quick_def: Cooke is a surname. A surname is the family name that a person shares with other family members.

wheatstone.quick_def: Wheatstone is a surname. A surname is the family name of a person.

telegraphy.quick_def: the process of sending messages by telegraph

morse.quick_def: Morse refers to Samuel Morse, an American inventor who created Morse code. It can also be related to things about him or his code.

signalling.quick_def: A signal is a gesture, sound, or action which is intended to give a particular message to the person who sees or hears it.

urbanisation.quick_def: Urbanisation is the process when more and more people move from the countryside to cities, and cities grow bigger.

opposition.quick_def: Opposition is strong, angry, or violent disagreement and disapproval.

luddites.quick_def: Luddites are people who don't like new technology and oppose its use.

objected.quick_def: An object is anything that has a fixed shape or form, that you can touch or see, and that is not alive.

knitting.quick_def: If you knit something, especially an article of clothing, you make it from wool or a similar thread by using two knitting needles or a machine.

unskilled.quick_def: People who are unskilled do not have any special training for a job.

robbing.quick_def: If someone is robbed, they have money or property stolen from them.

livelihood.quick_def: Your livelihood is the job or other source of income that gives you the money to buy the things you need.

smashing.quick_def: If you smash something or if it smashes, it breaks into many pieces, for example when it is hit or dropped.

ned.quick_def: Ned is a name for a person.

ludd.quick_def: Ludd is related to a person who is against new technology. It's from a person's name, and people who don't like new machines are sometimes called related to Ludd.

apprentice.quick_def: An apprentice is a young person who works for someone in order to learn their skill.

rumoured.quick_def: If something is rumoured to be the case, people are suggesting that it is the case, but they do not know for certain.

nottingham.quick_def: a large town in the county of Nottinghamshire, on the River Trent. It is traditionally known for its lace industry. It has a fine Roman Catholic cathedral and two universities.

machine-breaking.quick_def: Machine-breaking means the act of destroying machines.

exchanged.quick_def: If two or more people exchange things of a particular kind, they give them to each other at the same time.

gunfire.quick_def: Gunfire is the repeated shooting of guns.

uprisings.quick_def: When there is an uprising, a group of people start fighting against the people who are in power in their country, because they want to bring about a political change.

punishable.quick_def: If a crime is punishable in a particular way, anyone who commits it is punished in that way.

unrest.quick_def: If there is unrest in a particular place or society, people are expressing anger and dissatisfaction about something, often by demonstrating or rioting.  [journalism]

mill.quick_def: A mill is a building in which grain is crushed to make flour.

huddersfield.quick_def: a town in West Yorkshire in the north of England, near Bradford

hanged.quick_def: If something hangs in a high place or position, or if you hang it there, it is attached there so it does not touch the ground.

luddite.quick_def: If you refer to someone as a Luddite, you are criticizing them for opposing changes in industrial methods, especially the introduction of new machines and modern methods.  [disapproval]

athlete.quick_def: An athlete is a person who does a sport, especially athletics, or track and field events.

raducanu.quick_def: Raducanu is a surname. Usually, it refers to a person with this family name.

withdrawal.quick_def: The withdrawal of something is the act or process of removing it, or ending it.  [formal]

wimbledon.quick_def: a district of south-west London, consisting mainly of houses. It is well known around the world as the home of the All England Club. Many people refer to the major international tennis competition which takes place there each summer simply as Wimbledon. It was first held in 1877

accumulation.quick_def: An accumulation of something is a large number of things which have been collected together or acquired over a period of time.

buzz.quick_def: If something buzzes or buzzes somewhere, it makes a long continuous sound, like the noise a bee makes when it is flying.

unavoidable.quick_def: If something is unavoidable, it cannot be avoided or prevented.

succeeding.quick_def: If you succeed in doing something, you manage to do it.

responds.quick_def: When you respond to something that is done or said, you react to it by doing or saying something yourself.

positively.quick_def: If you are positive about things, you are hopeful and confident, and think of the good aspects of a situation rather than the bad ones.

opponent.quick_def: A politician's opponents are other politicians who belong to a different party or who have different aims or policies.

cricket.quick_def: Cricket is an outdoor game played between two teams. Players try to score points, called runs, by hitting a ball with a wooden bat.

batting.quick_def: A bat is a specially shaped piece of wood that is used for hitting the ball in baseball, softball, cricket, rounders, or table tennis.

golf.quick_def: Golf is a game in which you use long sticks called clubs to hit a small, hard ball into holes that are spread out over a large area of grassy land.

inhibits.quick_def: If something inhibits an event or process, it prevents it or slows it down.

tighter.quick_def: Tight clothes or shoes are rather small and fit closely to your body.

perspiration.quick_def: Perspiration is the liquid which comes out on the surface of your skin when you are hot or frightened.  [formal]

palpitations.quick_def: When someone has palpitations, their heart beats very fast in an irregular way.

tremors.quick_def: A tremor is a small earthquake.

shortness.quick_def: the fact of being short in length or height

headaches.quick_def: If you have a headache, you have a pain in your head.

nausea.quick_def: Nausea is the condition of feeling sick and the feeling that you are going to vomit.

weakness.quick_def: If someone is weak, they are not healthy or do not have good muscles, so that they cannot move quickly or carry heavy things.

overthinking.quick_def: If you overthink, or if you overthink a problem, you spend too much time thinking about something.

nervousness.quick_def: If someone is nervous, they are frightened or worried about something that is happening or might happen, and show this in their behaviour.

coaches.quick_def: A coach is someone who trains a person or team of people in a particular sport.

physiological.quick_def: connected with the scientific study of the normal functions of living things

nerves.quick_def: Nerves are long thin fibres that transmit messages between your brain and other parts of your body.

visualisation.quick_def: Visualisation is the act of forming a picture in your mind of something.

recreating.quick_def: If you recreate something, you succeed in making it exist or seem to exist in a different time or place from its original time or place.

picturing.quick_def: A picture consists of lines and shapes which are drawn, painted, or printed on a surface and show a person, thing, or scene.

scoring.quick_def: In a sport or game, if a player scores a goal or a point, they gain a goal or point.

practise.quick_def: If you practise something, you keep doing it regularly in order to be able to do it better.

coping.quick_def: If you cope with a problem or task, you deal with it successfully.

mirzakhani.quick_def: Mirzakhani is a surname. It is used to call a person.

medal.quick_def: A medal is a small metal disc which is given as an award for bravery or as a prize in a sporting event.

tehran.quick_def: Tehran is the capital city of Iran.

girls.quick_def: A girl is a female child.

hooked.quick_def: A hook is a bent piece of metal or plastic that is used for catching or holding things, or for hanging things up.

resolute.quick_def: If you describe someone as resolute, you approve of them because they are very determined not to change their mind or not to give up a course of action.  [formal]

sums.quick_def: A sum of money is an amount of money.

aha.quick_def: Aha is used in writing to represent a noise that people make in conversation, for example to express satisfaction or surprise.  [feelings]

heights.quick_def: The height of a person or thing is their size or length from the bottom to the top.

winners.quick_def: The winner of a prize, race, or competition is the person, animal, or thing that wins it.

unexceptional.quick_def: If you describe something as unexceptional, you mean that it is ordinary, not very interesting, and often disappointing.

zurich.quick_def: Zurich is a well-known city in Switzerland.

polytechnic.quick_def: In Britain, a polytechnic was a college where you could go after leaving school in order to study academic subjects up to degree level, or to train for particular jobs. In 1992, all the polytechnics in Britain became universities.

plugging.quick_def: A plug on a piece of electrical equipment is a small plastic object with two or three metal pins which fit into the holes of an electric socket, connecting the equipment to the electricity supply.

rewrote.quick_def: If someone rewrites a piece of writing such as a book, an article, or a law, they write it in a different way in order to improve it.

mechanics.quick_def: A mechanic is someone whose job is to repair and maintain machines and engines, especially car engines.

pathways.quick_def: A pathway is a path which you can walk along or a route which you can take.

contemporaries.quick_def: Contemporary things are modern and relate to the present time.

teens.quick_def: If you are in your teens, you are between thirteen and nineteen years old.

eyre.quick_def: Eyre is a proper name, often used as a last name for a person.

collaborated.quick_def: When one person or group collaborates with another, they work together, especially on a book or on some research.

performers.quick_def: A performer is a person who acts, sings, or does other entertainment in front of audiences.

anders.quick_def: Anders is a name for a person.

ericsson.quick_def: Ericsson is a name, usually for a person.

eminent.quick_def: An eminent person is well-known and respected, especially because they are good at their profession.

innately.quick_def: An innate quality or ability is one which a person is born with.

memories.quick_def: Your memory is your ability to remember things.

educationist.quick_def: An educationist is the same as an educationalist.  [British]

pause.quick_def: If you pause while you are doing something, you stop for a short period and then continue.

disciplines.quick_def: Discipline is the practice of making people obey rules or standards of behaviour, and punishing them when they do not.

ballet.quick_def: Ballet is a type of very skilled and artistic dancing with carefully planned movements.

neurology.quick_def: Neurology is the study of the structure, function, and diseases of the nervous system.  [medicine]

spin-off.quick_def: A spin-off is something new that is created from an existing thing, like a new product, idea or business from an old one.

meals.quick_def: A meal is an occasion when people sit down and eat, usually at a regular time.

disadvantaged.quick_def: People who are disadvantaged or live in disadvantaged areas live in bad conditions and tend not to get a good education or have a reasonable standard of living.

epitome.quick_def: If you say that a person or thing is the epitome of something, you are emphasizing that they are the best possible example of a particular type of person or thing.  [formal, emphasis]

intellect.quick_def: Intellect is the ability to understand or deal with ideas and information.

ceri.quick_def: Ceri is a name for a person.

shipton.quick_def: Shipton is a name, usually used as a person's last name.

obi.quick_def: a wide piece of cloth worn around the waist (= middle part) of a Japanese kimono

maluku.quick_def: Maluku is a place name, which is a region in Indonesia.

utara.quick_def: Utara is a word that often means 'north' in some languages, like in Indonesian. It is used to name places related to the north.
