voyaging.quick_def: A voyage is a long journey on a ship or in a spacecraft.

indonesian.quick_def: Indonesian means belonging or relating to Indonesia, or to its people or culture.

northernmost.quick_def: The northernmost part of an area or the northernmost place is the one that is farthest towards the north.

wallacean.quick_def: Wallacean means related to the Wallacea region. Wallacea is an area with special animals and plants.

easiest.quick_def: If a job or action is easy, you can do it without difficulty or effort, because it is not complicated and causes no problems.

stepping.quick_def: If you take a step, you lift your foot and put it down in a different place, for example when you are walking.

island-hopping.quick_def: Island-hopping means traveling from one island to another island.

kelo.quick_def: Kelo is the name of a village.

shelters.quick_def: A shelter is a small building or covered place which is made to protect people from bad weather or danger.

permission.quick_def: If someone who has authority over you gives you permission to do something, they say that they will allow you to do it.

clam.quick_def: Clams are a kind of shellfish which can be eaten.

gebe.quick_def: Gebe is the name of an island. It's a special word for a particular place.

rainforests.quick_def: A rainforest is a thick forest of tall trees which is found in tropical areas where there is a lot of rain.

encompassing.quick_def: If something encompasses particular things, it includes them.

bisa.quick_def: Bisa is the name of an island.

wetter.quick_def: If something is wet, it is covered in water, rain, sweat, tears, or another liquid.

heavy-duty.quick_def: If something is heavy-duty, it is very strong and can be used for difficult or hard work.

grind.quick_def: If you grind a substance such as corn, you crush it between two hard surfaces or with a machine until it becomes a fine powder.

judging.quick_def: A judge is the person in a court of law who decides how the law should be applied, for example how criminals should be punished.

rothschild.quick_def: the name of a British family of businessmen and politicians, originally from Germany. Nathan Mayer Rothschild (1777-1836) opened the bank of N M Rothschild and Sons in London in 1798, and became a British citizen in 1804. His son Lionel Nathan Rothschild (1808-79) became the first Jewish Member of Parliament in 1858 and worked to achieve new legal freedoms for British Jews. Lionel's son Nathaniel Mayer Rothschild (1840-1915) became the first Jew to be made a life peer, in 1885. Miriam Rothschild (1908-2005), the granddaughter of Nathaniel, was a famous scientist.

cuscus.quick_def: A cuscus is a small animal that looks like a possum.

routinely.quick_def: If something is routinely done, it is done as a normal part of a job or process.

departure.quick_def: Departure or a departure is the act of going away from somewhere.

re-occupied.quick_def: If a place is re-occupied, people start to live or stay there again after they left it before.

wwfn.quick_def: WWFN is an organization that works to protect nature around the world.

pieter.quick_def: Pieter is a name for a person.

buffers.quick_def: A buffer is something that prevents something else from being harmed or that prevents two things from harming each other.

substantially.quick_def: If something changes substantially or is substantially different, it changes a lot or is very different.  [formal]

in-demand.quick_def: If something is in-demand, many people want it.

commodities.quick_def: A commodity is something that is sold for money.  [business]

pulpwood.quick_def: Pulpwood is wood that is used to make pulp, which can be used to make paper and other products.

emitters.quick_def: An emitter is someone or something that produces emissions of heat, light or gas, especially when this causes harm.

silvius.quick_def: Silvius is a name for a person.

land-use.quick_def: Land-use refers to the way people use land, like for farming, building houses, or making parks.

peatland.quick_def: an area in which peat occurs naturally

revenues.quick_def: Revenue is money that a company, organization, or government receives from people.  [business]

ditches.quick_def: A ditch is a long narrow channel cut into the ground at the side of a road or field.

swamps.quick_def: A swamp is an area of very wet land with wild plants growing in it.

corn.quick_def: Corn is used to refer to crops such as wheat and barley. It can also be used to refer to the seeds from these plants.  [British]

subsidence.quick_def: When there is subsidence in a place, the ground there sinks to a lower level.

clearances.quick_def: Clearance is the removal of old buildings, trees, or other things that are not wanted from an area.

subsides.quick_def: If a feeling or noise subsides, it becomes less strong or loud.

sumatra.quick_def: Sumatra is a big island in Indonesia.

flooded.quick_def: If there is a flood, a large amount of water covers an area which is usually dry, for example when a river flows over its banks or a pipe bursts.

drops.quick_def: If a level or amount drops or if someone or something drops it, it quickly becomes less.

landmass.quick_def: A landmass is a large area of land.

documented.quick_def: A document is one or more official pieces of paper with writing on them.

dave.quick_def: a first name for boys, short for David

sediment.quick_def: Sediment is solid material that settles at the bottom of a liquid, especially earth and pieces of rock that have been carried along and then left somewhere by water, ice, or wind.

seldom.quick_def: If something seldom happens, it happens only occasionally.

speaks.quick_def: When you speak, you use your voice in order to say something.

comfortably.quick_def: If you do something comfortably, you do it easily.

translator.quick_def: A translator is a person whose job is translating writing or speech from one language to another.

laptops.quick_def: A laptop or a laptop computer is a small portable computer.

lecturers.quick_def: A lecturer is a teacher at a university or college.

hitchhiker.quick_def: If you hitchhike, you travel by getting lifts from passing vehicles without paying.

stranger.quick_def: Something that is strange is unusual or unexpected, and makes you feel slightly nervous or afraid.

voice-controlled.quick_def: If a device is voice-controlled, you can make it work by using your voice.

accumulating.quick_def: When you accumulate things or when they accumulate, they collect or are gathered over a period of time.

polite.quick_def: Someone who is polite has good manners and behaves in a way that is socially correct and not rude to other people.

inferential.quick_def: If something is inferential, it is based on making guesses or conclusions from what you know.

apparatus.quick_def: The apparatus of an organization or system is its structure and method of operation.

procedure.quick_def: A procedure is a way of doing something, especially the usual or correct way.

drawers.quick_def: A drawer is part of a desk, chest, or other piece of furniture that is shaped like a box and is designed for putting things in. You pull it towards you to open it.

shut.quick_def: If you shut something such as a door or if it shuts, it moves so that it fills a hole or a space.

experimenter.quick_def: An experiment is a scientific test which is done in order to discover what happens to something in particular conditions.

understands.quick_def: If you understand someone or understand what they are saying, you know what they mean.

equivalence.quick_def: If there is equivalence between two things, they have the same use, function, size, or value.

marbles.quick_def: Marble is a type of very hard rock which feels cold when you touch it and which shines when it is cut and polished. Statues and parts of buildings are sometimes made of marble.

jump.quick_def: If you jump, you bend your knees, push against the ground with your feet, and move quickly upwards into the air.

five-year-olds.quick_def: Five-year-olds are children who are five years old.

four-year-olds.quick_def: Four-year-olds are children who are four years old.

three-year-olds.quick_def: Three-year-olds are children who are three years old.

clarification.quick_def: the act or process of making something clearer or easier to understand

inc.quick_def: Inc is short for Incorporated. It means a company that is a legal entity separate from its owners.

ahi.quick_def: AHI is an abbreviation for a company's name. It stands for a group that runs hotels and hires workers.

employs.quick_def: If a person or company employs you, they pay you to work for them.

casual.quick_def: If you are casual, you are, or you pretend to be, relaxed and not very concerned about what is happening or what you are doing.

ventures.quick_def: A venture is a project or activity which is new, exciting, and difficult because it involves the risk of failure.

sydney.quick_def: the capital of New South Wales in south-eastern Australia. It was the first British settlement in Australia and is the country's largest city and chief port. It has a fine natural harbour, crossed by the Sydney Harbour Bridge (opened in 1932), and a striking opera house (opened in 1973).

sah.quick_def: SAH is an abbreviation. It usually stands for a specific thing, like a hotel in this case.

labour-cost.quick_def: Labour-cost is the money a company spends on paying its workers.

implement.quick_def: If you implement something such as a plan, you ensure that what has been planned is done.

front-line.quick_def: If something or someone is front-line, they are in the most important or direct position in a particular activity or situation.

supervisor.quick_def: A supervisor is a person who supervises activities or people, especially workers or students.

applicants.quick_def: An applicant for something such as a job or a place at a college is someone who makes a formal written request to be given it.

advertised.quick_def: If you advertise something such as a product, an event, or a job, you tell people about it online, in newspapers, on television, or on posters in order to encourage them to buy the product, go to the event, or apply for the job.

recruits.quick_def: If you recruit people for an organization, you select them and persuade them to join it or work for it.

exhibiting.quick_def: If someone or something shows a particular quality, feeling, or type of behaviour, you can say that they exhibit it.  [formal]

follower.quick_def: A follower of a particular person, group, or belief is someone who supports or admires this person, group, or belief.

heads.quick_def: Your head is the top part of your body, which has your eyes, mouth, and brain in it.

multi-skilled.quick_def: If a person is multi-skilled, they have many different skills.

housekeeping.quick_def: Housekeeping is the work and organization involved in running a home, including the shopping and cleaning.

benchmarking.quick_def: In business, benchmarking is a process in which a company compares its products and methods with those of the most successful companies in its field, in order to try to improve its own performance.  [business]

reservations.quick_def: If you have reservations about something, you are not sure that it is entirely good or right.

incomplete.quick_def: Something that is incomplete is not yet finished, or does not have all the parts or details that it needs.

charge.quick_def: If you charge someone an amount of money, you ask them to pay that amount for something that you have sold to them or done for them.

loop.quick_def: A loop is a curved or circular shape in something long, for example in a piece of string.

collated.quick_def: When you collate pieces of information, you gather them all together and examine them.

reviewed.quick_def: A review of a situation or system is its formal examination by people in authority. This is usually done in order to see whether it can be improved or corrected.

non-implementation.quick_def: Non-implementation means not carrying out or putting into action a plan, idea, or suggestion.

govern.quick_def: To govern a place such as a country, or its people, means to be officially in charge of the place, and to have responsibility for making laws, managing the economy, and controlling public services.

policing.quick_def: The police are the official organization that is responsible for making sure that people obey the law.

dissemination.quick_def: To disseminate information or knowledge means to distribute it so that it reaches many people or organizations.  [formal]

impede.quick_def: If you impede someone or something, you make their movement, development, or progress difficult.  [formal]

applies.quick_def: If you apply for something such as a job or membership of an organization, you write a letter or email, or fill in a form in order to ask formally for it.

dialects.quick_def: A dialect is a form of a language that is spoken in a particular area.

metaphorical.quick_def: You use the word metaphorical to indicate that you are not using words with their ordinary meaning, but are describing something by means of an image or symbol.

literal.quick_def: The literal sense of a word or phrase is its most basic sense.

publicity.quick_def: Publicity is information or actions that are intended to attract the public's attention to someone or something.

strikes.quick_def: When there is a strike, workers stop doing their work for a period of time, usually in order to try to get better pay or conditions for themselves.  [business]

fatal.quick_def: A fatal action has very undesirable effects.

accidents.quick_def: An accident happens when a vehicle hits a person, an object, or another vehicle, causing injury or damage.

poisonous.quick_def: Something that is poisonous will kill you or make you ill if you swallow or absorb it.

remedy.quick_def: A remedy is a successful way of dealing with a problem.

foreign-language.quick_def: A foreign-language is a language that is not your native language.

consulted.quick_def: If you consult an expert or someone senior to you or consult with them, you ask them for their opinion and advice about what you should do or their permission to do something.

periodicals.quick_def: Periodicals are magazines, especially serious or academic ones, that are published at regular intervals.

publications.quick_def: The publication of a book or magazine is the act of printing it and sending it to shops to be sold.

stark.quick_def: Stark choices or statements are harsh and unpleasant.

insularity.quick_def: If you say that someone is insular, you are being critical of them because they are unwilling to meet new people or to consider new ideas.  [disapproval]

non-english-speaking.quick_def: If a person or a group is non-English-speaking, they do not speak English.

exempt.quick_def: If someone or something is exempt from a particular rule, duty, or obligation, they do not have to follow it or do it.

rowntree.quick_def: Rowntree is the name of a firm. A firm is a business company.

mackintosh.quick_def: A mackintosh is a raincoat, especially one made from a particular kind of waterproof cloth.  [mainly British]

publish.quick_def: When a company publishes a book or magazine, it prints copies of it, which are sent to shops to be sold.

xhosa.quick_def: a member of a race of black people who live in South Africa

courses.quick_def: Course is often used in the expression 'of course', or instead of 'of course' in informal spoken English. See of course.

glossaries.quick_def: A glossary of special, unusual, or technical words or expressions is an alphabetical list of them giving their meanings, for example at the end of a book on a particular subject.

consistency.quick_def: Consistency is the quality or condition of being consistent.

delayed.quick_def: If you delay doing something, you do not do it immediately or at the planned or expected time, but you leave it until later.

dawned.quick_def: Dawn is the time of day when light first appears in the sky, just before the sun rises.

french-speaking.quick_def: If a person or an area is French-speaking, they can speak French or French is commonly spoken there.

permeates.quick_def: If an idea, feeling, or attitude permeates a system or permeates society, it affects every part of it or is present throughout it.

land-sea.quick_def: Land-sea means related to both land and sea.

mixing.quick_def: If two substances mix or if you mix one substance with another, you stir or shake them together, or combine them in some other way, so that they become a single substance.

generic.quick_def: You use generic to describe something that refers or relates to a whole class of similar things.

sea-linked.quick_def: If something is sea-linked, it is connected to the sea.

foreland.quick_def: an area of land that lies in front of something

landward.quick_def: The landward side of something is the side nearest to the land or facing the land, rather than the sea.

imports.quick_def: To import products or raw materials means to buy them from another country for use in your own country.

breakwaters.quick_def: A breakwater is a wooden or stone wall that extends from the shore into the sea and is built in order to protect a harbour or beach from the force of the waves.

madras.quick_def: A madras curry is a rather hot spicy curry.

colombo.quick_def: Colombo is the name of a city, which is a place where many people live and work.

expensively.quick_def: If something is expensive, it costs a lot of money.

highways.quick_def: A highway is a main road, especially one that connects towns or cities.  [mainly US]

buenos.quick_def: In Spanish, 'Buenos' is often used as a part of greetings or names, and it can mean 'good'.

aires.quick_def: Aires is often part of the name 'Buenos Aires', which is the capital city of Argentina.

jakarta.quick_def: Jakarta is the name of a big city and the capital of Indonesia.

calcutta.quick_def: Calcutta is the former name of a big city in India. Now it's called Kolkata.

disproportionately.quick_def: Something that is disproportionate is surprising or unreasonable in amount or size, compared with something else.

non-port.quick_def: Non-port means not related to a port. It describes a place or thing that doesn't have the features or functions of a port.

cosmopolitan.quick_def: A cosmopolitan place or society is full of people from many different countries and cultures.  [approval]

races.quick_def: A race is a competition to see who is the fastest, for example in running, swimming, or driving.

jostle.quick_def: If people jostle you, they bump against you or push you in a way that annoys you, usually because you are in a crowd and they are trying to get past you.

smell.quick_def: The smell of something is a quality it has which you become aware of when you breathe in through your nose.

microcosm.quick_def: A microcosm is a small society, place, or activity which has all the typical features of a much larger one and so seems like a smaller version of it.  [formal]

powered.quick_def: If someone has power, they have a lot of control over people and activities.

draught.quick_def: A draught is a current of air that comes into a place in an undesirable way.  [British]

formerly.quick_def: If something happened or was true formerly, it happened or was true in the past.

by-passed.quick_def: If a place is by-passed, people or things go around it instead of going through it.

enriching.quick_def: To enrich something means to improve its quality, usually by adding something to it.

backwaters.quick_def: A backwater is a place that is isolated.

charleston.quick_def: The Charleston is a lively dance that was popular in the 1920s.

salem.quick_def: the capital city of the US state of Oregon

surat.quick_def: Surat is the name of a place, like a city.

galle.quick_def: Galle is the name of a place, usually a city or a port.

melaka.quick_def: Melaka is the name of a place, a city or a state in Malaysia.

soochow.quick_def: Soochow is an old name for Suzhou, a city in China.

distributes.quick_def: If you distribute things, you hand them or deliver them to a number of people.

bulk.quick_def: You can refer to something's bulk when you want to emphasize that it is very large.  [written, emphasis]

unloading.quick_def: If you unload goods from a vehicle, or you unload a vehicle, you remove the goods from the vehicle, usually after they have been transported from one place to another.

refining.quick_def: When a substance is refined, it is made pure by having all other substances removed from it.

unload.quick_def: If you unload goods from a vehicle, or you unload a vehicle, you remove the goods from the vehicle, usually after they have been transported from one place to another.

repack.quick_def: When you repack something, you put it into a new package or container.

reship.quick_def: When you reship something, you send it again after it has been received or unloaded.

docks.quick_def: A dock is an enclosed area in a harbour where ships go to be loaded, unloaded, and repaired.

bund.quick_def: a wall of stone or earth, built to stop an area being covered by a large amount of water

proximity.quick_def: Proximity to a place or person is nearness to that place or person.  [formal]

bombay.quick_def: Bombay is an old name for Mumbai, a big city in India.

yokohama.quick_def: Yokohama is a big city in Japan. It has a busy harbor and many people live there.

grouped.quick_def: A group of people or things is a number of people or things which are together in one place at one time.

metropolis.quick_def: A metropolis is the largest, busiest, and most important city in a country or region.

mistake.quick_def: If you make a mistake, you do something which you did not intend to do, or which produces a result that you do not want.

absenteeism.quick_def: Absenteeism is the fact or habit of frequently being away from work or school, usually without a good reason.

brisbane.quick_def: the capital city of Queensland, Australia, a port on the Brisbane River

nurses.quick_def: A nurse is a person whose job is to care for people who are ill.

utilising.quick_def: When you are utilising something, you are using it to achieve a purpose.

entitlement.quick_def: An entitlement to something is the right to have it or do it.  [formal]

holiday.quick_def: A holiday is a period of time during which you relax and enjoy yourself away from home. People sometimes refer to their holiday as their holidays.  [British]

norton.quick_def: Norton is a name, usually a person's last name.

nursing.quick_def: Nursing is the profession of looking after people who are ill.

sympathetic.quick_def: If you are sympathetic to someone who is in a bad situation, you are kind to them and show that you understand their feelings.

respondents.quick_def: A respondent is a person who replies to something such as a survey or set of questions.

longitudinal.quick_def: A longitudinal line or structure goes from one end of an object to the other rather than across it from side to side.

hacket.quick_def: Hacket is a proper name, usually used as a person's name.

bycio.quick_def: Bycio is a person's last name. A last name is what a family members share.

guion.quick_def: Guion is a name, usually used for a person.

bereavement.quick_def: Bereavement is the sorrow you feel or the state you are in when a relative or close friend dies.

registered.quick_def: A register is an official list or record of people or things.

roster.quick_def: A roster is a list which gives details of the order in which different people have to do a particular job.

clinical.quick_def: Clinical means involving or relating to the direct medical treatment or testing of patients.  [medicine]

duty.quick_def: Duty is work that you have to do for your job.

communicated.quick_def: If you communicate with someone, you share or exchange information with them, for example by speaking, writing, or using equipment. You can also say that two people communicate.

ranged.quick_def: A range of things is a number of different things of the same general kind.

year-to-year.quick_def: Year-to-year means comparing one year with the next year.

two-year.quick_def: If something is two-year, it lasts for two years.

non-financial.quick_def: If something is non-financial, it has nothing to do with money.

momentum.quick_def: If a process or movement gains momentum, it keeps developing or happening more quickly and keeps becoming less likely to stop.

ceasing.quick_def: If something ceases, it stops happening or existing.  [formal]

disempowered.quick_def: If someone or something disempowers you, they take away your power or influence.

rosters.quick_def: A roster is a list which gives details of the order in which different people have to do a particular job.

management-employee.quick_def: Management-employee refers to the relationship or things related to both the management and the employees in a company or organization.

se.quick_def: SE is a written abbreviation for south-east.

vain.quick_def: A vain attempt or action is one that fails to achieve what was intended.

tangibly.quick_def: If something is tangible, it is clear enough or definite enough to be easily seen, felt, or noticed.

measurable.quick_def: If you describe something as measurable, you mean that it is large enough to be noticed or to be significant.  [formal]

motorways.quick_def: A motorway is a major road that has been specially built for fast travel over long distances. Motorways have several lanes and special places where traffic gets on and leaves.  [British]

buses.quick_def: A bus is a large motor vehicle which carries passengers from one place to another. Buses drive along particular routes, and you have to pay to travel in them.

taxis.quick_def: A taxi is a car driven by a person whose job is to take people where they want to go in return for money.

emit.quick_def: If something emits heat, light, gas, or a smell, it produces it and sends it out by means of a physical or chemical process.  [formal]

afflicted.quick_def: If you are afflicted by pain, illness, or disaster, it affects you badly and makes you suffer.  [formal]

conveniently.quick_def: If a way of doing something is convenient, it is easy, or very useful or suitable for a particular purpose.

wagon.quick_def: A wagon is a strong vehicle with four wheels, usually pulled by horses or oxen and used for carrying heavy loads.

one-way.quick_def: A one-way thing allows movement or traffic in only one direction.

injured.quick_def: If you injure a person or animal, you damage some part of their body.

blamed.quick_def: If you blame a person or thing for something bad, you believe or say that they are responsible for it or that they caused it.

surpass.quick_def: If one person or thing surpasses another, the first is better than, or has more of a particular quality than, the second.

mode.quick_def: A mode of life or behaviour is a particular way of living or behaving.  [formal]

transit.quick_def: Transit is the carrying of goods or people by vehicle from one place to another.

exhaust.quick_def: If something exhausts you, it makes you so tired, either physically or mentally, that you have no energy left.

neighbourhoods.quick_def: A neighbourhood is one of the parts of a town where people live.

democratic.quick_def: A democratic country, government, or political system is governed by representatives who are elected by the people.

blessed.quick_def: When someone such as a priest blesses people or things, he or she asks for God's favour and protection for them.

lean.quick_def: When you lean in a particular direction, you bend your body in that direction.

electronically.quick_def: An electronic device has transistors or silicon chips which control and change the electric current passing through the device.

tolled.quick_def: When a bell tolls or when someone tolls it, it rings slowly and repeatedly, often as a sign that someone has died.

charges.quick_def: If you charge someone an amount of money, you ask them to pay that amount for something that you have sold to them or done for them.

geared.quick_def: The gears on a machine or vehicle are a device for changing the rate at which energy is changed into motion.

predominate.quick_def: If one type of person or thing predominates in a group, there is more of that type of person or thing in the group than of any other.  [formal]

id.quick_def: If you have ID or an ID, you are carrying a document such as an identity card or driving licence which proves that you are a particular person.

identities.quick_def: Your identity is who you are.

authenticated.quick_def: If you authenticate something, you state officially that it is genuine after examining it.

verified.quick_def: If you verify something, you check that it is true by careful examination or investigation.

biometrics.quick_def: Biometrics is a technology that uses physical or biological features to tell people apart.

fast-growing.quick_def: If something is fast-growing, it grows very quickly.

high-security.quick_def: If a place is high-security, it has a lot of safety measures to protect it from danger or unauthorized entry.

popping.quick_def: Pop is modern music that usually has a strong rhythm and uses electronic equipment.

prisons.quick_def: A prison is a building where criminals are kept as punishment or where people accused of a crime are kept before their trial.

day-care.quick_def: Day-care is a service where people take their children or other dependents during the day so that they can be looked after.

fingerprints.quick_def: Fingerprints are marks made by a person's fingers which show the lines on the skin. Everyone's fingerprints are different, so they can be used to identify criminals.

biometric.quick_def: Biometric tests and devices use biological information about a person to create a detailed record of their personal characteristics.

storing.quick_def: A store is a building or part of a building where things are sold. In British English, store is used mainly to refer to a large shop selling a variety of goods, but in American English a store can be any size of shop.

digitised.quick_def: To digitize information means to turn it into a form that can be read easily by a computer.

wishes.quick_def: A wish is a desire or strong feeling that you want to have something or do something.

irises.quick_def: The iris is the round coloured part of a person's eye.

retinas.quick_def: Your retina is the area at the back of your eye. It receives the image that you see and then sends the image to your brain.

typing.quick_def: A type of something is a group of those things that have particular features in common.

odours.quick_def: An odour is a particular and distinctive smell.

fingerprint.quick_def: Fingerprints are marks made by a person's fingers which show the lines on the skin. Everyone's fingerprints are different, so they can be used to identify criminals.

scanners.quick_def: A scanner is a machine which is used to examine, identify, or record things, for example by using a beam of light, sound, or X-rays.

deployed.quick_def: To deploy troops, weapons, or resources means to make them ready to be used.

law-enforcement.quick_def: Law-enforcement means the activity of making sure people follow the laws. It is done by the police and other official groups.

verification.quick_def: the act of showing or checking that something is true or accurate

voted.quick_def: A vote is a choice made by a particular person or group in a meeting or an election.

handkey.quick_def: A handkey is a kind of hand scanner that can read the special shape, size and differences of people's hands.

irregularities.quick_def: If events or actions occur at irregular intervals, the periods of time between them are of different lengths.

powerplants.quick_def: Powerplants are places where power, like electricity, is made.

trainers.quick_def: A train is a number of carriages, cars, or trucks which are all connected together and which are pulled by an engine along a railway. Trains carry people and goods from one place to another.

airports.quick_def: An airport is a place where aircraft land and take off, which has buildings and facilities for passengers.

luggage.quick_def: Luggage is the suitcases and bags that you take with you when travel.

maker.quick_def: The maker of a product is the firm that manufactures it.

dispensers.quick_def: A dispenser is a machine or container designed so that you can get an item or quantity of something from it in an easy and convenient way.

iris.quick_def: The iris is the round coloured part of a person's eye.

attendance.quick_def: Someone's attendance at an event or an institution is the fact that they are present at the event or go regularly to the institution.

thorny.quick_def: A thorny plant or tree is covered with thorns.

abuse.quick_def: Abuse of someone is cruel and violent treatment of them.

tempted.quick_def: Something that tempts you attracts you and makes you want it, even though it may be wrong or harmful.

health-insurance.quick_def: Health-insurance is a kind of insurance that pays for people's medical costs when they are sick or hurt.

credit-card.quick_def: A credit-card is a small plastic card that you can use to buy things. You don't need to pay the money right away. You pay it later.

cigarettes.quick_def: Cigarettes are small tubes of paper containing tobacco which people smoke.

fatty.quick_def: Fatty food contains a lot of fat.

analyst.quick_def: An analyst is a person whose job is to analyse a subject and give opinions about it.

stigmatise.quick_def: If someone or something is stigmatized, they are unfairly regarded by many people as being bad or having something to be ashamed of.

recipients.quick_def: The recipient of something is the person who receives it.  [formal]

shoppers.quick_def: A shop is a building or part of a building where things are sold.  [mainly British]

misjudging.quick_def: If you say that someone has misjudged a person or situation, you mean that they have formed an incorrect idea or opinion about them, and often that they have made a wrong decision as a result of this.

mintel.quick_def: Mintel is the name of a market research organization. A market research organization studies the market to find out what people like and what products are popular.

untouched.quick_def: Something that is untouched by something else is not affected by it.

predicts.quick_def: If you predict an event, you say that it will happen.

climbed.quick_def: If you climb something such as a tree, mountain, or ladder, or climb up it, you move towards the top of it. If you climb down it, you move towards the bottom of it.

unconcerned.quick_def: If a person is unconcerned about something, usually something that most people would care about, they are not interested in it or worried about it.

spenders.quick_def: If a person or organization is a big spender or a compulsive spender, for example, they spend a lot of money or are unable to stop themselves spending money.

manual.quick_def: Manual work is work in which you use your hands or your physical strength rather than your mind.

hughes.quick_def: Hughes is a common surname. A surname is the family name that people in a family share.

armchair.quick_def: An armchair is a big comfortable chair which has a support on each side for your arms.

greens.quick_def: Green is the colour of grass or leaves.

dealings.quick_def: Someone's dealings with a person or organization are the relations that they have with them or the business that they do with them.

oppressive.quick_def: If you describe a society, its laws, or customs as oppressive, you think they treat people cruelly and unfairly.

regimes.quick_def: If you refer to a government or system of running a country as a regime, you are critical of it because you think it is not democratic and uses unacceptable methods.  [disapproval]

ethicals.quick_def: Ethicals are people who care about moral principles and do things in a right way.

twenty-first.quick_def: The twenty-first is the ordinal number that comes after the twentieth and shows the position in a series. It means the one in the 21st place.

honesty.quick_def: Honesty is the quality of being honest.

ozone.quick_def: Ozone is a colourless gas which is a form of oxygen. There is a layer of ozone high above the earth's surface.

agenda.quick_def: You can refer to the political issues which are important at a particular time as an agenda.

olds.quick_def: The word 'olds' is often used in the form 'year olds' to talk about people of a certain age. For example, '16 year olds' means people who are 16 years old.

impedes.quick_def: If you impede someone or something, you make their movement, development, or progress difficult.  [formal]

fruitless.quick_def: Fruitless actions, events, or efforts do not achieve anything at all.

illiteracy.quick_def: Illiteracy is the state of not knowing how to read or write.

tragic.quick_def: A tragic event or situation is extremely sad, usually because it involves death or suffering.

long-established.quick_def: If something is long-established, it has existed for a long time and is well-known and accepted.

primers.quick_def: Primer is a type of paint that is put onto wood in order to prepare it for the main layer of paint.

obtrusive.quick_def: If you say that someone or something is obtrusive, you think they are noticeable in an unpleasant way.

impoverished.quick_def: Something that impoverishes a person or a country makes them poor.

interfere.quick_def: If you say that someone interferes in a situation, you mean they get involved in it although it does not concern them and their involvement is not wanted.  [disapproval]

antipodes.quick_def: People sometimes refer to Australia and New Zealand as the Antipodes.  [British]

aloud.quick_def: When you say something, read, or laugh aloud, you speak or laugh so that other people can hear you.

fluently.quick_def: Someone who is fluent in a particular language can speak the language easily and correctly. You can also say that someone speaks fluent French, Chinese, or some other language.

barking.quick_def: When a dog barks, it makes a short, loud noise, once or several times.

formative.quick_def: A formative period of time or experience is one that has an important and lasting influence on a person's character and attitudes.

neighbours.quick_def: Your neighbour is someone who lives near you.

It was one of the original thirteen colonies, and the American Revolution was ended by the Battle of Yorktown in Virginia. Richmond became the capital of the Confederate States and the Civil War ended at Appomattox Court House. Eight presidents were born in Virginia, including George Washington, Thomas Jefferson and Woodrow Wilson. Local products include tobacco and electrical equipment. Among the tourist attractions are Williamsburg, Mount Vernon and Monticello.

exhibitions.quick_def: An exhibition is a public event at which pictures, sculptures, or other objects of interest are displayed, for example at a museum or art gallery.

installations.quick_def: An installation is a place that contains equipment and machinery which are being used for a particular purpose.

married.quick_def: If you are married, you have a husband or wife.

black-and-white.quick_def: If something is black-and-white, it is only in black and white colors, not in color.

portraits.quick_def: A portrait is a painting, drawing, or photograph of a particular person.

botanical.quick_def: Botanical books, research, and activities relate to the scientific study of plants.

magnified.quick_def: To magnify an object means to make it appear larger than it really is, by means of a special lens or mirror.

metre-wide.quick_def: If something is metre-wide, it has a width of one metre.

solitude.quick_def: Solitude is the state of being alone, especially when this is peaceful and pleasant.

sun-bleached.quick_def: If something is sun-bleached, its color has been made lighter by the sun.

sparked.quick_def: A spark is a tiny bright piece of burning material that flies up from something that is burning.

southwestern.quick_def: Southwestern means in or from the southwest of a region or country.

skull.quick_def: Your skull is the bony part of your head which encloses your brain.

pelvis.quick_def: Your pelvis is the wide, curved group of bones at the level of your hips.

convex.quick_def: Convex is used to describe something that curves outwards in the middle.

formations.quick_def: The formation of something is the starting or creation of it.

cliffs.quick_def: A cliff is a high area of land with a very steep side, especially one next to the sea.

close-up.quick_def: A close-up is a very near view or picture of something.

ghost.quick_def: A ghost is the spirit of a dead person that someone believes they can see or feel.

nestled.quick_def: If you nestle or are nestled somewhere, you move into a comfortable position, usually by pressing against someone or against something soft.

locales.quick_def: A locale is a small area, for example the place where something happens or where the action of a book or film is set.  [formal]

walled.quick_def: A wall is one of the vertical sides of a building or room.

patio.quick_def: A patio is an area of flat blocks or concrete next to a house, where people can sit and relax or eat.

reinvented.quick_def: To reinvent something means to change it so that it seems different and new.

aerial.quick_def: You talk about aerial attacks and aerial photographs to indicate that people or things on the ground are attacked or photographed by people in aeroplanes.

mural.quick_def: A mural is a picture painted on a wall.

proportions.quick_def: A proportion of a group or an amount is a part of it.  [formal]

derive.quick_def: If you derive something such as pleasure or benefit from a person or from something, you get it from them.  [formal]

tomorrow.quick_def: You use tomorrow to refer to the day after today.

It is a popular place for holidays because of the warm weather and Miami Beach, which is on an island three miles off the coast. The city is also an important financial and industrial centre. It became a town in 1892 and grew rapidly in the 1920s. Many immigrants live in the districts of 'Little Havana' and 'Little Haiti'. More than half of Miami's population are Hispanic.

yanira.quick_def: Yanira is a name used for a person.

pineda.quick_def: Pineda is a family name. People use it to identify a person.

coordinator.quick_def: If you coordinate an activity, you organize the various people and things involved in it.

seawalls.quick_def: Seawalls are walls built along the coast to protect the land from the sea, like waves and floods.

muddy.quick_def: Something that is muddy contains mud or is covered in mud.

trapping.quick_def: A trap is a device which is placed somewhere or a hole which is dug somewhere in order to catch animals or birds.

elevating.quick_def: When someone or something achieves a more important rank or status, you can say that they are elevated to it.  [formal]

semi-permeable.quick_def: If something is semi-permeable, it allows some substances to pass through but not others.

decision-makers.quick_def: Decision-makers are people who have the power to make important choices or decisions.

fluffy.quick_def: If you describe something such as a towel or a toy animal as fluffy, you mean that it is very soft.

puppy.quick_def: A puppy is a young dog.

affection.quick_def: If you regard someone or something with affection, you like them and are fond of them.

utah.quick_def: a western US state which is one of the Rocky Mountain States. About two-thirds of the population are Mormons. It was named after the UteNative American people, and its popular name is the Beehive State. Other Native American groups, such as the Navajo, lived in the area when the Mormons began to settle there in 1847. It became a state in 1896. Its products include cattle, pigs, copper (= a soft red-brown metal), gold, silver, oil and medical instruments. Tourist attractions include the Great Salt Lake, the Rainbow Bridge and Zion National Park.

ethiopian.quick_def: Ethiopian means belonging or relating to Ethiopia, or to its people, language, or culture.

aulus.quick_def: Aulus is a name for a person.

probable.quick_def: If you say that something is probable, you mean that it is likely to be true or likely to happen.  [vagueness]

incendiary.quick_def: Incendiary weapons or attacks are ones that cause large fires.

corps.quick_def: A Corps is a part of the army which has special duties.

tensile.quick_def: You use tensile when you are talking about the amount of stress that materials such as wire, rope, and concrete can take without breaking; a technical term in engineering.

cracking.quick_def: If something hard cracks, or if you crack it, it becomes slightly damaged, with lines appearing on its surface.

alloys.quick_def: An alloy is a metal that is made by mixing two or more types of metal together.

alpha.quick_def: the first letter of the Greek alphabet (A, α)

beta.quick_def: the second letter of the Greek alphabet (B, β)

toughening.quick_def: If you toughen something or if it toughens, you make it stronger so that it will not break easily.

rash.quick_def: If someone is rash or does rash things, they act without thinking carefully first, and therefore make mistakes or behave foolishly.

panes.quick_def: A pane of glass is a flat sheet of glass in a window or door.

contamination.quick_def: If something is contaminated by waste, dirt, chemicals, or radiation, it is made dirty or harmful.

photos.quick_def: A photo is the same as a photograph.

rhythms.quick_def: A rhythm is a regular series of sounds or movements.

temperate.quick_def: Temperate is used to describe a climate or a place which is never extremely hot or extremely cold.

midwinter.quick_def: Midwinter is the period in the middle of winter.

short-day.quick_def: If something is short-day, it needs a short period of daylight to grow or do something.

long-day.quick_def: A long-day thing means it needs a long period of daylight to grow or do something.

vegetative.quick_def: If someone is in a vegetative state, they are unable to move, think, or speak, and their condition is not likely to improve.  [medicine]

day-neutral.quick_def: If a plant is day-neutral, it can flower without being affected by the length of day or night.

chances.quick_def: If there is a chance of something happening, it is possible that it will happen.

temperate-zone.quick_def: A temperate-zone is an area on the Earth where the climate is neither too hot nor too cold.

ripening.quick_def: When crops ripen or when the sun ripens them, they become ripe.

annuals.quick_def: Annual events happen once every year.

abietifolia.quick_def: It is a word used to name a specific kind of thing, like a plant species.

photosynthetic.quick_def: If something is photosynthetic, it can use sunlight to make food.

maximal.quick_def: as great or as large as possible

one-quarter.quick_def: One-quarter means one part out of four equal parts. It is the same as 25% or 0.25.

shade-tolerant.quick_def: If a plant is shade-tolerant, it can grow well in places with little sunlight.

shade-intolerant.quick_def: If a plant is shade-intolerant, it can't grow well in the shade.

classification.quick_def: A classification is a division or category in a system which divides things into groups or types.

horticulture.quick_def: Horticulture is the study and practice of growing plants.

occupying.quick_def: The people who occupy a building or a place are the people who live or work there.

grime.quick_def: Grime is dirt which has collected on the surface of something.

directing.quick_def: Direct means moving towards a place or object, without changing direction and without stopping, for example in a journey.

understorey.quick_def: a layer of plants, bushes, etc. that is found below the main canopy of a forest (= the top leaves and branches of the trees that form a thick layer)

seeming.quick_def: You use seem to say that someone or something gives the impression of having a particular quality, or of happening in the way you describe.

ais.quick_def: AIS is short for the Australian Institute of Sport, which is a place where people can live and train under coaches' guidance.

asc.quick_def: ASC is an abbreviation. It stands for an organization, like the Australian Sports Commission in this case.

finances.quick_def: When someone finances something such as a project or a purchase, they provide the money that is needed to pay for them.

second-by-second.quick_def: Second-by-second means happening or measured every single second.

hundredth.quick_def: The hundredth item in a series is the one that you count as number one hundred.

millimetre.quick_def: A millimetre is a metric unit of length that is equal to a tenth of a centimetre or a thousandth of a metre.

world-beating.quick_def: If something is world-beating, it is the best in the world.

swimmers.quick_def: A swimmer is a person who swims, especially for sport or pleasure, or a person who is swimming.

slices.quick_def: A slice of bread, meat, fruit, or other food is a thin piece that has been cut from a larger piece.

side-on.quick_def: If you look at something side-on, you look at it from the side.

sweating.quick_def: Sweat is the salty colourless liquid which comes through your skin when you are hot, ill, or afraid.

cyclists.quick_def: A cyclist is someone who rides a bicycle, or is riding a bicycle.

all-encompassing.quick_def: If something is all-encompassing, it includes everything or everyone related to a particular thing.

delays.quick_def: If you delay doing something, you do not do it immediately or at the planned or expected time, but you leave it until later.

discs.quick_def: A disc is a flat, circular shape or object.

cargo-handling.quick_def: Cargo-handling means the work of moving, loading, and unloading cargo.

schedules.quick_def: A schedule is a plan that gives a list of events or tasks and the times at which each one should happen or be done.

worrying.quick_def: If you worry, you keep thinking about problems that you have or about unpleasant things that might happen.

importing.quick_def: To import products or raw materials means to buy them from another country for use in your own country.

portions.quick_def: A portion of something is a part of it.

dual-purpose.quick_def: If something is dual-purpose, it can be used for two different purposes.

loose.quick_def: Something that is loose is not firmly held or fixed in place.

deck.quick_def: A deck on a vehicle such as a bus or ship is a lower or upper area of it.

deregulate.quick_def: To deregulate something means to remove controls and regulations from it.

hauliers.quick_def: A haulier is a company or a person that transports goods by road.  [British]

freed.quick_def: If something is free, you can have it or use it without paying for it.

albeit.quick_def: You use albeit to introduce a fact or comment which reduces the force or significance of what you have just said.  [formal]

toleration.quick_def: If you tolerate a situation or person, you accept them although you do not particularly like them.

anti-competitive.quick_def: If something is anti-competitive, it stops or makes it hard for businesses to compete fairly.

unnecessarily.quick_def: without any need; in a way that is not needed or is more than is needed

camps.quick_def: A camp is a collection of huts and other buildings that is provided for a particular group of people, such as refugees, prisoners, or soldiers, as a place to live or stay.

thaws.quick_def: When ice, snow, or something else that is frozen thaws, it melts.

drips.quick_def: When liquid drips somewhere, or you drip it somewhere, it falls in individual small drops.

refreezes.quick_def: When something refreezes, it freezes again after it has melted.

shrink.quick_def: If cloth or clothing shrinks, it becomes smaller in size, usually as a result of being washed.

ice-free.quick_def: If a place is ice-free, there is no ice in it.

cloudier.quick_def: If it is cloudy, there are a lot of clouds in the sky.

jealously.quick_def: If someone is jealous, they feel angry or bitter because they think that another person is trying to take a lover or friend, or a possession, away from them.

hard-won.quick_def: If something is hard-won, it is achieved after a lot of effort and difficulty.

newest.quick_def: Something that is new has been recently created, built, or invented or is in the process of being created, built, or invented.

nunavut.quick_def: a territory of northern Canada, created in 1999 as an Inuit territory from a part of the Northwest Territories. The capital is Iqaluit.

treeless.quick_def: A treeless area or place has no trees in it.

meagre.quick_def: If you describe an amount or quantity of something as meagre, you are critical of it because it is very small or not enough.  [disapproval]

pickings.quick_def: You can refer to the money that can be made easily in a particular place or area of activity as the pickings.

colonists.quick_def: Colonists are the people who start a colony or the people who are among the first to live in a particular colony.

thule.quick_def: Thule refers to a group of people. They are a kind of ethnic group.

amagoalik.quick_def: Amagoalik is a name of a person.

murdoch.quick_def: Murdoch is a name, often used as a proper name for a person, a place or an institution.

newman.quick_def: Newman is a common name, usually used for a person.

inefficient.quick_def: Inefficient people, organizations, systems, or machines do not use time, energy, or other resources in the best way.

grossly.quick_def: You use gross to describe something unacceptable or unpleasant to a very great amount, degree, or intensity.

objection.quick_def: If you make or raise an objection to something, you say that you do not like it or agree with it.

oregon.quick_def: a state in the north-western US, also called the Beaver State. The largest city is Portland, and the capital city is Salem. Captain James Cook sailed along its coast in 1778, and Lewis and Clark visited the area in 1805. Oregon became a state in 1859. Its products include salmon and other fish, wood, paper, berries and nuts. Tourists can visit Crater Lake National Park, the Oregon Dunes National Recreation Area and the John Day Fossil Beds National Monument.

federal.quick_def: A federal country or system of government is one in which the different states or provinces of the country have important powers to make their own laws and decisions.

referendum.quick_def: If a country holds a referendum on a particular policy, they ask the people to vote on the policy and show whether or not they agree with it.

spectacularly.quick_def: Something that is spectacular is very impressive or dramatic.

commuting.quick_def: If you commute, you travel a long distance every day between your home and your place of work.

refutes.quick_def: If you refute an argument, accusation, or theory, you prove that it is wrong or untrue.  [formal]

starkly.quick_def: Stark choices or statements are harsh and unpleasant.

jams.quick_def: Jam is a thick sweet food that is made by cooking fruit with a large amount of sugar, and that is usually spread on bread.  [mainly British]

dispersal.quick_def: Dispersal is the spreading of things over a wide area.

flourishes.quick_def: If something flourishes, it is successful, active, or common, and developing quickly and strongly.

face-to-face.quick_def: When you have a face-to-face meeting or talk with someone, you are in the same place as them and can see each other directly.

afflicting.quick_def: If you are afflicted by pain, illness, or disaster, it affects you badly and makes you suffer.  [formal]

confirms.quick_def: If something confirms what you believe, suspect, or fear, it shows that it is definitely true.

manton.quick_def: Manton is a name, usually used for a person.

demographer.quick_def: a person who studies the changing number of births, deaths, diseases, etc. in a community over a period of time

downside.quick_def: The downside of a situation is the aspect of it which is less positive, pleasant, or useful than its other aspects.

better-educated.quick_def: If someone is better-educated, they have more knowledge and learning than others.

dressing.quick_def: A dress is a piece of clothing for a woman or girl that covers the body and part or all of the legs.

unaided.quick_def: If you do something unaided, you do it without help from anyone or anything else.

medicare.quick_def: In the United States, Medicare is a government program that provides health insurance to cover medical costs for people aged 65 and older.

greying.quick_def: If someone has greying hair, there is a lot of grey hair mixed with the person's natural colour.

burden.quick_def: If you describe a problem or a responsibility as a burden, you mean that it causes someone a lot of difficulty, worry, or hard work.

self-reliance.quick_def: Self-reliance means the ability to do things by yourself and not depend on others.

toilet.quick_def: A toilet is a large bowl with a seat, or a platform with a hole, which is connected to a water system and which you use when you want to get rid of urine or faeces from your body.

macarthur.quick_def: MacArthur is a proper name, often used as a surname for a person.

cotman.quick_def: Cotman is a surname, which is used to identify a person.

irvine.quick_def: Irvine is the name of a place, like a city or a town.

brain-derived.quick_def: If something is brain-derived, it comes from the brain.

coursing.quick_def: Course is often used in the expression 'of course', or instead of 'of course' in informal spoken English. See of course.

deteriorating.quick_def: If something deteriorates, it becomes worse in some way.

seeman.quick_def: Seeman is a surname, which is a family name used to identify a person's family.

epidemiologist.quick_def: An epidemiologist is a doctor who specializes in the occurrence, distribution, and control of epidemic diseases.

drawbacks.quick_def: A drawback is an aspect of something or someone that makes them less acceptable than they would otherwise be.

asleep.quick_def: Someone who is asleep is sleeping.

fare.quick_def: A fare is the money that you pay for a journey that you make, for example, in a bus, train, or taxi.

count.quick_def: When you count, you say all the numbers one after another up to a particular number.

numeration.quick_def: Numeration is the act of counting or the system of counting numbers.

paramount.quick_def: Something that is paramount or of paramount importance is more important than anything else.

semipermanent.quick_def: If something is semipermanent, it lasts for a long time but not forever.

counted.quick_def: When you count, you say all the numbers one after another up to a particular number.

suffice.quick_def: If you say that something will suffice, you mean it will be enough to achieve a purpose or to fulfil a need.  [formal]

gothic.quick_def: Gothic architecture and religious art was produced in the Middle Ages. Its features include tall pillars, high curved ceilings, and pointed arches.

tachund.quick_def: Tachund is an old-fashioned word that means ten.

teon.quick_def: Teon is an old-English word that means ten.

interchangeable.quick_def: Things that are interchangeable can be exchanged with each other without it making any difference.

hund.quick_def: In old-English, 'hund' is a word for the number 100.

anglo-saxon.quick_def: Anglo-Saxon refers to the people, language or culture of the Anglo-Saxons, who were a group of Germanic people in England long ago.

denoted.quick_def: If one thing denotes another, it is a sign or indication of it.  [formal]

teontig.quick_def: Teontig means ten. It is used to show the number 10.

notational.quick_def: If something is notational, it is related to a system of signs or symbols used to represent information.

tsimshian.quick_def: Tsimshian refers to a group of Native Americans in British Columbia, or their language.

numerated.quick_def: When you numerate something, you count it or give it a number.

intermixed.quick_def: If things are intermixed, they are mixed together.

pebbles.quick_def: A pebble is a small, smooth, round stone which is found on beaches and at the bottom of rivers.

des.quick_def: a first name for boys, short for Desmond

capucines.quick_def: Capucines is a name of a place, like a street or an area.

crush.quick_def: To crush something means to press it very hard so that its shape is destroyed or so that it breaks into pieces.

imply.quick_def: If you imply that something is the case, you say something which indicates that it is the case in an indirect way.

whim.quick_def: A whim is a wish to do or have something which seems to have no serious reason or purpose behind it, and often occurs suddenly.

hollywood.quick_def: You use Hollywood to refer to the American film industry that is based in Hollywood, California.

introduces.quick_def: To introduce something means to cause it to enter a place or exist in a system for the first time.

two-part.quick_def: If something is two-part, it has two parts.

dramatisations.quick_def: Dramatisations are performances or shows that turn a story or idea into a play-like form.

assisting.quick_def: If you assist someone, you help them to do a job or task by doing part of the work for them.

automatic.quick_def: An automatic machine or device is one which has controls that enable it to perform a task without needing to be constantly operated by a person. Automatic methods and processes involve the use of such machines.

effortless.quick_def: Something that is effortless is done easily and well.

paraconsciously.quick_def: When you do something paraconsciously, you do it almost without thinking clearly, in a half-aware way.

idiom.quick_def: A particular idiom is a particular style of something such as music, dance, or architecture.  [formal]

trance.quick_def: A trance is a state of mind in which someone seems to be asleep and to have no conscious control over their thoughts or actions, but in which they can see and hear things and respond to commands given by other people.

yoga.quick_def: Yoga is a type of exercise in which you move your body into various positions in order to become more fit or flexible, to improve your breathing, and to relax your mind.

silva.quick_def: Silva is a name, often used as a surname.

mind-control.quick_def: Mind-control is when someone controls another person's thoughts and actions.

ceremonies.quick_def: A ceremony is a formal event such as a wedding.

placebos.quick_def: A placebo is a substance with no effects that a doctor gives to a patient instead of a drug. Placebos are used when testing new drugs or sometimes when a patient has imagined their illness.

dispensed.quick_def: If someone dispenses something that they own or control, they give or provide it to a number of people.  [formal]

autocratic.quick_def: An autocratic person or organization has complete power and makes decisions without asking anyone else's advice.

insisting.quick_def: If you insist that something should be done, you say so very firmly and refuse to give in about it. If you insist on something, you say firmly that it must be done or provided.

capsule.quick_def: A capsule is a very small tube containing powdered or liquid medicine, which you swallow.

categoric.quick_def: Categoric means the same as categorical.

accredited.quick_def: If an educational qualification or institution is accredited, it is officially declared to be of an approved standard.  [formal]

emulate.quick_def: If you emulate something or someone, you imitate them because you admire them a great deal.  [formal]

typhoons.quick_def: A typhoon is a very violent tropical storm.

flimsiest.quick_def: A flimsy object is weak because it is made of a weak material, or is badly made.

pagodas.quick_def: A pagoda is a tall building which is used for religious purposes, especially by Buddhists, in China, Japan, and South-East Asia. Pagodas are usually very highly decorated.

hanshin.quick_def: Hanshin is a place name. It refers to a specific area in Japan.

toppled.quick_def: If someone or something topples somewhere or if you topple them, they become unsteady or unstable and fall over.

elevated.quick_def: When someone or something achieves a more important rank or status, you can say that they are elevated to it.  [formal]

devastated.quick_def: If something devastates an area or a place, it damages it very badly or destroys it totally.

kobe.quick_def: Kobe is the name of a city in Japan.

five-storey.quick_def: If a building is five-storey, it has five floors.

pagoda.quick_def: A pagoda is a tall building which is used for religious purposes, especially by Buddhists, in China, Japan, and South-East Asia. Pagodas are usually very highly decorated.

toji.quick_def: Toji is the name of a place, like a temple. It's a special name for a particular location.

unscathed.quick_def: If you are unscathed after a dangerous experience, you have not been injured or harmed by it.

levelled.quick_def: A level is a point on a scale, for example a scale of amount, quality, or difficulty.

mystified.quick_def: If you are mystified by something, you find it impossible to explain or understand.

absorbers.quick_def: Absorbers are things that can take in or soak up something, like energy or shock.

dampen.quick_def: To dampen something such as someone's enthusiasm or excitement means to make it less lively or intense.

sideways.quick_def: Sideways means from or towards the side of something or someone.

thirty-six-storey.quick_def: If a building is thirty-six-storey, it has thirty-six floors.

kasumigaseki.quick_def: Kasumigaseki is a place name in Tokyo, Japan.

pegs.quick_def: A peg is a small hook or knob that is attached to a wall or door and is used for hanging things on.

builder.quick_def: A builder is a person whose job is to build or repair houses and other buildings.

kobodaishi.quick_def: Kobodaishi is a person's name. A name is what we call a person.

hesitation.quick_def: If you hesitate, you do not speak or act for a short time, usually because you are uncertain, embarrassed, or worried about what you are going to say or do.

fifty-five.quick_def: Fifty-five is a number that comes after fifty-four and before fifty-six.

carpenters.quick_def: A carpenter is a person whose job is making and repairing wooden things.

buddhism.quick_def: Buddhism is a religion which teaches that the way to end suffering is by overcoming your desires.

watchtowers.quick_def: A watchtower is a high building which gives a person a good view of the area around the place that they are guarding.

staircase.quick_def: A staircase is a set of stairs inside a building.

eaves.quick_def: The eaves of a house are the lower edges of its roof.

rainwater.quick_def: Rainwater is water that has fallen as rain.

gushing.quick_def: When liquid gushes out of something, or when something gushes a liquid, the liquid flows out very quickly and in large quantities.

overhang.quick_def: If one thing overhangs another, it sticks out over and above it.

earthenware.quick_def: Earthenware bowls, pots, or other objects are made of clay that is baked so that it becomes hard.

trunk-like.quick_def: If something is trunk-like, it looks like a trunk (the main stem of a tree).

pillar.quick_def: A pillar is a tall solid structure, which is usually used to support part of a building.

shinbashira.quick_def: A shinbashira is a big central pillar in a Japanese pagoda, like the main trunk of a tree in the pagoda.

flexes.quick_def: A flex is an electric cable containing two or more wires that is connected to an electrical appliance.  [mainly British]

sways.quick_def: When people or things sway, they lean or swing slowly from one side to the other.

columns.quick_def: A column is a tall, often decorated cylinder of stone which is built to honour someone or forms part of a building.

shuzo.quick_def: Shuzo is a name used to call a person.

ishida.quick_def: Ishida is a family name. People use it to identify a person in a family.

shake-table.quick_def: A shake-table is a special table that can shake. People use it to test if things can stay safe when there is shaking, like during an earthquake.

pendulum.quick_def: The pendulum of a clock is a rod with a weight at the end which swings from side to side in order to make the clock work.

slither.quick_def: If you slither somewhere, you slide along in an uneven way.

banged.quick_def: A bang is a sudden loud noise such as the noise of an explosion.

column.quick_def: A column is a tall, often decorated cylinder of stone which is built to honour someone or forms part of a building.

tapers.quick_def: If something tapers, or if you taper it, it becomes gradually thinner at one end.

loads.quick_def: If you load a vehicle or a container, you put a large quantity of things into it.

hats.quick_def: A hat is a head covering, often with a brim round it, which is usually worn out of doors to give protection from the weather.

extra-wide.quick_def: If something is extra-wide, it is wider than normal.

tightrope.quick_def: A tightrope is a tightly stretched piece of rope on which someone balances and performs tricks in a circus.

jolt.quick_def: If something jolts or if something jolts it, it moves suddenly and quite violently.

graceful.quick_def: Someone or something that is graceful moves in a smooth and controlled way which is attractive to watch.

swaying.quick_def: When people or things sway, they lean or swing slowly from one side to the other.

shaking.quick_def: If you shake something, you hold it and move it quickly backwards and forwards or up and down. You can also shake a person, for example, because you are angry with them or because you want them to wake up.

enervation.quick_def: the feeling of being weak and tired

mechanisation.quick_def: Mechanisation is the process of using machines to do work instead of people or animals.

rearing.quick_def: The rear of something such as a building or vehicle is the back part of it.

half-century.quick_def: A half-century is a period of fifty years.

best-loved.quick_def: If something or someone is best-loved, they are liked by a lot of people more than others.

skylark.quick_def: A skylark is a small brown bird that sings while flying high above the ground.

partridge.quick_def: A partridge is a wild bird with brown feathers, a round body, and a short tail.

lapwing.quick_def: A lapwing is a small dark green bird which has a white breast and feathers sticking up on its head.

bunting.quick_def: In baseball, if you bunt or if you bunt the ball, you deliberately hit the ball softly, in order to gain an advantage.  [US]

ponds.quick_def: A pond is a small area of water that is smaller than a lake. Ponds are often made artificially.

faecal.quick_def: Faecal means referring or relating to faeces.  [formal]

filth.quick_def: Filth is a disgusting amount of dirt.

salmon.quick_def: A salmon is a large silver-coloured fish.

lochs.quick_def: A loch is a large area of water in Scotland that is completely or almost completely surrounded by land.

externalities.quick_def: Externalities are the effects that an activity has on other people or things, which are not part of the main activity and not directly paid for by the people doing the activity.

transaction.quick_def: A transaction is a piece of business, for example an act of buying or selling something.  [formal]

shame.quick_def: Shame is an uncomfortable feeling that you get when you have done something wrong or embarrassing, or when someone close to you has.

staggering.quick_def: If you stagger, you walk very unsteadily, for example because you are ill or drunk.

jules.quick_def: Jules is a name used to call a person.

essex.quick_def: a county in eastern England. Its administrative centre is Chelmsford

nitrates.quick_def: Nitrate is a chemical compound that includes nitrogen and oxygen. Nitrates are used as fertilizers in agriculture.

phosphates.quick_def: A phosphate is a chemical compound that contains phosphorus. Phosphates are often used in fertilizers.

bug.quick_def: A bug is an insect or similar small creature.  [informal]

cryptosporidium.quick_def: a parasite found in water that causes infections inside the body

memorable.quick_def: Something that is memorable is worth remembering or likely to be remembered, because it is special or very enjoyable.

threefold.quick_def: If something is threefold, it is three times as much as before or has three parts.

propping.quick_def: If you prop an object on or against something, you support it by putting something underneath it or by resting it somewhere.

premium.quick_def: A premium is a sum of money that you pay regularly to an insurance company for an insurance policy.

recommending.quick_def: If someone recommends a person or thing to you, they suggest that you would find that person or thing good or useful.

agrochemical.quick_def: any chemical used in farming, especially for killing insects or for making plants grow better

request.quick_def: If you request something, you ask for it politely or formally.  [formal]

makete.quick_def: Makete is the name of a place, like a district or an area.

south-western.quick_def: South-western means relating to the direction between south and west, or the area in that direction.

tanzania.quick_def: a country in East Africa which is a member of the Commonwealth. It was formed in 1964 when two other Commonwealth countries, Tanganyika and Zanzibar, combined. Its capital city is Dodoma and its official languages are Swahili and English. Its main industry is farming but tourism is also important. Many people visit Tanzania to see the wide variety of wild animals living there.

mirtp.quick_def: MIRTP is an abbreviation for a project, which means a plan or activity to achieve a special purpose.

co-ordinated.quick_def: If something is co-ordinated, different parts work together well.

donkeys.quick_def: A donkey is an animal which is like a horse but which is smaller and has longer ears.

slippery.quick_def: Something that is slippery is smooth, wet, or oily and is therefore difficult to walk on or to hold.

mills.quick_def: A mill is a building in which grain is crushed to make flour.

short-cuts.quick_def: Short-cuts are paths that are shorter than the usual ones to get to a place.

handrails.quick_def: A handrail is a long piece of metal or wood which is fixed near stairs or places where people could slip and fall, and which people can hold on to for support.

footbridges.quick_def: A footbridge is a narrow bridge for people travelling on foot.
