manufacturable.quick_def: If something is manufacturable, it can be made or produced in a factory.

wheelbarrow.quick_def: A wheelbarrow is a small open cart with one wheel and handles that is used for carrying things, for example in the garden.

refinement.quick_def: Refinements are small changes or additions that you make to something in order to improve it. Refinement is the process of making refinements.

institutionalisation.quick_def: Institutionalisation is the process of making something become a regular part of an institution or a system.

motorised.quick_def: A motorized vehicle has an engine.

wheelbarrows.quick_def: A wheelbarrow is a small open cart with one wheel and handles that is used for carrying things, for example in the garden.

shillings.quick_def: A shilling was a unit of money that was used in Britain until 1971 which was the equivalent of 5 p. There were twenty shillings in a pound.

criticise.quick_def: If you criticize someone or something, you express your disapproval of them by saying what you think is wrong with them.

top-down.quick_def: A top-down approach means making decisions at a high level and then passing them down to lower levels.

cognition.quick_def: Cognition is the mental process involved in knowing, learning, and understanding things.  [formal]

attackers.quick_def: You can refer to a person who attacks someone as their attacker.

chants.quick_def: A chant is a word or group of words that is repeated over and over again.

jingles.quick_def: When something jingles or when you jingle it, it makes a gentle ringing noise, like small bells.

slogans.quick_def: A slogan is a short phrase that is easy to remember. Slogans are used in advertisements and by political parties and other organizations who want people to remember what they are saying or selling.

martial.quick_def: Martial is used to describe things relating to soldiers or war.  [formal]

arouse.quick_def: If something arouses a particular reaction or attitude in people, it causes them to have that reaction or attitude.

embarrassment.quick_def: Embarrassment is the feeling you have when you are embarrassed.

armies.quick_def: An army is a large organized group of people who are armed and trained to fight on land in a war. Most armies are organized and controlled by governments.

confuse.quick_def: If you confuse two things, you get them mixed up, so that you think one of them is the other one.

ceaselessly.quick_def: If something, often something unpleasant, is ceaseless, it continues for a long time without stopping or changing.  [formal]

transmission.quick_def: The transmission of something is the passing or sending of it to a different person or place.

encoded.quick_def: If you encode a message or some information, you put it into a code or express it in a different form or system of language.

instincts.quick_def: Instinct is the natural tendency that a person or animal has to behave or react in a particular way.

herding.quick_def: A herd is a large group of animals of one kind that live together.

crafts.quick_def: You can refer to a boat, a spacecraft, or an aircraft as a craft.

overtaken.quick_def: If you overtake a vehicle or a person that is ahead of you and moving in the same direction, you pass them.  [mainly British]

cellulose.quick_def: Cellulose is a substance that exists in the cell walls of plants and is used to make paper, plastic, and various fabrics and fibres.

fertilise.quick_def: When an egg from the ovary of a woman or female animal is fertilized, a sperm from the male joins with the egg, causing a baby or young animal to begin forming. A female plant is fertilized when its reproductive parts come into contact with pollen from the male plant.

propagated.quick_def: If people propagate an idea or piece of information, they spread it and try to make people believe it or support it.  [formal]

ulrich.quick_def: Ulrich is a name for a person.

mueller.quick_def: Mueller is a common surname. It's a name people use to identify a person.

maryland.quick_def: an eastern state of the US on the Atlantic Ocean. It is also known as the Old Line State and the Free State. The largest city is Baltimore, and the capital city is Annapolis. Maryland was one of the original 13 states and gave some of its land to create Washington, DC. Tourists visit the Harpers Ferry National Historical Park and the Goddard Space Flight Center. Among the state's products are electronic equipment, wood and fish.

screened.quick_def: A screen is a flat vertical surface on which pictures or words are shown. Television sets and computers have screens, and films are shown on a screen in cinemas.

domesticating.quick_def: When people domesticate wild animals or plants, they bring them under control and use them to produce food or as pets.

settings.quick_def: A particular setting is a particular place or type of surroundings where something is or takes place.

wilson.quick_def: Wilson is a common name for a person.

supercolony.quick_def: A supercolony is a very large group of living things, like ants, that live together in one area.

formica.quick_def: Formica is a hard plastic that is used for covering surfaces such as kitchen tables or counters.  [trademark]

yessensis.quick_def: It is a scientific name used to name a specific kind of thing, like a type of ant.

ishikari.quick_def: Ishikari is the name of a place. It can be a coast, a city or an area.

hokkaido.quick_def: Hokkaido is a big island in Japan.

megalopolis.quick_def: A megalopolis is a very large city, or an urban area that consists of several towns and cities.

meshed.quick_def: Mesh is material like a net made from wire, thread, or plastic.

hail.quick_def: If a person, event, or achievement is hailed as important or successful, they are praised publicly.

twelve-year.quick_def: Twelve-year means lasting for twelve years or related to a period of twelve years.

ryabko.quick_def: Ryabko is a name of a person.

mobilise.quick_def: If you mobilize support or mobilize people to do something, you succeed in encouraging people to take action, especially political action. If people mobilize, they prepare to take action.

scout.quick_def: A scout is someone who is sent to an area of countryside to find out the position of an enemy army.

odour.quick_def: An odour is a particular and distinctive smell.

exhaustive.quick_def: If you describe a study, search, or list as exhaustive, you mean that it is very thorough and complete.

sounder.quick_def: A sound is something that you hear.

footing.quick_def: If something is put on a particular footing, it is defined, established, or changed in a particular way, often so that it is able to develop or exist successfully.

siberia.quick_def: Siberia is a very large and cold area in Russia.

bering.quick_def: Bering is used to name things related to a sea area. It's often used in geographical names.

strait.quick_def: You can refer to a narrow strip of sea which joins two large areas of sea as a strait or the straits.

williams.quick_def: the common name for Williams F1 (Williams Formula One), a British company that makes racing cars and organizes teams of drivers, mechanics (= people whose job is working on engines), etc. to enter competitions. It was established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, and has been one of the most successful teams in motor racing. Its full name is Williams Grand Prix Engineering Limited.

gm.quick_def: gm is a written abbreviation for gram.

allotypes.quick_def: Allotypes are different forms of a protein. They are like different versions of the same thing.

immunoglobin.quick_def: An immunoglobin is a kind of protein in the blood that helps the body fight against diseases.

proteins.quick_def: Protein is a substance found in food and drink such as meat, eggs, and milk. You need protein in order to grow and be healthy.

interbreeding.quick_def: Interbreeding means when different groups of animals or plants breed with each other.

calibrated.quick_def: If you calibrate an instrument or tool, you mark or adjust it so that you can use it to measure something accurately.  [technical]

interbred.quick_def: When different groups or types of animals or people interbred, they breed with each other.

sampled.quick_def: A sample of a substance or product is a small quantity of it that shows you what it is like.

twenty-year.quick_def: A twenty-year thing means it lasts for twenty years or is related to a period of twenty years.

corresponded.quick_def: If one thing corresponds to another, there is a close similarity or connection between them. You can also say that two things correspond.

eskimo.quick_def: An Eskimo is a member of the group of peoples who live in Alaska, Northern Canada, eastern Siberia, and other parts of the Arctic. These peoples now usually call themselves Inuits or Yupiks, and the term Eskimo could cause offence.

aleut.quick_def: An Aleut is a person from the Aleutian Islands or a member of the Aleut people.

paleo-indian.quick_def: A Paleo-Indian is a member of the earliest group of people who lived in the Americas a very long time ago.

na-dene.quick_def: Na-Dene refers to a group of people or a language family. It is about a certain ethnic or language-related group.

apache.quick_def: a member of a Native American people, many of whom live in the south-western US

wallace.quick_def: Wallace is a common surname. It is used to call a person.

mitochondrial.quick_def: relating to mitochondria (= small parts found in most cells, in which the energy in food is released)

pima-papago.quick_def: Pima-Papago refers to a group of Native Americans.

peninsula.quick_def: A peninsula is a long narrow piece of land which sticks out from a larger piece of land and is almost completely surrounded by water.

ticuna.quick_def: Ticuna is a group of Native Americans. They live in a certain area.

christy.quick_def: Christy is a name for a person, usually a girl or a woman.

tooth.quick_def: Your teeth are the hard white objects in your mouth, which you use for biting and chewing.

minimally.quick_def: Something that is minimal is very small in quantity, value, or degree.

crown.quick_def: A crown is a circular ornament, usually made of gold and jewels, which a king or queen wears on their head at official ceremonies. You can also use crown to refer to anything circular that is worn on someone's head.

incisor.quick_def: Your incisors are the teeth at the front of your mouth which you use for biting into food.

shoveling.quick_def: Shoveling is the action of using a shovel to move something, like snow or dirt.

scooping.quick_def: If you scoop a person or thing somewhere, you put your hands or arms under or round them and quickly move them there.

single-rooted.quick_def: If a tooth is single-rooted, it has only one root.

premolars.quick_def: Premolars are teeth between the canines and molars in your mouth. They are used for chewing and grinding food.

triple-rooted.quick_def: If a tooth is triple-rooted, it has three roots.

ties.quick_def: If you tie two things together or tie them, you fasten them together with a knot.

paleo-lndian.quick_def: Paleo-lndian refers to the early people who lived in North and South America a long time ago.

dental.quick_def: Dental is used to describe things that relate to teeth or to the care and treatment of teeth.

micro-evolution.quick_def: Micro-evolution is small-scale changes in the genes of a group of living things over a short time.

na-denes.quick_def: The Na-Denes are a group of people. They have their own culture and history.

eskimo-aleut.quick_def: Eskimo-Aleut refers to a group of people and their languages in the Arctic and sub-Arctic regions.

greenberg.quick_def: Greenberg is a name, usually used for a person.

amerind.quick_def: Amerind refers to the group of Native Americans whose languages are thought to belong to a large family.

credence.quick_def: If something lends or gives credence to a theory or story, it makes it easier to believe.  [formal]

backing.quick_def: If you move back, you move in the opposite direction to the one in which you are facing or in which you were moving before.

imbalances.quick_def: If there is an imbalance in a situation, the things involved are not the same size, or are not the right size in proportion to each other.

mismanagement.quick_def: Someone's mismanagement of a system or organization is the bad way they have dealt with it or organized it.

co-ordinate.quick_def: When you co-ordinate things, you organize them so that they work well together.

strasbourg.quick_def: Strasbourg is a city in France. It's a place where people live, work and visit.

hosted.quick_def: The host at a party is the person who has invited the guests and provides the food, drink, or entertainment.

ministerial.quick_def: You use ministerial to refer to people, events, or jobs that are connected with government ministers.

preparatory.quick_def: Preparatory actions are done before doing something else as a form of preparation or as an introduction.

nordic.quick_def: Nordic means relating to the Scandinavian countries of northern Europe.

recreational.quick_def: Recreational means relating to things people do in their spare time to relax.

non-polluting.quick_def: If something is non-polluting, it does not make the environment dirty or harmful when it is used.

unrivalled.quick_def: If you describe something as unrivalled, you are emphasizing that it is better than anything else of the same kind.  [emphasis]

unwind.quick_def: When you unwind, you relax after you have done something that makes you tense or tired.

unforeseen.quick_def: If something that has happened was unforeseen, it was not expected to happen or known about beforehand.

resolutions.quick_def: A resolution is a formal decision taken at a meeting by means of a vote.

policy-making.quick_def: Policy-making is the process of making policies. Policies are rules or plans made by a group or an organization. For example, a government makes policies to manage a country.

systematisation.quick_def: Systematisation is the act of organizing things in a systematic way, making them well-arranged and following a set order.

needles.quick_def: A needle is a small, very thin piece of polished metal which is used for sewing. It has a sharp point at one end and a hole in the other for a thread to go through.

accentuated.quick_def: To accentuate something means to emphasize it or make it more noticeable.

damages.quick_def: To damage an object means to break it, spoil it physically, or stop it from working properly.

databank.quick_def: a large amount of data on a particular subject that is stored in a computer

ministers.quick_def: In Britain and some other countries, a minister is a person who is in charge of a particular government department.

skiing.quick_def: Skis are long, flat, narrow pieces of wood, metal, or plastic that are fastened to boots so that you can move easily on snow or water.

preferential.quick_def: If you get preferential treatment, you are treated better than other people and therefore have an advantage over them.

relaunched.quick_def: To relaunch something such as a company, a product, or a scheme means to start it again or to produce it in a different way.

physiology.quick_def: Physiology is the scientific study of how people's and animals' bodies function, and of how plants function.

eurosilva.quick_def: Eurosilva is the name of a European research network about the physiology of trees.

scholarships.quick_def: If you get a scholarship to a school or university, your studies are paid for by the school or university or by some other organization.

theses.quick_def: A thesis is an idea or theory that is expressed as a statement and is discussed in a logical way.

harmonising.quick_def: When you are harmonising things, you are making them work well together or match each other.

commits.quick_def: If someone commits a crime or a sin, they do something illegal or bad.

on-going.quick_def: If something is on-going, it is happening now and will continue in the future.

representatives.quick_def: A representative is a person who has been chosen to act or make decisions on behalf of another person or a group of people.

marcus.quick_def: Marcus is a name for a person.

chown.quick_def: Chown is a proper name, usually used as a person's last name.

maureen.quick_def: Maureen is a common female name.

clemmons.quick_def: Clemmons is a surname, which is a family name used to identify a person's family.

perusing.quick_def: If you peruse something such as a letter, article, or document, you read it.  [formal]

postures.quick_def: Your posture is the position in which you stand or sit.

gharib.quick_def: Gharib is a proper name, usually used as a person's last name.

aeronautics.quick_def: Aeronautics is the science of designing and building aeroplanes.

emilio.quick_def: Emilio is a name for a person.

graff.quick_def: Graff is a name, usually used to call a person.

lifters.quick_def: Lifters are things or people that can lift heavy objects.

scale-model.quick_def: A scale-model is a small copy of something real, made to show what it looks like. It is in the same shape as the real thing but smaller.

wind-tunnel.quick_def: A wind-tunnel is a long tube where they make strong wind to test things like models of planes.

pulley.quick_def: A pulley is a device consisting of a wheel over which a rope or chain is pulled in order to lift heavy objects.

tent-shaped.quick_def: If something is tent-shaped, it has the same shape as a tent.

scaffold.quick_def: A scaffold was a raised platform on which criminals were hanged or had their heads cut off.

pulleys.quick_def: A pulley is a device consisting of a wheel over which a rope or chain is pulled in order to lift heavy objects.

apex.quick_def: The apex of an organization or system is the highest and most important position in it.

trolley.quick_def: A trolley is an object with wheels that you use to transport heavy things such as shopping or luggage.  [British]

jerk.quick_def: If you jerk something or someone in a particular direction, or they jerk in a particular direction, they move a short distance very suddenly and quickly.

brute.quick_def: If you call someone a brute, you mean that they are rough, violent, and insensitive.  [disapproval]

kite-lifting.quick_def: Kite-lifting is the act of using a kite to lift something up.

willeke.quick_def: Willeke is a name used to call a person.

wendrich.quick_def: Wendrich is a surname, which is a family name used to identify a person's family.

egyptology.quick_def: the study of the language, history and culture of ancient Egypt

harnessing.quick_def: If you harness something such as an emotion or natural source of energy, you bring it under your control and use it.

uncannily.quick_def: in a way that seems strange and is difficult to explain

glider.quick_def: A glider is an aircraft without an engine, which flies by floating on air currents.

dump.quick_def: If you dump something somewhere, you put it or unload it there quickly and carelessly.  [informal]

flaming.quick_def: A flame is a hot bright stream of burning gas that comes from something that is burning.

adobe.quick_def: Adobe is a mixture of mud and straw that is dried into bricks in the sun and used for building, especially in hot countries.

arches.quick_def: An arch is a structure that is curved at the top and is supported on either side by a pillar, post, or wall.

sensible.quick_def: Sensible actions or decisions are good because they are based on reasons rather than emotions.

aleutian.quick_def: Aleutian is used to describe things related to the Aleutian Islands. The Aleutian Islands are a group of islands in the North Pacific.

aleyska.quick_def: Aleyska is an old name for a place which is now called Alaska.

forty-ninth.quick_def: Forty-ninth means the position in a series that is number 49.

fisheries.quick_def: Fisheries are areas of the sea where fish are caught in large quantities for commercial purposes.

adf.quick_def: ADF is an abbreviation. Here it stands for the Alaska Department of Fish. It's a group that takes care of fish-related things in Alaska.

groundfish.quick_def: Groundfish are fish that live and feed near the bottom of the sea.

cod.quick_def: Cod are a type of large edible fish.

perch.quick_def: If you perch on something, you sit down lightly on the very edge or tip of it.

ewing.quick_def: Ewing is a name, usually used for a person.

factbook.quick_def: A factbook is a book that has a lot of facts about a certain thing or place.

circulating.quick_def: If a piece of writing circulates or is circulated, copies of it are passed round among a group of people.

nourishment.quick_def: If something provides a person, animal, or plant with nourishment, it provides them with the food that is necessary for life, growth, and good health.

spawners.quick_def: Spawners are animals that produce eggs or young.

eagles.quick_def: An eagle is a large bird that lives by eating small animals.

chinook.quick_def: a warm, dry wind that blows down the east side of the Rocky Mountains at the end of winter

chum.quick_def: Your chum is your friend.  [informal, old-fashioned]

coho.quick_def: A coho is a type of fish that lives in the Pacific Ocean and can be caught for business.

sockeye.quick_def: A sockeye is a kind of fish that lives in the Pacific Ocean.

alaskan.quick_def: Alaskan means related to Alaska, a state in the United States, or it can refer to a person from Alaska.

ex-vessel.quick_def: Ex-vessel means the price or value of something (usually fish) at the moment it leaves the fishing vessel.

overfishing.quick_def: the process of taking so many fish from the sea, a river, etc. that the number of fish in it becomes very low

onset.quick_def: The onset of something is the beginning of it, used especially to refer to something unpleasant.

statehood.quick_def: Statehood is the condition of being an independent state or nation.

mandates.quick_def: If a government or other elected body has a mandate to carry out a particular policy or task, they have the authority to carry it out as a result of winning an election or vote.

totalled.quick_def: A total is the number that you get when you add several numbers together or when you count how many things there are in a group.

in-season.quick_def: If something is in-season, it is available at the right time of the year when it is fresh and good to use or eat.

abundance-based.quick_def: If something is abundance-based, it is based on the amount of something that is available in large quantities.

streamside.quick_def: The streamside is the area beside a stream.

aeroplanes.quick_def: An aeroplane is a vehicle with wings and one or more engines that enable it to fly through the air.  [British]

pre-set.quick_def: If something is pre-set, it is set or arranged before it is used.

approximate.quick_def: An approximate number, time, or position is close to the correct number, time, or position, but is not exact.

prosper.quick_def: If people or businesses prosper, they are successful and do well.  [formal]

stewardship.quick_def: Stewardship is the responsibility of looking after property.  [formal]

msc.quick_def: An MSc is a master's degree in a science subject. MSc is an abbreviation for 'Master of Science'.

recognises.quick_def: If you recognize someone or something, you know who that person is or what that thing is.

appoints.quick_def: If you appoint someone to a job or official position, you formally choose them for it.

gathers.quick_def: If people gather somewhere or if someone gathers people somewhere, they come together in a group.

non-governmental.quick_def: If something is non-governmental, it is not related to the government.

yukon.quick_def: Yukon is the name of a place, like a territory in Canada or a river in North America.

kuskokwim.quick_def: Kuskokwim is the name of a place, like a river or an area.

culminating.quick_def: If you say that an activity, process, or series of events culminates in or with a particular event, you mean that event happens at the end of it.

reacted.quick_def: When you react to something that has happened to you, you behave in a particular way because of it.

closing.quick_def: When you close something such as a door or lid or when it closes, it moves so that a hole, gap, or opening is covered.

suppose.quick_def: You can use suppose or supposing before mentioning a possible situation or action. You usually then go on to consider the effects that this situation or action might have.

bursts.quick_def: If something bursts or if you burst it, it suddenly breaks open or splits open and the air or other substance inside it comes out.

loud.quick_def: If a noise is loud, the level of sound is very high and it can be easily heard. Someone or something that is loud produces a lot of noise.

troublesome.quick_def: You use troublesome to describe something or someone that causes annoying problems or difficulties.

interfered.quick_def: If you say that someone interferes in a situation, you mean they get involved in it although it does not concern them and their involvement is not wanted.  [disapproval]

dials.quick_def: A dial is the part of a machine or instrument such as a clock or watch which shows you the time or a measurement that has been recorded.

broadbent.quick_def: Broadbent is a name, usually used to call a person.

finkelman.quick_def: Finkelman is a name of a person.

predictability.quick_def: the quality something has when it is possible for you to know in advance that it will happen or what it will be like

intrusions.quick_def: If someone disturbs you when you are in a private place or having a private conversation, you can call this event an intrusion.

spaced.quick_def: You use space to refer to an area that is empty or available. The area can be any size. For example, you can refer to a large area outside as a large open space or to a small area between two objects as a small space.

annoying.quick_def: If someone or something annoys you, it makes you fairly angry and impatient.

after-effects.quick_def: After-effects are the results or problems that happen after an event or action.

proofread.quick_def: When someone proofreads something such as a book or an article, they read it before it is published in order to find and mark mistakes that need to be corrected.

proofreading.quick_def: When someone proofreads something such as a book or an article, they read it before it is published in order to find and mark mistakes that need to be corrected.

eliminates.quick_def: To eliminate something, especially something you do not want or need, means to remove it completely.  [formal]

busiest.quick_def: When you are busy, you are working hard or concentrating on a task, so that you are not free to do anything else.

cohen.quick_def: Cohen is a common surname. A surname is the family name that a person shares with other family members.

adaptability.quick_def: the quality of being able to change or be changed in order to deal successfully with new situations

distractible.quick_def: If a person is distractible, it's easy for them to stop what they're doing and pay attention to something else.

distractibility.quick_def: Distractibility is the quality of being easily distracted, which means a person can't focus on one thing because of other things around them.

ethnicity.quick_def: Ethnicity is the state or fact of belonging to a particular ethnic group.

babylonians.quick_def: The Babylonians are people who lived in an ancient city called Babylon in the past.

axis.quick_def: An axis is an imaginary line through the middle of something.

waxing.quick_def: Wax is a solid, slightly shiny substance made of fat or oil which is used to make candles and polish. It melts when it is heated.

waning.quick_def: If something wanes, it becomes gradually weaker or less, often so that it eventually disappears.

climes.quick_def: You use clime in expressions such as warmer climes and  foreign climes to refer to a place that has a particular kind of climate.  [literary]

northward.quick_def: Northward or northwards means towards the north.

chart.quick_def: A chart is a diagram, picture, or graph which is intended to make information easier to understand.

decans.quick_def: Decans are special groups of stars. People use them to mark a period of time.

sirius.quick_def: Sirius is the brightest star in the night sky.

sunrise.quick_def: Sunrise is the time in the morning when the sun first appears in the sky.

all-important.quick_def: If something is all-important, it is extremely important.

spanning.quick_def: A span is the period of time between two dates or events during which something exists, functions, or happens.

cosmic.quick_def: Cosmic means occurring in, or coming from, the part of space that lies outside Earth and its atmosphere.

sundials.quick_def: A sundial is a device used for telling the time when the sun is shining. The shadow of an upright rod falls onto a flat surface that is marked with the hours, and points to the correct hour.

shadow.quick_def: A shadow is a dark shape on a surface that is made when something stands between a light and the surface.

sundial.quick_def: A sundial is a device used for telling the time when the sun is shining. The shadow of an upright rod falls onto a flat surface that is marked with the hours, and points to the correct hour.

dripped.quick_def: When liquid drips somewhere, or you drip it somewhere, it falls in individual small drops.

satisfactorily.quick_def: in a way that is good enough for a particular purpose

cloudy.quick_def: If it is cloudy, there are a lot of clouds in the sky.

babylonian.quick_def: Babylonian means related to Babylon, an ancient city, or its people, culture.

midday.quick_def: Midday is twelve o'clock in the middle of the day.

commencing.quick_def: When something commences or you commence it, it begins.  [formal]

weight-driven.quick_def: If a thing is weight-driven, it is powered by the force of a weight.

bedfordshire.quick_def: a county in southern central England. Its administrative centre is Bedford.

timekeeper.quick_def: A timekeeper is a person or an instrument that records or checks the time.

escapement.quick_def: a machine in a clock or watch that transfers movement from the spring or weight to a wheel or pendulum that is connected to the hands

fusee.quick_def: A fusee is a thing that can keep a steady force for some moving parts even when the power source's tension changes.

mainspring.quick_def: If you say that an idea, emotion, or other factor is the mainspring of something, you mean that it is the most important reason or motive for that thing.  [written]

swung.quick_def: If something swings or if you swing it, it moves repeatedly backwards and forwards or from side to side from a fixed point.

arc.quick_def: An arc is a smoothly curving line or movement.

lever-based.quick_def: If something is lever-based, it is designed or works mainly with the use of a lever.

releases.quick_def: If a person or animal is released from somewhere where they have been locked up or looked after, they are set free or allowed to go.

floor-standing.quick_def: If something is floor-standing, it is designed to stand on the floor by itself.

timekeeping.quick_def: If you talk about someone's timekeeping, you are talking about how good they are at arriving in time for things.  [British]

quartz-crystal.quick_def: A quartz-crystal is a kind of hard and clear stone that can be used in things like clocks to make them work well.

beamed.quick_def: If you say that someone is beaming, you mean that they have a big smile on their face because they are happy, pleased, or proud about something.  [written]

calibrate.quick_def: If you calibrate an instrument or tool, you mark or adjust it so that you can use it to measure something accurately.  [technical]

stock-trading.quick_def: Stock-trading is the activity of buying and selling stocks.

power-distribution.quick_def: Power-distribution means the process of sending electricity from where it is made to different places where it is needed.

grids.quick_def: A grid is something which is in a pattern of straight lines that cross over each other, forming squares. On maps the grid is used to help you find a particular thing or place.

time-based.quick_def: If something is time-based, it depends on or is related to time.

aviation.quick_def: Aviation is the operation and production of aircraft.

faa.quick_def: FAA is an abbreviation for Federal Aviation Administration, which is an organization that controls and manages aircraft operations in the United States.

oversee.quick_def: If someone in authority oversees a job or an activity, they make sure that it is done properly.

atc.quick_def: ATC is short for air traffic control. It means the service that controls the movement of aircraft to make sure they fly safely.

vicinity.quick_def: If something is in the vicinity of a particular place, it is near it.  [formal]

flags.quick_def: A flag is a piece of cloth which can be attached to a pole and which is used as a sign, signal, or symbol of something, especially of a particular country.

beacons.quick_def: A beacon is a light or a fire, usually on a hill or tower, which acts as a signal or a warning.

flashing.quick_def: A flash is a sudden burst of light or of something shiny or bright.

airways.quick_def: A person's airways are the passages from their nose and mouth down to their lungs, through which air enters and leaves their body.

approximating.quick_def: An approximate number, time, or position is close to the correct number, time, or position, but is not exact.

full-scale.quick_def: If something is full-scale, it is done completely and on a large scale.

airspace.quick_def: A country's airspace is the part of the sky that is over that country and is considered to belong to it.

fortuitous.quick_def: You can describe something as fortuitous if it happens, by chance, to be very successful or pleasant.

margin.quick_def: A margin is the difference between two amounts, especially the difference in the number of votes or points between the winner and the loser in an election or other contest.

screens.quick_def: A screen is a flat vertical surface on which pictures or words are shown. Television sets and computers have screens, and films are shown on a screen in cinemas.

departing.quick_def: When something or someone departs from a place, they leave it and start a journey to another place.

blanketed.quick_def: A blanket is a large square or rectangular piece of thick cloth, especially one which you put on a bed to keep you warm.

vfr.quick_def: VFR means Visual Flight Rules. It is a set of rules for flying a plane when the weather is good and pilots can rely on what they see outside to fly safely.

ifr.quick_def: IFR means Instrumental Flight Rules. These are rules for pilots to fly safely when they can't see well outside, and they have to use the plane's instrument panel for information.

navigational.quick_def: Navigational means relating to the act of navigating a ship or an aircraft.

accommodates.quick_def: If a building or space can accommodate someone or something, it has enough room for them.

rating.quick_def: The rate at which something happens is the speed with which it happens.

license.quick_def: To license a person or activity means to give official permission for the person to do something or for the activity to take place.

turboprop.quick_def: A turboprop is a turbine engine that makes an aircraft propeller go round.

realm.quick_def: You can use realm to refer to any area of activity, interest, or thought.  [formal]

altitudes.quick_def: If something is at a particular altitude, it is at that height above sea level.

instrument-rated.quick_def: If a pilot is instrument-rated, they have the skills and a license to fly an aircraft using its instruments.

licensed.quick_def: To license a person or activity means to give official permission for the person to do something or for the activity to take place.

instrumentation.quick_def: Instrumentation is a group or collection of instruments, usually ones that are part of the same machine.

correspond.quick_def: If one thing corresponds to another, there is a close similarity or connection between them. You can also say that two things correspond.

medium-sized.quick_def: If something is medium-sized, it is neither very big nor very small, just in the middle in terms of size.

two-way.quick_def: If something is two-way, it allows things to go in two directions or have two sides of communication.

cruises.quick_def: A cruise is a holiday during which you travel on a ship or boat and visit a number of places.

telepathy.quick_def: If you refer to telepathy, you mean the direct communication of thoughts and feelings between people's minds, without the need to use speech, writing, or any other normal signals.

parapsychologists.quick_def: Parapsychologists are people who study things like telepathy and other psychic phenomena in a scientific way.

institutes.quick_def: An institute is an organization set up to do a particular type of work, especially research or teaching. You can also use institute to refer to the building the organization occupies.

derision.quick_def: If you treat someone or something with derision, you express contempt for them.

concur.quick_def: If one person concurs with another person, the two people agree. You can also say that two people concur.  [formal]

ganzfeld.quick_def: A ganzfeld is a situation or experiment where you experience a whole-field condition, like being in a place that gives you a feeling of a complete and uniform environment.

telepathic.quick_def: If you believe that someone is telepathic, you believe that they have mental powers which cannot be explained by science, such as being able to communicate with other people's minds, and know what other people are thinking.

meditation.quick_def: Meditation is the act of remaining in a silent and calm state for a period of time, as part of a religious training, or so that you are more able to deal with the problems of everyday life.

suspect.quick_def: You use suspect when you are stating something that you believe is probably true, in order to make it sound less strong or direct.  [vagueness]

faint.quick_def: A faint sound, colour, mark, feeling, or quality has very little strength or intensity.

swamped.quick_def: A swamp is an area of very wet land with wild plants growing in it.

meditation-like.quick_def: If something is meditation-like, it is similar to meditation, having the calm and peaceful feeling like when you are meditating.

filters.quick_def: To filter a substance means to pass it through a device which is designed to remove certain particles contained in it.

identification.quick_def: The identification of something is the recognition that it exists, is important, or is true.

sender.quick_def: The sender of a letter, email, package, or radio message is the person who sent it.

guessing.quick_def: If you guess something, you give an answer or provide an opinion which may not be true because you do not have definite knowledge about the matter concerned.

hit-rate.quick_def: The hit-rate is the percentage of successful attempts out of all attempts.

parapsychologist.quick_def: A parapsychologist is a person who studies things like telepathy and clairvoyance which are not explained by normal science.

honorton.quick_def: Honorton is a surname, which is used to identify a person.

hit-rates.quick_def: Hit-rates are the percentages that show how often something successful happens. For example, how often you can hit a target.

implication.quick_def: To implicate someone means to show or claim that they were involved in something wrong or criminal.

leakage.quick_def: A leakage is an amount of liquid or gas that is escaping from a pipe or container by means of a crack, hole, or other fault.

statistically.quick_def: Statistical means relating to the use of statistics.

autoganzfeld.quick_def: An autoganzfeld is an automated kind of test or technique that uses computers to do important tasks.

minimising.quick_def: If you minimize a risk, problem, or unpleasant situation, you reduce it to the lowest possible level, or prevent it increasing beyond that level.

defenders.quick_def: If someone is a defender of a particular thing or person that has been criticized, they argue or act in support of that thing or person.

marginally.quick_def: Marginally means to only a small extent.

esoteric.quick_def: If you describe something as esoteric, you mean it is known, understood, or appreciated by only a small number of people.  [formal]

quantum.quick_def: In physics, quantum theory and quantum mechanics are concerned with the behaviour of atomic particles.

answering.quick_def: When you answer someone who has asked you something, you say something back to them.

parapsychology.quick_def: Parapsychology is the study of strange mental abilities that seem to exist but cannot be explained by accepted scientific theories.

probing.quick_def: If you probe into something, you ask questions or try to discover facts about it.

mesopotamians.quick_def: Mesopotamians are the people who lived in Mesopotamia in the past.

soda.quick_def: Soda is the same as soda water.

celsius.quick_def: Celsius is a scale for measuring temperature, in which water freezes at 0 degrees and boils at 100 degrees. It is represented by the symbol ° C.

hardens.quick_def: When something hardens or when you harden it, it becomes stiff or firm.

unblemished.quick_def: If you describe something such as someone's record, reputation, or character as unblemished, you mean it has not been harmed or spoiled.

glassmakers.quick_def: Glassmakers are people who make glass.

squeezing.quick_def: If you squeeze something, you press it firmly, usually with your hands.

mangle.quick_def: If a physical object is mangled, it is crushed or twisted very forcefully, so that it is difficult to see what its original shape was.

polished.quick_def: Polish means belonging or relating to Poland, or to its people, language, or culture.

hardening.quick_def: When something hardens or when you harden it, it becomes stiff or firm.

pouring.quick_def: If you pour a liquid or other substance, you make it flow steadily out of a container by holding the container at an angle.

underside.quick_def: The underside of something is the part of it which normally faces towards the ground.

fortunate.quick_def: If you say that someone or something is fortunate, you mean that they are lucky.

six-millimetre.quick_def: It means something has a size or thickness of six millimetres. A millimetre is a very small unit of length.

marketable.quick_def: Something that is marketable is able to be sold because people want to buy it.  [business]

homogenising.quick_def: When you are homogenising something, you are making it the same throughout. For example, making the parts of a mixture have the same quality and consistency.

delivers.quick_def: If you deliver something somewhere, you take it there.

sub-millimetre.quick_def: If something is sub-millimetre, it is smaller than one millimetre.

marred.quick_def: To mar something means to spoil or damage it.

perfection.quick_def: Perfection is the quality of being as good as it is possible for something of a particular kind to be.

tremor.quick_def: A tremor is a small earthquake.

ripples.quick_def: Ripples are little waves on the surface of water caused by the wind or by something moving in or on the water.

on-line.quick_def: If something is on-line, it is connected to the Internet and can be used or found there.

locating.quick_def: If you locate something or someone, you find out where they are.  [formal]

flaws.quick_def: A flaw in something such as a theory or argument is a mistake in it, which causes it to be less effective or valid.

cutters.quick_def: A cutter is a tool that you use for cutting through something.

embark.quick_def: If you embark on something new, difficult, or exciting, you start doing it.

unchanging.quick_def: Something that is unchanging always stays the same.

opportunism.quick_def: If you refer to someone's behaviour as opportunism, you are criticizing them for taking advantage of any opportunity that occurs in order to gain money or power, without thinking about whether their actions are right or wrong.  [disapproval]

unaccustomed.quick_def: If you are unaccustomed to something, you do not know it very well or have not experienced it very often.  [written]

stock-raising.quick_def: Stock-raising is the activity of keeping and breeding animals such as cows, sheep, etc. for meat, milk or other products.

famine.quick_def: Famine is a situation in which large numbers of people have little or no food, and many of them die.

bitterly.quick_def: In a bitter argument or conflict, people argue very angrily or fight very fiercely.

iceland.quick_def: an island country in the northern Atlantic Ocean

seesaw.quick_def: A seesaw is a long board which is balanced on a fixed part in the middle. To play on it, a child sits on each end, and when one end goes up, the other goes down.

quarter-century.quick_def: A quarter-century means twenty-five years. A century is one hundred years, and a quarter of it is twenty-five years.

easterly.quick_def: An easterly point, area, or direction is to the east or towards the east.

abruptly.quick_def: An abrupt change or action is very sudden, often in a way which is unpleasant.

mild.quick_def: Mild is used to describe something such as a feeling, attitude, or illness that is not very strong or severe.

northeasterly.quick_def: A northeasterly point, area, or direction is to the northeast or toward the northeast.

reconstructing.quick_def: If you reconstruct something that has been destroyed or badly damaged, you build it and make it work again.

rings.quick_def: When you ring someone, you phone them.  [mainly British]

cores.quick_def: The core of a fruit is the central part of it. It contains seeds or pips.

tree-ring.quick_def: A tree-ring is a ring in the trunk of a tree. Each ring usually shows one year of the tree's growth.

amplified.quick_def: If you amplify a sound, you make it louder, usually by using electronic equipment.

peruvian.quick_def: Peruvian means belonging or related to Peru, or to its people or culture.

norse.quick_def: Norse means belonging or relating to Scandinavian countries in medieval times.

southward.quick_def: Southward or southwards means towards the south.

rerouted.quick_def: If vehicles or planes are rerouted, they are directed along a different route because the usual route cannot be used.

storminess.quick_def: Storminess is the state of being stormy, with strong winds, heavy rain, etc.

perished.quick_def: If someone is perished, they are extremely cold.  [British, informal]

continent-wide.quick_def: If something is continent-wide, it happens across an entire continent.

stormier.quick_def: If there is stormy weather, there are strong winds and heavy rain.

culminated.quick_def: If you say that an activity, process, or series of events culminates in or with a particular event, you mean that event happens at the end of it.

sixteenth.quick_def: The sixteenth item in a series is the one that you count as number sixteen.

staples.quick_def: A staple food, product, or activity is one that is basic and important in people's everyday lives.

basques.quick_def: The Basques are a group of people who live in a certain area. They have their own culture and language.

stemmed.quick_def: If a condition or problem stems from something, it was caused originally by that thing.

fodder.quick_def: Fodder is food that is given to cows, horses, and other animals.

land-hungry.quick_def: If people are land-hungry, they really want to get more land.

irish.quick_def: Irish means belonging or relating to Ireland, or to its people, language, or culture. Irish sometimes refers to the whole of Ireland, and sometimes only to the Republic of Ireland.

blight.quick_def: You can refer to something as a blight when it causes great difficulties, and damages or spoils other things.

humanly.quick_def: Humanly means relating to human beings.

proliferated.quick_def: If things proliferate, they increase in number very quickly.  [formal]

steeper.quick_def: A steep slope rises at a very sharp angle and is difficult to go up.

olfaction.quick_def: Olfaction is the ability to smell things.

aromas.quick_def: An aroma is a strong, pleasant smell.

surround.quick_def: If a person or thing is surrounded by something, that thing is situated all around them.

consciously.quick_def: If you are conscious of something, you notice it or realize that it is happening.

synott.quick_def: Synott is a name of a person.

concordia.quick_def: Concordia is the name of a place, like a university. It's used to call a specific thing or place.

comment.quick_def: If you comment on something, you give your opinion about it or you give an explanation for it.

evoke.quick_def: To evoke a particular memory, idea, emotion, or response means to cause it to occur.  [formal]

grimace.quick_def: If you grimace, you twist your face in an ugly way because you are annoyed, disgusted, or in pain.  [written]

olfactory.quick_def: Olfactory means concerned with the sense of smell.  [formal]

dislikes.quick_def: If you dislike someone or something, you consider them to be unpleasant and do not like them.

agreeable.quick_def: If something is agreeable, it is pleasant and you enjoy it.

disagreeable.quick_def: Something that is disagreeable is rather unpleasant.

bonding.quick_def: A bond between people is a strong feeling of friendship, love, or shared beliefs and experiences that unites them.

respondent.quick_def: A respondent is a person who replies to something such as a survey or set of questions.

spouses.quick_def: Someone's spouse is the person they are married to.

smells.quick_def: The smell of something is a quality it has which you become aware of when you breathe in through your nose.

register.quick_def: A register is an official list or record of people or things.

undervalued.quick_def: If you undervalue something or someone, you fail to recognize how valuable or important they are.

feeble.quick_def: If you describe someone or something as feeble, you mean that they are weak.

undeveloped.quick_def: An undeveloped country or region does not have modern industries and usually has a low standard of living.

noses.quick_def: Your nose is the part of your face which sticks out above your mouth. You use it for smelling and breathing.

answered.quick_def: When you answer someone who has asked you something, you say something back to them.

odourless.quick_def: An odourless substance has no smell.

unanswered.quick_def: Something such as a question or letter that is unanswered has not been answered.

nonphysical.quick_def: If something is nonphysical, it doesn't have a physical form or can't be touched.

attach.quick_def: If you attach something to an object, you join it or fasten it to the object.

interiorised.quick_def: When you interiorise something, you make it a part of your own thoughts and feelings.

thunderstorms.quick_def: A thunderstorm is a storm in which there is thunder and lightning and a lot of heavy rain.

fury.quick_def: Fury is violent or very strong anger.

inflicts.quick_def: To inflict harm or damage on someone or something means to make them suffer it.

leisurely.quick_def: A leisurely action is done in a relaxed and unhurried way.

terrifying.quick_def: If something terrifies you, it makes you feel extremely frightened.

dice.quick_def: A dice is a small cube which has between one and six spots or numbers on its sides, and which is used in games to provide random numbers. In old-fashioned English, 'dice' was used only as a plural form, and the singular was die, but now 'dice' is used as both the singular and the plural form.

lone.quick_def: If you talk about a lone person or thing, you mean that they are alone.

golfer.quick_def: A golfer is a person who plays golf for pleasure or as a profession.

neutralising.quick_def: When you are neutralising something, you are making it have no effect or no power.

brave.quick_def: Someone who is brave is willing to do things which are dangerous, and does not show fear in difficult or dangerous situations.

armoury.quick_def: A country's armoury is all the weapons and military equipment that it has.

storm.quick_def: A storm is very bad weather, with heavy rain, strong winds, and often thunder and lightning.

firing.quick_def: Fire is the hot, bright flames produced by things that are burning.

trailing.quick_def: A trail is a rough path across open country or through forests.

epri.quick_def: EPRI is the short name of the Electrical Power Research Institute, which is an organization for electrical power research.

bernstein.quick_def: Bernstein is a name of a person.

voltages.quick_def: The voltage of an electrical current is its force measured in volts.

someplace.quick_def: Someplace means the same as somewhere.  [US]

jean-claude.quick_def: Jean-Claude is a common male name.

diels.quick_def: Diels is a surname, which is a family name people use to show their family relationship.

high-powered.quick_def: If something is high-powered, it has a lot of power or strength.

laser.quick_def: A laser is a narrow beam of concentrated light produced by a special machine. It is used for cutting very hard materials, and in many technical fields such as surgery and telecommunications.

ionisation.quick_def: Ionisation is the process of changing an atom or a molecule into an ion by adding or removing electrons.

uncontrollable.quick_def: If you describe a feeling or physical action as uncontrollable, you mean that you cannot control it or prevent yourself from feeling or doing it.

conductors.quick_def: A conductor is a person who stands in front of an orchestra or choir and directs its performance.

cloud-zapper.quick_def: A cloud-zapper is a thing that can deal with clouds, maybe stop bad things from clouds like lightning.

stumbling.quick_def: If you stumble, you put your foot down awkwardly while you are walking or running and nearly fall over.

offing.quick_def: If you say that something is in the offing, you mean that it is likely to happen soon.

manageable.quick_def: Something that is manageable is of a size, quantity, or level of difficulty that people are able to deal with.

avalanche.quick_def: An avalanche is a large mass of snow that falls down the side of a mountain.

expects.quick_def: If you expect something to happen, you believe that it will happen.

cloud-zappers.quick_def: Cloud-zappers are machines that can zap or deal with clouds.

fingertips.quick_def: Your fingertips are the ends of your fingers.

mighty.quick_def: Mighty is used to describe something that is very large or powerful.  [literary]

meteorology.quick_def: Meteorology is the study of the processes in the Earth's atmosphere that cause particular weather conditions, especially in order to predict the weather.

thunder.quick_def: Thunder is the loud noise that you hear from the sky after a flash of lightning, especially during a storm.

flash.quick_def: A flash is a sudden burst of light or of something shiny or bright.

torrential.quick_def: Torrential rain pours down very rapidly and in great quantities.

shake.quick_def: If you shake something, you hold it and move it quickly backwards and forwards or up and down. You can also shake a person, for example, because you are angry with them or because you want them to wake up.

hailstones.quick_def: Hailstones are small balls of ice that fall like rain from the sky.

laser-toting.quick_def: If someone is laser-toting, they are carrying a laser.

geniuses.quick_def: Genius is very great ability or skill in a particular subject or activity.

prodigies.quick_def: A prodigy is someone young who has a great natural ability for something such as music, mathematics, or sport.

gens.quick_def: A gens is a group of families that are related by blood.

begetter.quick_def: The begetter of something has caused this thing to come into existence.  [formal]

divinity.quick_def: Divinity is the study of religion.

paterfamilias.quick_def: the man who is the head of a family

thence.quick_def: Thence means from a particular place, especially when you are giving directions about how to get somewhere.  [formal, old-fashioned]

astrology.quick_def: Astrology is the study of the movements of the planets, sun, moon, and stars in the belief that these movements can have an influence on people's lives.

ambivalent.quick_def: If you say that someone is ambivalent about something, they seem to be uncertain whether they really want it, or whether they really approve of it.

mistrust.quick_def: Mistrust is the feeling that you have towards someone who you do not trust.

weaklings.quick_def: If you describe a person or an animal as a weakling, you mean that they are physically weak.  [disapproval]

unrewarded.quick_def: You can say that someone goes unrewarded, or that their activities go unrewarded, when they do not achieve what they are trying to achieve.

adversity.quick_def: Adversity is a very difficult or unfavourable situation.

highbrow.quick_def: If you say that a book or discussion is highbrow, you mean that it is intellectual, academic, and is often difficult to understand.

egghead.quick_def: If you think someone is more interested in ideas and theories than in practical actions you can say they are an egghead.  [informal, disapproval]

blue-stocking.quick_def: A blue-stocking is a woman who is very interested in learning and intellectual things.

wiseacre.quick_def: a person who is annoying because they are very confident and think they know a lot

know-all.quick_def: A know-all is a person who thinks they know everything and often shows off their knowledge.

boffin.quick_def: A boffin is a scientist, especially one who is doing research.  [British, informal]

adjustment.quick_def: An adjustment is a small change that is made to something such as a machine or a way of doing something.

anecdotes.quick_def: An anecdote is a short, amusing account of something that has happened.

norm-referenced.quick_def: If something is norm-referenced, it is compared with a set of normal standards or the performance of a group.

upbringing.quick_def: Your upbringing is the way that your parents or carers treat you and the things that they teach you when you are growing up.

nobility.quick_def: The nobility of a society are all the people who have titles and belong to a high social class.

corporal.quick_def: A corporal is a non-commissioned officer in the army or United States Marines.

privileged.quick_def: A privilege is a special right or advantage that only one person or group has.

paediatrics.quick_def: Paediatrics is the area of medicine that is concerned with the treatment of children's illnesses.

mist.quick_def: Mist consists of a large number of tiny drops of water in the air, which make it difficult to see very far.

vantage.quick_def: A vantage is a good position that gives you an advantage or a good view.

marvel.quick_def: If you marvel at something, you express your great surprise, wonder, or admiration.

manifestations.quick_def: A manifestation of something is one of the different ways in which it can appear.  [formal]

outrageous.quick_def: If you describe something as outrageous, you are emphasizing that it is unacceptable or very shocking.  [emphasis]

sub-four-minute.quick_def: If something is sub-four-minute, it takes less than four minutes.

milers.quick_def: Milers are people who run races of one mile.

jogging.quick_def: If you jog, you run slowly, often as a form of exercise.

integrity.quick_def: If you have integrity, you are honest and firm in your moral principles.

descriptive.quick_def: Descriptive language or writing indicates what someone or something is like.

existent.quick_def: You can describe something as existent when it exists.  [formal]

immortality.quick_def: Someone or something that is immortal is famous and likely to be remembered for a long time.

disturb.quick_def: If you disturb someone, you interrupt what they are doing and upset them.

comrades.quick_def: Your comrades are your friends, especially friends that you share a difficult or dangerous situation with.  [literary]

sexes.quick_def: The two sexes are the two groups, male and female, into which people and animals are divided according to the function they have in producing young.

energetically.quick_def: If you are energetic in what you do, you have a lot of enthusiasm and determination.

equable.quick_def: If you describe someone as equable, you mean that they are calm, cheerful, and fair with other people, even in difficult circumstances.

attainments.quick_def: The attainment of an aim is the achieving of it.  [formal]

reasonably.quick_def: If you think that someone is fair and sensible, you can say that they are reasonable.

desks.quick_def: A desk is a table, often with drawers, which you sit at to write or work.

rows.quick_def: A row of things or people is a number of them arranged in a line.

mutual.quick_def: You use mutual to describe a situation, feeling, or action that is experienced, felt, or done by both of two people mentioned.

cartoon.quick_def: A cartoon is a humorous drawing or series of drawings in a newspaper or magazine.

approving.quick_def: If you approve of an action, event, or suggestion, you like it or are pleased about it.

homework.quick_def: Homework is school work that teachers give to pupils to do at home in the evening or at the weekend.

elaboration.quick_def: You use elaborate to describe something that is very complex because it has a lot of different parts.

homogeneity.quick_def: Homogeneity is the quality of being homogeneous.  [formal]

renders.quick_def: You can use render with an adjective that describes a particular state to say that someone or something is changed into that state. For example, if someone or something makes a thing harmless, you can say that they render it harmless.

progresses.quick_def: Progress is the process of gradually improving or getting nearer to achieving or completing something.

supportive.quick_def: If you are supportive, you are kind and helpful to someone at a difficult or unhappy time in their life.

glaring.quick_def: If you glare at someone, you look at them with an angry expression on your face.

non-targeted.quick_def: If something is non-targeted, it is not the main thing that you are trying to affect or deal with.

havoc.quick_def: Havoc is great disorder, and confusion.

non-commercial.quick_def: If something is non-commercial, it is not related to making money or for business purposes.

jamil.quick_def: Jamil is a name used to call a person.

perfecting.quick_def: Something that is perfect is as good as it could possibly be.

pressed.quick_def: If you press something somewhere, you push it firmly against something else.

devouring.quick_def: If a person or animal devours something, they eat it quickly and eagerly.

neochetina.quick_def: Neochetina is a kind of beetle.

majors.quick_def: You use major when you want to describe something that is more important, serious, or significant than other things in a group or situation.

minors.quick_def: You use minor when you want to describe something that is less important, serious, or significant than other things in a group or situation.

identifiable.quick_def: Something or someone that is identifiable can be recognized.

overlooks.quick_def: If a building or window overlooks a place, you can see the place clearly from the building or window.

meats.quick_def: Meat is flesh taken from a dead animal that people cook and eat.

utilised.quick_def: If you utilize something, you use it.  [formal]

funnels.quick_def: A funnel is an object with a wide, circular top and a narrow short tube at the bottom. Funnels are used to pour liquids into containers which have a small opening, for example bottles.
