sludge.quick_def: Sludge is thick mud, sewage, or industrial waste.

dichromate.quick_def: A dichromate is a kind of chemical substance. It can be used in some chemical experiments.

dyes.quick_def: If you dye something such as hair or cloth, you change its colour by soaking it in a special liquid.

excretions.quick_def: Excretions are the waste substances that come out of a living thing's body.

glandular.quick_def: Glandular means relating to or affecting your glands.  [technical]

mucus.quick_def: Mucus is a thick liquid that is produced in some parts of your body, for example the inside of your nose.

outrageously.quick_def: If you describe something as outrageous, you are emphasizing that it is unacceptable or very shocking.  [emphasis]

snail.quick_def: A snail is a small animal with a long, soft body, no legs, and a spiral-shaped shell. Snails move very slowly.

grasped.quick_def: If you grasp something, you take it in your hand and hold it very firmly.

tyrian.quick_def: Tyrian is related to a place called Tyre. It is often used to describe things that come from or are related to Tyre, like a special purple color.

mauve.quick_def: Something that is mauve is of a pale purple colour.

violet.quick_def: A violet is a small plant that has purple or white flowers in the spring.

pullar.quick_def: Pullar is a name, usually used for a person.

mentor.quick_def: A person's mentor is someone who gives them help and advice over a period of time, especially help and advice related to their job.

unlimited.quick_def: If there is an unlimited quantity of something, you can have as much or as many of that thing as you want.

synthetically.quick_def: Synthetic products are made from chemicals or artificial substances rather than from natural ones.

dyed.quick_def: If you dye something such as hair or cloth, you change its colour by soaking it in a special liquid.

empress.quick_def: An empress is a woman who rules an empire or who is the wife of an emperor.

flattered.quick_def: If someone flatters you, they praise you in an exaggerated way that is not sincere, because they want to please you or to persuade you to do something.  [disapproval]

fashionable.quick_def: Something or someone that is fashionable is popular or approved of at a particular time.

ladies.quick_def: You can use lady when you are referring to a woman, especially when you are showing politeness or respect.

outdone.quick_def: If you outdo someone, you are a lot more successful than they are at a particular activity.

gown.quick_def: A gown is a dress, usually a long dress, which women wear on formal occasions.

rage.quick_def: Rage is strong anger that is difficult to control.

clamoured.quick_def: If people are clamouring for something, they are demanding it in a noisy or angry way.  [journalism]

stain.quick_def: A stain is a mark on something that is difficult to remove.

bacilli.quick_def: A bacillus is any bacterium that has a long, thin shape.

anthrax.quick_def: Anthrax is a disease of cattle and sheep, in which they get painful sores and a fever. Anthrax can be used in biological weapons.

pleasing.quick_def: You say please when you are politely asking or inviting someone to do something.  [politeness]

vaccine.quick_def: A vaccine is a substance containing a harmless form of the germs that cause a particular disease. It is given to people, usually by injection, to prevent them getting that disease.

haunted.quick_def: If something unpleasant haunts you, you keep thinking or worrying about it over a long period of time.

acronym.quick_def: An acronym is a word composed of the first letters of the words in a phrase, especially when this is used as a name. An example of an acronym is 'NATO', which is made up of the first letters of the 'North Atlantic Treaty Organization'.

seti.quick_def: SETI is the search for intelligent life outside the Earth.

extra-terrestrial.quick_def: Extra-terrestrial means something that comes from outside the Earth.

tenuous.quick_def: If you describe something such as a connection, a reason, or someone's position as tenuous, you mean that it is very uncertain or weak.

ufos.quick_def: UFOs are flying things that people don't know what they are.

unidentified.quick_def: If you describe someone or something as unidentified, you mean that nobody knows who or what they are.

convincing.quick_def: If someone or something convinces you of something, they make you believe that it is true or that it exists.

resemble.quick_def: If one thing or person resembles another, they are similar to each other.

fellows.quick_def: You use fellow to describe people who are in the same situation as you, or people you feel you have something in common with.

orbiting.quick_def: An orbit is the curved path in space that is followed by an object going round and round a planet, moon, or star.

restrictively.quick_def: in a way that prevents people from doing what they want

milky.quick_def: If you describe something as milky, you mean that it is pale white in colour. You can describe other colours as milky when they are very pale.

galaxies.quick_def: A galaxy is an extremely large group of stars and planets that extends over many billions of light years.

observable.quick_def: Something that is observable can be seen.

inconceivable.quick_def: If you describe something as inconceivable, you think it is very unlikely to happen or be true.

carbon-based.quick_def: If something is carbon-based, it is made up of carbon or has carbon as an important part of it. For example, all life on Earth is carbon-based.

life-bearing.quick_def: If something is life-bearing, it can support or has life on it.

attenuated.quick_def: To attenuate something means to reduce it or weaken it.  [formal]

mhz.quick_def: MHz is a written abbreviation for megahertz.

parkes.quick_def: Parkes is the name of a place. It can be a town or a specific area.

detections.quick_def: Detections are the acts of finding or noticing something.

congress.quick_def: A congress is a large meeting that is held to discuss ideas and policies.

nasa.quick_def: NASA is the American government organization concerned with spacecraft and space travel. NASA is an abbreviation for 'National Aeronautics and Space Administration'.

hardware.quick_def: In computer systems, hardware refers to the machines themselves as opposed to the programs which tell the machines what to do. Compare software.

american-operated.quick_def: If something is American-operated, it is run or managed by Americans.

arecibo.quick_def: Arecibo is a place name, a city in Puerto Rico.

rico.quick_def: Rico is a name. People use it to call someone.

nancy.quick_def: an offensive word for a gay man, or a man who behaves in a way that is thought to be typical of women

undirected.quick_def: If something is undirected, it has no specific direction or guidance.

antennas.quick_def: The antennae of something such as an insect or crustacean are the two long, thin parts attached to its head that it uses to feel things with.

reply.quick_def: When you reply to something that someone has said or written to you, you say or write an answer to them.

impracticality.quick_def: the fact of not being sensible or realistic; a thing that is not sensible or realistic

urgency.quick_def: the quality of needing to be dealt with or happen immediately

debates.quick_def: A debate is a discussion about a subject on which people have different views.

drafts.quick_def: A draft is an early version of a letter, email, book, or speech.

enterprising.quick_def: An enterprising person is willing to try out new, unusual ways of doing or achieving something.

parched.quick_def: If something, especially the ground or a plant, is parched, it is very dry, because there has been no rain.

scorpions.quick_def: A scorpion is a small creature which looks like a large insect. Scorpions have a long curved tail, and some of them are poisonous.

woodlice.quick_def: A woodlouse is a very small grey creature with a hard body and fourteen legs. Woodlice live in damp places.

crabs.quick_def: A crab is a sea creature with a flat round body covered by a shell, and five pairs of legs with large claws on the front pair. Crabs usually move sideways.

centipedes.quick_def: A centipede is a long, thin creature with a lot of legs.

redesign.quick_def: If a building, vehicle, or system is redesigned, it is rebuilt according to a new design in order to improve it.

thoroughgoing.quick_def: You use thoroughgoing to emphasize that someone or something is fully or completely the type of person or thing specified.  [emphasis]

hard-earned.quick_def: If something is hard-earned, it is got after a lot of effort.

re-tooling.quick_def: Re-tooling means making changes or adjustments to something to make it work better or be more suitable for a new purpose.

intermediates.quick_def: An intermediate stage, level, or position is one that occurs between two other stages, levels, or positions.

cousins.quick_def: Your cousin is the child of your uncle or aunt.

ceased.quick_def: If something ceases, it stops happening or existing.  [formal]

reverted.quick_def: When people or things revert to a previous state, system, or type of behaviour, they go back to it.

ashore.quick_def: Someone or something that comes ashore comes from the sea onto the shore.

gills.quick_def: Gills are the organs on the sides of fish and other water creatures through which they breathe.

incarnation.quick_def: If you say that someone is the incarnation of a particular quality, you mean that they represent that quality or are typical of it in an extreme form.

vertebrate.quick_def: A vertebrate is a creature which has a spine. Mammals, birds, reptiles, and fish are vertebrates.

returnees.quick_def: A returnee is a person who returns to the country where they were born, usually after they have been away for a long time.

proganochleys.quick_def: Proganochleys is the name of an ancient kind of animal. It is related to the ancestors of modern turtles and tortoises.

quenstedti.quick_def: Quenstedti is a name, often used for a species in the field of fossils. It helps to identify a particular kind of ancient thing.

palaeochersis.quick_def: Palaeochersis is the name of an ancient kind of animal. It lived a long time ago, close to the time of dinosaurs and is related to modern turtles and tortoises.

talampayensis.quick_def: Talampayensis is a scientific name used to name a kind of thing, often for a species in biology.

dinosaur.quick_def: Dinosaurs were large reptiles which lived in prehistoric times.

ichthyosaurs.quick_def: Ichthyosaurs are ancient reptiles that lived at the same time as dinosaurs, having fins and streamlined bodies.

reptilian.quick_def: A reptilian creature is a reptile.

jacques.quick_def: Jacques is a common male given name in French-speaking areas.

gauthier.quick_def: Gauthier is a name, usually used for a person.

graph.quick_def: A graph is a mathematical diagram which shows the relationship between two or more sets of numbers or measurements.

dry-land.quick_def: Dry-land means the land that is not covered by water.

nested.quick_def: A bird's nest is the home that it makes to lay its eggs in.

re-emerged.quick_def: When something re-emerges, it comes out or appears again after being hidden or not seen for a while.

worm-like.quick_def: If something is worm-like, it looks or acts like a worm.

primeval.quick_def: You use primeval to describe things that belong to a very early period in the history of the world.  [formal]

driest.quick_def: If something is dry, there is no water or moisture on it or in it.

impairment.quick_def: If someone has an impairment, they have a condition which prevents their eyes, ears, or brain from working properly.

deficit.quick_def: A deficit is the amount by which something is less than what is required or expected, especially the amount by which the total money received is less than the total money spent.

nelson.quick_def: a move in which a wrestler stands behind his/her opponent, puts one or both arms under the opponent's arm(s) and holds the back of the opponent's neck. When done with one arm it is called a half nelson, and with both arms a full nelson.

soli.quick_def: Soli is a proper name, usually for a person.

possession.quick_def: If you are in possession of something, you have it, because you have obtained it or because it belongs to you.  [formal]

wnce.quick_def: WNCE is an abbreviation for the International Institute of Noise Control Engineering, which is an organization that works on noise-control-related things.

reverberation.quick_def: Reverberations are serious effects that follow a sudden, dramatic event.

disability.quick_def: A disability is a permanent injury, illness, or physical or mental condition that tends to restrict the way that someone can live their life.

deficits.quick_def: A deficit is the amount by which something is less than what is required or expected, especially the amount by which the total money received is less than the total money spent.

autistic.quick_def: If someone is autistic, they have a developmental disorder that can cause them to have difficulty in communicating with and responding to other people.

asd.quick_def: ASD is a kind of disorder that affects how a person communicates and interacts with others.

adhd.quick_def: ADHD is an abbreviation for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder.

life-long.quick_def: If something is life-long, it lasts for your whole life.

discrepancies.quick_def: If there is a discrepancy between two things that ought to be the same, there is a noticeable difference between them.

interlinking.quick_def: Things that are interlinked or interlink are linked with each other in some way.

janzen.quick_def: Janzen is a name of a person.

painful.quick_def: If a part of your body is painful, it hurts because it is injured or because there is something wrong with it.

extra-sensory.quick_def: Extra-sensory means related to senses that are beyond the normal five senses (sight, hearing, touch, taste, smell).

intrusive.quick_def: Something that is intrusive disturbs your mood or your life in a way you do not like.

adversely.quick_def: Adverse decisions, conditions, or effects are unfavourable to you.

sustaining.quick_def: If you sustain something, you continue it or maintain it for a period of time.

disinhibition.quick_def: the state of no longer feeling shy so that you can relax and show your feelings

unimportant.quick_def: If you describe something or someone as unimportant, you mean that they do not have much influence, effect, or value, and are therefore not worth serious consideration.

undiagnosed.quick_def: If a disease or problem is undiagnosed, doctors haven't found out what it is yet.

vitally.quick_def: If you say that something is vital, you mean that it is necessary or very important.

formulating.quick_def: If you formulate something such as a plan or proposal, you invent it, thinking about the details carefully.

promulgated.quick_def: If people promulgate a new law or a new idea, they make it widely known.  [formal]

transits.quick_def: Transits are the movements of one celestial body across the face of another.

heather.quick_def: Heather is a low, spreading plant with small purple, pink, or white flowers. Heather grows wild in Europe on high land with poor soil.

cooper.quick_def: A cooper is a person who makes barrels.  [old-fashioned]

henbest.quick_def: Henbest is a surname, which is a family name passed down through generations.

inched.quick_def: An inch is an imperial unit of length, approximately equal to 2.54 centimetres. There are twelve inches in a foot.

newcomb.quick_def: Newcomb is a surname, which is a family name used to identify a particular family.

schoolmistresses.quick_def: A schoolmistress is a female teacher in a school.  [old-fashioned]

outperformed.quick_def: If one person or thing outperforms another, the first is more successful or efficient than the second.  [journalism]

astronomers.quick_def: An astronomer is a scientist who studies the stars, planets, and other natural objects in space.

polymath.quick_def: a person who knows a lot about many different subjects

edmond.quick_def: Edmond is a name for a person.

halley.quick_def: Halley is a proper name, often used for a person.

desolate.quick_def: A desolate place is empty of people and lacking in comfort.

helena.quick_def: Helena is a name for a person or a place.

disc.quick_def: A disc is a flat, circular shape or object.

widely-separated.quick_def: If two things are widely-separated, they are far away from each other.

parallax.quick_def: Parallax is when an object appears to change its position because the person or instrument observing it has changed their position.  [technical]

johannes.quick_def: Johannes is a name for a person.

pin.quick_def: Pins are very small thin pointed pieces of metal. They are used in sewing to fasten pieces of material together until they have been sewn.

guillaume.quick_def: Guillaume is a male given name, which is used to call a man.

gentil.quick_def: Gentil is a French word. In English, it can be similar to 'kind' or 'gentle'. It describes a person who is nice and friendly.

thwarted.quick_def: If you thwart someone or thwart their plans, you prevent them from doing or getting what they want.

besieging.quick_def: If you are besieged by people, many people want something from you and continually bother you.

pondicherry.quick_def: Pondicherry is a place name, a city in India.

fleeing.quick_def: If you flee from something or someone, or flee a person or thing, you escape from them.  [written]

undaunted.quick_def: If you are undaunted, you are not at all afraid or worried about dealing with something, especially something that would frighten or worry most people.

clouded.quick_def: A cloud is a mass of water vapour that floats in the sky. Clouds are usually white or grey in colour.

dispiriting.quick_def: Something that is dispiriting causes you to lose your enthusiasm and excitement.

timings.quick_def: Timings are the times when something happens or is planned to happen.

dogged.quick_def: A dog is a very common four-legged animal that is often kept by people as a pet or to guard or hunt. There are many different breeds of dog.

smeared.quick_def: If something is smeared, it has dirty or oily marks on it.

diffraction.quick_def: In physics, diffraction is a change in the direction of a sound wave or a light wave caused by the presence of an obstacle in its path.

halo.quick_def: A halo is a circle of light that is shown in pictures round the head of a holy figure such as a saint or angel.

refracting.quick_def: When a ray of light or a sound wave refracts or is refracted, the path it follows bends at a particular point, for example when it enters water or glass.

laboured.quick_def: Labour is very hard work, usually physical work.

johann.quick_def: Johann is a male given name.

franz.quick_def: Franz is a common male name.

encke.quick_def: Encke is a name, usually used for a person.

berlin.quick_def: Berlin is the capital city of Germany.

observatory.quick_def: An observatory is a building with a large telescope from which scientists study things such as the planets by watching them.

spectacle.quick_def: Glasses are sometimes referred to as spectacles.  [formal]

earth-sized.quick_def: If something is Earth-sized, it has the same size as the Earth.

neuroeconomics.quick_def: Neuroeconomics is a field that studies how the brain works in economic situations.

iconoclastic.quick_def: If you describe someone or their words or ideas as iconoclastic, you mean that they contradict established beliefs.  [formal]

briefly.quick_def: Something that happens or is done briefly happens or is done for a very short period of time.

iconoclast.quick_def: If you describe someone as an iconoclast, you mean that they often criticize beliefs and things that are generally accepted by society.  [formal]

iconoclasts.quick_def: If you describe someone as an iconoclast, you mean that they often criticize beliefs and things that are generally accepted by society.  [formal]

utilizes.quick_def: If you utilize something, you use it.  [formal]

naysayers.quick_def: Naysayers are people who always say no or disagree with others.

drumbeat.quick_def: A drumbeat is the sound of a beat on a drum.

impeded.quick_def: If you impede someone or something, you make their movement, development, or progress difficult.  [formal]

quickest.quick_def: Someone or something that is quick moves or does things with great speed.

shortcuts.quick_def: A shortcut is a quicker way of getting somewhere than the usual route.

rumblings.quick_def: A rumbling is a low continuous noise.

photons.quick_def: A photon is a particle of light.  [technical]

iconoclasm.quick_def: the beliefs and behaviour of an iconoclast (= a person who criticizes popular beliefs or established customs and ideas)

curse.quick_def: If you curse, you use rude or offensive language, usually because you are angry about something.  [written]

conjectures.quick_def: A conjecture is a conclusion that is based on information that is not certain or complete.  [formal]

bombard.quick_def: If you bombard someone with something, you make them face a great deal of it. For example, if you bombard them with questions or criticism, you keep asking them a lot of questions or you keep criticizing them.

impediment.quick_def: Something that is an impediment to a person or thing makes their movement, development, or progress difficult.  [formal]

ridicule.quick_def: If you ridicule someone or ridicule their ideas or beliefs, you make fun of them in an unkind way.

phobias.quick_def: A phobia is a very strong irrational fear or hatred of something.

afflicts.quick_def: If you are afflicted by pain, illness, or disaster, it affects you badly and makes you suffer.  [formal]

one-third.quick_def: One-third means dividing something into three equal parts and taking one of those parts.

coordinate.quick_def: If you coordinate an activity, you organize the various people and things involved in it.

fairness.quick_def: Fairness is the quality of being reasonable, right, and just.

intertwined.quick_def: If two or more things are intertwined or intertwine, they are closely connected with each other in many ways.

asset.quick_def: Something or someone that is an asset is considered useful or helps a person or organization to be successful.

deteriorates.quick_def: If something deteriorates, it becomes worse in some way.

invective.quick_def: Invective is rude and unpleasant things that people shout at people they hate or are angry with.  [formal]

polemic.quick_def: A polemic is a very strong written or spoken attack on, or defence of, a particular belief or opinion.

usages.quick_def: Usage is the way in which words are actually used in particular contexts, especially with regard to their meanings.

hurt.quick_def: If you hurt yourself or hurt a part of your body, you feel pain because you have injured yourself.

unfeelingly.quick_def: If you do something unfeelingly, you do it without showing any kindness or sympathy.

prescriptivism.quick_def: Prescriptivism is the idea that one kind of language is better than others and should be used by everyone.

propounded.quick_def: If someone propounds an idea or point of view they have, they suggest it for people to consider.  [formal]

adherents.quick_def: An adherent is someone who holds a particular belief or supports a particular person or group.

prescriptively.quick_def: When you do something prescriptively, you follow strict rules or instructions to do it.

grammars.quick_def: Grammar is the ways that words can be put together in order to make sentences.

codify.quick_def: If you codify a set of rules, you define them or present them in a clear and ordered way.

settling.quick_def: If people settle an argument or problem, or if something settles it, they solve it, for example by making a decision about who is right or about what to do.

authoritarian.quick_def: If you describe a person or an organization as authoritarian, you are critical of them controlling everything rather than letting people decide things for themselves.  [disapproval]

proscribed.quick_def: If something is proscribed by people in authority, the existence or the use of that thing is forbidden.  [formal]

half-measures.quick_def: Half-measures are actions that are not done completely or strongly enough to achieve the desired result.

grammarian.quick_def: A grammarian is someone who studies the grammar of a language and writes books about it or teaches it.

pronounce.quick_def: To pronounce a word means to say it using particular sounds.

summarised.quick_def: If you summarize something, you give a summary of it.

halting.quick_def: When a person or a vehicle halts or when something halts them, they stop moving in the direction they were going and stand still.

priestley.quick_def: Priestley is a name of a person. People use this name to call a specific individual.

rudiments.quick_def: When you learn the rudiments of something, you learn the simplest or most essential things about it.

tenet.quick_def: The tenets of a theory or belief are the main principles on which it is based.  [formal]

descriptivists.quick_def: Descriptivists are people who describe how language is actually used in real life.

prescriptivists.quick_def: Prescriptivists are people who think there are fixed rules for language and everyone should follow them.

unreal.quick_def: If you say that a situation is unreal, you mean that it is so strange that you find it difficult to believe it is happening.

prescriptive.quick_def: A prescriptive approach to something involves telling people what they should do, rather than simply giving suggestions or describing what is done.  [formal]

quasi-political.quick_def: If something is quasi-political, it is almost like a political thing but not completely political.

liberalism.quick_def: Liberalism is a belief in gradual social progress by changing laws, rather than by revolution.

elitist.quick_def: Elitist systems, practices, or ideas favour the most powerful, rich, or talented people within a group, place, or society.  [disapproval]

conservatism.quick_def: Conservatism is a political philosophy which believes that if changes need to be made to society, they should be made gradually. You can also refer to the political beliefs of a conservative party in a particular country as Conservatism.

undersea.quick_def: Undersea things or activities exist or happen below the surface of the sea.

propellers.quick_def: A propeller is a device with blades which is attached to a boat or aircraft. The engine makes the propeller spin round and causes the boat or aircraft to move.

earner.quick_def: An earner is someone or something that earns money or produces profit.

undercutting.quick_def: If you undercut someone or undercut their prices, you sell a product more cheaply than they do.  [business]

ailing.quick_def: If something ails a group or area of activity, it is a problem or source of trouble for that group or for people involved in that activity.

pentland.quick_def: Pentland is a name, usually a person's last name.

firth.quick_def: (especially in Scottish place names) a narrow area of the sea that runs a long way into the land, or a part of a river where it flows into the sea

orkney.quick_def: Orkney is a group of islands in Scotland. It's a place on the map.

alderney.quick_def: the furthest north of the Channel Islands

channel.quick_def: A channel is a television station.

megawatts.quick_def: A megawatt is a unit of power. One megawatt is a million watts.

sizewell.quick_def: a group of nuclear power stations on the east coast of England, in Suffolk. The first one, Sizewell A, was built in 1966 and Sizewell B, a much larger power station, began producing electricity in 1995. Sizewell A stopped production in 2006.

suffolk.quick_def: a county in East Anglia, eastern England. It consists mainly of agricultural land. The administrative centre is Ipswich.

campbelttown.quick_def: Campbelttown is the name of a place, like a town or a city.

turbine.quick_def: A turbine is a machine or engine which uses a stream of air, gas, water, or steam to turn a wheel and produce power.

lynmouth.quick_def: Lynmouth is the name of a place, like a town or a village.

devon.quick_def: a county in south-west England. With two national parks, Dartmoor and Exmoor, and two coasts, north and south, it is a popular area for holidays. The administrative centre is Exeter.

shortly.quick_def: If something happens shortly after or before something else, it happens not long after or before it. If something is going to happen shortly, it is going to happen soon.

jointly.quick_def: Joint means shared by or belonging to two or more people.

abubakr.quick_def: Abubakr is a name for a person.

bahaj.quick_def: Bahaj is a name of a person.

blade.quick_def: The blade of a knife, axe, or saw is the flat sharp part that is used for cutting.

subsidiary.quick_def: A subsidiary or a subsidiary company is a company which is part of a larger and more important company.  [business]

coasts.quick_def: The coast is an area of land that is next to the sea.

indented.quick_def: When you indent a line of writing, you start it further away from the edge of the paper than all the other lines.

slow-turning.quick_def: If something is slow-turning, it turns around very slowly.

tower.quick_def: A tower is a tall, narrow building, that either stands alone or forms part of another building such as a church or castle.

re-imported.quick_def: When something is re-imported, it is brought back into a country after it was sent out before.

cable.quick_def: A cable is a thick wire, or a group of wires inside a rubber or plastic covering, which is used to carry electricity or electronic signals.

cavitation.quick_def: Cavitation is a situation where low pressure makes air bubbles form in a liquid.

vibration.quick_def: If something vibrates or if you vibrate it, it shakes with repeated small, quick movements.

submerged.quick_def: If something submerges or if you submerge it, it goes below the surface of some water or another liquid.

dvd.quick_def: A DVD is a disc on which a film or music is recorded. DVD discs are similar to compact discs but hold a lot more information. DVD is an abbreviation for 'digital video disc' or 'digital versatile disc'.

probe.quick_def: If you probe into something, you ask questions or try to discover facts about it.

voyager.quick_def: A voyage is a long journey on a ship or in a spacecraft.

saturn.quick_def: a large planet in the solar system that has rings around it and is 6th in order of distance from the sun

instruct.quick_def: If you instruct someone to do something, you formally tell them to do it.  [formal]

spares.quick_def: You use spare to describe something that is the same as things that you are already using, but that you do not need yet and are keeping ready in case another one is needed.

pluto.quick_def: one of a number of round objects in space that are not as large as planets but which go around the sun. In August 2006, the International Astronomical Union declared that Pluto should be called a dwarf planet because it is smaller and has different characteristics from the other planets in our solar system; in 2008 it declared that dwarf planets further from the sun than Neptune could also be called plutoids.

switchover.quick_def: a change from one system, method, policy, etc. to another

longest-distance.quick_def: If something is the longest-distance, it covers the greatest length from one point to another compared to others.

highlighted.quick_def: If someone or something highlights a point or problem, they emphasize it or make you think about it.

claude.quick_def: Claude is a name for a person.

shannon.quick_def: a first name for boys or girls

petoskey.quick_def: Petoskey is the name of a place, like a town or a city.

bell.quick_def: A bell is a device that makes a ringing sound and is used to give a signal or to attract people's attention.

shunned.quick_def: If you shun someone or something, you deliberately avoid them or keep away from them.

single-handedly.quick_def: If you do something single-handedly, you do it alone without any help from others.

inveigled.quick_def: If you inveigle someone into doing something, you cleverly persuade them to do it when they do not really want to.  [formal]

dvds.quick_def: DVDs are small round discs that can store movies, music, or other data. You can play them on a DVD player.

down-to-earth.quick_def: If a person or thing is down-to-earth, they are practical and realistic, not having unrealistic ideas.

generalises.quick_def: If you generalize, you say something that seems to be true in most situations or for most people, but that may not be completely true in all cases.

error-free.quick_def: If something is error-free, it has no mistakes.

bandwidth.quick_def: A bandwidth is the range of frequencies used for a particular telecommunications signal, radio transmission, or computer network.

coding.quick_def: A code is a set of rules about how people should behave or about how something must be done.

ravages.quick_def: A town, country, or economy that has been ravaged is one that has been damaged so much that it is almost completely destroyed.

information-carrying.quick_def: If something is information-carrying, it can hold and take information from one place to another.

stunningly.quick_def: A stunning person or thing is extremely beautiful or impressive.

error-detecting.quick_def: Error-detecting means being able to find out if there are mistakes or errors.

check-out.quick_def: A check-out is a place in a store where you pay for the things you want to buy.

crumpled.quick_def: If you crumple something such as paper or cloth, or if it crumples, it is squashed and becomes full of untidy creases and folds.

bag.quick_def: A bag is a container made of thin paper or plastic, for example one that is used in shops to put things in that a customer has bought.

crisps.quick_def: Food that is crisp is pleasantly hard, or has a pleasantly hard surface.  [approval]

turbo.quick_def: A turbo is a fan in the engine of a car or plane that improves its performance by using exhaust gases to blow fuel vapour into the engine.

videophone.quick_def: a type of phone with a screen that enables you to see the person you are talking to

superfluous.quick_def: Something that is superfluous is unnecessary or is no longer needed.

cn.quick_def: CN is a short way to write 'can'. 'Can' means to be able to do something.

cram.quick_def: If you cram things or people into a container or place, you put them into it, although there is hardly enough room for them.

sklodowska.quick_def: Sklodowska is a family name. People use it to tell one family from another.

radioactivity.quick_def: Something that is radioactive contains a substance that produces energy in the form of powerful and harmful rays.

henri.quick_def: Henri is a male given name. It's used to call a man.

completion.quick_def: You use complete to emphasize that something is as great in extent, degree, or amount as it possibly can be.  [emphasis]

sister.quick_def: Your sister is a girl or woman who has the same parents as you.

bronia.quick_def: Bronia is a name for a person, usually a girl or woman.

sorbonne.quick_def: The Sorbonne is a very famous university in Paris.

uranium.quick_def: Uranium is a naturally occurring radioactive metal that is used to produce nuclear energy and weapons.

thorium.quick_def: a chemical element. Thorium is a white radioactive metal used as a source of nuclear energy.

pitchblende.quick_def: Pitchblende is a kind of mineral that has radioactivity.

polonium.quick_def: a chemical element. Polonium is a radioactive metal that is present in nature when uranium decays.

radium.quick_def: Radium is a radioactive element which is used in the treatment of cancer.

chiefly.quick_def: You use chiefly to indicate that a particular reason, emotion, method, or feature is the main or most important one.

radiations.quick_def: Radiations are forms of energy that travel through space or matter. They can be like light or heat that spreads out from a source.

metallic.quick_def: A metallic sound is like the sound of one piece of metal hitting another.

debierne.quick_def: Debierne is a surname, which is used to call a person.

doctorate.quick_def: A doctorate is the highest degree awarded by a university.

eve.quick_def: The eve of a particular event or occasion is the day before it, or the period of time just before it.  [journalism]

interrupt.quick_def: If you interrupt someone who is speaking, you say or do something that causes them to stop.

normale.quick_def: In some contexts, 'Normale' is related to a special type of school. These schools are often for training teachers and are known for high-level education.

henceforth.quick_def: Henceforth means from this time onwards.  [formal]

professorship.quick_def: A professorship is the post of professor in a university or college.

vacant.quick_def: If something is vacant, it is not being used by anyone.

x-radiography.quick_def: X-radiography is a way to take pictures of the inside of a body using X-rays. Doctors use it to find problems in bones or organs.

curies.quick_def: Curies are units used to measure the amount of radioactivity.

wounded.quick_def: injured by a weapon, for example in a war

radioactive.quick_def: Something that is radioactive contains a substance that produces energy in the form of powerful and harmful rays.

triumphant.quick_def: Someone who is triumphant has gained a victory or succeeded in something and feels very happy about it.

czechoslovakia.quick_def: Czechoslovakia was a country in Europe before. It doesn't exist now.

inauguration.quick_def: When a new leader is inaugurated, they are formally given their new position at an official ceremony.

warsaw.quick_def: Warsaw is the capital city of Poland.

neutron.quick_def: A neutron is an atomic particle that has no electrical charge.

chadwick.quick_def: Chadwick is a name of a person. People use it to call someone.

joliot-curie.quick_def: Joliot-Curie is a family name. People with this name are well-known scientists.

leukaemia.quick_def: Leukaemia is a disease of the blood in which the body produces too many white blood cells.

isotopes.quick_def: Isotopes are atoms that have the same number of protons and electrons but different numbers of neutrons and therefore have different physical properties.  [technical]

remarking.quick_def: If you remark that something is the case, you say that it is the case.

cooley.quick_def: Cooley is a surname, which is a family name used to identify a person's family.

self-understanding.quick_def: Self-understanding is when you know about your own feelings, abilities, and what kind of person you are.

self-as-subject.quick_def: Self-as-subject means the part of yourself that is aware of your own thoughts, feelings, and actions, like the 'you' that knows what you're thinking and doing.

distinctiveness.quick_def: Distinctiveness is the quality that makes someone or something different from others.

caregivers.quick_def: A caregiver is someone who is responsible for looking after another person, for example, a person who has a disability, or is ill or very young.  [mainly US]

cry.quick_def: When you cry, tears come from your eyes, usually because you are unhappy or hurt.

vocalizations.quick_def: Vocalizations are the sounds that people or animals make with their voices.

brooks-gunn.quick_def: Brooks-Gunn is a person's name. People use names to call and identify different individuals.

co-operate.quick_def: When you co-operate with others, you work together with them to achieve a goal.

dunn.quick_def: Dunn is a common surname, which is used to call a person.

self-awareness.quick_def: Self-awareness is the ability to know about yourself, like your feelings, thoughts, and actions.

self-as-object.quick_def: Self-as-object means seeing yourself as something that can be observed and thought about, like looking at yourself from the outside.

trustworthiness.quick_def: the quality of always being good, honest, sincere, etc. so that people can rely on you

shyness.quick_def: A shy person is nervous and uncomfortable in the company of other people.

looking-glass.quick_def: A looking-glass is an object that can show your reflection, just like a mirror.

mead.quick_def: In former times, mead was an alcoholic drink made of honey, spices, and water.

visually.quick_def: Visual means relating to sight, or to things that you can see.

birthday.quick_def: Your birthday is the anniversary of the date on which you were born.

dabbed.quick_def: If you dab something, you touch it several times using quick, light movements. If you dab a substance onto a surface, you put it there using quick, light movements.

bronson.quick_def: Bronson is a name for a person.

disagreements.quick_def: Disagreement means objecting to something such as a proposal.

tug-of-war.quick_def: A tug-of-war is a game where two teams pull on opposite ends of a rope to try to pull the other team over a line.

disputing.quick_def: A dispute is an argument or disagreement between people or groups.

wanting.quick_def: If you want something, you feel a desire or a need for it.

infallible.quick_def: If a person or thing is infallible, they are never wrong.

testimony.quick_def: In a court of law, someone's testimony is a formal statement that they make about what they saw someone do or what they know of a situation, after having promised to tell the truth.

chronicles.quick_def: To chronicle a series of events means to write about them or show them in broadcasts in the order in which they happened.

veracity.quick_def: Veracity is the quality of being true or the habit of telling the truth.  [formal]

relic.quick_def: If you refer to something or someone as a relic of an earlier period, you mean that they belonged to that period but have survived into the present.

facto.quick_def: In 'ipso facto', it means by the fact itself. When something is true ipso facto, it is true just because of a certain fact.

showcases.quick_def: A showcase is a glass container with valuable objects inside it, for example at an exhibition or in a museum.

jorvik.quick_def: Jorvik is the name of a place, like a city or an area.

bradford.quick_def: an industrial city in Yorkshire, England. Since the Middle Ages it has been an important centre for the wool trade and for textile (= cloth) production. It now has a large Asian community and is the home of the National Museum of Photography, Film and Television.

williamsburg.quick_def: a historic US town in south-eastern Virginia. It was settled in 1633 as Middle Plantation but soon named after the English king William III. It was the capital of the colony from 1699 to 1779. The College of William and Mary was established there in 1693. The 18th-century town was built again in the 1930s as Colonial Williamsburg and is now very popular with tourists.

re-enactment.quick_def: A re-enactment is when people do or show an event again, just like it happened before.

intolerable.quick_def: If you describe something as intolerable, you mean that it is so bad or extreme that no one can bear it or tolerate it.

vulgarization.quick_def: the process of making something less good by changing it so that it is more ordinary than before and not of such a high standard

evaporating.quick_def: When a liquid evaporates, or is evaporated, it changes from a liquid state to a gas, because its temperature has increased.

borrow.quick_def: If you borrow something that belongs to someone else, you take it or use it for a period of time, usually with their permission.

theming.quick_def: Theming means creating or organizing something around a particular theme.

authenticity.quick_def: An authentic person, object, or emotion is genuine.

research-based.quick_def: If something is research-based, it is made or done according to the results of research.

cages.quick_def: A cage is a structure of wire or metal bars in which birds or animals are kept.

burgers.quick_def: A burger is a flat round mass of minced meat or vegetables, which is fried and often eaten in a bread roll.

presentation.quick_def: You use present to describe things and people that exist now, rather than those that existed in the past or those that may exist in the future.

fulfil.quick_def: If you fulfil something such as a promise, dream, or hope, you do what you said or hoped you would do.

attractively.quick_def: A person who is attractive is pleasant to look at.

professionally.quick_def: Professional means relating to a person's work, especially work that requires special training.

attractiveness.quick_def: A person who is attractive is pleasant to look at.

income-generating.quick_def: If something is income-generating, it can help you make money.

pithecanthropus.quick_def: Pithecanthropus is an old-fashioned name for an early kind of human-like creature.

erectus.quick_def: Erectus is a scientific term used to describe a species that can stand upright.

malay.quick_def: Malay means belonging or relating to the people, language, or culture of the largest racial group in Malaysia.

neanderthal.quick_def: Neanderthal people lived in Europe between 35,000 and 70,000 years ago.

gesture.quick_def: A gesture is a movement that you make with a part of your body, especially your hands, to express emotion or information.

transitory.quick_def: If you say that something is transitory, you mean that it lasts only for a short time.

castles.quick_def: A castle is a large building with thick, high walls. Castles were built by important people, such as kings, in former times, especially for protection during wars and battles.

furnishings.quick_def: The furnishings of a room or house are the furniture, curtains, carpets, and decorations such as pictures.

premises.quick_def: The premises of a business or an institution are all the buildings and land that it occupies in one place.

leyden.quick_def: Leyden is the name of a town. It's a place where people live.

nostalgia.quick_def: Nostalgia is an affectionate feeling you have for the past, especially for a particularly happy time.
